Patreon help

This guide holds Patreon’s own help, gathered from support.patreon.com in November 2026. Patreon is a site where creators earn from members who pay each month for their work. It covers joining and paying as a member, and setting up, earning and getting paid as a creator. Each heading names who it is for, then the subject. Ko-fi, a similar site, has a guide of its own in this collection.

Left out on purpose: legal pages such as terms and privacy policies, pages for law enforcement and developers, and Android-only articles, as this collection covers Windows, the web, iPhone and iPad, and Alexa. The categories are the publisher’s own.

The help text belongs to its publisher and is gathered here unchanged for accessible reading. This guide’s own arrangement and wording are available under CC BY-SA 4.0.

Creators: Discovery

Clips

Grow your membership using Clips. On iOS, Clips suggests shareable moments from videos you upload to Patreon. Use these clips to share your work with fans and promote your paid membership on Patreon using Quips.

How it works

Clips automatically turns your Patreon videos into shareable moments, ready to Quip.

  • Open the Clip composer and tap the bottom-right entry point to open the clip library.
  • Browse featured and generated clips, filtering by post; tap a clip to open the viewer and swipe up to see more.
  • Tap “Trim” to adjust start and end points, then “Save”. Tap thumbs down to leave feedback.
  • Tap “Add” to attach the clip to a Quip, add a caption, and share.
  • You can also download a clip to share it off platform.
  • Videos must be Patreon native, at least eight minutes long, and have audio in English to have clip suggestions.
  • You’ll need to be on the latest version of the app to access Clips. If you search Patreon on the app store, it should say “Update”.

After you publish a video post, we’ll send you a push notification once clips are ready. Tap it to jump straight into your Clip library.

FAQ

  • We use AI to generate a transcript from your video and suggest the start and end times of clips. We do not use your content to train AI models. Clips are never published unless you explicitly attach one to a Quip. You can learn more about our CEO Jack Conte’s thoughts on AI here.
  • Clips are generated for new video posts, not for videos you uploaded in the past. New video posts will have clips generated from them automatically if they exceed the eight-minute minimum duration and have audio in English. If you’d like clips generated for a specific past video, please reach out with the post URL.
  • We generate up to eight clips per video. Each video must be over 8 minutes to be eligible for clip generation.
  • Occasionally, a video won’t get suggested clips. Clip suggestions are powered by Google’s generative AI, which follows Google’s Prohibited Use Policy. If a video’s transcript gets flagged under that policy, we aren’t able to generate clips for it.
  • This only affects clip suggestions. Your video itself is untouched, stays live, and works exactly as normal.
  • You are eligible if you have used the iOS app within the last 30 days and have uploaded eligible videos to Patreon (8min+, English audio). If you don’t see the feature, log in to your iOS Patreon app and check back after your next uploaded video.
  • Videos must be at least eight minutes long and have audio in English.
  • This depends on the length of the video. It typically takes up to ten minutes to generate clips after publishing a video post.
  • No. Unless you explicitly attach a clip to a Quip and post it, no one else can see a clip.
  • Check the App Store for an update to the Patreon app.
  • Clips is only available on iOS. You can still upload your long-form video in a post on web as you usually do. It’s just the clips themselves that are iOS only.
  • Just tap the thumbs down button when creating a clip to leave us feedback on the feature.
  • Yes, you can download a clip to share off-platform or you can share it directly to a Quip.
  • Not at this time. If a video has DRM enabled, Clips won’t be generated for it. We’ll share updates if that changes.
  • Yes, please reach out to support if you’d like us to turn this feature off.

Collaboration posts

Collaboration posts allow you to publish content with other creators. Collaboration posts are made to help you grow your audience on Patreon seamlessly by introducing yourself to an entirely new set of fans. These posts are always public, and they’ll show up on the Home feed.

For Adult/18+ creators, you’ll only be able to publish collaboration posts with other creators who make work for Adult/18+ audiences.

How collaboration posts work

A post can have up to 3 collaborators, and the built-in invite system makes it easy for creators to invite each other, review pending requests, and accept or decline collaboration.

You can’t add yourself as a collaborator to another creator’s post, they must invite you. When you’re invited as a collaborator, you’ll receive an email and notification. Once you accept a collaboration invite, the post can also be shared with your members, depending on the post status (already published or not) and your notification settings. As a collaborator, you can remove yourself from a collaboration if needed at any time.

Collaboration posts can be created on both the desktop and the Patreon mobile app, and will appear in the Home feed with up to 3 collaborators’ names in the byline.

Looking to collaborate and reach new audiences? Check out “Engage with Other Creators to Fuel Discovery” on Patreon for Creators. Currently, Patreon for Creators is only available in English.

How to make a collaboration post

To make a collaboration post as the original author, follow the steps below:

- Click +
- Go to the Collaborators section in the editor in the right side panel and click + Add
- A pop-up will appear, then type the name of the creator you want to invite in the search field
- Once you have found them, select the corresponding creator
- They'll appear on the Selected creators list right below the search bar
- You can invite up to 3 creators per post. If you want to remove someone you've added, just click the ✓ icon beside their name, and they'll be removed from the list
- Click on the Send invite button, and the collaborators you invited get an email with the option to preview the post and accept your collaboration request
- They'll now appear on the list under the Collaborators section
    - Below the collaborator's name will show if the invite is pending or has been accepted
    - You can still remove someone you've invited by clicking the X next to their name, and they'll be removed from the list
- You can either Publish your post right away or Set publish date, regardless of whether all the collaborators haven't accepted the invite yet
- If you decide to publish it before collaborators accept the invite, click on the Publish button at the top
- A pop-up will appear, then click on Publish anyway
- Your post is now live, and you'll be notified when collaborators accept or decline. Their names will be added to the byline when they accept
- When creating the new post, make sure to select Free access for the audience
- To invite a collaborator, tap the Settings button in the top menu
- In the settings, find the Collaborators section
- Tap the + Add button
- A pop-up will appear, then type the name of the creator you want to invite in the search field
- Once you have found them, tap the corresponding creator
- They'll appear on the Selected creators list right below the search bar
- You can invite up to 3 creators per post. If you want to remove someone you've added, just tap the ✓ icon beside their name, and they'll be removed from the list
- Tap on the Send invite button, and the collaborators you invited get an email with the option to preview the post and accept your collaboration request
- They'll now appear on the list under the Collaborators section
    - Below the collaborator's name will show if the invite is pending or has been accepted
    - You can still remove someone you've invited by tapping the X next to their name, and they'll be removed from the list
- You can either Publish your post right away or Set publish date, regardless of whether all the collaborators haven't accepted the invite yet
- If you decide to publish it before collaborators accept the invite, tap on the Publish button at the top
- A pop-up will appear, then tap on Publish anyway
- Your post is now live, and you'll be notified when collaborators accept or decline. Their names will be added to the byline when they accept

What happens when you’re invited as a collaborator

If another creator invites you as a collaborator, here’s what you can expect:

  • You’ll receive an email and a notification letting you know that you’ve been invited as a collaborator on a post
  • Once you accept the invite, a notification is sent out to your members, and the post will automatically appear on your feed, showing the creators’ names in the byline
  • When the invitation is accepted, but the post is still in draft mode, you’ll receive a notification once the original author publishes it
  • You can view the post, even before it’s published, and share it just like your own
  • If you remove the post from your feed, it’ll stay published on the original creator’s page
  • You can’t edit or delete the post directly; only the original creator can make changes
  • Fans can comment on collaboration posts as they do on regular public posts. For combined creators, new public posts default to Anyone can comment. The original author controls the comment settings for the post and can adjust them at any time in the post editor. For more details, visit our guide on Comment settings

Managing collaborations

In case you experience abuse (e.g., spam) as a collaborator, you have the option to remove yourself from the post.

For invites that haven’t been accepted yet, a message will appear at the top of the post stating that you’re a collaborator. From there, select Decline, and your name won’t be added to the post. After declining, you’ll lose access to the preview page if the post is unpublished. If the post is already published, you’ll still be able to view it, but your name won’t be listed as a collaborator.

Once an invite has been accepted, you can remove yourself from a post by following the steps below:

- Go to the post where you were invited as a collaborator — you'll receive an email and a notification on your Patreon account when someone invites you as a collaborator
- Click More right below the post title to open the menu, then click Remove name
- A pop-up will appear for you to confirm if you'd like to remove it
- Since this is an irreversible process, once you're sure, click on the Confirm button
- Your name is now removed from the post
- Go to the post where you were invited as a collaborator — you'll receive an email and a notification on your Patreon account when someone invites you as a collaborator
- Tap on More in the top right corner, then tap Remove name
- A pop-up will appear for you to confirm if you'd like to remove it
- Since this is an irreversible process, once you're sure, tap on the Confirm button
- Your name is now removed from the post

If the original author deletes a collaboration post, the post will no longer be available to collaborators, and the collaboration ends. If you try to open the post from a notification or link after it’s been deleted, you’ll see a message letting you know the post is no longer available.

Where collaboration posts appear

On your page, collaboration posts will appear alongside your other public posts, and they’ll also show up in the Home feed. Collaboration posts can’t be added to collections or sold, and the original post will always remain public.

FAQ

  • Create collaborations with creators who partnered with you on the content and are co-authors. The invite system ensures collaborators must accept before being added to a post, so no one is included without their consent.
  • Collaborators receive invitation emails with post previews and can decide on their own timeline whether to accept them. Once an invitation is accepted, a notification is sent to the collaborator’s members. Your members won’t get duplicate notifications if they follow multiple creators on the post.

How can fans discover me on Patreon

This article explains how fans can discover you on Patreon via the Explore tab and offers tips to improve your visibility and attract more potential members. Discovery is now also fueled by new features like Quips and Collab Posts, which appear in feeds and during interactions.

The Explore tab

The Explore tab is a place where fans can find their favorite creators and discover new ones based on their interests. Creators are categorized into various genres and niches based on their content type, taglines, and descriptions. Each fan’s Explore tab is personalized to show creators that align with their memberships, activities, and interests.

As a creator, you can also use the Explore tab to find other creators you follow or support. To learn more about finding other creators and navigating the Explore tab, check out our Find creators on Patreon guide.

Improving your chances of being found

Want to boost your visibility on the Explore tab? Here are some tips to help you get featured more often:

  • Refine your taglines and descriptions: Make sure they clearly and accurately describe your work. This helps potential fans quickly understand your content and decide if they want to learn more
  • Update your About section: Craft a concise, engaging summary of what you create. Highlight what makes your work unique and interesting
  • Offer content previews: Providing previews of your audio or video content allows potential fans to sample your work before committing to supporting you
  • Create public or free Content: Offering free or public content can attract new fans, giving them a taste of your work and encouraging them to become members
  • Post Quips regularly: those lightweight public posts appear in feeds and help fans discover you beyond Explore
  • Collaborate with other creators using Collaboration posts to tap into their audiences
  • Engage with other creators (likes, comments, reshares) — your interactions influence feed recommendations

Can I change the category I’m placed in?

You can’t manually change the category in which you’re featured. Patreon automatically categorizes creators based on their content, descriptions, and taglines. Consider updating those to improve your search results, and contact support if you have any questions.

Can I opt out of the Explore tab?

At this time, there isn’t an option to opt out of being featured on the Explore tab. However, you can always share your thoughts or concerns with Patreon support.

Adult/18+ visibility

We are enhancing the Explore experience by including age-verified Adult/18+ creators in search results for fans over 18 who choose to view that content. Those who meet the age requirements can find these creators by adjusting their account preferences. For members who already support an Adult/18+ creator, this visibility is active by default. For detailed instructions on modifying these settings to see all creators, see our guide on Find creators on Patreon.

Adult/18+ creators must be age-verified. To learn more about age verification for Adult/18+ classified creators, please visit the Age Verification FAQ.

How can I optimize my page for SEO?

SEO is an important channel for increasing the organic visibility of your Patreon page. A high SEO ranking is how fans find you through Google and other search engines. Above all, search engines prioritize a few key factors, including:

  • Relevance: does your page provide the content that people are looking for? That is, does it have the keywords people search for?
  • Readability: is your content structured clearly (no excess of run-on sentences)? Is it formatted clearly (with headers, subheads, and body copy)?
  • Authority: is your content reliable, valuable, and shareable? Does it link form and to credible sites?

With these factors in mind, there are a few simple ways to start improving the SEO of your creator page:

Create a consistent page name and URL

Your page name is how fans and eventual patrons will most easily find you on Patreon. We recommend using the name your followers already know you by around the web, whether it’s your actual name or the name of your creative group, like a band or channel, for example.

The length and simplicity of your URL also impacts SEO, which is why you also have the option to choose a vanity link for your page (patreon.com/creatorname). For consistency and relevance, we recommend using your page name.

Write a relevant, compelling tagline

Your page tagline gives your audience a concise view of what your membership is about. Aside from your page name, it’s the other piece of information that shows up in the title of Google search results. Phrases like “Digital paintings and tutorials,” or “Genuine BTS reaction videos,” which capture common search keywords — yet are descriptive — help improve your page visibility.

Link from and to other reputable sites

Search engines want to surface content that’s reliable, valuable, and shareable. By linking to your Patreon page on other social profiles, websites, or press coverage, you’re establishing its credibility. You don’t necessarily need a mainstream media publication for a reputable link, either. You can do so simply by collaborating with other creators by co-creating or co-promoting content — even just linking to each others’ pages!

Relevant content

Adding more relevant content to your site creates more opportunities to show up in search results. It also gives your audience even more reason to love your work, share with their friends, and support you on Patreon.

Identify what makes you and your creations truly unique and include relevant keywords in your content (try your About page) and HTML tags. Whether it’s “alien webcomic with psychic female characters” or “funk covers of rock classics.” Be specific! You can bet the person searching for those hyper-descriptive keywords who finds your work might become one of your biggest fans.

How to get traffic to your Creator page

Promoting your Patreon is key to driving traffic to your page, which in turn leads to more members joining your membership. Sharing your page is the first step to promoting your Patreon. Here are some more tips to help you get started:

1. Share your link

Your link will help your followers on your different social platforms find your page. You should include your link in your social bios, email newsletters, or whatever platform you use to share news and content with your followers. You can use the copy link button to grab your Patreon URL in one quick and easy motion.

  • Go to the Dashboard in the left-side menu
  • Once in the Home tab, click on the “…” icon beside the Edit page button, and select Share
  • A pop-up will appear, and you can either choose to Copy link, Download image, or Share directly on your social media

Add in your bios

Instagram: Go to my Instagram

Twitter: Twitter → Edit Profile → Add description

Youtube: Youtube → Your Channel → Customize Channel → Basic Info

2. Create an intro video

You can create an intro video to share on your socials to attract your followers to your Patreon page. An intro video is a great way to talk about why you started a Patreon, highlight the different types of benefits you will offer, and ask your followers to check out your page and become a member today. You can also add this intro video to your Patreon to help visitors understand why they should join your membership.

3. Poll your audience

One way to keep our members engaged is to create polls. Ask your followers on your different platforms how they can be involved in your membership. You can gauge their interest in what type of content and benefits they’d like to receive.

4. Be consistent

Think about all the different spaces where you can promote. The more consistent you are with mentioning and including your Patreon page in your content or on your other platforms, the more your followers will be aware of how important Patreon is to you. For example, if you are a video creator, you can make a habit of reminding your viewers at the end of your videos that you have a Patreon.

Sharing Quips

Quips are lightweight, public posts that appear in the Home feed for existing and potential fans. They’re perfect for sharing quick updates, behind-the-scenes content, or snippets from your paid work. For Adult/18+ creators, Quips will roll out in the coming months and will initially be visible only to your members.

Key things to know about Quips

Quips are always public: All Quips are public by default and must remain public. This is what makes them discoverable. They appear in the Home feed for fans who may not know you yet, serving as an entry point to your page, in addition to your members.

Anyone on Patreon can engage: By default, anyone with a Patreon account can comment on your Quips. This is one of the main ways Quips drives engagement and helps new fans discover your page. You can adjust comment settings when creating a Quip to limit replies to members only or turn them off entirely.

Availability: You can create Quips on both desktop and the Patreon mobile app. On desktop, they appear in the Quips tab on a creator’s page, while in the app, they can be viewed on the Home feed, memberships tab, and creator home page. This ensures you can Quip wherever you go, making it easy to stay connected on all your devices.

Quips stay on your page: Quips appear in your fans’ Home feed and on your page under a dedicated tab. Older Quips don’t disappear. They remain visible on your page even after they stop appearing in the feed. Each Quip also has its own individual page. Click into any Quip to read its comments, likes, and reshares, and scroll to the bottom to find related posts and Quips you might be interested in.

What you can include: Quips can include text, images, or short videos. For media specifications, see the Technical details section below.

Members are notified about Quips: Your members receive in-app notifications for Quips, not emails. They can adjust their notification settings at any time. For a step-by-step guide, visit the notification section in the Navigate the Patreon app as a member guide.

Want examples of Quips that drive discovery? Check out “Case Studies: Creators Growing With Quips” on Patreon for Creators. Currently, Patreon for Creators is only available in English.

How to use Quips

Want to create a Quip? Here’s how:

- Click Create
- Select Quip
- A pop-up will appear, then add text, media, or both to your Quip
    - To include media, click the Add button and select the file on your desktop
- You can tag other creators in a Quip by @ mentioning them
- By default, anyone can reply to your Quips, but you can adjust the comment settings by selecting Public in the Quip's bottom menu
    - You can allow replies from anyone, all members, paid members, or no one
- Once you're done, click the Share button
- Tap Create
- Select Quip
- Then add text, media, or both to your Quip
    - To include images, tap the button; for videos, tap the button; and if you want to use your mobile camera, tap the button
- You can tag other creators in a Quip by @ mentioning them
- By default, anyone can reply to your Quips, but you can adjust the comment settings to all members, paid members, or no one by selecting Public above the keyboard
- Once you're done, tap the Share button in the top right corner

Technical details

Character limit for Quips

There’s no strict character limit, but after 9 lines of text, readers will see a read more link. Quips appear in the Home feed and in a dedicated tab on your page.

Supported media

Quips are designed for quick and engaging content. Here are the supported media types:

  • Video: Up to 2 minutes
  • Photo galleries: Up to 10 photos
  • Formats supported: vertical, square, portrait, or landscape
  • Links: You can include links and reposts in your Quips

How to see your Quips

Immediately after posting a Quip, you’ll get a pop-up notification that lets you know your Quip has been posted. You can tap View to see your Quip in your Home feed.

You can find your Quips, or any creator’s Quips, by visiting the creator’s page and selecting the Quips tab. Each Quip can be clicked to open its own individual page.

Fans and creators can view Quips directly on a creator’s page, both on desktop and the Patreon mobile app. Here’s how:

  • Go to the creator’s page on desktop or the app
  • Select the Quips tab in the navigation menu on the creator’s page
  • Scroll through the creator’s recent Quips in the feed
  • Select any Quip to open its individual page, where you can see the full post, comments, likes, and reshares, as well as a feed of related posts at the bottom

The Quips tab is only visible on a creator’s page if you’ve posted at least one Quip.

Engaging with Quips

Creators and fans can interact with Quips in different ways.

As a creator, you can:

  • Comment: On any Quip, tap or click the comment to engage directly
  • Like: Tap or click the like icon to show your appreciation
  • Repost: Share a Quip to your own feed by selecting the repost option
  • Quote: Add your own commentary when reposting a Post or a Quip by selecting the quote option
  • Mention creators: Use @CreatorName in your Post, Quip, or comments to tag other creators

Your fans can:

  • Comment: Leave a comment on any Quip they have access to
  • Like: Tap or click the like icon to show their appreciation

Repost or quote a Post or Quip

If you’d like to reshare a post or a Quip, select Reshare at the bottom of any creation. You can then opt to Reshare or Quote. When you reshare, the content appears directly in your fans’ feed. If they don’t have access to a post you’re resharing, it will appear as Locked. By selecting Quote, you can craft a new Quip by adding your own comments and media alongside the attached content.

Select text from one of your published Posts and share it in a Quip as a quote card that links back to the original Post. Because Quips are public, anyone can view the passage, but access to the full Post doesn’t change. This feature is currently in early access for eligible creators on iOS.

Mentions

You can mention other creators in a post or a Quip by using @CreatorName. The creator will be tagged, and a link to their page will appear in your publication. This will also notify the creator that you mentioned them once your post or Quip is published. Some things to keep in mind:

  • If the mention is in a paid post, it doesn’t grant the creator access; they’ll still see the paywall
  • Mentioning another creator doesn’t make them a collaborator on the post or distribute the content to their fans – see our guide on Collaboration posts for more details
  • If the creator disabled Mentions, you won’t be able to tag them
How to control Mentions

Mentions are allowed by default. If you’d like to change it, follow the steps below:

  • Go to Page settings
  • Find the Mentions section
  • Select the option you’d like
    • Allow mentions: let people @mention you
    • Don’t allow mentions: prevent people from @mentioning you
  • Once you’re done, click Save changes in the top right corner

Content ideas

Quips are a quick and flexible way to share updates with potential fans. Here are some ideas you can try:

  • Commentary or hot takes on topics in your segment
  • Behind-the-scenes moments from your creative process
  • Quick tutorials or how-to tips
  • Personality-driven lifestyle posts
  • Sneak peeks or previews of your paid content

FAQ

  • Yes, you can schedule a Quip on Desktop. In the editor, click Schedule Quip , select the date and time you want your Quip to be published, and click Save. Once you’re done editing your Quip, click on the Schedule button.
  • Visit your creator’s page on desktop or the app and select the Quips tab. For full steps, see the How to see Quips section above. To find Quips from other creators that don’t appear in your feed, you can search for the creator and visit their page on desktop or the app.

  • Follow the steps below to identify which Quip you want to edit or delete:
    • Go to your creator’s page on Desktop or tap your profile image on the bottom right corner of the app, and then select View page
    • Next, select the Quips tab from the navigation bar
    • Scroll through all the Quips you’ve posted
    • Once you have the Quip you want to edit or delete, click More at the bottom right on Desktop or at the top right in the Patreon mobile app, then select the action you’d like to take
  • On Desktop, you can edit or delete a Quip by navigating to the Library and selecting the Quips tab. Find the desired Quip in the list, then click More on the right side of the publication to choose your preferred action.
  • Deleting a Quip is permanent and can’t be undone. Once deleted, the Quip is removed from the Home feed and your page immediately. All comments, likes, and reshares associated with it are permanently lost.

Additionally, if you head to Post Insights, you’ll be able to see Impressions (total number of times the Quip has appeared across Patreon) and Seen (total number of times the Quip was seen for longer than 3 seconds across Patreon).

If you want to limit who can engage with your Quips, you can adjust your comment settings when creating a Quip to restrict replies to members only or turn them off entirely.
  • If fans reach out about Quips notifications, they can adjust them in their notification settings. They can turn off notifications for Quips from creators they don’t yet follow and adjust notifications for a specific creator. For a step-by-step guide, they can visit the notification section in the Navigate the Patreon app as a member guide.

Your creator and fan profiles are now combined into a single identity

As of July 6, 2026, all creators were required to combine profiles into a single identity. If you didn’t take action by August 17, 2026, your profiles were automatically combined.

Creators previously had two separate profiles: one for their creator page and another for the memberships they held as fans. When profiles were combined, they merged into a single identity, and any past member activity, such as likes, comments, chats, and DMs, was updated to reflect the creator name.

Combining profiles gave you access to Patreon’s network features, including Quips, collaboration posts, and a new all-audiences Home feed (currently only available in English). Adult/18+ creators got access to collaboration posts immediately after combining, with Quips and Native Video rolling out in the coming months.

Starting July 6, all creators, including Adult/18+ creators, were required to combine their profiles to access Patreon. After August 17, we automatically started combining the profiles of any creators who had not yet taken action. Check the timeline section below for all the details.

With a combined profile, you can manage your page and interact across Patreon as yourself (a creator), without switching between profiles. Your existing creator page, members, and posts didn’t change.

Want the bigger picture on how discovery is evolving? Read “Go get discovered!” on Patreon for Creators. Currently, Patreon for Creators is only available in English.

Benefits of a single identity

  • Access to Patreon’s network features: With combined profiles, you have access to Patreon’s network, including Quips, Collaboration posts, and a new Home feed.
  • Get discovered through your activity: When you comment or engage in other communities, your creator page is visible to new fans, turning everyday activity into discovery opportunities.
  • Interact with other creators as yourself: No more switching to a fan profile to engage. You show up as your creator identity across Patreon.
  • Find and follow creators more easily: A unified navigation makes it simpler to explore Patreon and discover creators in your space.
  • One consistent identity: Your creator and fan activity live in one place.

Key info about combining profiles

Combining your profiles is a one-time, irreversible change, and your public display name and profile image will default to your creator name and creator profile image.

What stayed the same

  • Your login credentials didn’t change
  • Your creator page URL didn’t change
  • Paid members will continue to see your creator posts exactly as they did before

For Team accounts, the primary creator account is the one that opted in to combining profiles and network access. To learn more about how this works for teammates, see Team accounts.

What changed after combining profiles

The most important changes that occurred when your profiles were combined:

  • All existing memberships you have as a fan display under your creator name
  • Your past activity (comments, chats, and messages, etc) was updated to use your creator name unless you deleted that activity
  • Any future activity across your memberships will display under your creator name
  • You’ll always have control over the visibility of your memberships to others
    • A list of the creators you subscribe to may appear on your creator page, and you can hide this at any time in your Page settings
    • You can control whether your memberships are shown publicly and whether you have a Memberships tab on your creator page, at any time in your Privacy settings
  • Your activity on posts may show up in the feeds of other creators and fans, helping you get discovered
    • This includes likes and comments on public posts, as well as activity on members-only posts that are visible to other members in the same community, which means people can naturally discover you through the communities you engage with as part of the network experience
    • You can control whether your activity is highlighted in others’ feeds and whether you have an Activity tab on your creator page, at any time in your Privacy settings
  • Your comment settings for new public posts and Quips default to anyone can comment, which helps boost your content in the feed. You can adjust this at any time in the post or Quip editor. Once you change it, your preference is saved for future posts. This doesn’t apply to paid access posts, which keep their existing comment settings
  • Your navigation is streamlined. See the section below for what the experience looks like on desktop and the app
  • When a fan visits your page, they see mutual members of your community they also subscribe to, subject to those creators’ privacy settings, and cannot be turned off

What the experience looks like

On desktop, you have a unified navigation experience. You can find your Dashboard, Library, and other creator tools in your Creator Studio . Your personal and creator settings are under Your account. You can do everything in one place without switching profiles.

In the Patreon mobile app, you don’t need to switch views after combining. You’re always in your single identity view.

A unified inbox

Once your creator and fan profiles were combined, you gained access to all of your chats and direct messages from a unified inbox.

Your unified inbox has two tabs:

  • You can view direct messages from fans and chats you manage nested under your Patreon inbox tab. From this inbox, you can review your moderation hub, search through messages, send new direct messages, or create a new chat for fans.
  • Direct messages from creators you support and chats you participate in as a fan are nested under the Your membership inbox tab. From here, you can search through your messages and send new direct messages to creators you support.

You’ll be able to start a new group chat for your fans, whether you’re in your memberships or your Patreon inbox.

Timeline

See below for a summary of the key dates and milestones throughout the combining profiles process.

Date

What happens

April 28

All audience creators could combine profiles to unlock access to new discovery features.

May 27

Adult/18+ creators could combine profiles to unlock access to collaboration posts and be prioritized for the rollout of Patreon Video and Quips.

Creators had new controls and options to protect their privacy, as combining profiles was required for all creators. These controls included the ability to delete all activity, cancel memberships, and limit the visibility of current memberships and activity. See below for more information about privacy.

July 6

Combining profiles became required for all creators moving forward.

Starting July 6, creators who hadn’t combined their profiles couldn’t access Patreon, including posting and receiving payouts. When that happened, you could restore access immediately by combining your profiles. You were prompted to take action when you logged in to Patreon, and we also sent an email with steps to restore access when you’ve been temporarily locked out of your account.

Starting on August 17

If you still haven’t combined your profiles by August 17, we began doing it automatically for you. Here’s what happened starting August 17 and continuing through the following weeks:

  • If you had memberships and/or past activity, we deleted all your member activity, and your memberships remained in place but were hidden from the creator
  • We notified you before your profiles were automatically combined. Once your profiles were automatically combined, you could resume using Patreon as normal
  • If your creator page was unpublished and has never been published, we automatically combined your profiles, and moving forward you appear with your member name in your account instead of your creator name
  • If your page was currently unpublished, but has previously been published, we automatically combined your profiles, and moving forward you appear with your creator name in your account
  • Once your profiles were combined, you received a notification on Patreon

Your privacy after combining

Read on to learn more about how your identity shows up on Patreon after your profiles were combined and what controls you have to adjust these defaults. You can also visit our Privacy Policy for more information.

How your identity changed after your profiles were combined

  • Your public display name became your creator name across Patreon — unless you’ve never published your creator page, in which case it stayed as your member name
    • You can change your name at any time by following our guide on How to change your page name
  • Past comments, group chat messages, and other activities you made under your fan profile were updated to show your creator name
  • Your activity (e.g., likes and comments) may be highlighted on your creator page and in others’ feeds. You can change this at any time in your Privacy settings; see Manage your membership and activity visibility for more information. Activity on paid posts will only be visible to other paid members of those communities

Privacy controls creators have access to

Patreon offers all creators more ways to manage how your memberships and activity show up across Patreon. As part of this, we updated some defaults around membership and activity visibility and replaced older profile settings with new, more granular controls. You can update your Privacy Settings at any time using the controls below.

  • Adjust whether your memberships are shown publicly: Choose whether your name will be shown publicly as a member of your creators.
  • Adjust if your activity is highlighted: Choose whether your activity (e.g., likes and comments) can be highlighted in others’ feeds and if you’ll have an Activity tab on your creator page.
  • Customize visibility per creator: Choose whether to show memberships publicly and whether to highlight membership activity for specific creators. You’ll be able to select the memberships you don’t want to show publicly and the activity you don’t want to highlight on a per-creator basis.

All creators on Patreon have access to the controls listed above, regardless of whether their profiles have been automatically combined. These controls only manage your past fan activity, and they don’t erase your account.

Adult/18+ creators

Combining profiles was required for all creators, including Adult/18+ creators, by July 6. For creators with content for Adult/18+ audiences, the available features are slightly different.

After your profiles were combined, you got access to collaboration posts right away.⁠⁠

Quips and Patreon Video are coming to Adult/18+ creators in the coming months. At first, Quips will be visible only to your members and to any fans who visit your page and are over 18 years old.

Creators who combined profiles before July 6 may be prioritized as Patreon rolls out Quips and Patreon Video. You’ll receive an email when you get access.⁠⁠

  • The Patreon network is a set of features that helps fans find creators beyond those they already follow and helps creators reach new audiences on Patreon. For a full overview of the network features, see the Patreon network guide.
  • Patreon’s network has a set of new features, including:
    • Quips: Quips are a lightweight, public type of post that appears in the Home feed. It’s a quick way to share an update or engage with your community without creating a full post. For more details, visit our guide on Sharing Quips
    • Memberships to creators: A new section on your creator page that lists the creators you subscribe to. You can hide it at any time in your Page settings
    • Mutuals: When a fan visits your page, they’ll see other members of your community they also subscribe to, helping new fans feel at home right away. Which creators appear depends on each creator’s privacy settings

Creators: Going Live

Creator and trusted moderator tools for Live

The same moderation tools available in Community Chats can also be used for Live chats. Patreon’s Community Guidelines apply everywhere, including Live chats, and detail the sorts of behaviors that are permitted and prohibited on Patreon. Members are presented with these guidelines any time they choose to join a chat while attending a Live. We encourage you to review, uphold, and enforce these guidelines to keep your community safe. Here are some tools that allow you to do so:

Assign Trusted Moderators

You have the ability to assign up to 10 teammates or trusted fans from the community as a Moderator for your Live. These Moderators have access to reported actions through the Moderation Hub on the Patreon app, and will show up with a Moderator tag on their profile.

Moderators must be members of tiers that have access to chats to be able to view chats gated to paid tiers.

Here’s how to nominate moderators for your chats:
- Select Creator studio from the left navigation and click Moderation Hub
- Switch to the Moderators tab
- From there, you can use the search bar to add or remove moderators
- Go to the Patreon mobile app (Android or IOS) and tap the Community tab from the bottom app menu
- From this screen, tap on any chat you want
- At the top right corner, tap Moderation next to your profile
- You'll land on Reported messages
- Switch to Moderators at the top of the screen
- From there, you can add or remove Moderators

Pin a message

Want to keep something visible at the top of your Live chat? You and your trusted moderators can pin one chat message at a time — handy for calling out a link, an announcement, or a question you want your community to see.

How pinning works
  • You can pin one message at a time per chat
  • Pinning a new message automatically unpins the previous one
  • The pinned message stays at the top of the chat until you unpin it or pin a different one
How to pin a message
- Hover over the message you want to pin
- Click Pin
  • To unpin a message, go to the pinned message at the top of the chat (not the original message) and click Pin . The message will now be unpinned.
    • Tap and hold the message you want to pin
    • Tap Pin
  • To unpin a message, go to the pinned message at the bottom of the chat (not the original message), tap it to open the menu, then select Unpin message. The message will now be unpinned.

View and Action Reported Messages

Your fans are able to flag a message in your community chats as being potentially inappropriate or at odds with your community culture. When a member reports a message, you’ll receive a push notification or message within the app that a message has been reported, and you or one of your trusted moderators can choose to keep or delete that message from your Moderation Hub.

How to access your reported messages:
- Select Creator studio from the left navigation and click Moderation Hub
- You'll land in the Reported Content panel
- You'll find a list of all messages reported from the chat and the reason for the report. You can choose to keep or delete the reported messages
- Want to access the moderation hub during a live? Click the shield in the left side navigation bar to access the Moderation Hub and see a list of all reported messages. From here, you can choose to keep or delete the reported messages
- Go to the Patreon mobile app (Android or iOS) and tap the Community tab from the bottom app menu
- From this screen, tap the chat you want to check
- At the top right corner, tap Moderation next to your profile
- You'll find a list of all the messages reported from that chat and the reason for the report. You can choose to keep or delete any reported messages
- Want to access the moderation hub during a live? Click More and select View Reported Messages. The Moderation Hub will pull up from within the live viewer, from where you can choose to keep or delete any reported messages

Delete Messages

You or one of your trusted moderators can delete messages directly within a chat. When you delete a message, the person who sent the message will not be notified, but everyone in the chat will see it as a deleted message.

How to delete messages:
- Visit the specific chat you'd like to delete, or from the chat window within a live
- Hover over the message, and click More
- Click Delete message
- Visit the specific chat you'd like to delete
- Tap the message to expand menu options
- Click Delete message

Mute Members

Need to cool things down in the chat—without removing someone completely? You can now mute members for a set amount of time during your Live or within a Community Chat. This feature lets creators and trusted moderators temporarily silence a member in chat while still allowing them to watch the stream and read messages.

How muting works
  • You or a trusted moderator can mute a member for 15 minutes, 1 hour, or 24 hours
  • Muted members can’t post messages during that time
  • They can still view the chat, and if in a Live chat, still watch the Live

This is a useful way to manage disruptions or give someone a time-out without removing or blocking them. You’ll see a confirmation once the member is muted—and the action is quiet. You will also see a “Muted” label attached to the member’s previous messages while they are muted. Other members won’t be notified and won’t see this label.

How to mute a member:
- Click on or hover over the member's name in the chat or participant list, and click More
- Select Mute and choose a time duration
- Tap to confirm
- The member will be muted for that duration, will be notified that they are muted, and will be unable to participate in the chat. After the duration expires, they will be able to participate in the chat once again, and will be notified that they are unmuted
- Tap the member's name in the chat or participant list, and click More
- Select Mute and choose a time duration
- Tap to confirm
- The member will be muted for that duration, and will be unable to participate in the chat. After the duration expires, they will be able to participate in the chat once again

Turn Off Chats

Need to slow things down during your Live? You can now turn off the chat for viewers—while still keeping control of the conversation. It’s a flexible way to manage the pace or tone of the chat—whether you need a break, want to refocus attention, or handle a spike in activity. This feature lets creators and trusted moderators pause chat for members at any time, on mobile and web.

What happens when chat is turned off?
  • Members can no longer send messages in the Live chat. They can still see all past messages, including any new ones from you or your moderators
  • Creators and trusted moderators can continue chatting as usual
How to turn chat off (or back on)
- In an active Live, navigate to the … menu
- Select Turn off chat to lock the chat for members. Members will be notified when the chat has been turned off
- Select Turn on chat from same location anytime to reopen the conversation
- In an active Live, navigate to the … menu
- Select Turn off chat to lock the chat for members
- Select Turn on chat from same location anytime to reopen the conversation

Remove from Live

You and your trusted moderators can remove someone from a Live without blocking them permanently, or disrupting their membership. This is one way to step in if someone’s being disruptive, without escalating to a full block.

  • The member is removed from both the Live video and chat immediately
  • Their messages are deleted from the Live chat automatically
  • They can’t rejoin that specific Live
  • They aren’t blocked—their membership will not be affected, and they’ll still be able to watch and participate in future Lives

You’ll see a quick confirmation that the viewer has been removed—they’ll be quietly exited from the session with no public notification. Their messages will also be deleted automatically from the Live chat.

How to remove someone from your Live
- Tap on or hover over a message in chat or open the Participants list
- Select the member you want to take action on
- Tap Remove from Live in the action menu
- Confirm when prompted
- Tap on a message in chat or open the Participants list
- Select the viewer you want to take action on
- Tap Remove from Live in the action menu
- Confirm when prompted

Block User

Need to block a member permanently? Creators and trusted moderators can remove someone from membership directly from a live. This means the member will lose access to the creator’s page.

How to remove a member from membership:
- Visit the specific chat that you'd like to remove the member in and find the member's most recent message. If already in a Live, scroll to a message from the member you'd like to remove
- Tap on the member's name to pull up the actions menu
- Tap on Block person
- You'll need to select a reason for blocking the member, select one, then confirm when prompted
- The member will no longer be part of membership, be able to interact with you or your community, or interact with your posts and Lives
- Visit the specific chat that you'd like to remove the member in and find the member's most recent message. If already in a Live, scroll to a message from the member you'd like to remove
- Tap on the member's name to pull up the actions menu
- Tap on Block person
- You'll need to select a reason for blocking the member, select one, then confirm when prompted
- The member will no longer be part of membership, be able to interact with you or your community, or interact with your posts and Lives

Auto-moderation

Auto-moderation is a machine-learning powered moderation tool that automatically removes chats that go against Patreon’s Community Guidelines during lives.

Note: This product is in early testing, and may miss or remove messages incorrectly. We encourage creators to leverage the other tools available in addition to Auto-moderation if you’re still encountering offensive or upsetting messages.

Once enabled, auto-moderation reviews incoming messages in real time. If something breaks the rules, the message is removed and replaced with a note that it was auto-moderated. Auto-moderation is optional, and can be turned on or off by creators at any time.

Here’s how it works:
- Before going Live, find the auto-moderation toggle in the Live preview. Enabling the toggle sets auto-moderation up from the minute you start your Live
- Want to turn auto-moderation on during an active live? Click the Shield in the top right corner of your Live chat, and click Enable auto-moderation
- Need to turn auto-moderation off during an active live? Click the Shield in the top right corner of your Live chat, and click Disable auto-moderation
- Before going Live, find the auto-moderation toggle by clicking the Settings in the Live preview. Enabling the toggle sets auto-moderation up from the minute you start your Live
- Want to turn auto-moderation on during an active live? Tap More in the top right corner of your Live chat, and click Enable auto-moderation
- Need to turn auto-moderation off during an active live? Tap More in the top right corner of your Live chat, and click Disable auto-moderation

Fan tools for keeping Live safe (Creators: Going Live)

Report a message

Members can report messages that they feel are violating Patreon’s Community Guidelines directly to creators. We encourage everyone to review, uphold, and enforce these guidelines to keep your community safe.

How to report a message:
- Visit the specific chat you’d like to delete
- Hover over the message, and click More
- Click Report Message
- Visit the specific chat you’d like to delete
- Tap and hold the message to expand menu options
- Tap Report Message

Block a member

Members can also block other members in order to continue interacting with a chat while hiding messages from particular members.

How to block a member:
- Visit the specific chat you’d like to delete
- Hover over the message, and click More
- Click Block Member
- Visit the specific chat you’d like to delete
- Tap and hold the message to expand menu options
- Tap Block Member

Report a live

Members can report an ongoing Live if they feel the content or environment violates Patreon’s Community Guidelines. We encourage you to review, uphold, and enforce both sets of guidelines to keep your community safe. Once you report a live, the creator’s stream is suspended for all viewers, and the creator is notified.

How to report a live:
- In an active Live, click More
- Click Report this creator
- Indicate why you’re reporting the live, and click Continue
- In an active Live, tap More
- Tap Report
- Indicate why you’re reporting the live, and tap Continue

Closed Chats

If you’re watching a Live and suddenly can’t send messages in the chat, don’t worry—it just means the creator or their moderators temporarily turned chat off.

This is a normal part of how some Lives are managed, especially when things get busy or the creator wants to focus attention elsewhere.

What you can still do
  • You can still watch the Live and enjoy the stream.
  • You’ll still see all previous chat messages, including new ones from the creator or moderators.
  • Once chat is turned back on, you’ll be able to post again.

Muting

If you’re watching a Live or participating in a Community Chat and suddenly can’t send messages, it may be because you’ve been temporarily muted by the creator or a trusted moderator. This feature helps creators keep things respectful and on track for everyone watching.

This isn’t a ban—you can still enjoy the Live and follow the chat, but you won’t be able to post messages for a little while.

What being muted means
  • You’ve been muted for a limited time: 15 minutes, 1 hour, or 24 hours. You will see a message letting you know how long the mute lasts.
  • You can still watch the Live and read messages in the chat.
  • You just won’t be able to send messages until the mute expires.

Removal from Live

If you suddenly can’t access a Live you were just in, it’s possible the creator or a trusted moderator removed you from that Live session. This action—called Remove from Live—is used to help keep the experience safe and respectful for everyone.

What it means
  • You were removed from the Live video and chat.
  • You won’t be able to rejoin that specific Live session.
  • You’re not blocked—you can still watch future Lives from that creator, unless you’re blocked separately.
Why it happens

Creators and their moderators use this option to keep the Live environment comfortable for everyone. It might be used if something you said or did was disruptive or against community guidelines.

Going Live on Patreon through OBS

Patreon Live is currently available to creators who meet the following criteria:

  • You’ve published your Patreon page
  • Your Patreon page is Safe for All Audiences
  • Your Patreon page is in good standing and complies with our Community Guidelines and Terms of Use

While Patreon Live is not yet available to creators in the Adult/18+ category, we’re working to responsibly expand access for more creators and ensure the product meets our community’s needs.

You can also stream directly to Patreon from Streamlabs Desktop or the Streamlabs Plugin for OBS. Visit Streamlabs’ native Patreon integration setup guide to learn more.

Steps to go live via OBS

  • Open OBS and go to Settings → Stream
  • In the Service dropdown, select Custom
  • Once you select Custom, OBS will display a Destination section with fields for the server URL and stream key. Leave this tab open — you’ll come back to it after setting up your Live on Patreon
  • Tip: If this is your first time using OBS, make sure you’ve allowed access to your camera and microphone when prompted
  • Open a new tab and go to Patreon. From your creator profile, click Create on the left-hand side and select Live
  • In the Camera source section, select Other streaming source. Your preview panel will load with a server URL and stream key. These are unique to each Live session
  • Copy the server URL and stream key. Paste the server URL into the Server field. Paste the stream key into the Stream Key field
  • Click OK in OBS, then click Start Streaming. Starting the stream in OBS does not start the Live on Patreon — it only sends the feed to your preview window
  • Return to Patreon. You should now see your OBS stream appear in the Live preview panel
  • Enter a title for your Live and select your audience (all members, free members, or specific paid tiers). If you’re eligible, you can also sell one-time access to a Live. Note: Ticketed access is currently in beta. You can share interest by filling out this form
  • Click Start Live to begin streaming. If you scheduled your Live, you’ll be able to access the Live setup 5 minutes before the scheduled time to finalize setup and preview your stream
  • Once you’re finished streaming, click End Live on Patreon and Stop Streaming on OBS

Key things to know

  • The server URL and stream key are different for each Live you create, so you’ll need to go through this setup again each time you schedule a new one
  • You can also create a scheduled event. This lets you complete this setup ahead of time and check on it anytime before your Live by heading to Library → Drafts and editing the post

Troubleshooting OBS streaming

This guide helps diagnose and resolve common issues encountered during livestreaming with OBS Studio and RTMP. Use the steps below to quickly identify performance problems and apply the right fixes to keep your stream running smoothly.

Types of frame issues
- Frames are encoded but fail to reach Patreon due to a weak or unstable internet connection
- Often results in buffering or frozen video
- Skipped frames due to encoding lag indicates CPU overload
- Frames missed due to rendering lag indicates GPU overload
- Results in choppy, low frame-rate streams
Monitoring with OBS stats and logs
  • Open via OBS: View → Stats
  • Keep an eye on the following indicators:
    • Dropped frames (network): Should remain 0%. A rising number means network issues
    • Skipped frames (encoding lag): Indicates CPU overload
    • Frames missed (rendering lag): Indicates GPU overload
    • CPU usage: High CPU usage (>80-90%) may cause issues
    • FPS: Ensure this matches target FPS (usually 30 or 60fps)
  • OBS logs provide deeper technical details about what’s happening in the background of your stream.
  • Access via OBS: Help → Log Files → View Last Log
  • Look for the following terms:
    • Encoder overloaded: This means your CPU or GPU is under too much load to keep up
    • Lagged frames: Your GPU is having trouble rendering the video feed
    • Dropped frames: OBS is unable to maintain a stable connection to the server
Resolving network dropped frames
  • Reduce bitrate: In OBS settings, make sure your video bitrate is set to no more than 75% of your upload speed. For example, if your upload speed is 10 Mbps, set bitrate to 7,500 Kbps or lower
  • Wired connection: Always prefer Ethernet over Wi-Fi
  • Enable QoS: If your router supports it, enable QoS and prioritize RTMP or streaming traffic
  • Check ISP or server: Try alternate ingest servers or monitor for ISP issues
  • Adaptive bitrate: In OBS, go to Settings → Advanced and enable Dynamic Bitrate. This allows OBS to automatically adjust your bitrate during sudden drops in network performance
Resolving encoding overload (CPU)
  • Lower resolution/FPS: Try streaming at 720p instead of 1080p, or reducing frame rate from 60fps to 30fps. These changes significantly reduce CPU usage
  • Encoder preset: In Settings → Output, choose a faster preset like veryfast or superfast. Faster presets require less CPU power but may reduce visual quality slightly
  • Hardware encoding: Leverage GPU encoders (NVENC, AMF, QuickSync) if available
  • Close unnecessary apps: Shut down background apps and browser tabs that may consume CPU power during your stream
  • Upgrade hardware: If CPU overload persists across multiple sessions, it may be time to consider a system upgrade
Resolving rendering lag (GPU)
  • Limit GPU load: Cap the frame rate of any games or apps running while streaming to free up GPU resources
  • Reduce scene complexity: Avoid using too many high-resolution images, video sources, or animated overlays in your OBS scenes
  • Lower output resolution: Match your OBS Canvas Resolution and Output (Scaled) Resolution closely to reduce unnecessary GPU work
  • Update GPU drivers: Ensure graphics drivers are current and properly configured
  • Monitor GPU usage: Keep GPU load below 90% for smooth performance

Going Live on Patreon through Zoom

This article walks you through how to connect Zoom to Patreon Live using a custom RTMPS streaming setup.

Who can use Patreon Live?

Patreon Live is currently available to creators who meet the following criteria:

  • You’ve published your Patreon page
  • Your Patreon page is Safe for All Audiences
  • Your Patreon page is in good standing and complies with our Community Guidelines and Terms of Use

While Patreon Live is not yet available to creators in the Adult/18+ category, we’re working to responsibly expand access for more creators and ensure the product meets our community’s needs.

What you’ll need

Before you begin, make sure that:

  • You own the Zoom meeting or webinar
  • You’re the host of the Zoom meeting or webinar (co-host permissions are not sufficient to access livestreaming settings)
  • You have Zoom Premium

Steps to go live via Zoom

You can stream to Patreon Live using either a Zoom Meeting or a Zoom Webinar. The setup process is the same for both.

  • Log in to Zoom on a web browser and go to your Zoom Meeting Settings
  • Click the Meetings tab in the horizontal navigation bar
  • Scroll to the In Meeting (Advanced) section and enable Allow livestreaming of meetings
  • Check the box for Custom Live Streaming Service
  • Create or open the Zoom meeting you want to stream
  • In the meeting, click on More → Live on Custom Live Streaming Service. This causes a browser window to open, prompting you to enter livestreaming credentials. Leave this tab open — you’ll come back to it after setting up your Live on Patreon
  • Open a new tab and go to Patreon. From your creator profile, click Create on the left-hand side and select Live
  • In the Camera source section, select Other streaming source. Your preview panel will load with a server URL and stream key — these are unique to each Live session.
  • Copy the server URL and stream key from the preview panel on Patreon and paste them into the corresponding fields in Zoom:
    • The server URL into the Streaming URL field
    • The stream key into the Streaming key field
    • The Live Streaming Page URL: This can be the link to your Patreon creator page (required by Zoom). It should follow this format: patreon.com
    • Leave Resolution at 720p
  • In Zoom, click Go Live!
  • Zoom will start sending the stream to Patreon, but your Live will not be visible to members until you click Start Live on Patreon
  • Mute your Patreon browser tab to prevent audio feedback
  • When streaming through Zoom, Zoom becomes your audio source. After clicking Go Live! in Zoom, return to your Patreon tab, right-click the browser tab, and select Mute site
  • In your Patreon Live setup page, you should now see your Zoom feed in the preview window
  • Add a title for your Live and choose your audience (all members, free members, or a specific paid tier). If you’re eligible, you can also sell one-time access to a Live. Note: Ticketed access is currently in beta. You can share interest by filling out this form
  • Click Start Live on Patreon to begin streaming to your members
  • If you scheduled your Live in advance, you’ll be able to enter the setup 5 minutes before your scheduled time to complete these steps
  • When you’re ready to end your stream, click End Live on Patreon first
  • After your Live has fully ended on Patreon, return to Zoom and end your meeting or webinar. If you end the Zoom session first, your Patreon Live will continue running without audio or video until you manually end it on Patreon

Key things to know

  • This setup works for both Zoom Meetings and Zoom Webinars
  • The server URL and stream key are different for each Live you create, so you’ll need to go through this setup again each time you schedule a new one
  • You can also create a scheduled event. This lets you complete this setup ahead of time and check on it anytime before your Live by heading to Library → Drafts and editing the post
  • If you need to change the streaming URL after it’s already been configured, you’ll need to go to your Zoom Dashboard. Go to My Meetings and click the meeting name you want to change. In the Livestreaming tab, you can configure or preset the credentials before or while the Zoom meeting is starting
  • Screen sharing behavior: Whoever is screen sharing in your Zoom meeting will automatically appear as the screen share on your Patreon Live

How to Livestream with Vimeo

Go live with Vimeo Livestream and give members an exclusive experience.

You can Livestream with Vimeo if you have a Vimeo Advanced account. Patreon creators receive 10% off of their 1st year of Vimeo Advanced

Set up a Patreon exclusive Livestream with Vimeo

  • While logged in to your Patreon account, click on Create and then the Post button from the left-hand side
  • Click the Livestream button
  • Click the Use Vimeo button
  • Click the Create a member-only Vimeo Livestream link
  • Authenticate your Vimeo Advanced account or create a new one
  • We’ll direct you to Vimeo’s live video creation flow. Here you can use all of Vimeo’s Livestream features like; Live Q&A, polling, moderation tooling, etc.
  • Select New event to create your live event! Here’s Vimeo’s guide to creating a live event
    • When creating a live event, select the Link Privacy as Unlisted. This makes it easy and secure for members to access the post
    • Once you create your event, you can change the Embed privacy — select Specific domains, and type patreon.com domain
  • Copy the Livestream URL from the Share link button at the top right corner
  • Paste the Livestream URL into the textbox of your new post on Patreon
  • Fill out the rest of your post details like Title, description, and Who can access this post
  • You can add your post to a collection to help members find more of what they’re looking for. You can think of collections as your own library where you can get to organize your work however you want. Learn more about creating a collection
  • You can preview your post before publishing by clicking the View button
  • Schedule to publish it later (default setting) or publish it immediately if you’re ready to go live!

FAQ

  • Once your Livestream post is published, it will populate eligible members ’ feeds on both the web and mobile. After your Livestream ends, your post will appear as an embedded Vimeo video with expected video playback functionality.
  • Exclusive Livestream events are a valuable experience that can help keep and draw in new members. Here are some examples of experiences you can offer with Livestreaming:
    • Host a live Q&A session with members
    • Put on an intimate, member-only concert
    • Give real-time life updates
    • Host a live podcast recording
    • Insert awesomely creative live event here…
  • Vimeo Livestreaming is currently available for Vimeo Advanced accounts. Receive 10% off of your 1st year of Vimeo advanced when you sign up through Patreon.
  • If you have any paid Vimeo account — Standard or above — you can use our video integration to upload member-only exclusive content, safe from link-sharing.
  • If you have a free Vimeo account, you can still publish your videos on Patreon. Simply upload your video directly to Vimeo, grab the URL directly from Vimeo, and paste the link into the Video post creator.
  • Here’s our guide to using Vimeo to share your videos on Patreon: Upload your videos with Vimeo

How to Stream to Patreon with Streamlabs

Live streaming on Patreon lets you connect with your community in real time — no algorithm, no ads, just you and the people who show up for your work. This guide explains how to go live with the Streamlabs integration — using Streamlabs Desktop or the Plugin for OBS, complete with custom overlays, Dual Output for vertical and horizontal layouts, and multistreaming to other platforms.

What you’ll need

  • A Patreon creator account
  • Streamlabs Desktop or Streamlabs Plugin for OBS installed
  • A stable internet connection
  • A webcam and microphone (built-in or external)
  • Any overlays you’d like to use

Connect your Patreon account

You can connect your account through Streamlabs Dashboard (which works for both Desktop and Plugin for OBS) or directly inside each app.

Via Streamlabs Dashboard
  • Log in and go to your Streamlabs Dashboard. Click your profile image in the top right and select Account Settings
  • Open the Platforms tab. Scroll down until you see Patreon
  • Click Merge next to Patreon and authorize your account. Once you click Accept, Patreon will appear as a linked destination — and it’ll be available in both Desktop and Plugin for OBS automatically
Via Streamlabs Desktop
  • Open Streamlabs Desktop and go to Stream Settings in the bottom left navigation bar
  • Scroll down to find Patreon listed as a destination. Click Connect and authorize your account. You’ll be redirected back to Desktop once it’s linked
Via Streamlabs Plugin for OBS
  • Click Start Streaming inside OBS. The plugin window will open and show your list of destinations
  • Toggle on Patreon and you’ll be redirected to authorize your account. Once done, Patreon will appear as an available destination

Go live from Streamlabs Desktop

  • Click Go Live. You’ll see your connected destinations — make sure Patreon is toggled on
  • Enter your stream title and description, then choose which audience you’d like to have access. You can select any tier or combination of membership levels
  • Review your stream details and click Confirm & Go Live

When your stream wraps up, you’ll have the option to post a replay for anyone who missed it live. Replays stay on your Patreon page based on your settings.

Go live from Streamlabs Plugin for OBS

  • Set up your stream in OBS, then click Start Streaming. The plugin window will open
  • Make sure Patreon is toggled on as a destination. Enter your title, description, and choose your audience
  • Click Confirm & Go Live

Multistream to Patreon and other platforms

Want to go live on Patreon and another platform at the same time?

Multistreaming requires a Streamlabs Ultra subscription.

From Streamlabs Desktop
  • Click Go Live and toggle on Patreon plus any other platforms you’d like to stream to
  • Fill in your title, description, and streaming category (if required by other platforms). Scroll down to select your Patreon audience
  • Choose your primary chat in the bottom left of the Go Live window
  • Click Confirm & Go Live

Patreon chat isn’t currently supported within Desktop, so select another platform you’re streaming to if you’d like chat visible.

From Streamlabs Plugin for OBS
  • Go to Multistream in the left navigation bar. Toggle on Patreon along with your other preferred platforms
  • Enter your title, description, and audience. Click Confirm & Go Live

Enable Dual Output

Dual Output lets you optimize your stream layout for both horizontal and vertical viewing simultaneously — great if you’re streaming to platforms with different format preferences.

Via the Sources panel
  • Toggle on the Dual Output button at the top of the Sources panel in Streamlabs Desktop. From there, you can adjust both your horizontal and vertical layouts
  • When you click Go Live, you’ll see horizontal and vertical icons next to each platform. Assign the layout you want for each, then fill in your stream details and click Confirm & Go Live
Via the Go Live window
  • Click Go Live and check the Dual Output box. Use the icons next to each destination to select horizontal or vertical
  • Click out of the Go Live window to finalize your layouts, then click Go Live again to review your details before clicking Confirm & Go Live

Unlink your Patreon account

Via Dashboard
  • Go to Account Settings in your Streamlabs Dashboard and open the Platforms tab
  • Click Unmerge next to Patreon. This will unlink your account in both Desktop and Plugin for OBS
Via Streamlabs Desktop
  • Open Streamlabs Desktop and go to Stream Settings
  • Click Unmerge next to your Patreon account. You’ll be redirected to Dashboard to confirm
