Live Set Up and Overview

📢 Crowdcast is transitioning to Patreon Live. Beginning October 28, 2026, Crowdcast will no longer be available as a livestreaming option on Patreon.

What this means for creators:

• After October 28, 2026, you won’t be able to create new posts using the Crowdcast entrypoint in the editor.

• Existing posts that used Crowdcast will automatically become link posts — your Crowdcast link keeps working exactly as it does today, on Crowdcast’s own site.

• We recommend downloading any recordings you want to keep directly from Crowdcast, since Patreon doesn’t control if or when Crowdcast removes content on their end.

What this means for fans:

• Nothing changes about how you access posts you already have access to.

• New livestreams from creators you support will either be Crowdcast links for you to follow, or hosted natively on Patreon if your creator decides to use this.

Patreon Live is currently available to creators who meet the following criteria:

  • You’ve published your Patreon page
  • Your Patreon page is Safe for All Audiences
  • Your Patreon page is in good standing and complies with our Community Guidelines and Terms of Use

While Patreon Live is not yet available to creators in the Adult/18+ category, we’re working to responsibly expand access for more creators and ensure the product meets our community’s needs.

What is Live?

Live is another way creators can offer shared experiences to their members, right on Patreon. It lets you connect with your true fans in real time and is integrated with everything you do on Patreon.

Going Live from Patreon will immediately notify your members, whether it’s time to hang out and chat, give your biggest fans a behind-the-scenes experience, teach your members something new, or discuss upcoming releases. Each Live also has a Chat, letting you connect with your fans and letting them chat with one another – no more switching between apps.

Ticketed Livestreams (Beta)

We’re launching a new way for creators to host ticketed live events directly on Patreon, all within their creator page. We’re excited to help you bring these experiences to life with our new Ticketed Livestreams feature.

With Ticketed Livestreams, you’ll be able to:

  • Host paid or free live events for your fans
  • Sell tickets or include access as part of your membership
  • Stream natively on Patreon, with replay options for attendees
  • Keep your audience and earnings in one place

👉 Interested in joining the beta? Creators can indicate interest by filling out this form. We’ll reach out directly if you’re a good fit for the early access program and a spot becomes available. If you’re already in the beta, check out our Ticketed Lives FAQ.

Quick start on how to go live

You can start a Live the same way you create any post.

  • Click on Create from the left-side navigation (desktop) or from the bottom menu (app)
  • Select Live

Once you’re on the Live setup screen, you can customize everything from your title and audience to how you stream.

Keep reading below to learn how to set up your Live based on your device or preferred streaming method.

Setting up Live

You can use a desktop, the Patreon mobile app, or a third-party streaming software to go live. To host an audio-only Live, simply turn off your camera when setting up your stream.

  • You can go live directly from your computer using your webcam.
  • Here’s how to get started:
    • Click on Create from the left-side navigation
    • Select Live
    • In the right side panel, find the Camera source section and select Computer webcam
      • When you select it for the first time, your browser will prompt you to grant camera and microphone permissions. Click Always Allow
    • Adjust your Live settings:
      • Audience: You can go live to All Members (free and paid) or to any Paid members tier. For eligible creators, it’s also possible to sell one-time access to a Live. Note: Ticketed access is currently in beta. Creators can share interest by filling out this form
      • About: Set your title and description. Your audience will see the title you created when they’re notified about the event
      • Thumbnail: Upload an image in JPG, JPEG, PNG, or GIF, up to 2 GB. Recommended size 1024x1024px
      • Enable chat replay (On by default): If you keep chat replay enabled, viewers will be able to rewatch the recording with chat messages appearing in sync with the video timeline — just like during the original Live
      • More settings: Check other settings, such as Email and push notifications to alert members when you schedule or start a Live, and Auto-moderation to filter spam in chat
    • Take a look at your Live preview before you go Live. Make sure you’ve allowed access to your camera and microphone and test your video and audio
      • Camera turned on, but your preview is not showing up? You may not have granted permission for Patreon to use your webcam’s inputs. Head to your browser settings to change your permissions
    • Want to host an audio-only live? In the live preview, select Computer webcam as the camera source, then go to the bottom of the preview screen to turn off the camera
    • Ready to go? You can Go live now or Schedule a live for a specific day. Scheduling gives your members time to plan ahead — we’ll also send them email and push notifications when your Live is coming up. You can enter your scheduled Live up to 5 minutes early to test your setup. Learn more about notifications we send for Live
    • To finish your live, click End in the center of the Live viewer: Your recording is automatically saved to Drafts, where you can publish it as a post or download it for editing. After your Live ends, you’ll return to your Library and see a summary of how many members joined and how active the chat was. If Chat Replay was enabled during setup, chat messages will appear in sync when viewers watch the recording later
  • You can go live directly from your phone using the phone’s camera.
  • Here’s how to get started:
    • Tap Create from the bottom menu
    • Select Live
      • When you select it for the first time, your phone will ask for camera and microphone permissions. Tap Allow
    • Set your audience, title, and description
    • Select Settings to adjust advanced preferences
      • Display chat replay: Let viewers rewatch the stream with chat messages in sync
      • Auto-moderation: Filter spam or disruptive messages in chat
      • Notify members: Send email and app notifications when you schedule or start a Live
    • Want to host an audio-only live? In the live preview, navigate to the top right and tap the camera icon to turn off the camera
    • Ready to Go? You can Start live, or Schedule live for a specific day. Scheduling gives your members time to plan ahead — we’ll also send them email and push notifications when your Live is coming up. You can enter your scheduled Live up to 5 minutes early to test your setup. Learn more about the notifications we send for Live
    • To finish your live, tap End in the top-right corner: Your recording is automatically saved to Drafts, where you can publish it as a post or download it for editing. After your Live ends, you’ll return to your Library and see a summary of how many members joined and how active the chat was. If Chat Replay was enabled during setup, chat messages will appear in sync when viewers watch the recording later
  • RTMPS streaming software is supported on Patreon Live. Using streaming software lets you manage an advanced or existing production setup (such as a few cameras and microphones) or share your screen or broadcast your gameplay.
  • Here’s how to get started:
    • Click on Create from the left-side navigation
    • Select Live
    • In the right side panel, find the Camera source section and select Other streaming source — the preview panel will load with the Server URL and Stream Key
    • Adjust your Live settings:
      • Audience: You can go live to All Members (free and paid) or to any Paid members tier. For eligible creators, it’s also possible to sell one-time access to a Live. Note: Ticketed access is currently in beta. Creators can share interest by filling out this form
      • About: Set your title and description. Your audience will see the title you created when they’re notified about the event
      • Thumbnail: Upload an image in JPG, JPEG, PNG, or GIF, up to 2 GB. Recommended size 1024x1024px
      • Enable chat replay (On by default): If you keep chat replay enabled, viewers will be able to rewatch the recording with chat messages appearing in sync with the video timeline — just like during the original Live
      • More settings: Check other settings, such as Email and push notifications to alert members when you schedule or start a Live, and Auto-moderation to filter spam in chat
    • In your streaming software of choice, add the server URL and stream key from your Live preview on Patreon. Some streaming software, like Zoom, may also ask for a stream URL. In this case, paste the browser link to your Live (the patreon… link at the top of your web browser)
      • Click Start Streaming in your streaming software when complete
    • Navigate back to your Live preview on Patreon. Clicking Start Streaming in your streaming software should now successfully bring your stream over to Patreon
    • Ready to go? You can Go live now or Schedule a live for a specific day. Scheduling gives your members time to plan ahead — we’ll also send them email and push notifications when your Live is coming up. If you schedule a live with a streaming setup, you’ll be able to head in and check the setup 5 minutes before your Live begins
    • To finish your live, click End in the center of the Live viewer: Your recording is automatically saved to Drafts, where you can publish it as a post or download it for editing. After your Live ends, you’ll return to your Library and see a summary of how many members joined and how active the chat was. If Chat Replay was enabled during setup, chat messages will appear in sync when viewers watch the recording later

Sharing your Live

Once your Live is scheduled, you’ll be taken to a countdown page where you can share or download a promo card or copy your Live link to share it manually. This makes it easy to promote your stream across your social media and let fans know when to tune in.

Anyone who clicks your link will see the countdown page until your stream begins.

After a Live

After your live ends, a recording will automatically be saved as a draft in your Library. Sharing a recording with other members keeps lives working even after they’re over.

Here’s how to access your recordings:

- After you end your Live, you’ll be notified via email and push notification that your recording is being processed. For longer lives, expect to wait a few minutes before your live recording is ready
- Once ready, you can find it under Library → Drafts
- From here, you can:
    - Post the recording directly to your page — Posted recordings of a live are subject to video content and volume guidelines
    - Download the recording if you'd like to edit further in a video editor
- After you end your Live, you’ll be notified via email and push notification that your recording is being processed. For longer lives, expect to wait a few minutes before your live recording is ready
- Once ready, you can find it under the Profile tab → Manage posts
- Post the recording directly to your page — Posted recordings of a live are subject to video content and volume guidelines
Chat Replay

Chat Replay lets members catch up on the conversation even if they missed your Live. Here’s how it works:

  • If Chat Replay was enabled before your stream, the chat messages from your Live will appear in sync with the recording when members watch it later.
  • This allows viewers to experience the conversation as it happened, even if they couldn’t join live.

Live Hosting and Storage Limits

Resolution limits

Creators can currently livestream at 720p or 1080p resolutions. For members, Patreon automatically optimizes viewing resolution for both native video and live streaming content. By default, viewers will see content at 720p resolution, though this may be adjusted to 480p in cases where 720p provides no additional benefit. Viewers can manually toggle to higher resolutions when available.

Media storage and creation guidelines
  • Draft content: Any recorded live sessions in draft status will be automatically deleted after 6 months
  • Published content: Published native video content is stored indefinitely, maintaining our current policy
  • Monthly upload limits: To prevent abuse and ensure fair platform usage, creators are limited to 100 hours of media per month across both native video uploads and livestreaming. This limit applies monthly and is separate from any lifetime upload restrictions. Exceptions may be made for new creators with substantial existing content libraries
  • Upload limits with no paying members: To prevent abuse and ensure fair platform usage, creators with no paying members will have an upload limit of 100 hours total. This limit will increase to 100 hours monthly once a paying member joins
  • Single stream limitation: Creators cannot broadcast live on more than one post simultaneously to ensure optimal streaming quality
  • Maximum stream duration: Individual livestream sessions are limited to a maximum of 12 hours of continuous broadcasting. After this limit is reached, creators must start a new live

Make a Livestream post with YouTube

Even if you already have a YouTube channel, the steps in this guide are required to make sure you can Livestream. This will take some time to complete, but you only have to do it once!

Important: If you don’t yet have a YouTube channel, click here: Create a YouTube channel. Please note that you’ll need a Google account in order to set up a YouTube channel.

Verify your YouTube account and activate for Live Events

  • To activate your YouTube channel for Live Events, log in to your YouTube account
  • Open the camera plus sign icon and select Go Live
  • To verify your YouTube channel, select whether you’d like to receive a one-time text or phone call and enter your phone number
  • Enter the code that you receive on the textbox
  • You’ll need to wait 24 hours for your YouTube channel to be activated for Live Events. Once your account has been activated, you’re all set to have your first Livestream!

Create a Live Event on YouTube

Follow the steps below to create a Live Event in YouTube Studio:

  • While logged in to your YouTube account, select the Create icon in the upper right, and select “Go Live.” Ensure you’re on the WEBCAM option
  • Select when you want to go live
  • Give your Live Event a title and description. You’ll also want to select the option to keep your Live Event Unlisted so that it isn’t listed on YouTube
    • You’ll find the option to say whether your Livestream is for kids or not. You can also set an age restriction for your video. Learn more about how to Age restrict your video
  • Select Next! YouTube will ask you to take a picture for your thumbnail. Don’t worry – you can upload a different image after you’ve created your Live Event
  • Select the Share option, and copy the link that shows up. This is the link you’ll use for your Livestream post on Patreon

Posting your Livestream link to Patreon

Make sure you follow this guide while in your creator profile. You can switch to your creator profile by clicking on your name in the bottom-left corner of the home screen and selecting your Creator profile from the menu

  • Click on Create from the left-hand navigation
    • If you also sell digital products, you’ll need to select Post from the drop-down list
  • Select Livestream at the top of the post editor
  • Select the option to Use YouTube Live
  • Enter your YouTube Live link in the field provided. You’ll find your preview thumbnail populate
  • You’ll need to create a title for your post(required) and a description (optional)
  • You can organize your work by adding Tags or adding your post to a Collection to help fans find more of what they want
  • Click Next to add additional publishing options like Post access, Preview settings and Fan activity
  • On desktop, you can preview your post before publishing by clicking the View post button
  • If you’re planning on starting your Livestream immediately, feel free to publish your post now
  • If your live stream is several days away, we recommend publishing a teaser post to get fans excited and schedule your post to publish an hour or so before you go live. You can let fans know the exact time you’ll be live in the title or description of the post.

Managing comments on your Live Event

While your YouTube Live Event will play from your Patreon Livestream post, comments that members leave on the YouTube Live Event directly (on YouTube’s site) will not populate in the comment section of your post.

The same is true for your post comments – if members make a comment in the comment section of your Patreon post, it will not populate on the comment feed of your YouTube Live Event.

To ensure you’re getting both sides of the conversation, we recommend having both your post page and your YouTube Studio page open at the same time. That way you won’t miss any of your members’ comments.

Want to turn comments off for your YouTube Live Event?

You can control whether or not you allow commenting directly on your YouTube Live Event. You’ll want to take this step while you’re setting your Live Event up.

After you’ve titled your Event, and scheduled the time, open More options > Advanced settings and toggle off the comments.

Safety Best Practices for going Live

Patreon continues to put creators and communities first, working hard to build spaces where direct creator-to-fan and fan-to-fan relationships are stronger and safer than ever. Here are some of the ways creators, trusted moderators, and communities can build and maintain an even safer environment in Lives.

  • Put auto-moderation on duty. Creators should enable auto-moderation before they start their lives: think of it as a helpful co-host that automatically keeps things respectful and allows everyone else to remain in the moment
  • Assign moderators. Creators can assign up to 10 moderators to help maintain the norms of their community. A good moderator is someone who deeply understands the community and has an interest in engaging with members–someone you can rely on to stick to the moderation standards you’ve set. Check in regularly with moderators to make sure the expectations are clear and that you’re all on the same page about the norms being enforced
  • Lean on the arsenal of tools to keep Lives safe. Members should continue to rely on options like muting and reporting members, while creators and their trusted moderators should feel empowered to delete messages, mute members, kick members from chats, or turn off chats entirely
  • Keep up with Moderation Hub. Creators and their trusted moderators should consistently review flagged messages and decide whether to keep them, delete them, or report them to the Patreon Trust & Safety team
  • If you see something you believe violates our Community Guidelines, we encourage you to report the message or the user
  • If you have questions or concerns about our Community Guidelines, we welcome you to write to us at guidelines@patreon.com

Ticketed Lives FAQ

This guide covers the most frequently asked questions about Ticketed Lives on Patreon. Ticketed Lives are currently in beta testing, so access may be limited, and the feature may change as we continue to improve it.

👉 Interested in joining the beta? Creators can indicate interest by filling out this form, and we’ll reach out directly if you’re a good fit for early access.

If you’re looking to learn more about Live events on Patreon, including how Lives work and what tools are available, check out our Live Overview Help Center article.

FAQ

  • The minimum price for a ticketed live is $3 USD, which is the same minimum as other one-time purchases on Patreon. You can set your ticket price above that amount based on the value of your event.
  • Ticketed lives follow the same fee structure as one-time purchases on Patreon. Fees are deducted automatically when a fan purchases a ticket.
  • Yes. If you choose to publish the Live replay after your event, all ticket purchasers automatically get access to it. When publishing the replay, you can also choose to:
    • Open it up to all members
    • Limit it to paid members only
    • Sell it separately as a VOD
  • No matter which option you choose, anyone who bought a ticket to the live event will keep access to the replay once it’s published.
  • If you cancel or delete a ticketed live, all ticket purchasers will be refunded automatically. If you don’t start your ticketed live, it will be automatically cancelled 15 minutes after the scheduled start time, and ticket purchasers will be refunded automatically.
  • Yes. For refunds outside of cancellations or no-shows, ticketed lives follow the same refund process as other one-time purchases on Patreon.
  • To protect fans and keep payouts predictable for you, Patreon places a temporary hold on ticket earnings until the live is complete. The usual fees and rules of one-time purchases also apply to Ticketed Lives. Learn more about one-time payments and payouts here.
  • Fans can purchase a ticket in a few different ways:
    • When they see your Live event directly on Patreon (on web or in the app)
    • When they visit your Live using a link you’ve shared
  • Both members and non-members can buy tickets. If you’ve made the Live available to specific membership tiers, those members can join without purchasing a ticket.
  • After purchasing a ticket, fans will:
    • Receive a confirmation email with access to the event
    • See the scheduled (or in-progress) Live on patreon.com and in the Patreon app
  • They can use either the confirmation email or the Live entry point on Patreon to join the event when it starts.

Creators: Growth and audience insights

Automate your growth with Autopilot

This article is a general guide to joining and using our Autopilot feature. You can also check our Autopilot FAQ for additional information.

Note that Autopilot is now automatically enabled for all creators. To change this setting, check the Autopilot section in the Promotions tab in the Creator Studio. Additional details can be found in the dedicated section of this article.

Autopilot overview

Autopilot is an easy and automatic way to give your fans promotional offerings to drive your growth on Patreon. The feature currently includes:

  • Grow your community: tools to turn fans into paid or higher-tier members
    • Free member upgrade offer: Encourage free members to become paid members by offering them a one-time discount on their first month of membership
    • Paid member upgrade emails: Share locked posts from higher tiers with paid members in lower tiers to motivate upgrades
    • Targeted unlocked posts (beta): Automatically unlock a selection of your paid posts for non-members and free members to encourage them to join
    • Teaser campaign: Share a selection of your paid posts with free members to showcase what they’re missing out on
    • Abandoned cart emails: Remind fans who have added your membership to their cart to check out
  • Retain existing members: help to keep members in your community
    • Annual membership: You can offer members yearly membership access and give a discount to encourage them to sign up
    • Cancellation offer: Selected members who are cancelling their paid membership can receive a discount from creators
    • Benefit expiration emails: Send a reminder 24 hours before a membership is about to expire, and encourage fans to renew it

We plan to add more growth and promotional features to Autopilot over time. See below the current options available and how to make the most of them.

Trying to grow on autopilot? Check out “How to put growth on Autopilot” on Patreon for Creators. Currently, Patreon for Creators is only available in English.

Grow your community

Tools to encourage membership upgrades and grow your community by converting fans into paid members.

  • Autopilot will automatically help you send upgrade offers to selected free members and encourage them to become paid members. Offers will be a one-time discount to your free members who seem likely to upgrade to a paid membership. Subsequent months will be at full price.
Availability
  • The free member upgrade offer is enabled for creators who have met the following requirements:
    • Creators must be on Subscription billing
    • 18+ creators must be ID-verified
How to edit it
  • Follow the instructions below on desktop or mobile web:
    • Click Creator Studio , then click Promotions
    • Select Autopilot
    • Under the section Grow your community, select Free member upgrade offer to open the details
    • Patreon will automatically start with smart settings and optimize the offers for you.
      • Discounts will be between 5% - 90%
      • You can also check the Set a maximum discount option to set a manual cap on the highest discount amount you want to offer. This means Patreon will only send out discounts ranging up to that maximum amount.
    • Select which tiers you want to include in the discount offer
    • Click Save
  • You can turn Free member upgrade offers on or off by using the toggle in the details section. Once turned on, Autopilot will start gradually sending discount offers to your free members. Please note that not all free members will receive an offer.
What free members see
  • Free members who receive an Autopilot offer will get the following email indicating how much of a discount they are receiving and how long until the offer expires. It will be attached to a locked post that’s part of your paid membership.
  • Details on offers:
    • Only eligible free members who are likely to upgrade will receive a discount. This includes those who have previously purchased or interacted with your work, or have never redeemed an offer before, etc.
    • Discount will only apply to their first month of membership
    • Free members will have 7 days since receiving the email to claim it
    • Discounts can only be claimed once and are unique to the recipient
  • We’ll send paid members in lower tiers locked posts from your higher tiers to encourage them to upgrade. This feature is enabled by default but can be disabled, if you’d like to, by simply turning off the toggle. We’ve seen paid members were 23% more likely to upgrade to a higher tier after receiving a paid member upgrade email.
Availability
  • Paid member upgrade emails are enabled for creators who have met the following requirements:
    • Creators must have more than one tier
How to edit it
  • Follow the instructions below on desktop:
    • Click Creator Studio , then click Promotions
    • Select Autopilot
    • Under the section Grow your community, check the status on Paid member upgrade offer. If you’d like to change it, click on it to open the details
    • A pop-up will appear
    • Select the tiers you want to include in the offer
    • Click Save
What your paid members see
  • Paid members will get an email similar to the view below showing a post from the tier below.
  • With Teaser campaign, you can give free members a preview of your paid content by sharing a selection of your paid posts. It’s an effective way to showcase the value of upgrading without creating new content. This feature is not enabled by default and requires review. Learn below how to set up.
Availability
  • The Teaser campaign is enabled for creators who have met the following requirements:
    • Creators must have their work categorized as All Audiences
    • Creators must be on Subscription billing
How to set up
  • Follow the instructions below on desktop:
    • Click Creator Studio , then click Promotions
    • Select Autopilot
    • Under the section Grow your community, check the status on Teaser campaign
    • Click on Add posts to choose up to 5 posts to include
      • Posts will be unlocked on different days to keep free members engaged
    • Select the posts you want to offer and click on Update
      • You can search for any posts you want by typing in the Search or by using the available Filters
    • Click Save
What your free members see
  • Once Teaser campaign is set up, free members who join after activation will receive teaser emails:
    • The first email will be sent 24 hours after they join as a free member
    • They will receive one email per day showcasing a different paid post from your selected content
  • Targeted unlocked posts is currently in beta and rolling out to a limited group of creators. If you don’t see this option in your Autopilot settings yet, it may not be available to you at this time.
  • Targeted unlocked posts automatically unlocks a selection of your existing paid posts for non-members, giving them a taste of your work before they join. Patreon selects and rotates the posts from your back catalog most likely to convert visitors into members — no extra work required. Your paid members won’t see any change to their experience.
How it works
  • The first time you log in after Targeted unlocked posts becomes available on your account, you’ll see a prompt with two options:
    • Let Patreon automatically optimize which posts to unlock
    • Choose specific posts or collections to keep locked (you can exclude up to 50 posts or collections)
  • Select Save selection to confirm your choice, or Not now to decide later.
How to edit it
  • You can turn Targeted unlocked posts on or off, or update your exclusions, at any time. Follow the instructions below on desktop:
    • Click Creator Studio , then click Promotions
    • Select Autopilot
    • Under the section Grow your community, select Targeted unlocked posts to open the details
    • Use the toggle to turn Targeted unlocked posts on or off
    • To exclude specific posts or collections, select Edit next to Excluded posts or Excluded collections
    • Click Save
What non-members see
  • Non-members who visit a creator’s page may see a dedicated shelf featuring a curated selection of the creator’s unlocked posts. Selecting a locked post prompts them to join for free to unlock it and continue exploring the creator’s work.
  • We’re continuing to experiment with and expand where unlocked posts are surfaced to fans. To see which posts are unlocked on your creator page, you can view it in incognito mode anytime.
  • Fans who have started to purchase your membership but did not finish the process will receive a reminder to complete their purchase. This feature is enabled by default but can be disabled, if you’d like to, by simply turning off the toggle. All creators are eligible, except those with active per-creation campaigns.
How to edit it
  • Follow the instructions below on desktop:
    • Click Creator Studio , then click Promotions
    • Select Autopilot
    • Under the section Grow your community, check the status on Abandoned cart reminder. If you’d like to turn this off, click on it to open the details
    • A pop-up will appear
    • Adjust the toggle as needed to enable or disable the feature
    • Click on Done to save the changes

Retain existing members

Tools to retain and maintain your members by preventing cancellations and encouraging renewals.

  • With Patreon, you can offer members yearly membership access. You receive one annual payment from members, cutting down on member processing fees and payment method upkeep. This feature is not enabled by default and requires review. Check below for the eligibility and how to set up.
Availability
  • To enable Annual membership, the following requirements must be met:
    • Creators must be on Subscription billing or already offer charge upfront billing
    • Creator page must have been launched at least three months ago
    • Creator account must have a well-established payment history, including at least $200 earnings/month in the previous three months
    • 18+ creators must be ID-verified
How to set up
  • Follow the instructions below on desktop or mobile web:
    • Click Creator Studio , then click Promotions
    • Select Autopilot
    • Click the arrow on the Annual membership row to open up details
    • Select the Discount amount to be offered to members
    • Click on Save
  • For creators who are not yet eligible for Annual membership, a pre-enroll feature will be available. Once eligible, creators who opted-in will automatically be enrolled and receive an e-mail confirmation.
What your members see
  • Once Annual membership is set up within Autopilot, select free and paid members will receive an email notification offering to switch to a yearly plan. This is only sent once you’ve turned it on for the first time.
  • Patreon will automatically send a discount offer to fans going through the cancellation flow to incentivize them to stay in the membership. This feature is automatically enabled for all eligible creators. You can disable it by using the toggle in the details section. You can reactivate Autopilot by turning it back on at any time.
Availability
  • The Cancellation offer is enabled for the creators who have met the following requirements:
    • Creators must be on Subscription billing
    • 18+ creators must be ID-verified
How to edit it
  • Follow the instructions below on desktop or mobile web:
    • Click Creator Studio , then click Promotions
    • Select Autopilot
    • Under the section Retain existing members, select Cancellation offer to open the details
    • Patreon will automatically start with smart settings and optimize the offers for you. Discounts can range from 5% to 90%.
      • You can also check the Set a maximum discount option to set a manual cap on the highest discount amount you want to offer. This means Patreon will only send out discounts ranging up to that maximum amount.
    • Select which Tiers you want to include in the discount offer
    • Click Save
What your members see
  • With the cancellation offer, eligible members will see a pop-up with a discount for their next month before they complete the cancellation. If a paid member has already previously redeemed a cancellation offer, they will not receive another one.
  • Send a reminder 24 hours before a membership is about to expire, and encourage fans to renew it. This feature is enabled by default but can be disabled, if you’d like to, by simply turning off the toggle. All creators are eligible.
How to edit it
  • Follow the instructions below on desktop:
    • Click Creator Studio , then click Promotions
    • Select Autopilot
    • Under the section Retain existing members, check the status on Benefit expiration reminder. If you’d like to change it, click on it to open the details
    • A pop-up will appear
    • Adjust the toggle as needed to enable or disable the feature
    • Click on Done to save the changes

Turning Autopilot off completely

If you don’t want Autopilot on for your Patreon, you can head to Autopilot settings to turn it off completely.

  • Toggling this off will mean that all Autopilot features that are currently on will be turned off
  • Offers that are already sent out can still be redeemed, but no future offers will be sent out

If you want to turn off Autopilot but have future features turned on, you can check the box that says Turn on future Autopilot features automatically.

  • This means that any eligible features added to Autopilot over time will be automatically turned on for you but existing features will remain off
  • To turn off Autopilot completely, turn the toggle off and uncheck the box. No Autopilot features will be turned on for you and all features will remain off

Track Autopilot conversions

On the Autopilot tab, you’ll see a View Insights button at the top of the page. Clicking this will show you more metrics on how your offers are performing.

Please note that Autopilot insights will show data for Free member upgrade offer, Teaser campaign, and Cancellation offer, but Annual membership statistics will be available in the general Insights tab.

You will also be able to see which members have redeemed an Autopilot discount in their payment history. First, head to the Audience tab, click on a member, and anyone who has redeemed will have an “Autopilot discount applied” tag next to them. If the payment history extends beyond 3 months, you may have to click See all payment history.

Can I delete a member?

Since rolling out our blocking feature, creators are no longer able to delete members.

Here’s why: Deleting members was a way for creators to temporarily remove members from their list of members. This didn’t stop members from rejoining the creator’s Patreon community, so it was essentially a band-aid effect.

When a member’s payment declines, that member is automatically revoked access to a creator’s member-only posts, until that member’s payment processes. A creator does not need to delete a member to prevent the member from viewing the creator’s posts.

What can a creator do instead of deleting a member?

If you have a member whose pledge has declined, they will automatically be revoked access to your member-only posts and will receive an email from us to update their payment info. You can also send them a message yourself, which is sometimes more effective.

If you have a member who has been detrimental to your success on Patreon, you have the option of blocking them. Blocking a member will remove their pledge to you as well as prevent them from becoming your member again.

Learn more about how to block a member on our article.

Downloading your earnings and payout reports

You can download 3 reports (CSV files) to check your numbers, match your earnings with your bank deposits, or share your records with an accountant. Each report follows the months you choose on the page, and we email it to you when it’s ready.

Which report to use

Each report answers a different question:

Report

Use it to

Where to find it

Monthly payouts

See how much money became available to withdraw each month, how much you paid out, your payout fees, and what reached your payout account

Payouts page and Documents tab

Earnings breakdown by month

See your gross earnings, fees, refunds, and net earnings for each month, matching your Earnings dashboard

Earnings Insights and Documents tab

Member transaction history

Follow each member payment from the day it was charged to the day it became available to withdraw, including refunds

Payouts page, Earnings Insights, and Documents tab

How to download a report

  • On desktop, select Creator studio in the left-side navigation menu, then click Payouts. For the Earnings breakdown by month, go to Insights and click Earnings instead
  • Choose the months you want with the date range picker
  • Click CSV and choose the report you want
  • We’ll email the report to the address on your Patreon account

Large reports can take several minutes to arrive. You can also download all 3 reports from the Documents tab on your Payouts page.

What’s in each report

Monthly payouts

This report has 1 row for each month and currency, with the newest month first.

Column

What it shows

Month

The calendar month, in Pacific time

Currency

Your payout currency for that month

Finalized earnings

Earnings that finished processing that month and became available to withdraw

Membership to other creators

Memberships to other creators paid from your balance. Shows only if you have them

Total payout

The amount you withdrew from your balance that month

Payout fees

Fees for sending your payout to your payout method

Total received after fees

What we sent to your payout account after payout fees

Payout adjustments

Changes to a payout, such as a payout that was returned to your balance. Shows only if you have them

A few things to know about this report:

  • Total payout and Total received after fees are positive amounts. Payout fees and Membership to other creators are negative. Total payout plus Payout fees equals Total received after fees.
  • Payout fees include only the fees Patreon charges. PayPal, Payoneer, or your bank may charge their own fees, which aren’t in this report

What they show

Fees show as negative numbers. Refunds and recovered payments are listed in their own columns and aren’t included in gross earnings.

This report has 1 row for each transaction, such as a member payment or a refund. It includes payments that are still pending, so you can match them with Pending earnings on your Payouts page.

If an export has more than 2 million transactions, we send the newest 2 million and the email tells you which dates are included. To get the rest, request another export for the earlier dates.

Tax documents

Your tax documents are in the Documents tab on your Payouts page:
