Earnings Insights

When it comes to your earnings, be sure to use the Earnings page for an accurate record of your gross and net income (after fees) for each month.

The Overview section on your main web page provides an estimate by averaging earnings from annual memberships and displaying net monthly earnings after fees. This section is useful for identifying trends and is visible to members if you choose to make your earnings public. However, it should not be relied upon as an accurate representation of your true earnings for any specific month.

After processing a payment, fees and refunds are deducted, with the remaining amount going to your Creator Balance. This dashboard summarises the flow of funds based on when the transactions occurred.

Your Earnings dashboard counts a payment as soon as it goes through. Some payments are then held before you can withdraw them, such as iOS in-app purchases, one-time purchases, and tickets for Live events. To see what you can withdraw now and when held payments become available, go to your Payouts page.

To explore your other dashboards, see our main guide on Insights dashboards.

Earnings insights filters

Customize your earnings view by:

  • Date range: You can view data from past 6 months, Past year (past 12 months), All time, or set a Custom range
  • Earnings type: You can filter by All earnings, Membership, or Shop
  • Currency (Early access): If you’ve changed your shop currency in the past, you can use the currency toggle to view your earnings in your current or any previously used currencies. Note: This feature is currently in early access, which means not all creators will see it yet. It will be gradually rolled out to all users
  • Free or Paid member view: Select either the free or paid member view at the top of the dashboard to filter insights accordingly
  • Daily or Monthly view: Switch between Monthly and Daily views to track earnings trends over different timeframes
  • Tier: Filter your earnings by a specific membership tier to understand which tiers are driving your revenue each month
  • Billing cadence: Filter by monthly or annual to see how payment frequency affects your earnings

Key sections in earnings insights

The earnings dashboard summarizes the income associated with your Patreon. We organize data by the time transactions occur. All dates are in Pacific time (PT). The Gross revenue column on your Earnings dashboard may display a different amount than your total memberships calculated from your Relationship manager due to mid-month tier switches and refunds.

  • Membership: The amount earned from your memberships before any fees, refunds, and declines
  • Shop (Web and Android): The amount earned from purchases made through your shop on both Web and Android, before subtracting any fees, refunds, or declines
  • Shop (iOS): The amount earned from purchases made through your shop on the iOS App Store, before the deduction of any fees, refunds, or declines. Please note that purchases on iOS are subject to an Apple App Store fee. Learn more about iOS pricing here
  • Declines: The value of attempted charges declined this month. This column value will likely decrease as we retry your declined members and process them to your creator balance
  • Refunds: The amount of any refunds issued in that month. This column only includes the creator’s share of any refunds; Patreon’s fee, processing fees, and taxes are refunded by Patreon and therefore do not appear here. This also does not include fraud refunds. Here’s an article with more information on fraud refunds
  • Membership: The amount earned from your memberships after any fees, refunds, and declines
  • Shop (Web and Android): The amount earned from purchases made through your shop on both Web and Android, after subtracting any fees, refunds, or declines
  • Shop (iOS): The amount earned from purchases made through your shop on the iOS App Store, after the deduction of any fees, refunds, or declines. Please note that purchases on iOS are subject to an Apple App Store fee. Learn more about iOS pricing here
Timing examples:
  • Paid member A joins your community on 16 February but isn’t charged until 1 March. The earnings from that transaction will appear in March.
  • If a refund is processed in October for a transaction that initially occurred in July, the refund will appear in October.

Why your earnings and finalized earnings can differ

Your Earnings dashboard and the Finalized earnings on your Payouts page can show different amounts for the same month. Earnings count a payment when it goes through. Finalized earnings count money when it becomes available to withdraw, after any hold ends.

The Earnings page explains this difference for each month. If you use Patreon for merch, your merch costs also show in this breakdown. To learn more, visit Why is my payout less than I expected?

Download your earnings data

On the Earnings page, click CSV and choose a report:

  • Earnings breakdown by month: your earnings for each month, matching your Earnings dashboard
  • Member transaction history: every transaction, including refunds

The report follows the date range you selected, and we’ll email it to you when it’s ready. To learn what’s in each report, visit Downloading your earnings and payout reports.

FAQ

  • The Earnings dashboard shows money when the payment goes through, not necessarily when someone signs up. So if a member upgrades mid-month, gets refunded, or their payment is delayed, the numbers might not match what you expected.
  • Yes, you can filter earnings by type, like Membership or Shop, and view daily or monthly totals. There’s also a breakdown showing things like platform fees, refunds, declines, and your final net earnings.

Everything you need to know about blocking another user

Patreon should be a safe space for all creators to share their work and for all members to celebrate these creations and build community with one another. If you notice someone constantly changing their membership, harassing you or your community, or spamming your posts or community chats, blocking will help.

What a blocked user CAN do

What a blocked user CAN NOT do

  • See any existing Direct Message history between you and them

  • Join your Patreon

  • Direct Message you

  • Access any content on your page

  • Engage with your posts or in your community chats

How do I block someone?

Patreon’s Community Guidelines outline what is and isn’t allowed on Patreon. You can report someone who may not be following these guidelines by clicking the More button and selecting Report. You can also block them at any time. Here’s how:

  • You can block someone directly from their comment on your posts or quips. This works on the Patreon app:
    • Click More on the comment
    • Select Block user
    • Click the Block button
  • If the user is a paid member, you’ll be asked to select a reason from the list and click the Submit button.
  • You can block someone by going directly to their public profile. This works on both desktop and the Patreon app:
    • Click or tap the name of the person you’d like to block anywhere you see them
    • On their public profile, select more to open a menu
    • Select Block and confirm your decision
  • You can block paid or free members directly from your Relationship manager on desktop:
    • Select Creator studio from the left navigation, then click Audience
    • In your Relationship manager, locate a specific member by searching for their Patreon username or email address
    • Click the member’s name to expand the member details on the right side of the page
    • Click More and select Block user
    • Select the reason why you’re blocking the user
    • Click the Block button to confirm
When you block someone
  • They won’t be able to join as a member, access your posts, or interact with you and your community
  • If they’re a current member, their membership will be ended
  • If you choose to delete their comments, all their comments will be removed from your posts. If you choose not to delete them, their comments will appear grayed out with a “You blocked [username]” label
  • Their chat messages will appear grayed out and hidden in your chat channels
  • Their direct messages will appear grayed out
  • You won’t see their comments or messages anymore, and they won’t see yours (except during lives and in chats)

How do I unblock someone?

If you’ve changed your mind about blocking someone, you can unblock them at any time. Once unblocked, they’ll be able to find and interact with your Patreon again, but they’ll need to rejoin as a member on their own.

- Tap their profile photo or the error message to view the blocked member's profile
- Tap the three dots menu to reveal the Unblock option
- Tap Unblock to remove the block from this person
  • If you want to see a full list of people you’ve blocked, you’ll need to use a web browser on desktop.
    • Select Creator studio from the left navigation, then click Audience
    • Click the Blocked users tab to find a complete list of blocked members, along with the date you blocked them
    • Locate the member and click the Unblock button by their name
    • Confirm your decision to finalize the unblocking process
  • You can also find your blocked users under Your account → Settings → Blocked users.

FAQ

  • As soon as an active member is blocked, they’re immediately removed from your community and Relationship manager, and Patreon sends them an email notification of removal. This email lets them know they’ll no longer access or receive benefits from your page, that their membership has been canceled, and that they won’t be charged again. If you chose to delete their comments during the blocking process, all their comments on your posts will also be removed.
  • If the user isn’t an active member, they’ll be removed from your Relationship manager but won’t receive an email notification.
  • Yes, but only indirectly. If someone tries to follow a link to something you’ve previously shared with them on Patreon, or if they can’t see your posts, messages, or comments, they’ll still be able to see the public information on your profile: your page or member name, profile picture, and bio. If you have one, they’ll also still have access to your shared direct message history. From these pages, they’ll see a notification that says, “This person has blocked you.”
  • When you block someone on Patreon, the block applies everywhere. Blocked members won’t be able to see your posts or engage with you or your community. They also won’t be able to see your comments and messages in other communities.
  • A blocked member or creator can’t become a member of your page again unless you unblock them.
  • If you block someone you’re a member of, your membership will be removed, and any recurring payments will be canceled. You’ll no longer receive messages from them or see their posts and community messages on Patreon.

Find my members’ shipping addresses

If you haven’t already enabled our shipping address feature for your tiers, you’ll need to go to your Tiers and enable Shipping address collection from the Advanced section. Here’s our guide that will take you through the steps: Get member shipping addresses

If you already have shipping address collection enabled for your tiers, this article will help you find and utilize your members’ email addresses.

View your members’ mailing addresses in your relationship manager

You can view your members’ mailing addresses within your Relationship manager. Here’s how:

  • Click Creator studio
  • Click on Audience
  • You’ll land on your Relationship manager, where you can review members’ shipping addresses
  • Locate the member you are sending something to, and click on their name
  • The member’s details will populate on the right-hand side of the page
  • The member’s address will be listed under the Contact information card — if you don’t see an address, it’s possible that the member did not provide an address and has opted out of physical benefits

How do I view all of my members’ shipping addresses at once?

To find all of your members’ shipping addresses at once, you can download a CSV from your relationship manager. All of your members’ shipping addresses will be listed on the CSV.

How do I find my paid member count?

All creators are now using subscription billing. If your account was still on a legacy billing model on November 1, 2026, we switched it automatically and emailed you when the switch was complete.

Key details depending on your previous billing model:

  • Per-creation: If you haven’t resumed billing yet, it stays paused until you review your new tier prices. Learn how to resume billing
  • First-of-the-month: Your existing members are still billed on the 1st of each month. New members are billed on the date they join

Your Membership insights

Your Membership insights dashboard shows your total member count, including active members, new members, and cancellations. It also breaks down your total paid member count and your estimated monthly earnings. If you’ve enabled membership visibility from your page settings, the total member count will also be publicly available on your Patreon.

Your active paid member count includes members with an active payment, members with a retrying payment, free trial members, gifted members, and members who have canceled but whose access hasn’t expired yet.

Visit your Membership insights to analyze your membership health over time. Here’s how to get a breakdown of paid members in each tier:

  • Click Creator studio from the left-side navigation menu, then select Insights from the sub-menu to get to your Membership insights
  • Use the date drop-down menu at the top of the page to filter your view by the past 30 days, past 6 months, past year, and all time
    • When you open your membership insights, your insights will be filtered by 30 days by default
  • Click on the audience drop-down menu and choose the Paid members filter
  • Directly under the insights graph, click on the Tiers button to view a breakdown of each of your tiers

Please note that insights are filtered by the past 30 days by default when you first open it.

Membership insights are great for getting a sense of your membership count over stretches of time, but they do not show your member count on a single date.

Get a list of paid members in each tier

You can use the filtering tool at the top of your Relationship manager to find the number of members in each of your tiers as well as free members. Here are the steps to find your member count and a list of members in a given tier:

  • Click Creator studio from the left-side navigation menu, then select Audience from the sub-menu to get to your Relationship manager
  • Choose your audience:
    • Click the Paid members button and go to Step 3
    • Click the Free members button to get a list of free members — if all you need is a list of free members, then you don’t need to go any further! Click the CSV button to download your list
  • Click the Filters button
  • By default, all of your paid tiers will be selected. You can deselect any tiers you don’t want to include in your list. You can also use the Paid status filter to break down members by active payments, retrying payments, free trials, and gifted memberships
  • Scroll down to click Save filters. Your filters will apply automatically, and your member count will update to reflect your selection

To learn more about other valuable data, visit our guide on Relationship manager.

How to use your Relationship manager

The Relationship manager is your central place to view, filter, and communicate with your members. You can filter members by details such as email address, tier, join date, membership status, and payment information.

On Desktop, select Creator studio in the left-side navigation menu, then select Audience from the sub-menu to access it. This guide explains how to filter, review, export, and communicate with your members.

To identify members who are eligible for benefits for a specific month, use the Benefit Eligibility Status tool by going to the Benefits tab.

Member type

Paid members

Members who have paid or are scheduled to be billed. Active paid members have access to membership benefits.

Free members

A free member is not a paying member. They can see your public posts and other publications set to this audience, but don’t have access to paid member-only content on Patreon.

Member statuses

The Relationship manager gives a membership status to each paid member, so you can identify who currently has access and who doesn’t.

Use the toggle below to find the definitions for each one.

  • STATUS
  • DEFINITION
  • Active payment
  • The member has paid or is scheduled to be billed. Active paid members have membership access. To confirm whether a member is eligible for benefit delivery for a specific month, use the Benefit tab.
  • Retrying payment
  • The member’s most recent charge attempt declined, and we are currently retrying the payment. During this period, the member’s access is revoked. If the payment is successfully processed, access is restored.
  • Payment failed
  • After retrying a failed payment, the charge still failed. We’ll make a new attempt, or the member can retry directly. Share the Failed payment help with them if needed. A member with a failed payment for ~30 days will be converted to a free membership.
  • Canceled
  • The member has deleted their subscription. Their membership access remains active until their current billing period ends. They will appear as Canceled in your Relationship Manager from the date their access expires, not the date they canceled. No new bills will be created for their membership.
  • Refunded
  • The most recent charge was refunded. Please note that members must also cancel their membership to avoid auto-renewal.
  • Fraud
  • The most recent charge was deemed fraudulent, and their payment has been declined. If a charge is potentially fraudulent, we will not automatically retry the payment. While a member’s payment is marked as fraudulent, they will not have access to your member-only content. There are many reasons why this might occur. You can let your members know to contact their bank, then our support team, to clear this up.
  • Gifted by others
  • Members who redeemed a gift from another fan and are actively in their gifted membership period.
  • Gifted by you
  • Members who redeemed a gift created by you and are actively in their gifted membership period.

Additional filters

Beyond the quick filters at the top of your Relationship Manager (Paid members, Free members, Active, Canceled, Payment declined, New this month), click the Filters button to dive deeper into your member list.

Use the toggle below to see a full breakdown and how to use them.

  • FILTER
  • DEFINITION
  • Member type
  • Filter by Paid members or Free members
  • Status
  • Filter by Active payment, Declined, Canceled, Refunded, Fraud, Gifted by others, or Gifted by you.
  • Tiers
  • Select all tiers or choose specific ones to focus on a particular membership level.
  • Discount
  • Check the Discount code used checkbox and select from the discount codes you’ve created to filter members who joined using a specific discount
  • Join date
  • Filter by Anytime, This week, Last week, This month, Last month, or a Custom range.
  • Membership duration
  • Filter by how long a member has had a membership. You can set a minimum or an exact number of months or years
  • Lifetime pledge amount
  • Filter members by the total amount they’ve paid you over their membership lifetime. Select an amount range to narrow your list. Note: this amount may not update immediately, and there may be a delay for members on legacy billing models
  • Last charge date
  • Filter by a date range to find members whose most recent charge falls within a specific period
  • Next charge date
  • Filter by a date range to find members whose next scheduled charge falls within a specific period
  • Pledge amount
  • Filter by a member’s current payment amount. If you have annual memberships, some members may appear marked as “per year.” Learn more about annual plans
  • Subscription source
  • Filter by Patreon or Apple in-app subscriptions to see where members originally signed up
  • Benefits
  • Select a specific benefit using the checkbox to filter all members who are eligible to receive it
  • Charge frequency
  • If you offer Annual memberships, you’ll find an additional Charge frequency filter in your Relationship Manager, so you can filter members who pay monthly versus per year. To learn more, visit our guide on Annual membership creators.

Your member list

Once you’ve applied filters, you’ll see a list of members that match your criteria. You can customize which columns are displayed by clicking on Settings , including Shipping Address, Notes, Discord handle, Canceled Date, and more.

For a full description of each filter, use the toggle below.

  • COLUMN
  • DEFINITION
  • Name
  • Your members’ profile name. Members can be anonymous, just as creators can, so their profile name may not be their actual name.
  • Email
  • The email address of your member. Fans can opt out of sharing their email address with creators — if you’re not seeing a fan’s email address, they may have chosen not to share it.
  • Discord
  • Your member’s Discord handle (if you offer Discord).
  • Current Tier
  • The tier that your member is currently on.
  • Address
  • Your member’s shipping address, if they’ve provided one.
  • Pledge
  • Their current payment amount. If you are using annual memberships, you may also find members marked as “per year.” To learn more, visit our guide on Annual memberships.
  • Lifetime
  • The total amount they’ve paid you as their member. Please note that the Lifetime payment amount does not update immediately, and there may be a delay in this number updating for members, particularly during billing processing on the 1st of each month.
  • Status
  • This column shows the status of the member’s most recent attempted charge.
  • Join date
  • The date the member first joined your membership.
  • Last Charge Date
  • The last time we attempted to process that member’s payment. You can find whether or not the attempt was successful in the “Status” column directly to the right.
  • Next Charge Date
  • The date on which a membership will be renewed, and we’ll attempt to process the payment.
  • Notes
  • If you have added any notes that might help you in your relationship with particular members, you’ll find them located in this column.
  • Cancel Date
  • The last day of a member’s access, not the date they hit cancel.
  • Access Expiration
  • The date on which a member’s access expires, and they can no longer see posts or receive benefits.
  • Subscription Source
  • It’s where a membership came from, the channel or path that led someone to subscribe or convert to paid.

Payment history

Click on a member’s name to open the side drawer, then click See all payment history to view their complete billing history. You can refund a member’s three most recent charges. For older refunds, you’ll need to arrange these outside of Patreon.

Use the toggle below to find definitions for the statuses that may show up in a member’s payment history.

  • STATUS
  • DEFINITION
  • Paid
  • This means the payment was successful
  • Declined
  • Learn more about viewing member payment history in this help center guide. If it displays as declined, it means that we’ve attempted to process their payment, but their bank has declined the charge. We regularly reattempt failed payments; however, oftentimes, the member will want to contact their bank to ensure nothing is blocking the payment. Feel free to share this with members in a declined state: How do I retry my payment?
  • Upgraded
  • The member has successfully increased their payment amount or tier level
  • Downgraded
  • The member has successfully decreased their payment amount or tier level
  • Deleted
  • This means that the member deleted their membership
  • Repledged
  • This means the member has rejoined
  • Refunded
  • This means that this particular bill has been refunded to the member. You can find a full list of refunded members by downloading the Refund CSV from the Documents section of your Payouts
  • Tier deleted
  • When you’ve removed a Tier from your page. When you delete a Tier, it doesn’t delete a member’s payment, so be sure to communicate the change with members ahead of time. Learn more about retiring a tier
  • Refunded by Patreon
  • The pledge was found to be fraudulent in a fraud review, and the funds for this pledge have been refunded to the cardholder

Check benefits eligibility

Use the Benefit Eligibility Status tool to confirm which members were eligible for benefits for a specific month.

To access it:

  • On desktop, select Creator studio in the left-side navigation menu
  • Click Audience from the creator navigation
  • Select the Benefits tab
  • Choose the tier and the month you want to review

Looking for the Benefit Tracker? Benefit Tracker is being retired and replaced by the new Benefit Eligibility Status tool. Check the guide on Track delivery with Benefits features for the former experience.

This tool helps you:

  • See which monthly and annual members have successfully paid for the current month
  • Filter by tier to see benefit eligibility by group
  • Download a CSV or message selected members directly
  • Switch to the previous month if you deliver benefits after billing is complete

This view is especially helpful if you deliver benefits monthly or want to avoid messaging members who haven’t paid yet. If you haven’t added specific benefits to your tiers yet, check some Ideas for benefits to offer members.

Downloading your members’ data

To download your member list, click the CSV button at the top of the page. Your current filters will apply to the export. If you offer Annual memberships, the CSV will include an additional Charge frequency column. Note that the Last charge date for annual members reflects the date they started their membership.

If you need month-specific benefit-eligibility information, use the dedicated CSV export from Audience → Benefits. This export includes Eligibility Tier and Eligibility Month columns, which show the tier each member held in the selected month.

Messaging paid members

You can bulk message groups of paid members, whether you’re reaching out to members who are retrying a payment or sending benefits to all members in a specific tier.

Once your filters are applied, click the Message button above the list to reach everyone on it. While you can send mass messages, each message is private, and responses will arrive as separate direct messages in your inbox.

To message members based on their eligibility for a specific month, use the Benefit Eligibility Status tool from Audience → Benefits. Select the relevant tier and month, then check your filters before sending your message.

Note: It’s recommended to filter by Member type (Paid members) and Status (Active payment) before messaging, to avoid sending your message to members who no longer wish to receive your updates.

Why are some member details missing?

Some member details may be hidden because the member was removed. Personal information (e.g., name, email address, etc.) about members may be hidden due to one or more of the following reasons:

  • The member has been blocked by the creator
  • The member has been removed for violating Patreon’s Terms of Use
  • The member has requested removal in line with GDPR compliance
  • The member was migrated from our Following feature to a Free membership
  • The creator has been blocked by the member (only possible if the member has a creator profile)
  • The member has opted out of sharing their email address with creators. You can learn more in our article on sharing email with creators

How do I find customers’ information?

If you’re looking for customers who purchased digital products, from Audience, select Sales. There you’ll find the product, purchase date, status, and amount paid. You can also export customer details and transactions. Learn more about Managing customers.

Common actions and how-to tips

Now, let’s go over common uses of Relationship manager to help you manage, message, and engage with members:

  • I want to message my filtered list of members or an individual member
  • Click the Filters button and select your desired filters. Once your view is set, click individual checkboxes next to members’ names — or the checkbox at the top of the list to select all — then click Message.
  • I want to send a welcome message to new paid members
  • By default, your member list is sorted by Join Date with the newest members at the top. Click Paid members at the top of the page, select your new members using the checkboxes, and click Message to send a group or individual message.
  • I want to find members who paid for a specific month
  • Go to Audience → Benefits and choose the tier and month you’re delivering for. You can message those members or export the list from there.
  • I want to filter paid memberships by a specific monthly amount
  • Click Filters and use the Pledge amount filter to set your range.
  • I want to filter members by their total lifetime payments
  • Click Filters and use the Lifetime pledge amount filter to set a cumulative range.
  • I want to filter failed payments within a specific payment range
  • Click the Declined button, then click Filters and set the Last charge date filter.
  • I want to filter members with failed payments this month
  • Click Declined, then click Filters and set the Last charge date. Once you have your filtered list, you can click Message to reach out to declined members.
  • I want to find members with a “have-not-paid” status
  • Sort by payment status and look for members with “–” or no value in the Status column.
  • I want to filter members from a specific time period
  • Click Filters and set the Last charge date range. You can also use the Active quick filter to narrow by status. To find members who paid during a specific month so you can deliver benefits, use the Benefit Eligibility Status tool instead. Last charge date only shows each member’s most recent charge, so members who have renewed since won’t appear for earlier months.
  • I want to view my newest members this month
  • Members are sorted by Join Date by default. Click New, then click Filters and set a shortcut or custom range from the Join date filter. New and continuing members are also grouped in the Benefit Eligibility Status tab.
  • I want to search across all my members
  • The Search bar looks across all your members — not just those visible on the current page. You can search by name, email address, or Discord handle.
  • I want to find members from a previously deleted tier
  • We advise against deleting a tier that still has members. If you need to retire a tier, consider unpublishing it instead. To find members from a deleted tier, click Filters, then under Tiers select All.
  • I want to filter and sort members by tier
  • Click Filters and choose your tier. You can select multiple tiers — useful when delivering a benefit that spans more than one.
  • I want to see who’s supported me the longest
  • Click the arrows next to the Join Date column to sort by sign-up date.
  • I want to filter members who’ve paid the most over their lifetime
  • Click Filters and set a range in Lifetime Pledge Amount.
  • I want to save a filter set to reuse regularly
  • Once your filters are set, click Save Filters at the bottom of the side drawer and give your list a name. To access it again, go to the Saved Filters tab.

I’m a creator. How do I know if a member is suspicious?

Creators, we know how important your memberships are, and we’re here to support you.

If you notice a payment or email address that feels unusual, unexpected, or potentially suspicious, you can reach out to us for help.

Please submit a request here and include a note that you’d like us to review a suspicious member. Our team will take a closer look and confirm whether everything checks out.

Importing your email list to Patreon (Beta)

Importing an existing mailing list to Patreon is currently available in early access. If you’re interested, please fill out this form, and we’ll review whether you qualify.

Overview

Importing your email list lets you bring subscribers you already have permission to contact into Patreon, so you can reach them using posts and emails on Patreon.

How it works

For you (the creator)
  • Contacts you import who aren’t already members will receive all emails you send to free members or all members
  • You’ll have the option to send them a welcome email upon import. After that, imported subscribers can’t be targeted or excluded as a separate group
  • Imported subscribers who don’t create a Patreon account won’t be counted as active members in Membership insights or your Relationship manager. Instead, they’ll be included in a Total audience banner in Membership insights, which combines email-only subscribers and active members
  • Imported contacts will appear under Audience > Imported users
For imported subscribers
  • Imported subscribers who don’t create a Patreon account are known as email-only subscribers
  • They’ll receive your posts via email, but will need a Patreon account to comment on posts, vote in polls, join chats or livestreams, or play audio and video content
  • They can unsubscribe from emails at any time using the Unsubscribe link at the bottom of your emails
  • They won’t receive Patreon system emails (such as upgrade prompts or chat notifications) unless they create a Patreon account

Insights dashboards

This article explains how our Insights dashboards work and how to use them to understand your earnings and membership trends.

Creator earnings funnel

The following chart identifies the four main steps in the process and the associated dashboards that describe them:

Want to put your data to work? Check out “Reimagined dashboards for deeper insights” on Patreon for Creators. Currently, Patreon for Creators is only available in English.

How to use Insights

  • From the Creator studio in the left-side navigation menu, click on Insights in the sub-menu. This allows you to select specific dashboards to view relevant data about your page.
  • From the Profile tab in the bottom menu, you can have an overview of key metrics across various dashboards. You can access the data from the past 30 days.

Explore your Insights

The Insights dashboard is designed to give you a clear view of your creator activity by breaking it down into different sections. You can use the toggles below to dive into insights on Membership, Shop, Earnings, Posts, Traffic, and Surveys. Each section will help you understand how you’re performing and spot any trends in those areas.

  • The Membership Insights dashboard helps you track active members, new members, and cancellations, so you can monitor your community’s growth over time.
    • Active members: includes free members, members with an active or retrying payment, free trial members, gifted members, and anyone who’s canceled but hasn’t lost access yet
    • New members: tracks first-time joins as well as anyone who rejoined after canceling
    • Canceled members: they are recorded on the date their access expires, not the date they hit cancel — that’s why you’ll often see a spike in cancellations around the 1st of the month
  • You can customize your view using filters such as date range, membership tiers, billing cycle, and paid status to get the most relevant insights. Get the full picture, including how failed payments are reflected in your numbers, in our dedicated article on Membership Insights.
  • The Shop dashboard shows up for creators selling digital products with Commerce on Patreon, whether the buyer is a paid member or not.
    • Track Total earnings and Total sales across all your products
    • See your Top-selling products ranked by earnings — only active (published, non-deleted) products appear here
    • View results over the past 30 days, 6 months, the past year, or all time
  • Head to our dedicated article on Shop Insights for filters, earnings breakdowns, and sales history.
  • The Earnings dashboard gives you an accurate record of your gross and net income after fees.
    • Data is organized by when the transaction occurred, not when a member first signed up
    • See exactly how Declines and Refunds affect your final net earnings each month
  • Customize your view using filters such as date range, earnings type, membership tiers, and billing cadence to get the most relevant insights. For the full breakdown, including filters and definitions, see our dedicated article on Earnings Insights.
  • Post Insights gives you visibility into how your work is reaching your fans and growing your audience and business, allowing you to identify which areas to focus on or expand.
    • Reach covers impressions (how often a post showed up) and seen (how many people actually engaged)
    • Conversion shows new revenue and new free members driven by a specific post
    • Live metrics include unique viewers and average view time for your live events
    • View up to 25 posts at a time in the dashboard, or export a CSV for RSS downloads, likes, and comments
  • Dive deeper into our dedicated article on Post Insights, or check our guide on View Insights for an individual post.
  • The Traffic Insights dashboard helps you understand where your visits are coming from and how often they occur, all presented in a visual graph format.
    • Monitor Total visits to track your overall traffic engagement, or filter by Public visits to measure the effectiveness of your promotions in reaching potential new members
    • Break traffic down by Source: Patreon, social platforms, direct links, and more
    • Data is displayed in GMT/UTC
  • Note that Visitors are individual people checking out your page, while Visits are how many times they’ve landed on it—so one person might have multiple visits.
  • To understand each term and definition in more depth, visit our dedicated article on Traffic Insights.
  • Surveys help you collect feedback from members at two key moments: when they join and when they cancel.
    • Welcome surveys ask new or upgrading paid members what they’re most looking forward to, with an optional free-form follow-up. They’re on by default, and you can turn them off from the survey insights tab
    • Exit surveys capture why someone canceled and live separately in your settings. All results are anonymous
  • Note that free members and anyone rejoining your Patreon won’t see the welcome survey.
  • Explore both Welcome and Exit surveys in our dedicated article on Survey Insights.

Managing members with custom pledges

What is a custom pledge?

A custom pledge is a membership amount that isn’t tied to one of a creator’s tiers. Some members pay a custom amount because they want to give more than their tier price; in other cases a member is paying a creator who doesn’t have paid tiers set up. New members can’t choose a custom amount when they join through a tier.

Existing members who want to change their pledge amount can do so from their active membership settings — see Editing your Membership.

What happens when a member has a custom pledge?

A member who joins with a custom pledge isn’t assigned to a tier, so no rewards are attached. Likewise, a member who edits their pledge to an amount higher than their tier price isn’t automatically moved into the nearest tier.

Why is $1 the minimum?

Some members want to pay a creator but the tier minimums are outside their budget. The “no tier” custom pledge lets them still take part even when they can’t join a tier. As the name suggests, there are no benefits or tiers attached to a custom pledge, regardless of the amount given. $1 is the minimum so the pledge still covers processing fees.

Post access for custom pledge members

Custom pledge (“no reward”) members only have access to posts you publish for Paid members only or All members.

For example, a member with a $2 custom pledge who isn’t in a $2 tier won’t have access to that tier’s post content — only to posts published for Paid members only or All members.

If a member would like to move to the correct tier, share this guide: I’m locked out of posts I should see.

Note: If you’d like a post locked to members paying you outside of your tiers, publish it for Selected tiers so you can choose exactly which tiers get access.

How to find your “no reward” or custom pledge members

Members who pay you with a custom pledge aren’t tied to a specific tier (if you’ve created tiers). They appear with the No tier status in your Relationship Manager, because their payment isn’t connected to a tier’s benefits. Since they aren’t part of a tier, they aren’t tracked for benefits and won’t get tier-specific benefits like Discord roles.

How to filter no-reward pledges

Use your Relationship Manager filters to generate a list of your active no-reward members. Set these filters:

  • Active membership type
  • No reward
  • Any time period you’d like

FAQ

  • No — there’s currently no way to increase, decrease, or remove the $1 minimum. It lets members take part even when they can’t join a higher-priced tier or are fine without a reward.
  • No — creators can’t move members into tiers, mainly because it can affect a member’s billing.
  • If a member isn’t in a tier and wants to be, share this guide: I’m locked out of posts I should see.

Membership Insights

In a one-time update, members who have been in a failed payment state since Jan 2024 will become free members. In addition, members in a failed payment state between Dec 2025 and Jan 2026 will also be counted as paid canceled members. This means you may see a one-time increase in free and paid canceled members, which will be reflected in both Membership Insights and Relationship Manager.

Note: Members in a failed payment state prior to Jan 2024 will become canceled members. However, this will only be updated in Relationship Manager, not Membership Insights.

For additional information, please see the How failed payments are reflected in Insights section below.

The Membership Insights dashboard helps you track and analyze key membership trends, including active members, new members, and cancellations. Use it to monitor your community’s growth, understand payment behaviors, and evaluate what’s driving memberships.

Navigating Membership Insights

When you first access the Membership Insights dashboard, it defaults to the past 30 days with a daily trend line, giving you an overview of recent activity. You can customize your view using various filters to focus on specific trends, timeframes, and member behaviors.

Understanding Membership Views

Your Membership dashboard is divided into three main views, each helping you analyze different aspects of your membership:

  • Active Members: All members who currently have access to your Patreon within the selected timeframe. This includes free members, members with an active payment, members with a retrying payment, free trial members, gifted members, and members who have canceled but whose access hasn’t expired yet
  • New Members: Tracks all new members, both free and paid, who joined your page for the first time, as well as former members who rejoined after canceling
  • Canceled Members: Includes free and paid members who have left your membership. Free members are canceled immediately when they leave. For paid members, the cancellation is recorded on the date their access expires, not the date they cancel

Since a large number of members are billed on the 1st of the month, you may notice a corresponding spike in cancellations around that date, as this is when members lose access and the cancellation is recorded.

Looking for a breakdown of just your paid members? See our guide on How do I find my paid member count?

Customizing Membership Insights

Each membership view can be filtered to help you analyze trends more effectively:

  • Date Range: From the dropdown menu at the top-left, you can select to view data for the Past 30 days, 6 months, 12 months, All time, or a Custom range
  • Daily or Monthly view: Use the dropdown menu across the view name to select from Daily or Monthly options to monitor day-to-day changes or identify broader monthly trends
  • Overall: See a summary of your entire membership, with the option to filter by Free vs. Paid members
  • Membership tier: Get a detailed breakdown of how specific membership tiers are performing
  • Billing cadence: Filter by billing cycle to see whether members are subscribed monthly or annually, helping you understand payment preferences
  • Paid status: See members according to their payment status, such as paid, trials, gifted, or retrying payments

You can also hover over points on the graphs to view detailed insights for specific timeframes. The data card updates based on your selected view (e.g., daily, monthly), making it easy to analyze trends at a glance.

The data on your Membership dashboard updates every 4 hours.

To explore your other dashboards, see our main guide on Insights dashboards.

How failed payments are reflected in Insights

Now, members whose payment retries repeatedly fail for ~30 days will become free members. This way, you’ll be able to stay connected with them while also opening up space in limited-spot tiers (if applicable). We will continue to show the member as Active in Insights for the time we are retrying the payment. If they become a free member, they’ll also show up as a paid canceled member.

Understanding Member Payment Statuses

In the Paid status filter, you’ll find a streamlined overview of your members by their payment behavior. Understanding these statuses helps you manage your community, proactively address payment issues, and analyze your page’s health and growth.

Find below the definitions for each status:

  • Paid: The member has paid or is scheduled to be billed. Active members have access to membership benefits and are eligible to receive them
  • Trial: Member redeemed an offer for a 7-day trial for one of your tiers. For guidance about how it works, visit our Free Trials FAQ
  • Gifted by others: Members who redeemed a gift from another fan and are actively in their gifted membership period
  • Gifted by you: Members who redeemed a gift created by you and are actively in their gifted membership period
  • Retrying payment: The member’s most recent charge attempt declined, and we are currently retrying the payment. During this period, the member’s paid access is revoked. A member with a failed payment for ~30 days will be converted to a free membership
  • Payment failed: The member’s payment was not successful after ~30 days of retries. They are converted to a free member and will appear as a paid canceled member in your insights.

You can also find a detailed breakdown of your members by paid status, including active payments, retrying payments, free trials, and gifted memberships, in your Relationship Manager.

Monitor Upgrades & Downgrades

The Upgrades & Downgrades section, in the Active Members view, helps you track membership changes across tiers. This data provides insights into how members adjust their subscriptions, whether by upgrading to higher-value tiers or downgrading to lower ones.

  • Upgrades to tier: Shows the number of members who moved to a higher-value tier. The left-hand column displays the tier members upgraded to, and the right-hand column shows how many members made this move
  • Downgrades from tier: Shows the number of members who moved to a lower-value tier. The left-hand column displays the tier members downgraded from, and the right-hand column shows how many members made this move

Analyze Your Growth

Understanding how new members are joining your community is key to growing your membership. By navigating to the New members view, you can track where your audience is coming from, how they are converting to paid members, and what’s driving memberships, helping you refine your strategy and attract more members.

Learn How Fans Are Becoming Paid Members

The Path to Paid filter in the New members view helps you track how fans and free members become paying members. It brings together all your growth insights in one place, so you can see what’s driving conversions and optimize your strategy.

In this section, you can also use the filters to get more granularity on how your fans are becoming paid members:

  • Direct to Paid: Fans who joined your page with a paid membership
  • Free to Paid: Fans who started as free members before upgrading to a paid membership
Popular Posts

This section highlights your top-performing posts, specifically posts where fans clicked to become members. The report shows your top posts on the left and how many fans initiated their membership on these posts.

You can filter the data to focus on either new paid members or new free members, giving you a better understanding of what content resonates most with your audience. By analyzing these trends, you can refine your content strategy to attract more members.

Free Trial Conversions

If you offer free trials, this section provides insights into how members engage with them. You can track how many people started a free trial, how many completed it, and how many canceled before it ended.

Additionally, it shows how many trial users converted into paying members and calculates your trial conversion rate. This data can help you evaluate the effectiveness of your trial offering and optimize it to encourage more conversions.

Free trial members are included in your Active member count for the duration of their trial period.

FAQ

  • As part of a one-time update, members who have been in a failed payment state between January 2024 and January 2026 have been converted to free members as of March 2026. This may appear as a one-time increase in your free member count.
  • Members whose payment retries fail for ~30 days are converted to free members and also appear as paid canceled members in your insights. If you’re seeing a one-time spike, this may be related to the update on how failed payments are represented. Please see the How Failed Payments Are Reflected in Insights section above.
  • A large number of members are billed on the 1st of the month. Cancellations are recorded on the date a member’s access expires — not when they click cancel — so you’ll naturally see more cancellations logged around that date.
  • The definition of active members now includes free trial members, members with a retrying payment, gifted members, members with an active payment, and members who have canceled but whose access hasn’t expired yet. This may result in a higher active member count than you previously saw.

Relationship manager billing statuses

The table below lists member statuses in your Relationship manager and a brief definition of each:

Status

Definition

Active payment

The member has paid or is scheduled to be billed. Active paid members have membership access. To confirm whether a member is eligible for benefit delivery for a specific month, use the Benefit tab.

Retrying payment

The member’s most recent charge attempt declined, and we are currently retrying the payment. During this period, the member’s access is revoked. If the payment is successfully processed, access is restored.

Payment failed

After retrying a declined payment, the charge still failed. We’ll make a new attempt, or the member can do it directly. We’ve crafted a Failed payment help guide that you can send to members to support them through retrying their payment. A member with a failed payment for ~30 days will be converted to a free membership.

Canceled

The member has deleted their subscription. Their membership access remains active until their current billing period ends. They will appear as Canceled in your Relationship Manager from the date their access expires, not the date they cancelled. We will not create new bills for their membership with you.

Refunded

The most recent charge was refunded. Please note that members must also cancel their membership to avoid auto-renewal.

Fraud

The most recent charge was deemed fraudulent, and their payment has been declined. If a charge is potentially fraudulent, we will not automatically retry the payment. While a member’s payment is marked as fraud, they will not have access to your member-only content. There are many reasons why this might occur. You can let your members know to contact their bank, then our Support team, to clear this up.

Gifted by others

Members who redeemed a gift from another fan and are actively in their gifted membership period.

Gifted by you

Members who redeemed a gift created by you and are actively in their gifted membership period.

Shop Insights

Available for creators selling digital products with Commerce, your shop insights give you valuable data about overall product sales and which products are selling best. In this article, we’ll take you through ways to analyze your product sales and answer common questions you may have about your shop earnings.

Analyzing your product sales

To get to your shop insights, click the Insights link from your left navigation and click on the Shop tab. You can review shop insights for the past 30 days, past 6 months, past year, and all time. Here, you can see your earnings for each product and identify your top-selling items.

Creators in the early access group can also use a currency filter to view their results in their current currency or any previously used currencies. This feature is still rolling out, so some creators may not have access yet.

On your Shop tab, you can also check your earnings from the products and collections you sell. For more information, visit our Selling Posts and Collections article.

Your shop insights include:

  • Total Earnings: earnings from your product sales specifically
  • Total Sales: number of products sold
  • Top-selling products: a list of top-selling products with earnings from product sales
    • Be aware that only active products will show up in the list. Any unpublished or deleted product will not appear in this section.

Click the Export data link at the bottom of the shop page to get a CSV file of your shop data to further analyze with any tool you’d like.

To explore your other dashboards, see our main guide on Insights dashboards.

Shop earnings

The earnings tab of your insights can be filtered by all earnings, membership earnings (if you offer paid membership), and shop earnings. The earnings graph displays earnings on a monthly basis, and the detailed table below the graph shows a monthly breakdown of the total processed amount and your earnings once refunds, fees, and taxes are deducted.

Click on the Export data link at the bottom of the earnings page for a CSV download of your earnings. the CSV will further break down how fees were applied, including currency conversion fees, platform fees, and any other applicable taxes.

You can learn more about fees that may be applied to your product sales transactions in our Commerce fees article.

Sales insights

You can review purchaser history from the Sales tab of your Audience page. You’ll be able to view and export a CSV with essential information about each sale, including:

  • The product purchased
  • The date purchased
  • Status (complete vs. refunded)
  • Total amount paid

Visit our guide on Managing customers to learn more about Sales insights.
