Communicating the change to your members

Before you resume billing, we recommend creating a post for all paid members so everyone with an active membership sees it. Here’s a template you can customize:

We wanted to let all of our members know about a change to how memberships are billed on Patreon. We’ve switched from “per creation” to “monthly” billing, effective [date]. This means that every month you’ll have a consistent price for all of the benefits we provide, and it won’t change based on the number of paid posts that month.

Your membership was converted from a “per creation” amount to a “monthly” amount. You’ll stay on the same tier and receive the same benefits. Here are the new monthly tier prices:

  • Tier 1 – XX per month
  • Tier 2 – XX per month
  • Tier 3 – XX per month

If you set a monthly maximum for the number of posts you pay for, you won’t pay more than that amount, even if it’s lower than the new tier price.

If you’d like to change your membership, you can change your tier or increase your payment amount.

Thanks for your understanding, and please reach out if you have any questions.

How to adjust your benefit delivery for subscription billing

With per-creation billing, members pay each time you publish a paid post. With subscription billing, members pay a set monthly price instead. Existing members are charged on the 1st, and new members are charged on the date they join. If you deliver benefits beyond your posts, such as downloads, physical items, or Discord access, you can adjust how you deliver them:

  • Monthly delivery: After the month ends, select that month in the Benefit Eligibility Status tool and download the list of members who paid. Deliver benefits to everyone on the list in the first few days of the following month.
  • Batch delivery: Deliver benefits on a set cadence, such as every Sunday or twice a month. Use the Benefit Eligibility Status tool to see which members have paid so far this month, and sort by Last charge date to find members who paid since your last delivery.

To find the tool, select Creator studio, click Audience, then go to the Benefits tab. For full instructions, see Track your members’ benefit eligibility status.

Control how Apple’s fee is applied to your prices

Switching to subscription billing does not necessarily mean all fans will be required to use in-app purchases. Currently, iOS users in the U.S. can continue to sign up through Patreon’s mobile web checkout, which is not subject to Apple’s App Store fee.

For those fans who do choose to purchase via Apple’s in-app system, creators can choose to:

  • Increase the prices of the memberships and digital goods sold in the iOS app. This will help creators earn the same across platforms in spite of the Apple fee and is the default option
  • Keep prices the same across all platforms. This means that the creator absorbs the Apple App Store fee themselves and therefore earns less from sales in the iOS app

You can switch from the default setting that increases the prices of membership and digital goods sold in the iOS app by visiting your Billing and payouts settings.

Visit our How iOS in-app purchases work on Patreon page to learn more about our approach to the Apple App Store fee requirement.

How to pause billing for your members

All creators are now using subscription billing. If your account was still on a legacy billing model on November 1, 2026, we switched it automatically and emailed you when the switch was complete.

Key details depending on your previous billing model:

  • Per-creation: If you haven’t resumed billing yet, it stays paused until you review your new tier prices. Learn how to resume billing
  • First-of-the-month: Your existing members are still billed on the 1st of each month. New members are billed on the date they join

This article is intended for creators who offer paid tiers. Whether you’re taking a well-deserved break or have had an unexpected delay in delivering benefits, you can put a pause on billing your members for a month at a time. Keep reading to learn more about how to pause and what your paid members can expect.

How do I pause membership billing?

  • While logged in, click on Your account from the left navigation, then select Settings
  • Select Billing and payouts
  • Click the Pause billing button
  • Click the Confirm button to pause the current billing cycle

We’ll display a yellow banner on your account settings page, letting you know that we have paused your billing. A similar message will let members know that they won’t get billed.

Enjoy your break — when you’re ready to come back, we’ll be here!

Considerations for pausing membership billing

  • On Subscription Billing:
    • New members who join while your page is paused will be charged upfront. This allows creators to continue earning from new members during a billing pause while granting them immediate access to posts, work, and community. Please note that members will not have their membership extended. Their billing cycle will resume once you reactivate billing
      • Example: If you pause billing in December, new members who join during that month will still be charged upfront and gain full access to your content
    • New members are only charged when they first join. They won’t be charged again unless billing is resumed. The pause only stops renewals for existing members
  • Impact on billing dates and charges:
    • Pausing billing prevents members from being charged but does not change their billing date
    • Once a billing cycle has been paused, you cannot retroactively charge members for any paused period
  • For Creators with Digital Shops (Commerce):
    • Pausing membership billing does not affect your Shop. Customers can still access and purchase digital products
  • Member Access During a Pause:
    • Members retain access to your Patreon and all posts while billing is paused. Your Patreon remains live, but existing paid members aren’t billed while billing is paused. Memberships aren’t extended: members resume billing once the pause ends.
  • Pausing Multiple Months:
    • To pause multiple consecutive months, you’ll need to log in after the current pause month ends and request to pause again
    • For subscription billing creators, this depends on your pause date. Example: If you pause on March 10, you’ll need to log in after April 10 to pause again
    • For monthly billing, you can log in after the pause ends (after the 1st of the next month) to request another pause
  • Resuming Billing:
    • You can choose to resume billing at any time before your pause month ends

How do I resume membership billing?

Existing members will not be charged for 1 month starting from the day you pause. Billing automatically resumes on or around the same calendar day the following month (for example, if you pause on July 5, billing resumes on August 5). Memberships aren’t extended during the pause.

  • While logged in, click on Your account in the left navigation and select Settings
  • Select Billing and payouts
  • Click the Resume (this month) billing button
  • Click the Confirm button

We recommend letting members know that you’ll be pausing billing for one month. You can do this with a post or by sending a bulk direct message through your Relationship manager.

FAQ

  • Your billing stays paused until you review your new tier prices and resume billing. It doesn’t resume automatically after one month. Follow the steps in How to move from per-creation to subscription billing.
  • If you resume billing before your scheduled pause end date, there’s a chance that billing for some members may still be skipped. This edge case may apply to members who joined using iOS in-app purchases.
  • Here’s how it works:
    • Three days before a member’s billing date, we notify Apple to pause the upcoming payment
    • If you resume billing (unpause) within this three-day window, Apple cannot reverse the pause request, and the member’s payment will still be skipped
    • This edge case may result in billing still being skipped for members whose billing dates falls within the three days following the date you resume billing early
  • Example Scenario:
    • You pause billing on October 15, with the pause set to end on November 15
    • On November 5, you decide to resume billing early
    • For a member whose billing date is November 6 and who signed up with iOS in-app purchases, their next payment will be skipped. Their billing will resume on December 6 instead
  • To avoid skipped payments for members who signed up with iOS in-app purchases, we recommend letting the pause expire naturally or planning your unpause date to avoid overlap with the three-day pre-billing window.
  • For additional questions or concerns, feel free to reach out to Patreon Product Support.
  • We won’t process payments for existing paid members when you pause your membership billing.
  • If you are on the subscription billing model, new members who join while your page is paused will still be charged upfront, giving them immediate access to your content. However, they won’t be charged again until billing resumes. You can learn more about this in the Subscription billing FAQ.
  • For the charge-upfront billing model, new members will also pay when they join for access to your catalog of work, and members upgrading their membership will be charged immediately to unlock upgraded benefits.
  • If you’d like to prevent any earnings or membership changes from happening while you’re paused, you can also set a cap on the number of members you’ll allow in each tier and set the limit to the current member count in each tier. Alternatively, you can unpublish your tiers until you’re ready to accept new members in that tier again. While prospective members could still join with the “No tier/Custom” option, you won’t be obligated to fulfill benefits related to your tiers.
  • Here’s how to unpublish a tier:
    • Navigate to your Membership tiers page, and click the Edit button for the tier you’d like to unpublish
    • Scroll to the bottom and click the Show more tier options “…” button
    • Click the Unpublish tier button. Your tier will still be editable, but it won’t populate on your page for fans to choose from
  • Patreon’s pausing feature allows you to skip 1 billing cycle. You can continue to enable our pause feature; however, you’ll need to log in each month to re-enable it.
  • Once you’ve paused billing, we’re unable to charge your members retroactively.
  • If you are taking an indefinite break, you have 2 options:
    • You can pause billing one cycle at a time and return after each cycle to pause again
    • You can also unpublish your creator page if you want to stop accepting new members and make your page unavailable to the public
  • Important: If you unpublish your creator page and later republish it, you’ll be subject to Patreon’s current pricing at the time you republish.
  • Learn more about publishing your page here: Unpublish my creator page
  • Starting from the day you pause your membership billing, existing paid members will not be charged for one month. Billing will automatically resume on/around the same calendar day the following month.
  • Billing pauses will only prevent members from being charged. Charge dates are not affected by pausing. When the pause ends, members’ normal billing schedule resumes.
  • When new members join while your page is paused, they’ll be charged upfront for immediate access to your content. They won’t be charged again until billing resumes.
  • If you resume billing within a month of when you paused, you won’t be able to go back and charge members whose billing date was skipped while you were paused.
  • Fans who redeem a gift link you created before pausing billing will continue to have access until the end of their gifted term. However, while your membership is paused, you cannot generate new gift links.
  • On the Subscription Billing model, pausing billing does not affect annual memberships — their renewal date stays the same.
  • Example: Say a member has an annual subscription set to end on November 1st, 2025. If you pause your billing cycle in August 2025, their membership will still end on November 1st, 2025
  • Yes! You can still post content even if you’ve paused billing. Members can still access your page and posts during a paused billing cycle. Additionally, you and your members can still interact via comments and direct messages.

Patreon’s supported currencies

Our mission is to get creators paid – and when we say creators, we mean the global community of creators, no matter where you are located. As a creator on Patreon, you can choose your payout to be in your preferred currency, and your patrons can also choose to pledge in their own local currency.

Your tier prices are converted based on Patreon’s Price Book, in which we use current and historical exchange rates to arrive at an average exchange rate for each currency. For more detailed information, you can read through our guide on currency conversion.

Patrons can select their local currency during checkout or they can change their currency for existing pledges in Manage memberships. For detailed steps on how your patrons can do this, you can visit this guide on selecting local payment currency.

Patrons can choose to pay in any of our supported currencies listed above; however, all pricing will be based on your selected currency. If your patron is paying you in a different currency, a 2.5% conversion fee is applied.

  • Example: Your payout currency is € and a patron pays you in $, a 2.5% conversion fee will be applied.

You can message patrons to switch their billing currency to your payout currency to avoid this conversion fee. Review our suggested messaging for asking patrons to switch to your currency.

Note: For creators with Founder’s status, when changing currencies you are moving from the variable Founder’s processing fees to the associated payment processing fees related to your new currency choice. This change can not be reversed. Your platform fee stays the same at 5%.

Setting my creator currency FAQ

To support Patreon’s global community, we offer payments in different currencies. There are two places where you can choose one of Patreon’s supported currencies as your currency:

  • When you start your creator page. During the page creation process, you’ll be prompted to choose your currency
  • After you’ve launched your page. You can change currencies once every 31 days from your Creator settings

Choosing a currency that aligns with your location or your member base can help reduce fees.

  • If we support the member’s currency, your tier prices are converted from your currency into their currency. They won’t experience any additional foreign transaction fees.
  • If a member’s bank operates in a currency that we don’t currently support, their processing currency will default to USD. As they are paying in a currency different from that of their local bank account, their bank may charge them an additional foreign transaction fee.
  • When you set the price of your tiers, you’ll have the opportunity to preview your tier prices in other currencies we support from the tier editor.
  • There are several reasons why you may want to bill in a currency other than USD. For example, if you reside outside the U.S., you may prefer to receive your earnings in your local currency. Or, if a large portion of your member base uses a supported local currency, switching can help minimize conversion-related fees. Paying out in your local currency also results in the lowest payout fees and avoids the need for conversion fees upon payout to your bank.
  • Keep in mind: there is a 2.5% processing fee on member payments made in a currency different from your payout currency. Choosing a currency that aligns with your member base may help reduce overall fees.
  • If you’re an international creator receiving payouts in USD, you have two direct payout options available to you alongside PayPal and Payoneer:
    • Cross currency bank transfer – $0.25 flat fee + 1.55% currency conversion fee (this is inclusive of any currency conversion fees). Eligible countries can payout from USD in Patreon directly to their local currency
    • USD to USD bank transfer – $0.50 flat fee. As an international creator, you can set up and pay out to a US bank account at any time via a USD to USD local ACH transfer. Just be sure to select the United States as your bank country.
  • You can find these options in your Billing & payouts settings.
  • Yes — but your page must have been published at least once.
  • If your page is still in draft mode and has never been published, you won’t be able to change your billing currency after selecting it during page creation.
  • Once your page has been published at least once — even if you later unpublish it — you can change your currency once every 31 days by following these steps:
    • On Desktop, click on Your account from the bottom left corner and then select Settings
    • In the Creator settings section, select Billing and payouts
    • Under Your currency, click on the Change currency button to start the change process
    • Follow the prompts step-by-step to change your currency
  • Note: To change your currency, your available balance must be $0. If you have an available balance, you’ll need to withdraw it before starting the currency change process. Pending balances (like iOS payments) won’t prevent the switch and will be converted into your new currency once they clear.
  • Members can choose one of our supported currencies as their default processing currency. We’ll display your tiers at a converted price for their currency, based on your currency.
  • To learn more about how we convert your tier prices visit our help center article: How tiers are converted into other currencies
  • What this would mean for you:
    • To continue receiving payouts after changing your currency, you’ll need to re-add your payout method
    • By changing your payout currency, you’ll be subject to the associated payment processing fees related to the new currency choice
    • When receiving a pledge in a different currency than your payout currency, Patreon charges you a 2.5% currency conversion fee. This fee applies to both new and existing members
    • If you’re a creator with Founders status, switching currencies may remove your access to Founders payment processing fees. Your platform fee will remain unchanged
  • What this would mean for your members:
    • This will not affect your existing members
    • Anyone new to your page will see prices in their local currency when supported. If not, your selected currency will be shown instead
    • While you update your currency, anyone trying to join will see a maintenance message and be asked to try again in 15 minutes. The process will time out after 1 hour if not completed

Subscription Billing FAQ

All creators are now using subscription billing. If your account was still on a legacy billing model on November 1, 2026, we switched it automatically and emailed you when the switch was complete.

Key details depending on your previous billing model:

  • Per-creation: If you haven’t resumed billing yet, it stays paused until you review your new tier prices. Learn how to resume billing
  • First-of-the-month: Your existing members are still billed on the 1st of each month. New members are billed on the date they join

How subscription billing works

Subscription billing is the billing model used by all creators on Patreon.

With subscription billing, new paid members are charged when they join and then monthly on the same date (e.g., a member who joins on April 12 is charged again on May 12). At checkout and in their Memberships tab, members can see their next charge date.

Members who joined before your account switched

If your account switched from a different billing model, here’s how members who joined before the switch are billed:

  • Previously first-of-the-month billing (charge upfront or non-charge upfront): they’re still charged on the 1st of each month
  • Previously per-creation billing: they pay a set monthly price on the 1st of each month, up to any monthly limit they set

Your payout schedule doesn’t change. You can receive an automatic payout on the 5th or manually withdraw funds anytime.

When are funds from subscription billing payments available?

Funds become available as soon as they are settled. Most creators choose automatic payouts on the fifth of each month, but you can also manually withdraw a lump sum whenever you prefer.

The key difference between subscription billing and first-of-the-month billing is how your account balance accumulates—steadily throughout the month or as a larger amount at the start. However, the total accumulation remains the same if payouts are made at the same time each month.

You can request payouts as often as every 24 hours, but note that we may limit the number of monthly payouts if payout costs or patterns change significantly in the future.
