Member Experience FAQ

  • New members will see clear messaging at checkout, letting them know their next payment will be the following month on the same date, just as they expect from other recurring subscriptions. Their Billing History will also reflect their specific billing date. They can see their next charge date and amount under Settings in their Memberships tab.
  • Existing members won’t be billed any differently than they are now.
  • If you used per-creation billing, your existing members moved to a set monthly price, so let them know before you resume billing. For first-of-the-month, they’ll continue to be billed in the beginning of every month. See our suggested messaging template.
  • The member’s bill will be renewed on the last available date of next month, and that date will be the monthly billing date going forward. Someone who joins on January 30 will renew on February 28 and then on the 28th of each month after that. Members can view their next charge date in their Memberships tab at any time. This renewal date is also displayed for creators in Relationship Manager under Next Charge Date.
  • New members on an annual membership will renew the following year on their New members on an annual membership renew the following year on their signup date. For example, a member who signs up on November 3, 2021, would renew on November 3, 2022. These members will still receive a reminder email before their membership renews.
  • If a member’s payment fails, their access to your exclusive content is immediately revoked while we retry the payment. Once their payment is successfully processed, they’ll regain access. Their billing date remains their join date, not the payment resolution date. If retries continue to fail for ~30 days, the member will be automatically converted to free membership. To help guide members through failed payments, you can share the Failed payment help article with them.
  • On subscription billing, every membership renews separately on the date the member signed up for that membership. This means members who subscribe to multiple creators throughout the month will be charged on the unique bill dates for those memberships throughout the month. If a member signs up for multiple memberships on the same day, those would all have the same monthly bill date and be charged in one transaction.
  • Over the past year, we tested a variety of billing models, including some that combined members’ bills to multiple creators. This current subscription billing model ensures creators are paid in full and upfront when a member signs up (which is important for content protection and benefit delivery), and provides a simple, familiar billing experience for members.
  • Additionally, members can see a clear view of what and when they’ll be charged for all memberships each month in their Memberships tab.
  • Upgrading or downgrading will not change a member’s billing date. As happens today, members who upgrade get charged the outstanding amount straight away and get access to the higher tier straight away for the remainder of their billing period. Downgrades will remain on the original tier until the next billing date.
  • Just like today, if a member cancels their membership and signs up again after their original access has ended, that member will be considered a new member. They will be charged at signup, and that date will be their renewal date going forward. For example, if a member joins and renews on the 17th of each month, cancels on November 15, and resubscribes on December 21, their new billing date will be the 21st going forward.
  • If a member cancels their membership and signs up again on the same tier before their original access has ended, their billing date remains their original join date. For example, if a member joins on September 17, cancels on October 8, and signs up again on October 15, they’ve already paid for their membership through October 17 and wouldn’t be charged again until then.
  • The process for refunding members doesn’t change. You can refund a member’s three most recent payments from the Relationship Manager, as long as you have an account balance to cover the refunded amount. You can only refund a charge within 90 days of the original processing date. For annual pledges, you can initiate a partial refund up to a specific day.
  • As happens today, members and customers earn merch after they complete a required number of consecutive payments to any tier that contains that merch item. If you add a merch item to a tier after a member has already joined, they earn a month towards an item for each month of membership they pay for after the item goes live.
  • For example, if you add a merch item to a tier on May 15th, an existing member with a billing date of the 20th would make their eligible payments on May 20th and June 20th, and earn the item with their third payment on July 20th. Learn more about Merch eligibility.
  • You can no longer create new Special Offers. Offers that were already running continue until their end date. To run an offer yourself, add the benefit to your tier and use the Benefit Eligibility Status tool to track who’s eligible. You can also try Gifting, Discounts, or a free trial.

Creator Experience FAQ

  • If you used per-creation billing: your billing was paused, and your tiers have new monthly prices. Review your new prices and resume billing when you’re ready. You can change your prices after you resume. Learn more.
  • If you used first-of-the-month billing: nothing changes for your existing members, who are still billed on the 1st. New members are billed on the date they join. Learn more.
  • The Relationship Manager will continue to be the source of truth for member information. To identify whether a member is on subscription billing, enable the custom column Next Charge Date in Relationship Manager. This column also appears in the CSV download. To see which members are eligible for benefits in a specific month, use the Benefits tab.
  • Member bills on subscription billing renew on UTC (the global payments processing standard) instead of PT, like the other monthly billing models. The dates displayed in Relationship Manager are in your local time zone, which may be ahead or behind UTC by up to one day.
  • Yes, you can continue using the API to deliver benefits as expected.
  • To see which members successfully paid during a specific month, use the Benefit Eligibility Status tool:
    • On desktop, select Creator studio in the left-side navigation menu
    • Click Audience from the creator navigation
    • Select the Benefits tab
    • Choose the tier and the month you want to review
  • Looking for the Benefit Tracker? Benefit Tracker is being retired and replaced by the new Benefit Eligibility Status tool. Check the guide on Track delivery with Benefits features for the former experience.
  • If you need a date range that doesn’t match a calendar month, you can use the Last Charge Date filter in your Relationship manager:
    • On Desktop, select Creator studio in the left-side navigation menu
    • Click on Audience from the sub-menu
    • You’ll land in your Relationship manager
    • Select the Filters button, and adjust the Last Charge Date time range
    • To export it, click the CSV button
  • Last Charge Date shows each member’s most recent charge only. Members who have renewed since the end of your date range won’t appear, so this works best for recent dates.
  • You can use the Last Charge Date filter in combination with other filters, such as Status, Join date, and Tiers, to communicate with specific groups of members.
  • If you offer Discord access as a benefit, you’ll still be able to do so as expected. The Patreon-Discord bot runs every day and will sync members who join or lose access any day of the month. Eventually, subscription billing will lead to access changes spread more evenly throughout the month. Combined with the architectural improvements we’re making to the integration (across all billing models), creators who use Discord will soon see more accurate syncing and surfacing of errors as they occur.
  • You can pause your membership in your Account Settings. Existing members will not be charged for one month starting from the day you pause. If new members join while your page is paused, they’ll be charged upfront for immediate access to your content, but they won’t be charged again until billing resumes.
  • Founding creators will still experience the same payment processing fees, with some reductions from shared members whose bills renew on the same date. In other words, if you have members who also sign up for other creators on the same date (and with the same payment method), all of those bills are processed in one transaction, and you split the payment processing fee with those creators.
  • If your new members subscribe to other founding creators on different days of the month, which may be more common with subscription billing, each membership will be processed as a separate transaction with its own processing fee.
  • Processing fees from shared members already being charged on the 1st of the month will still be split among that member’s creators who are on founder’s pricing. There is no change to your platform fee or fixed third-party payment processing rates. See more details on the founder’s plan pricing.
  • Use the Benefit Eligibility Status tool to see which members successfully paid during a specific month. You can filter by tier, message those members, or export the list as a CSV.
  • If you currently limit benefits to members who have paid by a certain date each month, one way to adapt is to deliver benefits to all members who are active at the time you’re processing benefits.
  • Another way is to deliver benefits at the start of each month to any member who has paid throughout the previous month. For example, if you typically mail a sticker on the 5th of each month to members who have paid by the 1st, you can mail the sticker on November 5 to all members who had a successful payment in October. On December 5, you can mail the November sticker to all members who had a successful payment in November. In the Benefit Eligibility Status tool, select the previous month to get this list.
  • If you deliver benefits on a fixed date that isn’t the start of the month, such as the 8th, you can use the Last Charge Date filter in your Relationship manager to get a custom date range. See “How will I know which members paid during a certain period of time?” above.
  • We know some creators have concerns about how switching billing models may impact the way they run their business. To hear directly from creators who’ve already made the switch, check out Creator stories on Patreon for Creators.

What are my members’ payment options?

To serve our global community, we have multiple payment methods available for members to pay creators. Below, you’ll find our current offerings and a summary of how each works:

Credit/Debit Card

Members can add their credit/debit cards to their account or during checkout. We process payment to the card on file. The funds are then sent to your creator balance.

We accept the following cards:

  • Visa
  • Master Card
  • Discover
  • JCB
  • Diners Club

If funds are not available on the card or the card has expired, the member’s payment will decline until they add a new payment method. A member with a payment decline for over 1 month will be switched to a Free membership.

PayPal

If your members have a PayPal account, they can add it to Patreon to pay you for membership. We process payment through the member’s PayPal wallet funding source. Then funds are sent to your creator balance.

If there is an issue with the PayPal funding source (i.e., the card on file has declined, or the bank blocks the charge), PayPal will decline the payment. The member can log in to their PayPal account or contact PayPal support to resolve. They can then retry their payment on Patreon.

Please note that beginning March 7, 2022, consumers in Thailand will no longer be able to use PayPal as a payment method as a result of new local regulations. Thailand-based consumers can update their payment method to Credit Card or Apple Pay.

Apple Pay

Members paying in US dollars can choose Apple Pay from an authorized device when they first join your page or if they edit their membership. With Apple Pay, the member asks Apple Pay to process payment with the wallet funding source they select. We submit payment through Apple Pay and send it to your creator balance.

Apple Pay is device-specific. If the card on file was added from a deactivated device, or there aren’t enough funds on the funding source, the member’s payment will decline. The member should resolve the issue with their Apple Pay account.

Our article on using Apple Pay offers more details for members with Apple Pay.

Venmo

US members can add their Venmo account through the Patreon app. This can be done during checkout or when they attempt to edit their existing memberships. Once Venmo is added via the app, members can use it as a payment method across all browsers and devices.

Similar to PayPal needing a funding source, members need a payment method attached to Venmo to make the payment go through successfully. Members cannot make a payment with the balance on their Venmo account.

If there is an issue with the Venmo funding source (i.e., the card on file has declined, or the bank blocks the charge), Venmo will decline the payment. The member can log in to their Venmo account or contact Venmo support to resolve the issue. They can then retry their payment on Patreon.

Why are my payments queued?

Payments are queued on the 1st prior to processing. If you ever have a question about our site status, check out our status page, status.patreon.com.

You’ll find that payments are queued at the start of the 1st of each month (Pacific Time - from San Francisco) and are processed throughout the day. Processing payments after queuing ensures that we can have a smoother payment day for creators and members.

Payment processing typically completes within 24 - 48 hours, so you’ll want to check your Relationship Manager at the end of the day to confirm the status of your members.

You may have noticed your payments began processing a bit later. Your pledges will be queued at the start of the day (PT) like always, but we’ll be making a change to when we process them so our team can be on-hand in case there are any issues. This means you may find your payouts arrive a bit later in the day than you’re used to.

Additionally, as Patreon grows, we have to process a much higher number of payments. The way we processed payments a few years ago might not be the most sustainable today or in the future. We’re committed to continually improving payment processing to make it faster and more reliable.

Moving the time we begin processing payments is the first step in improving this process.

What does it mean when my payments are queued?

It means that your members’ payments are in line to begin processing. Payment processing is usually completed within 24 - 48 hours.

How does payment queueing benefit me as a creator?

Queuing payments early and processing them over the course of a full day improves stability in our payment processing. After 24 - 48 hours, you can visit your Relationship manager and filter through your members to review their status and determine when to send out rewards.

Note: We regularly reattempt declined payments and email your members to alert them to their failed payments. Read more in our dedicated article about How to manage declined member payments. Please note that a member with a payment decline for over 1 month will be switched to a Free membership.

Why are there refunds I didn’t initiate?

Since Patreon only provides the platform for transactions between users, we don’t issue refunds on behalf of creators.

If a member wants to request a refund, they can request it through their Billing History within 60 days of the original payment. Note that per-creation charges can’t be refunded this way and must go through Patreon Product Support. Creators can issue refunds from their Refunds dashboard or Relationship Manager. Here’s our guide to refunding a member, if you need help with that.

Once a refund is issued, processing can take up to 10 business days.

Refunds I didn’t initiate are listed as “Refunded by Patreon”

There are instances in which a refund may be issued due to fraudulent activity or other circumstances, as determined at Patreon’s sole discretion. Under your member’s payment history, these are considered fraudulent refunds and will be listed as “Refunded by Patreon” in your Relationship Manager.

When a member is suspected of fraudulent activity, their account is disabled, and the funds from their pledges are returned to the cardholder if we do not hear back from them within 10 days of the notice.

Creators do have the option to submit an appeal. Appeals are typically responded to within 5 business days.

What is a failed refund?

A refund may fail if you attempt to refund a member without sufficient funds in your account balance. It can also occur if there was a technical error on our end. You’ll find these failed refunds listed as $0 in the Refunds CSV download. You can reattempt a failed refund at any time from your Relationship Manager.

Creators: Paying out your earnings

Account Identity Verification FAQ

We’ve introduced an identity verification process for your account to ensure the security and safety of the Patreon community, preventing fraud, abuse, and illegal activities on the platform. If you are invited to verify your identity, this article will guide you through what to expect, how to complete it, and why it matters for your page.

General

  • You’ll receive a notification from Patreon if you’re required to verify.
  • In most cases, verification is a one-time process. However, you may need to reverify if your information changes or if regulations require periodic updates.
  • We’re rolling this requirement out slowly. If you earn money on Patreon, you may be subject to Patreon’s account identity verification requirement.
  • No. This account verification is separate from the age verification process required for 18+ creators.
  • If you’ve already completed age verification as an 18+ creator, you’ll still need to complete account verification when prompted to continue receiving payouts.

Process and timeline

  • You’ll receive instructions via email. Please complete the “Account Verification” section in your settings page upon receiving the email notification.
  • You have 60 days from enrollment to complete your initial verification before your account is suspended. Enrollment immediately locks payouts.
  • If you don’t complete verification, your account will first be suspended, and you will not be able to make any new payments or receive payouts. After 30 days of suspension, it will be scheduled for deletion, and any eligible funds will be refunded.
  • After we process your information, your payouts will be released. Most requests are processed within a few minutes.
  • Yes, the form can be completed in languages other than English.
  • You can complete the verification flow on a web browser on your mobile device or a desktop device.
    • Enrollment: Payouts are locked, and you have 60 days to complete the verification process
    • After 60 days: Account is suspended — you can’t receive new subscriptions or payouts, but can still log in and verify
    • 30 days into suspension: Account is scheduled for permanent deletion (reversible for 28 days)
    • If not reversed: Account will be deleted and refunded — a total of 118 days from enrollment
  • If we’re unable to verify your account’s identity based on the details you provided, you’ll be asked to upload one or more of the following depending on whether you are an individual or business:
    • A photo of yourself
    • A government-issued photo ID
    • Documents that verify your business
  • Your payouts will remain temporarily frozen until verification is successfully completed.
  • If verification isn’t completed within 60 days of your initial enrollment date, your account will be suspended. You won’t be able to accept payments, gain new subscribers, or withdraw funds.

Privacy and data security

  • Patreon will collect your legal name, date of birth, an ID number (such as a social security number), and other details necessary to verify the identity of your account.
  • Information is collected in accordance with our Privacy Policy. Patreon partners with Persona, a trusted verification provider, to help verify your identity.
  • No, your verified name is used for internal compliance only and won’t be displayed on your profile.
  • If you delete your account, your data will be handled according to our Privacy Policy; you can permanently delete your account at any time by going to our Privacy Center.

Account and payments

  • Your ability to pay out will be frozen until account verification is complete. If verification isn’t done within 60 days of enrollment, your account will be suspended and you’ll be unable to accept new memberships or payout your earnings. Failing to verify within 30 days of suspension results in permanent deletion and a refund of the remaining funds.
  • After we process your information, your payouts will be released. Most requests are processed within a few minutes. You must manually request a payout after the information has been processed.
  • Enter the information of the individual in control on the financial settlement account.
  • You can update your information on your Patreon account if your details change. You may need to reverify if your information changes.

Regulatory and compliance

  • The account verification is separate from tax reporting, though both processes help Patreon comply with regulations and meet industry standards.
  • Payment providers verify identities for their own compliance. Patreon must also verify accounts to meet its own compliance obligations.
  • This is part of Patreon’s ongoing efforts to strengthen security, prevent fraud, and meet industry standards.

Adding your payout details

Beginning September 1, 2026, Payoneer will no longer support Belarus-based creators

This applies across all Payoneer programs: Payoneer Account (Wallet), Payoneer Card, and bank transfer (direct-to-bank). To keep receiving payouts through Payoneer, you’ll need to re-register with a country of residence and a bank account outside of Belarus.

If you use a Belarusian bank account, please update your payout details on your Billings and payouts settings page by following these steps:

  • Disconnect your Payoneer payout method
  • Reconnect with an applicable bank account in a different region (if available)
  • Or explore an alternative payout method (like Paypal/Hyperwallet)

If you have no alternative bank or decide not to switch to PayPal, we recommend paying out your existing balance before August 31, 2026.

This article will walk you through how to set up your payout method for the first time, what to expect if you need to make changes later, and the different payout options available. Depending on how you’ve set up currency and location, you may be able to receive payouts via direct deposit to a local bank account, PayPal, or Payoneer.

Setting up your payout details for the first time

  • On Desktop, click on Your account from the bottom-left corner and then select Settings
  • In the Creator settings section, click on the Billing and payouts
  • Scroll down to find the Payout method section, then click on Add payout method
  • Let us know:
    • Your payout country from the drop-down list
    • If you are a US creator or a non-US creator
    • If you’re an individual or a business/corporation
  • Once you have selected all the required information, click on Next
  • Let us know how you would like to be paid from the available options, and complete the payout method form
    • Your payout method options will depend on the payout country you select. Your bank, Payoneer, or PayPal account country location information must match the information you provide
  • Click the Save button, and you’re all set!

When you add a payout method for the first time or when you edit your payout method, an automatic 5-day payout lock is placed on your balance. After the 5-day payout lock period, you’ll be able to withdraw funds from your balance.

Changing your payout details

Once you’ve set up your payout method, you can return to your Billing and payouts settings at any time to make changes — whether that’s switching from PayPal or Payoneer to a local bank transfer, updating your payout country, or submitting new tax information.

Keep in mind: Any changes to your payout details — including updating your payout method, citizenship, or submitting a W-9 form — will trigger a 5-day payout lock. You’ll receive an email confirming the hold, including the exact date and time (in Pacific Time) when your funds will become available again.

Payout options

Mobile payouts are gradually rolling out on iOS, with Android coming soon. From the Profile tab, you’ll see a new payout section where you can initiate a withdrawal on the go.

You can withdraw all or part of your available balance at any time. The amount field defaults to your full available balance — you can leave it as-is or enter a specific amount. The minimum payout amount can vary depending on the method, currency, and country. You’ll see the payout fee and your estimated net amount before you confirm. Once initiated, payouts typically take 1–5 days to appear in your payout account.

  • We recommend using a checking account to transfer payouts. Using a non-standard bank account, such as a savings account or a virtual bank account, may increase the risk of payout failure.
  • To use Stripe direct deposit, you’ll need:
    • Your checking account number
    • Your routing number
  • If your payout to a standard checking account fails, call your bank to confirm that your account information (including your address) is up to date before reattempting.
  • If your payout to a non-standard account (savings or virtual) fails, update your payout method to a standard checking account. Once updated, Stripe will reattempt the payout immediately.
  • Creators outside the United States can receive payouts directly to their bank accounts.
Eligibility
  • Whether a bank transfer appears as a payout option depends on your selected currency and your bank’s country. These options are available to creators who reside outside the U.S. — see the full list of eligible countries here.
How to set it up:
- Go to your [Billing and payouts](https://www.patreon.com/settings-creator/payout) settings and click Add payout method
- Choose your payout country and confirm your payout currency
- Select your desired payout method and complete your bank details
- You’ll be redirected to Payoneer to provide additional information
  • Bank transfer is not the same as creating a Payoneer Wallet account — you do not need a Payoneer account to use direct bank transfer.
  • For details about fees, minimum payout amounts, and choosing the right option for you, visit our Payouts guide for creators outside of the U.S.
Important notes
- A 5-day payout lock applies after adding or changing this payout method
- Your information will be reviewed by Payoneer and may require additional details. You’ll be notified once your account is approved or if more information is needed
  • Payoneer doesn’t support Russia-based creators (as of December 16, 2022) or Belarus-based creators (beginning September 1, 2026). If this affects you, you’ll need a bank account outside these countries or an alternative payout method, like PayPal/Hyperwallet. See which countries are not supported in our Payoneer FAQs for full details.
  • Please check that you’re logged in to the PayPal account where you’d like to receive your payouts. This ensures that your funds are directed to the correct account.
  • If you choose to use PayPal, you will be prompted to log in to your PayPal account using our PayPal integration. You will need to enter your PayPal email and password to link your account.
  • If you have an issue with your PayPal account, please contact PayPal support to resolve it, then try logging in again. Creators located in Ukraine currently do not have the PayPal/Hyperwallet payout option available.
  • When you select Payoneer (for accounts outside the US only), you will be guided through setting up the account and linking it to your checking account. If you come across any issues with using Payoneer, please refer to this troubleshooting guide: Payoneer FAQs
  • Please note that you can only link one Payoneer account to your Patreon account.
  • Payoneer doesn’t support Russia-based creators (as of December 16, 2022) or Belarus-based creators (beginning September 1, 2026). If this affects you, you’ll need a bank account outside these countries or an alternative payout method, like PayPal/Hyperwallet. See which countries are not supported in our Payoneer FAQs for full details.

When can I payout?

Apple requires us to use iOS in-app purchases for digital goods and new memberships to keep the Patreon app available on the Apple App Store. We can’t expedite Apple’s processing timeline. Visit our How iOS in-app purchases work on Patreon page to learn more.

Funds from products purchased through Commerce on Web and Android will appear as pending for up to 7 days before they can be withdrawn from your balance. Funds from iOS in-app purchases remain pending for up to 75 days before they’re available for payout, as Apple requires that time to process and confirm them. Funds from membership payments may also appear as pending until they’re successfully processed. Once funds are no longer pending and appear as available to withdraw, you can pay out from your balance.

You’ll be able to pay out once every 24 hours. Once you initiate a payout, it typically takes 1-5 days for the funds to appear in your payout account. If we’re unable to send funds to your account for any reason, we typically return them to your creator balance.

Changing your payout currency

Are you considering changing your payout currency? Do you want to learn more about how changing currencies might impact your income and your members’ payment experience? Then this article is for you!

For a list of currencies currently supported on our platform, visit Patreon’s supported currencies.

Changing your payout currency: What to expect

Here’s a breakdown of what the change means for you and your members, along with key steps and requirements to keep in mind.

What this means for you
  • You can change your payout currency once every 31 days
  • Your available balance must be $0 to initiate the switch. (Pending balances — like iOS payments — won’t block it)
    • Example: Available Balance = $0, Pending Balance = $42 → You can switch
    • Example: Available Balance = $42, Pending Balance = $0 → You cannot switch
  • After changing your currency, you’ll need to re-add your payout method. This will trigger a 5-day payout lock, during which time payouts will be paused. Once the lock period ends, you’ll be able to withdraw your balance as usual
  • You’ll have the opportunity to adjust your tier prices during the currency switch. This change will only affect new members — existing members will continue paying their original tier price
  • You’ll be subject to payment processing fees specific to your new currency. View supported currencies and rates
  • If a pledge is made in a currency different from your payout currency, Patreon applies a 2.5% currency conversion fee. This applies to both new and existing members
    • If a creator in the UK changes their payout currency from USD to GBP, an existing US member will continue paying the same amount in USD — their pledge doesn’t change. However, the creator will be subject to the 2.5% currency conversion fee for receiving that pledge in a different currency.
  • If you’re a Founders creator, changing currencies may remove access to Founders-specific payment processing – however, your platform fee will stay the same
  • If you’re using Stripe and plan to switch to EUR or GBP, you’ll need to choose an alternative payout method. This can be PayPal, Payoneer, or — if available in your country — direct-to-bank payouts
  • If you use PayPal, ensure your account is set up to manage multiple currencies. Do this by following the instructions in this PayPal help article: How can I use PayPal to manage multiple currencies?
What this means for your members
  • Your existing members will not be affected — they’ll continue paying in their original currency
  • New visitors will see your tiers in their local currency if supported. If not, they’ll see your selected payout currency
  • If a member’s bank operates in a currency that we don’t currently support, their payment will default to USD. Because they’ll be paying in a different currency than their local bank account, their bank may charge them an additional foreign transaction fee
  • While you’re updating your payout currency, members who try to pledge will see a temporary maintenance message and will be asked to try again in 15 minutes.

Encourage local members to update their pledge to match your payout currency — this can help them avoid currency conversion or foreign transaction fees.

How changing your payout currency works

While changing your currency won’t take long, the process will time out after 1 hour if you haven’t completed the change. If you exit out at any point before completing the currency change, your changes will not be saved, and your currency will not be updated.

While you are making this change, anyone trying to pledge will receive a maintenance notification and will be asked to try again in 15 minutes.

  • On Desktop, click on Your account from the bottom left corner and then select Settings
  • In the Creator settings section, select Billing and payouts
  • Under Your currency, click on the Change currency button to start the change process. Make sure you have read through the key things to know before changing your currency
  • Your available balance must be zero before changing your payout currency. You may still have a pending balance — that won’t prevent the switch
  • After that, you can select your new currency. Note the payment processing rates of your newly chosen currency. We recommend reviewing payment processing rates for supported currencies before changing your currency
  • Next, confirm your tier prices. The tier prices shown are the same as your previous currency. If you’d like to, you can change your tier prices for new members — existing members will continue to pay the original price
  • Finally, click the Confirm and Save button to finalize the switch to our new currency
Refunding members after you change your payout currency

Once you change your payout currency, if you need to refund a member, this will be deducted from your balance in your new currency and refunded to the member in their choice of currency (if supported).

If you’d like guidance, read this article on how to refund a member.

Payout currency changes in your dashboards

Earnings dashboard

In the month that you change your payout currency, your balance will display as a stacked chart with both currencies reflected. We’ll display your monthly balance in your new payout currency from that point on. The data in the dashboard will update automatically every 4 hours.

Audience Relationship Manager

All surfaces in the Relationship Manager will be updated with your newly selected currency, except for the pledge amount, which will always be displayed in each member’s preferred currency. Each member’s Lifetime Value and the amount you receive are shown in your currency. Similarly, when you download your CSV report from Relationship Manager, this will show amounts in your payout currency.

FAQ

  • Patreon does not currently support holding multiple currency balances. In order to change currencies and start receiving payment in your local currency, your available balance must be zero.
  • You can change your payout currency even if you have a pending balance (for example, from iOS transactions). The only requirement is that your available balance is $0 at the time of switching.
    • Example 1: Available Balance = $0, Pending Balance = $42 → You can switch currencies
    • Example 2: Available Balance = $42, Pending Balance = $0 → You cannot switch currencies
  • You can change your payout currency once every month. So if you decide to switch again — including going back to your previous currency — you’ll just need to wait until a month has passed since your last change.
  • There are a couple of reasons why you might not be able to change currencies at the moment.
    • If you are a merch creator, changing currencies while using merch isn’t yet supported: this will be available soon.
    • It’s the first or last day of the month — your currency balance must be withdrawn and closed out before you can accrue earnings in a new currency. Therefore, you cannot change currencies on the first and last days of the month during payment processing.
    • We also retry declined payments on varying days throughout the month between 4 am and 10 am Pacific Time. If you find that you cannot change currencies, please try again after 10 am Pacific Time to make sure that the declined payment retries have been completed.
  • You can learn more about ordering a Payoneer card for your new currency here.
  • If you changed your currency, you’ll be able to review the Shop and Earnings Insights in each currency by using the dropdown menu.
  • Note: This feature is currently in early access, which means not all creators will see it yet. It will be gradually rolled out to all users.

How do I request a Proof of Income letter?

What is a Proof of Income letter?

A Proof of Income letter (also sometimes known as an Income Verification letter) is an automatically generated document on official Patreon letterhead that shows your creator earnings from the past number of months.

You can use this letter for things like:

  • Housing applications
  • Loan applications
  • Other financial processes that require income verification

The letter includes:

  • Your creator name
  • A summary of your total earnings on Patreon for the selected calendar year (excluding refunds)
  • Your estimated monthly earnings, which are based entirely on your earnings to date. (We think you can beat this!)
  • Patreon’s company details and official letterhead

How to request your Proof of Income letter

You can generate a Proof of Income letter instantly from your account. Here’s how:

  • From your creator page, go to your Payouts on the left-hand side
  • Select the Documents tab
  • Scroll to the Proof of Income section
  • Choose the year you’d like to generate a letter for
  • Click Proof of Income letter to download your document

You can generate a new letter anytime.

Example of a Proof of Income letter

Your letter will look like an official document on Patreon letterhead. It will display your creator name, earnings summary, and monthly average.

How payouts work

This article details how payouts work, when you can expect to receive a payout you’ve initiated, and what payout locks or holds you may encounter.

Setting up your payout details

Before you can withdraw your funds, you’ll need to add a payout method. On Desktop, click on Your account in the bottom left corner and then select Settings. In the Creator settings section, select Billing and payouts.

When you add or edit your payout method, a 5-day payout hold will automatically be placed on your balance. After the 5-day hold, you’ll be able to withdraw your balance normally.

If you are a brand-new creator on Patreon, please note that there will be a 5-day hold in place from the date of adding your first payout method or from the date of receiving your first payment.

Available payout options

Mobile payouts are gradually rolling out on iOS, with Android coming soon. From the Profile tab, you’ll see a new payout section where you can initiate a withdrawal on the go.

Depending on your payout country, you can choose from one of the following options:

  • Bank transfer (processed by Stripe) – available for creators based in the U.S
  • Bank transfer (processed by Payoneer) – available to creators who reside outside of the U.S — please see full country eligibility list here
  • PayPal
  • Payoneer Wallet – available only for international creators

For step-by-step setup and details about each payout method, visit our Adding your payout details guide.

If you’re an international creator, check our Payouts guide for creators outside of the U.S for more information about available payout methods, currencies, and supported countries.

Pending payments

Apple requires us to use iOS in-app purchases for digital goods and new memberships to keep the Patreon app available on the Apple App Store. The iOS in-app purchase system requires a 75-day pending period while Apple processes and confirms the funds. This timeline is managed by Apple and falls outside Patreon’s control. Funds from iOS in-app purchases will appear as pending in your account until Apple has settled the transaction. Visit our How iOS in-app purchases work on Patreon page to learn more about this change.

There are several situations when you can expect funds to appear as pending in your account:

Source

Hold Period

Details

Commerce (Web & Android)

Up to 7 days

Funds pending while payment is confirmed

Commerce (iOS in-app)

Up to 75 days

Apple’s processing timeline applies

Ticketed Live events

7 days after the event

iOS tickets: whichever is later

(7 days post-event or 75 days from purchase)

Here are the details for each situation:

  • One-time purchases: Funds from digital products purchased through Commerce on Web and Android will appear as pending for up to 7 days before they can be withdrawn from your balance. Funds from product sales made via iOS in-app purchases will remain pending for up to 75 days before they are available for payout, reflecting the time Apple requires to process and confirm the funds
  • Ticketed Live events: When fans purchase tickets to a Live event, those earnings are placed on hold until 7 days after the live event has completed. If a ticket was purchased through the iOS app, the standard 75-day iOS in-app purchase hold also applies, meaning iOS ticket earnings will be available at whichever date is later: 7 days after the event ends, or 75 days from the original purchase date. If an event is canceled, ticket purchases will be automatically refunded to fans and will not be paid out to the creator.

Once funds are successfully processed, they’ll appear as available to withdraw, and you can payout whenever you’d like, as long as there are no locks or holds on your payouts.

Payouts timeline

Once funds are no longer pending and appear as available to withdraw, you can pay out all or part of your available balance.

Once a payout is initiated, it typically takes 1-5 days for the funds to appear in your personal account. If, for any reason, we are unable to send funds to your account successfully, funds are typically returned to your creator balance.

If you find there’s a message stating that your transfer may take up to 10 business days, that is because our team is running a few checks on your account due to the volume you’ve processed. This is part of our effort to keep creators and members safe on our platform. Once those checks are complete, you’ll receive an email to let you know that your funds are on the way.

Currently, you’re only able to initiate a payout once every 24 hours.

Navigate to your Payouts dashboard to review your recent payout status. Each payout attempt will include a status. If you encounter an error, we’ll provide you with more information when possible.

Below are the status definitions for payout attempts:

Status

Definition

Complete

Payout arrived in your wallet and is available to use.

Sent

Payout was sent and arrival times may vary; or payment was sent to support other Patreon creators.

Pending

Payout is being processed and is on the way.

Returned

Payout didn’t go through. The funds will return to your Patreon balance.

Incomplete

There was an issue processing the payout. You may need to take action before it can be processed.

Automatic payouts

If you’d prefer to have one less item on your task list, you can also opt in to automatic payouts. When enabled, automatic payouts are initiated on the 5th of each month, as long as you have a positive balance, and send your full available balance. You can enable or disable automatic payouts from your Payouts page.

To withdraw a specific amount instead of your full balance, use a manual payout from your Payouts dashboard.

Payout fees

When you enter your withdrawal amount, you’ll see the applicable payout fee and the net amount you’ll receive before you confirm.

Funds in your Patreon balance already reflect the platform fee, payment processing fees, and any currency conversion fees.

When you transfer funds to your payout account, a payout transaction fee also applies.

Fees vary depending on your payout method, currency, and country of residence.

For the full breakdown of fees, including detailed tables by currency and payout type, please visit: Creator fees overview

Payout holds

A 5-day payout hold will be placed on your account in the following situations:

  • You add your payout method for the first time or update your payout information
  • You are a creator who is subject to receive a 1099-K without having filed out your W-9 form
    • Creators who are subject to receive a 1099-K will be required to submit a Form W-9. Once required, all payouts will be locked until Form W-9 is successfully submitted. To learn more, visit our guide on Will I receive a 1099-K form?

If you are under the 5-day payout hold, you’ll receive an email with more details, including the specific time that the payout lock will be released in Pacific Time (PT)

I need help with a payout

If you need any assistance with locating a payout or fixing an issue with a payout, please submit a request for one-on-one assistance. Be sure to select ‘Payouts and earnings’ from the dropdown so we can help you as quickly as possible.

Patreon billing time zones overview

To provide a more consistent and reliable experience for your members, Patreon billing follows global standards. This ensures members are always charged on the correct calendar day in their local time zone and makes billing more predictable worldwide.

How billing works

  • All charges (except on the 1st of the month) process at 12am UTC (5pm PT).
  • 1st-of-the-month billing processes at 12am PT (8am UTC) so US-based creators see their earnings update early in the day on the 1st
  • Billing always aligns with each member’s local time zone, ensuring they’re charged on the correct calendar date.

What this means for you

  • Your members are always billed on the correct payment day in their own time zone.
  • US creators will see their monthly earnings update early in the day on the 1st of the month
  • Your total earnings aren’t affected by timing shifts, only the time of day when charges are processed and appear in your account.
  • These updates around 1st-of-the-month timing were made in response to creator feedback that 1st-of-the-month earnings appeared too late in the day, which caused confusion and disrupted financial workflows.
  • Processing renewals earlier in the day helps you track payouts more predictably and makes your monthly Earnings Insights easier to follow.

FAQ

  • In July and August, all charges, including 1st-of-the-month charges, were processed at 12am UTC. This meant many US creators saw their earnings appear later in the day.
    • Some charges were processed on the evening of the last day of the month (after 5pm PT)
    • The rest were processed on the 1st of the month (after 5pm PT)
  • This split caused some of your usual 1st-of-the-month earnings to appear earlier or later than expected, and totals for July and August may look lower as a result. Rest assured, all members were still charged correctly on their billing dates in their own local time zones.
  • Starting September 1, 2025, 1st-of-the-month charges are processed at 12am PT (8am UTC). This ensures creators, especially those in the US, see their balance update earlier in the day. Your insights should now reflect your actual earnings more clearly and consistently.

Pausing billing for an extended period

In this article, we’ll go over how extended pause periods work. It’s limited to creators moving from per-creation billing to subscription billing, and it becomes available once they migrate to subscription billing. If that’s not your case, visit the How to pause billing for your members article.

When you pause billing, the options available depend on your eligibility. Most creators can pause for 1 month. Eligible creators who previously used per-creation billing can pause billing for longer than one more pause without an end date. This makes it easier to switch to subscription billing.

What’s the difference between a regular and an extended pause?

An extended pause offers more flexibility than a regular pause setting by letting you customize the duration of the pause period and control how new members are billed during the break.

Standard pause period

Under the standard pause period, billing pauses for 1 month and resumes automatically afterward unless you pause again for another month. During this time, new members are charged when they join. This feature is available for everyone on subscription billing.

Extended pause period

An extended pause period allows you to pause until a selected date or with no end date, resuming either on that date or when you manually resume it. You can extend or shorten an existing pause and choose whether to charge new members upon signing up during a pause. We limit access to pause billing for an extended period of time beyond 1 month to creators moving from per-creation to subscription billing to make the switch easier.

What remains the same for both regular and extended pause:

  • Your page stays published
  • Existing members retain access to paid content
  • Existing members aren’t charged while billing is paused
  • The pause applies to your entire page, not an individual tier
  • You can resume billing early

How to pause membership billing

  • While logged in, click on Your account from the left navigation, then select Settings
  • Select Billing and payouts
  • Click the Pause billing button
  • Choose how long the pause period should last:
    • For one month
    • Until a specific date
    • No end date
  • Once you select the desired period, click Continue
  • Then, decide if new members should be charged during the pause period or only when billing resumes, and click Continue
  • Confirm your pause period settings
  • If everything looks fine, click the Confirm button to pause the current billing cycle

We’ll display a yellow banner on your account settings page, letting you know that we’ve paused your billing. A similar message will let members know that they won’t get billed.

Enjoy your break — when you’re ready to come back, we’ll be here!

Should new members be charged during pause?

New members can still join and get access to your existing posts during the pause period. Choose whether new members pay when they join or wait until you resume billing.

Difference between the options

Option

What happens when someone joins

Best suited to

Charge new members when they join

The new member pays once when joining, receives immediate access, and isn’t charged again while billing remains paused.

Creators whose archive, community, or other existing benefits still provide meaningful value during the break.

Don’t charge new members until billing resumes

The new member adds a payment method and selects a paid tier but pays nothing when joining. They still receive immediate access and are first charged after billing resumes.

Creators who don’t want anyone paying while they aren’t actively publishing or delivering benefits.

New member treatment by membership type

Membership Type

Charge new members when they join

Don’t charge new members until billing resumes

Monthly membership

Pays once upon joining, gets immediate access, and isn’t charged again while billing remains paused.

Selects a tier and adds a payment method but pays nothing immediately. Gets immediate access and is first charged after billing resumes.

Annual membership

Pays the full annual price immediately and gets immediate access. Next annual charge is scheduled after accounting for the pause and paid term.

Joins and receives immediate access without paying upfront. First annual charge is scheduled after billing resumes on the original subscription date.

Existing members aren’t charged under either option. The selection only changes what happens to people who join after the pause begins.

iOS exception: New members who purchase through Apple’s in-app purchase system are charged when they join, even if you selected not to charge new members during your pause. The option not to charge new members until billing resumes applies only to web subscriptions.

What new fans see during a paused billing period

When new fans purchase a subscription membership during a paused billing period, the checkout screen informs them directly that recurring billing is currently paused. If they’re being charged upon joining, they receive access to the back catalog of content and see clear details regarding their initial payment and future billing schedule.

How annual memberships behave during a pause

Annual members keep access to your Patreon while billing is paused. If an annual membership is due to renew during your pause, the member won’t be charged on their original renewal date. We’ll extend their membership by the length of the pause, moving their next renewal date forward so they don’t lose any of the time they’ve already paid for.

Example: Fan signs up for annual membership on January 1, 2026. On April 1, 2026, you pause billing for 10 months. On January 1, 2027, there’s no charge, and billing resumes on February 1, 2027. Fan is billed for annual membership on November 1, 2027.

What happens when someone starts an annual membership during your pause depends on how you’ve chosen to handle new members.

If you charge new members when they join

They’ll pay the full annual membership price and receive access immediately. Their next annual charge won’t occur until after the pause and their paid membership term have been accounted for.

If you wait to charge new members

They can join and receive access without paying immediately. Their first annual payment will be scheduled after you resume billing on the date they subscribed to your membership.

How to edit a paused membership billing

  • While logged in, click on Your account from the left navigation, then select Settings
  • Select Billing and payouts
  • Click the Manage pause period button
  • Find the section you want to edit and select Change next to it — you can adjust:
    • Length of pause period
    • New member treatment
  • Once you’re satisfied with your adjustments, click Continue, followed by Confirm to save them

How to resume a pause

  • While logged in, click on Your account from the left navigation, then select Settings
  • Select Billing and payouts
  • Click the Manage pause period button
  • Select Resume billing
  • Check the information for resuming your pause
  • If everything’s all right, click Confirm and resume

When payments and earnings restart

When your pause ends or you choose to resume billing early, members aren’t necessarily charged immediately. If you pause billing for less than 2 months, billing resumes automatically on their next applicable billing dates. Otherwise, if you pause for 2 months or more, there’s a 14-day wait before we start billing fans again.

Because members may have different billing dates, your earnings may resume gradually rather than all at once. You’ll begin earning again as individual member payments process successfully.

Before billing restarts:

  • We’ll notify members about their upcoming charge
  • Members who joined during the pause and haven’t paid yet will be charged for the first time
  • Members who paid when they joined won’t be charged again until their next applicable billing date
  • Annual members will be charged on their adjusted renewal dates

Who can manage a billing pause?

Only the creator account owner can start, change, or end a billing pause. Other teammates, including team leads, can’t manage billing pauses. If you’re a teammate and need to make a change, contact the creator account owner.

What happens to memberships purchased through iOS?

New members can join through iOS while your billing is paused. We recommend that they use the web subscription option. Members can also purchase the membership through Apple’s in-app purchase system by selecting the smaller link below the main button.

Apple limits memberships purchased through iOS to 2 paused billing cycles per year. If an iOS membership exceeds that limit, Apple will cancel the membership.

When this happens:

  • The member moves to your free membership, if available
  • Their paid membership won’t automatically restart when you resume billing
  • They’ll need to rejoin a paid tier to gain paid access
  • You won’t receive future payments from that membership unless they rejoin

Before confirming an extended pause, review the warning about members who joined through the iOS app and may be affected.

Paying out your earnings

So, you got your first paid members or, perhaps, your first customers have purchased your digital products, and we’ve processed their payments. Now let’s get you paid out!

Your share will be available in your creator balance once we process membership payments/product sales and applicable fees. You can find a breakdown of your earnings and fees by checking your Insights dashboard.

Once funds are available to withdraw, you can pay out your balance manually, wait for the automatic payout on the 5th of the month (if enabled), or keep funds in your balance. You can leave them there until you’re ready to withdraw (note: please read our Unclaimed Funds article for more information). If you choose to pay out manually, you can withdraw all or part of your available balance.

Deposits typically arrive within 10 days, depending on your payout method. If it’s taking longer, refer to this guide to get answers: Where is my Payout?

Currently, you’re only able to initiate a payout once every 24 hours.

How to set up your payout method

First things first, let us know where to transfer your funds! We offer different payout methods depending on your location, including PayPal, Payoneer and bank transfers where available. You’ll see the options for your country when setting up your payout method. To learn more about the different payout methods, visit our dedicated article on Adding your payout details.

  • On Desktop, click on Your account from the bottom left corner
  • Click the Settings button on the left navigation side
  • Click Billings and payouts tab
  • Click Add payout method and follow the prompts

An automatic 5-day payout lock is placed on your balance whenever you add or edit a payout method.

How to pay out your balance

  • On Desktop, select Creator studio in the left-side navigation menu, then click on Payouts from the sub-menu to access it
  • Click the Withdraw button. If this button is grayed out and your current account balance is $0, please check your Relationship Manager to review your paid members’ membership history – depending on your chosen billing method, they may not have been charged yet
  • Enter the amount you want to withdraw — the field defaults to your full available balance
  • Review the payout fee and the net amount you’ll receive
  • Click Confirm — a success message will appear once your withdrawal has been initiated

Funds from one-time purchases on Web and Android will appear as pending for up to 7 days before they can be withdrawn from your balance. Funds from product sales and membership purchases made via iOS in-app purchases will remain pending for up to 75 days before they will be available for payout, accounting for the time Apple requires to process and confirm the funds

You can pay out once every 24 hours. If you have automatic payouts turned on, this counts as one payout. However, we may cap the number of payouts available per month if payout costs and patterns change dramatically in the future.

Payout via Patreon mobile app (Early access)

You can now pay out from the Patreon mobile app (iOS). Mobile payouts are gradually rolling out on iOS, with Android coming soon. From the Profile tab, you’ll see a new payout section where you can initiate a withdrawal on the go.

A few things to know before paying out on mobile:

  • You can only withdraw your full available balance on mobile — partial withdrawals aren’t supported on the app yet
  • You can only pay out once every 24 hours
  • There is a minimum payout amount, which varies by method, currency, and country
  • To withdraw your balance, you may need to update your account info, such as submitting tax documents, verifying your identity, or changing your payout method

How to set up Auto Withdrawal

You can tell us to trigger your balance payout every month on your behalf with our Auto-withdrawal feature. Once enabled, auto-withdrawals occur on the 5th of each month and send your full available balance.

  • On Desktop, select Creator studio in the left-side navigation menu, then click on Payouts from the sub-menu to access it
  • Click the Edit button next to auto-withdrawal
  • Click Turn on to enable auto-withdrawal

Now, we’ll send your full available balance to your designated payout method every month.

With auto-withdrawal, you can still manually transfer your balance from your payout preferences page.

Any payout hold on your account will interfere with the auto-withdrawal process. If you add or edit your payout method within 5 days of the 5th of the month (i.e., the 1st), your balance payout lock will prevent our auto-withdrawal. Don’t worry! You can manually pay out once your payout lock expires.

Payoneer FAQs

Beginning September 1, 2026, Payoneer will no longer support Belarus-based creators. Update your payout details on your Billing and payouts settings page as soon as possible. If you don’t have an alternative bank account or payout method, we recommend paying out your existing balance before August 31, 2026. See which countries are not supported below, what this means for you, and what to do next.

This article will cover frequently asked questions for creators utilizing the Payoneer service. You’ll find answers to questions about payout status, necessary documentation, and troubleshooting your Payoneer account.

FAQ

  • Payoneer’s support for creators varies by country. Payoneer doesn’t support Russia-based creators as of Dec 16, 2022. Please see the article about the Impact of international sanctions against Russia for more information.

  • To keep receiving payouts through Payoneer, you’ll need to re-register with a country of residence and a bank account outside of Russia and Belarus. If you use a Russian or Belarusian bank account, please update your payout details on your Billing and payouts settings page by following these steps:
    • Disconnect your Payoneer payout method
    • Reconnect with an applicable bank account in a different region (if available)
    • Or explore an alternative payout method (like Paypal/Hyperwallet)
  • For Belarusian-based creators, if you have no alternative bank or decide not to switch to PayPal, we recommend paying out your existing balance before August 31, 2026.
  • We are working closely with payment partners to find the best ways to support you and other creators in Russia and Belarus during this time.
  • To log in or create your account from the Payoneer website, you can use Payoneer’s welcome page.
  • You can also head to your Creator payout settings page and click on the Set up Payoneer Account button.
  • Payoneer will notify you via email when a payment arrives in your account. In addition, you can find the payment on the Transactions page in your Payoneer account.
  • If the selected payment method for receiving earnings is through bank transfer, the funds will be sent automatically to your bank and you will receive a confirmation via email. It can take up to 5 business days for the payment to reach your bank account.
  • Transactions Page
  • Balance Page
  • If you have not received the payout to your bank account after 5 business days, please contact Payoneer and refer to their troubleshooting instructions.

  • If you created a Payoneer account but have not yet received any earnings from Patreon, it is possible your account with Payoneer is not fully approved. To verify this, please log in to your Payoneer account and check the following:
    • Navigate to the Activity tab and select Funding sources to confirm that your Payoneer account is linked to Patreon. If you created an account directly through Payoneer, you will not be linked to Patreon and therefore may not have this option in the dropdown menu. If this is the case, you will need to log in to your Patreon account and link it to the Payoneer account you created.
    • Open the Verification Center in your Payoneer Settings. Here, you can view if there are any open requests for additional information to complete a review of your account. If the document is not accepted, Payoneer will send you an email explaining why. Additionally, you will find a message in Verification Center, under the Required tab.
    • Any open requests from Payoneer to complete your registration or to resolve an issue that might be stopping your payments will also be sent to you via e-mail. Be sure to check your inbox often. If you don’t have any messages from Payoneer, check your Spam folder to be sure.
    • If you have no open requests from Payoneer either in your e-mail or in My Account, and you appear to be successfully linked to Patreon, please contact Payoneer Customer Care for further assistance by clicking on this link to Payoneer Customer Care.
  • For more detailed information, visit Payoneer’s Support center here.
  • To upload a verification document, please follow these steps:
    • Sign in to your Payoneer account
    • Select Verification Center under the Settings menu
    • Select the relevant requirement from the list
    • Upload the relevant document and click SUBMIT
    • You will find a confirmation that the documents were uploaded successfully.
  • If you are providing an ID, please note that depending on your country, you may not find every ID type listed and instead will only find one or two options. We strongly suggest providing one of the recommended ID types, as this will shorten review time. If you do not have a document matching that option, you may upload another ID but please note the review time will be extended.
  • We recommend taking a picture of the document with your smartphone. Please make sure the document is complete (all four corners of the document should be visible and the image should be full size), document is not cropped, and the image is in high quality. If you are using the camera on your smartphone, please make sure the flash is not covering information on the document.
  • Payoneer reserves the right to request a variety of different documents to satisfy their regulatory requirements. Depending on the situation, you may be asked to provide:
  • Identity Verification

    • A picture of yourself holding a government-issued photo ID and a piece of paper with today’s date
    • Marriage certificate
    • Birth certificate
  • Address Verification
    • Utility bill
    • Rental agreement or lease
    • Bank Account verification documents (such as bank statements or voided checks)
  • Company Verification
    • Certificate of Incorporation
    • Articles of Organization
    • Business License
    • Certificate of Registration
    • Tax Document
  • If you have any more questions on documentation verification, please visit Payoneer’s guide to documentation verification.
  • If you have a reason to remove Patreon as a funding source on your Payoneer account, you can disconnect your account in your settings or reach out to Payoneer and Patreon support for assistance. We recommend disconnecting your Payoneer account in your Patreon settings as it is faster.

Payouts Dashboard

The Payouts dashboard is where you can withdraw all or part of your available balance, see what’s still pending, follow how your balance changed each month, review your payout withdrawal history, and download essential earnings and tax CSV files.

To open it on desktop, select Creator studio in the left-side navigation menu, then click Payouts. We redesigned the Payouts page in November 2026. How much you earn, when you get paid, and how you withdraw haven’t changed.

Once you initiate a payout, it can take 3–5 business days to be fully processed and credited to the method you set up. Please visit our guide on How payouts work for more detailed information.

Currently, you’re only able to initiate a payout once every 24 hours.

Mobile payouts are gradually rolling out on iOS, with Android coming soon. From the Profile tab, you’ll see a new payout section where you can initiate a withdrawal on the go.

Your balance

At the top of the page, you’ll find two amounts:

Term

Definition

Available to withdraw

Money you can pay out now. This amount updates in real time.

Pending

Money that’s still processing and can’t be withdrawn yet

Click the pending amount to see each hold and the date the money will become available.

Pending earnings can include:

  • iOS in-app purchases, held for up to 75 days while Apple processes them
  • One-time purchases on web and Android, held for up to 7 days
  • Ticketed Live events, held until 7 days after the event
  • Recovered payments from any of the above
  • VAT remittance and income tax withholding, where they apply

To learn more about each hold, visit How payouts work.

To withdraw your available balance, click Withdraw. You’ll see the payout fee and the amount you’ll receive before you confirm. For step-by-step instructions, visit Paying out your earnings or Set up automatic payouts.

Balance history

Balance history works like a bank statement. It groups your activity by month, with the most recent month first. Each month can include:

Term

Definition

Starting balance

What was in your balance at the start of the month

Finalized earnings

Earnings that finished processing that month and became available to withdraw

Withdrawal

Each payout you made, with its date and status

Memberships to other creators

Memberships paid from your balance that month

Money added to your balance shows as a positive amount, and money taken out shows as a negative amount. To change the months you see, use the menu next to Balance history. You can also choose All time. Click any row to see its details.

A few things to know about balance history:

  • All dates are in Pacific time (PT), the same as your Earnings dashboard
  • Your balance at the top updates in real time, but balance history can take up to 4 hours to update

Payouts guide for creators outside of the US

Patreon provides several payout options and supports multiple currencies for creators outside the U.S. This guide will walk you through each option, the fees involved, and how to choose the payout method and currency that best fit your needs.

International payout options

Creators outside the US have the following options available for payouts:

Bank Transfers (Via Payoneer)

What is a bank transfer?
  • When you select this payout option, your funds are sent directly to your bank account. How it works depends on whether you’ve set your payout currency to your local currency or to USD. It also depends on what the currency of your intended bank account is.
Local currency bank transfers
  • Example: An Australian creator sets their payout currency to AUD.
    • How it works: Patreon sends your funds in your local currency (AUD, GBP, EUR, etc.) straight to your bank account.
    • Fees: A small flat fee (e.g., about $0.50 local equivalent per payout, varies by currency). Minimum payout of $10 or local equivalent.
    • Conversion: No additional currency conversion happens at payout time because Patreon already collects payments in your local currency.
    • Best for: Creators who want predictable, low fees and who have most members paying in the same local currency.
USD Bank Transfers (cross currency)
  • Example: An Australian creator sets USD as their payout currency, even though their bank account is in AUD.
    • How it works: Funds accrue in your Patreon account in USD. When you pay out via USD bank transfer, your funds are automatically converted to your local currency and sent to your bank in your local currency (AUD in this case), less the fee amount.
    • Fees: 1.55% of payout amount + $0.25 per payout. No additional currency conversion fee is applied. Minimum payout of $10.
    • Conversion: Patreon handles the conversion from USD → local currency before sending to your bank. Because exchange rates change throughout the day, the exact rate applied may vary slightly depending on when your withdrawal is processed in the hours after you initiate it.
    • Best for: Creators who want to stay in USD for member billing but still need their payouts deposited into a local account.
USD Bank Transfers (USD to USD)
  • Example: An Australian creator sets USD as their payout currency and also sets the US as their payout country. They’ve set up a USD bank account (via a company like Wise) to accept USD payouts directly.
    • How it works: Patreon sends your funds in USD straight to your USD bank account via an ACH transfer. This option will only appear if you’re an international creator who selects the United States as your bank/payout country.
    • Fees: $0.50 per payout.
    • Conversion: No additional currency conversion happens at payout time, since the transfer is from USD to a USD bank account.
    • Best for: Creators who live outside the U.S. and want to keep their Patreon USD, but prefer to pay out to a US bank account.
  • Note: You don’t need a Payoneer Wallet account to use direct USD bank transfers.
Why choose a local bank transfer?
- Lowest-cost option if most of your fans are paying in your local currency.
- Steady and reliable payouts directly into your bank.
Why choose a USD bank transfer?
- Best if most of your fans pay in USD. You’ll avoid the 2.5% conversion fee that applies to member payments when your payout currency differs from theirs.
- Steady and reliable payouts directly into your bank.
- Keeps your balance in USD. This can be helpful if you want to minimize currency fluctuations or keep your reporting simple.
- Often cheaper than PayPal or Payoneer Wallet, since you avoid extra conversion or withdrawal fees.
​​Tradeoffs: Local vs. USD Bank Transfer
  • Local Bank Transfer
    • Lowest payout fees (flat fee, $0.50 or local equivalent).
    • Funds land in your local currency with no extra conversion at payout.
    • If your fans pay in any currency other than your local currency, Patreon applies a 2.5% conversion fee on each member payment.
  • USD Bank Transfer
    • Avoids the 2.5% member conversion fee for any fan paying in USD. Any fan paying in non-USD will still see this fee apply.
    • Your funds will still convert into local currency before landing in your bank (conversion built into the payout fee).
    • Higher payout fees (1.55% + $0.25 per payout) if paying out to your local bank account. Equal fees to local transfer if paying out to a USD bank account
  • Quick comparison rule of thumb:
    • If most of your members pay in your local currency → choose Local Bank Transfer for the lowest fees overall
    • If most of your members pay in USD → choose USD Bank Transfer to avoid potential member-side conversion costs, even though payout fees may be higher
  • You can check your fans’ pay-in currency by going to Payouts>Documents and downloading Member Transaction History. You will be able to sort the downloaded CSV by currency.
  • More info on changing currency
  • Switching to your local currency can unlock lower payout fees, but if most of your fans pay in USD, sticking with USD may save you on member-side conversion costs. You can find step-by-step instructions and more information on making this choice in our dedicated article about Setting my creator currency.

PayPal

What is PayPal?
  • PayPal lets you receive your Patreon earnings directly into your PayPal account. From there, you can transfer funds to your bank or spend via PayPal.
What are the fees?
- Non-US creators receiving payouts in USD
    - 1% of the amount transferred with a minimum of \$0.25, capped at \$20 USD.
    - PayPal may add additional fees if you transfer from PayPal to your bank account. Fees vary depending on the currency of your account and your location. Learn more.
    - $10 minimum to be able to pay out.
- Non-US creators receiving payouts in their local currency
    - See exact payout fees per currency in the table below.
Why choose PayPal?
- Widely available in most countries.
- Convenient if you already use PayPal for other transactions.
- Flexible for moving funds quickly, but note that fees can be higher than bank transfer or wire transfer, depending on your currency and location.

Payoneer Wallet

What is Payoneer Wallet?
  • For creators outside the U.S., Payoneer Wallet offers a way to receive payouts into your Payoneer account. From there, you can move funds to your bank or use a Payoneer Prepaid Debit MasterCard®.
What are the fees?
- Non-US creators receiving payouts in Dollars
    - $1.00 USD per payout to your Payoneer account.
    - Payoneer may add additional fees if you transfer from Payoneer to your bank account. Fees vary depending on the currency of your account and your location. Learn more.
    - Option to withdraw funds from your Payoneer account to your local bank account or the Payoneer Prepaid Debit MasterCard®, or $3.00 USD per global bank transfer*.
    - $25 minimum to be able to pay out.
- Non-US creators receiving payouts in their local currency
    - Supported. See exact fees in the table below.
Why choose Payoneer Wallet?
- Flexible — funds can be used directly with the prepaid card or transferred to a bank.
- Can be useful if you already rely on Payoneer for international payments.
- Typically more expensive than bank transfer, but offers potential flexibility.
