FAQ

  • In most cases, we recommend sticking with the currency you’ve already chosen. If you’re deciding for the first time, we recommend selecting the local currency of the country you live in, if supported by Patreon. This makes payouts simpler and usually ensures the lowest payout fees, since it unlocks local bank payout options. If you have a large U.S. fanbase or want to receive payouts to a USD bank account, you may want to choose USD instead. Ultimately, it’s up to you—pick the option that best fits your financial needs.
  • Local bank transfer is only available if you’re set to receive payouts in your country’s local currency and live in a supported country. If your payout currency is set to something different, like USD outside the U.S., the local transfer option won’t appear. Instead, you’ll see options for USD Bank transfer.
  • You only need your bank details to get set up such as your account number and the name on the account. No extra paperwork is usually required and no Payoneer account is required.
  • That’s okay! As long as you live in a country supported by Payoneer, you can still register your bank account, even if it’s located in a different country.
  • First, check whether you’re in the standard 5-day payout hold that applies whenever a new payout method is added. If that’s not the case, try re-entering your details. If the issue continues, reach out to us and we’ll work with our bank partner to get it resolved.
  • Special characters aren’t supported. Please enter your bank information using letters and numbers only. If you’ve already done so, you should be all set.
  • For most creators paying out by direct bank transfer, there’s no payout limit. If you’re paying out through PayPal or Payoneer Wallet, we don’t set a fixed cap on our end — though your bank or the payment processor may occasionally apply their own limits. If a withdrawal request is larger than what can go through in a single transfer, we’ll send the maximum amount right away and keep the rest in your account balance, ready for your next payout. You can request a payout once every 24 hours.

Paypal supported countries

Patreon uses PayPal as an option to process payouts. In some cases, your payout may be processed through a service called HyperWallet, which is a global platform provided by PayPal, to handle payouts for users around the world.

This may mean our list of supported countries and regions could differ from PayPal’s official list. While we strive to keep this list current, the supported locations may occasionally be updated by PayPal/Hyperwallet. For the most up-to-date information, please refer to PayPal support.

Recovering unclaimed funds

This article is for creators who have received an email from Patreon’s Tax team regarding funds being remitted to their state’s unclaimed property division. We make every effort to ensure funds do not go unclaimed, so will try to email inactive creators multiple times before the ‘escheatment period’ has run. Continue reading for guidance on recovering unclaimed funds from Patreon or your state’s unclaimed property division.

You can visit our Paying Out help page for information on how payouts work at Patreon.

Recovering unclaimed funds from Patreon

If you’ve received a notice from Patreon’s Tax team letting you know that your funds will soon be remitted to your state on file as unclaimed property, you can log into Patreon to claim your funds or respond directly to the email you received. By logging into your Patreon, your account will no longer be considered inactive.

Once you’ve logged in to your account, here’s how to withdraw your funds:

  • If your Patreon was unpublished, you can republish your Patreon to access your Payouts
  • Click Creator Studio , then click Payouts — you can review or set up your payout method from your Payouts settings if it’s your first time paying out
  • Click Withdraw

If you are setting up or changing your payout method, a 5-day payout lock will be placed on your account. Once a payout is initiated, it can take up to 10 days for the funds to appear in your personal account.

Learn more about how payouts work.

Recovering unclaimed funds from your state

If the timeline to recover funds from Patreon has passed, your funds can still be claimed directly through your state’s unclaimed property division. If you are a non-US creator and the timeline to recover funds from Patreon has passed, you can claim your funds from the State of Delaware’s unclaimed property division.

How to recover unclaimed funds from your state:
  • Visit our Contact Us page and start a chat to begin gathering your details
  • File a claim with the unclaimed property division for your state and include the information provided by Patreon’s Product Support team

FAQ

  • If you’re having difficulty logging into your account, we’ve created a troubleshooting guide that may help you regain access. If you continue to have difficulty logging into your Patreon account, please complete an account recovery form so that Patreon’s Product Support team can assist you.
  • If you deleted your Patreon account and received an email about unclaimed funds on your account, please visit the Contact Us page for further assistance.
  • If your Patreon is deemed inactive, your creator Patreon page will be unpublished. When a Patreon is unpublished, it will no longer appear on members’ membership lists or in search, and payment processing for the Patreon ceases.
  • Here’s how to republish your Patreon on Desktop:
    • Click Creator Studio , then click Edit page under Home
    • Make any adjustments you need to before you republish your page
    • If you’re ready, click the Publish
  • If there has been an extended period of account inactivity (i.e., no login), any remaining funds on the account are considered unclaimed.
  • An account is considered inactive if there is no login activity for an extended period. The length of time required to determine whether or not an account is inactive, depends on a creator’s location of residency set by their address on file.

Set up automatic payouts

Mobile payouts are gradually rolling out on iOS, with Android coming soon. From the Profile tab, you’ll see a new payout section where you can initiate a withdrawal on the go.

Don’t want to think about transferring your payouts every month? We’ve got you covered with automatic transfers.

To enable automatic transfers:

  • Click on the Payouts button from the creator menu on the left-hand side of your page
  • Click on the Edit link under the Withdraw Balance button
  • A confirmation window will populate, and you need to click on the Turn on auto-withdrawal button

Once your transfer is initiated, it can take 3-5 business days to deposit into your PayPal or bank account.

If you enable automatic transfers on or after the 5th, you won’t be paid out automatically until the following 5th of the month. You can manually payout using the withdraw balance button if you need your payout sooner than that. Manually paying out your funds will not affect future automatic transfers. Please note that you can only pay out once every 24 hours, and the automatic transfer counts as a payout.

Funds from product sales made with Commerce will appear as pending for up to 7 days before they can be withdrawn from your balance

When you withdraw funds, a payout fee will be deducted from the payout amount. Visit this section on Payout Fees to learn more about what payout fees you can expect depending on your payout method.

To withdraw a specific amount instead of your full balance, use a manual payout from your Payouts dashboard.

Upload my verification document for Stripe direct deposit

In this article, we’ll guide you through what to do if you receive an email from our payout processing partner, Stripe, asking you to upload a form of government issued ID. This email is legitimate and is a requirement from Stripe in order to send your direct deposit payouts.

Why do I need to provide identification?

Stripe has responsibilities to their financial partners that involve verifying your identity and confirming the legitimacy of your business. In some cases, Stripe may need to collect a bit more information from you to ensure we can continue making transfers to your bank account.

In order to get you fully up and running with your Stripe account, you may need to upload a scan or photograph of a government-issued photo ID (driver’s license or passport). Once you do so, Stripe will take 3 - 5 business days to verify your identity.

Verification document requirements
  • Documents can be uploaded in .png or .jpg format (High quality photos and color scans acceptable)
  • Front and back of government issued photo ID (if applicable) on one file
  • Photocopies of identity documents are not acceptable
  • Documents must be valid and not expired
  • Complete documents must be uploaded. A complete document is defined as:
    • Both front and back of a driver’s license or identity card
    • The entire personal information page of a passport
Acceptable forms of identification:
  • Passport
  • Passport card
  • Driver license
  • State issued ID card
  • Resident permit ID / U.S. Green Card
  • Border crossing card
  • Child ID card
  • NYC card
  • U.S. visa card
Acceptable forms of legal entity verification:
  • IRS Letter 147C
  • IRS SS-4 confirmation letter
Acceptable forms of bank account ownership verification:
  • Bank account statement
  • Voided cheque
  • Bank letterhead

Learn more about what documents Stripe can accept for verification of identity, address, and legal entity.

Uploading your verification document

To upload your required verification documents, log in to your Patreon creator page account and follow these steps:

  • Click Your account , then click on the Settings
  • Click Billing and payouts
  • Select Update in the Payout method section
  • Click Update Stripe Connection and follow the instructions in the Stripe portal to upload your document

The information you are providing to us is not stored on Patreon and is securely kept with Stripe. You can learn more about how they secure and encrypt that data here: Information about Stripe Security.

If you have trouble uploading your verification documents or are having trouble getting verified please reach out directly to our support team.

Where is my Payout?

It can take 1-5 business days for your payout to be fully processed to your payout method of choice. If you’re experiencing any issues with your payout, please go through the troubleshooting steps below.

Check your payout status

Navigate to your Payouts dashboard to review your recent payout status. Each payout attempt will include a status. If you encounter an error, we’ll provide you with more information when possible.

Below are the status definitions for payout attempts:

Status

Definition

Complete

Payout arrived in your wallet and is available to use.

Sent

Payout was sent and arrival times may vary; or payment was sent to support other Patreon creators.

Pending

Payout is being processed and is on the way.

Returned

Payout didn’t go through. The funds will return to your Patreon balance.

Incomplete

There was an issue processing the payout. You may need to take action before it can be processed.

Funds from products purchased through Commerce on Web and Android will appear as pending for up to 7 days before they can be withdrawn from your balance. Funds from product sales made via iOS in-app purchases will remain pending for up to 75 days before they will be available for payout, accounting for the time Apple requires to process and confirm the funds. As soon as funds are available in your balance, you may pay them out immediately, as long as there are no blocks or holds on your payouts.

Confirm your payout method

Double-check your payout method. You may have added a payout method that you don’t often use or aren’t checking.

To add or update your payout method:
  • On Desktop, click on Your account in the bottom left corner and then select Settings
  • In the Creator settings section, select Billing and payouts
  • From here, you can add or update your payout method.

An automatic 5-day payout lock is placed on your account balance whenever you add or update a payout method.

Troubleshooting Stripe payouts

Stripe direct deposit payout is only available for US creators.

We recommend that you use a checking account to transfer payouts. Using a non-standard bank account, like a savings account or virtual bank account, may result in a higher chance of payout failure. If you entered non-standard bank account (savings or virtual bank account) information, follow the steps below to update your payout method to a checking account and trigger a retry.

Payments can be delayed in Stripe for two reasons:
  • Holidays or weekends
  • Incorrect account information

If it’s been more than 3 days since you sent your payout through Stripe and there is no holiday, we recommend getting in touch with your bank to inquire about pending deposits on their end.

There’s also a chance that the account information submitted isn’t quite right. You can resubmit your information on Patreon to trigger a retry.

To trigger a direct deposit retry:
  • On Desktop, click on Your account in the bottom left corner and then select Settings
  • In the Creator settings section, select Billing and payouts
  • Scroll down and click the Update Stripe Connection button
  • and re-enter your bank account and routing numbers
  • Scroll down and click the Save button
  • Stripe will automatically reattempt transfers to the updated bank information within 1-3 business days.

Troubleshooting PayPal payouts

If you’re using PayPal, the slightest typo can direct your balance to a non-existent account. Double-check the PayPal email you have connected to your Patreon account.

To check the PayPal email we have on file:
  • On Desktop, click on Your account in the bottom left corner and then select Settings
  • In the Creator settings section, select Billing and payouts
  • Scroll down to the Payout method section and check the PayPal email address
  • If there is any typo, correct it as soon as possible, and Submit a request with our support team for assistance

Troubleshooting Payoneer payouts

Payoneer is only available as a payout option for creators outside of the US.

Whether you use Payoneer to send direct deposits to your local bank or you get funds auto-loaded to a Payoneer card, there are a few issues that could cause a delay.

If it’s been longer than 5 business days since you paid out, we recommend getting in touch with Payoneer directly. You may need to verify your Payoneer account or send documentation to receive payouts. Payoneer can help you through that process.

Here’s our FAQ to help you contact Payoneer.

Other payout issues

  • If you check your balance and see some or all of your funds as pending, it means they are not yet available for withdrawal.
  • There are a couple of different reasons why you might see pending funds:
    • Funds from membership payments may appear as pending until they are successfully processed
    • Funds from products purchased through Commerce on Web and Android will appear as pending for up to 7 days before they can be withdrawn from your balance. Funds from product sales made via iOS in-app purchases will remain pending for up to 75 days before they will be available for payout, accounting for the time Apple requires to process and confirm the funds.
  • Once funds are no longer pending and appear as available to withdraw, you can pay out your balance.
  • Check your Relationship Manager, where you’ll find a list of all your members. You will only receive payouts to your account from paid members who have an active membership with you. If your Patreon is per post, your paid members would have needed to have a membership with you before you posted a paid post; if your Patreon is on the 1st-of-the-month billing schedule, they will have needed to join before we started processing payments on the 1st of the month.
  • If you have paid members whose payments have declined, you will not receive their payments until their payments clear. Learn more about declining members in this help guide: Why have my members’ payments declined?
  • To ensure the security of your account, we sometimes need to place a temporary hold on your payouts. Visit this help guide for more information about temporary payout holds: How payouts work.
  • You should receive a notification as well as an email when this happens, so if you haven’t received either, this is probably not the issue. If you get a notification letting you know the time and date you can pay out your funds, this means that you are within 24 hours of the last time you manually paid out.
  • A payout lock will be lifted after 5 days, at which time you’ll be able to manually pay out any funds from your account.
  • We use the balance in your account to cover any memberships you have to other creators, so if the amount you are paying other creators is more than you are collecting for your Patreon, you won’t have a positive balance in your account. You can check this within your Payouts Dashboard.
  • We recently removed the payout progress bar from the payouts dashboard since it was causing confusion. With most creators now on subscription billing — and member payments happening throughout the month — the progress bar that appeared during the first few days of the month no longer gave an accurate view of your total payments coming in for the month.
  • If most of your earnings are still being processed on the 1st, don’t worry — you can check your Available Balance from the 1st through the 5th for the clearest picture of what’s been successfully processed. You can also visit your Earnings dashboard any time to track ongoing payment activity. Most payments will be in by the 5th, with any remaining charges continuing to retry automatically after that.

Why is my payout less than I expected?

This article will cover possible reasons why the amount you earned is less than you anticipated or why the amount you withdrew is more or less than what you earned.

There are 3 main reasons: timing, fees, and pending holds. Your Payouts page shows each of them, so you can trace the difference month by month.

If you’re wondering…

The likely reason

Where to check

“Where did part of my earnings go?”

Your earnings and your payout cover different dates

Balance history

“Why is my deposit lower?”

Fees come out before and during your payout

Finalized earnings and your withdrawal details

“Why isn’t it available yet?”

Some payments are on hold before you can withdraw them

The pending amount under your balance

Your earnings and your payout cover different dates

Your Earnings dashboard groups payments by the calendar month they went through. Your payout works differently: it sends the amount you choose to withdraw, or your full available balance on the 5th of the month if you use automatic payouts.

So a single payout can mix money from more than 1 month. For example, your April 5 payout can include money from the last days of March and from the first days of April.

To see how your balance changed, open Balance history on your Payouts page. Each month shows your starting balance and the money that came in and went out. Click Finalized earnings for any month to see why it can differ from the net earnings in your Earnings dashboard.

Fees may be missing from your estimation

One of the most common reasons your payout is lower than expected is that fees are deducted before earnings are added to your creator balance. In other words, the total in your balance already reflects fee deductions from successful payments.

For a detailed explanation of how each fee works, check out our Creator fees overview guide.

Here’s a quick summary of the fees you may see:

  • Platform fee – A percentage of successfully processed payments. This depends on your plan: creators on the standard plan pay 10%, while legacy plan creators may pay 5%, 8% or 11%. You can check which plan you’re on in your Settings
  • Payment processing fees – These cover the cost of processing payments from your members. They vary based on your members’ location, currency, and payment method
  • App Store fee (iOS purchases) – If a member makes a purchase through Apple’s in-app purchase system within the Patreon iOS app, Apple takes a 30% service fee. This fee replaces Patreon’s standard payment processing fee for that transaction
  • Currency conversion fee – A 2.5% fee is applied when a member pays in a different currency than your payout currency.
  • Taxes on fees – In some regions, tax must be collected from your members by law. Your payment processing fee is calculated based on the total payment amount, including any applicable tax. Learn more about sales tax and VAT
  • Payout fee – A small fee for transferring your balance to your selected payout method (e.g., PayPal, bank transfer, or Payoneer). The fee depends on both the payout method and your payout currency. You’ll see the payout fee and the amount you’ll receive before you confirm a withdrawal, and you can find it later by clicking the withdrawal in Balance history

You can see your fees in Earnings Insights, which updates every 4 hours. To see your fees for a specific month, click Finalized earnings in Balance history on your Payouts page. For a per-transaction breakdown, download your Member transaction history.

The fees on your Payouts page include only the fees Patreon charges. PayPal, Payoneer, or your bank may charge their own fees for currency conversion or withdrawals, which we can’t see.

Pending balance

Funds from one-time purchases on Web and Android will appear as pending for up to 7 days before they can be withdrawn from your balance. Funds from in-app purchases will appear as pending for up to 75 days before they will be available for payout, accounting for the time Apple requires to process and confirm the funds. Earnings from ticketed Live events are held until 7 days after the event. iOS tickets become available on whichever date is later: 7 days after the event or 75 days after purchase.

On your Payouts page, click the pending amount under your balance to see each hold and the date the money will become available. To learn more about holds, visit How payouts work.

Declined membership payments

Another cause is if some of your members’ payments declined. These are payments that Patreon attempted to process, but failed. In your Relationship manager, you can check if any member’s payments were declined. Visit our declined payments resource to learn more about failed payments.

Your Merch cost has been deducted from your balance

If you use Patreon for Merch fulfillment, the cost of the merchandise itself (based on the quantity and SKUs of the associated items) and shipping will usually be deducted from your balance on the 4th of each month. This may impact your balance if you are enrolled in automatic 5th-of-the-month payouts, so you may see a decrease in the amount you receive from the amount that was available to withdraw. Merch costs are included in your finalized earnings. To see them, click Finalized earnings for that month in Balance history.

You may have memberships with other creators

If you have a paid membership to other creators, we’ll subtract the cost of those memberships from your creator payout. This prevents unnecessary additional fees, and your card or PayPal account will be billed less or not at all. In Balance history, memberships to other creators show as their own line.

Also, the number listed on your public page is an estimate and is not an accurate representation of what you may actually earn. You can learn more about this here: Understand the numbers listed on my creator page

Still doesn’t add up?

Download your Monthly payouts report and your Member transaction history to compare each payment with your payouts. The member transaction history shows the date each payment was charged, went through, and became available to withdraw. Learn more in Downloading your earnings and payout reports.

Creators: Podcasting and RSS

Control download links for audio posts

If you share audio posts with your members as a benefit, you can choose whether or not to display a download link for your audio files.

Follow these steps to show or hide audio download links:

  • Click on Creator Studio , then click Dashboard
  • Click More on the right side of the page, next to the Edit page button
  • Select Edit page details
  • Click Posts and Products in the top menu bar
  • Go to the Audio settings section
  • Select or deselect the option to allow members to download audio files from posts and products

Note: By default, audio download links are enabled. This setting applies to all audio posts (past and future). At this time, you can’t change download settings on a per-post basis.

Customizing Audio Previews

Due to issues in processing, off platform audio clips will no longer be generated at this time. On platform audio previews will still be available for your visitors to view on your page. We’ll let you know when this feature is available again.

Audio previews are short audio snippets that allow creators to tease their content both on their Patreon page and across their social media platforms. When you publish a post and audio previews are enabled, we automatically generate an audio clip, which is a short animated video that includes the audio preview. This audio clip can then be directly shared to select social media platforms or downloaded for sharing on other social channels.

Using audio previews

This article is about using and sharing audio previews. Audio previews are available when you create an audio post on Desktop or mobile web by uploading an audio file from your device. You can also share audio on Patreon by embedding URLs or attaching audio files to posts.

Audio previews are enabled by default for your posts if:

  • Your Patreon is in the All Audiences category
  • The audio file is at least 30 seconds long to generate a preview. To generate an audio clip from a preview, the audio file needs to be at least 2 minutes long. Learn more about Audio clips below
  • Your post is locked to paid or free members (posts published for everyone cannot have an audio preview)
Turning audio previews off

Once you’ve uploaded your audio file, audio previews will be on by default. You can toggle the switch to turn audio previews on or off when editing/creating an audio post.

Customizing your audio previews

By default, audio previews are between 30 seconds and 5 minutes based on the length of the content. You can choose up to 50% of your content or a maximum of 10 minutes as an audio preview.

- Click on the Create button and choose the Audio post option
- Once you’ve uploaded your audio file and entered your other post details, click the Next button
- In the Audio preview section, you can drag the box parameter to the desired section of the clip and drag the ends of the box parameter to increase or decrease the audio preview length
- Click on Preview to listen to the sample you chose
- Once you're satisfied, click the Save changes button
- If you’re editing your audio preview for an already published post, you’ll need to click the Save button to publish your changes

Audio clips

Audio files must be at least 2 minutes long to be able to generate a clip from a preview.

Audio clips are animated video previews of your audio posts. When you enable audio previews in an audio post and publish it, an audio clip is automatically generated for you. This feature saves you time and effort, allowing you to easily share these clips on your social media platforms and promote your posts off-platform, helping turn followers into members.

Audio clips consist of:
  • Audio preview: when played, fans can listen to your preview
  • Animated soundwave: soundwave visualization that plays along with the audio
  • Animated captions: automatically generated captions (currently not customizable)

Some audio clips may not be ready right away. You may need to leave the flow as the audio clip processes in the background. Audio clips are typically generated within a few minutes. You will receive an in-platform and email notification when the audio clip is ready for download.

How to share audio clips on your socials

Once your audio post goes live, a prompt will appear, allowing you to directly share it to select platforms or export it as a downloadable file to the platform of your choice. You can also share it later by going to your audio post and selecting the Share icon.

Generating audio clips for published posts

Audio clips are not retroactively generated for posts published before May 2024. To generate an audio clip for an older post, you’d like to share on socials, you can edit the audio preview for that post, and we’ll automatically generate your audio clip.

  • On the My page section of your Patreon, you can filter or search for a post published before the launch of clips in May 2024
  • Click the … more menu and click Edit
  • Click on Next if there are no other changes you need to make
  • Ensure previews are toggled on
  • Click the Edit link in the preview section and customize any continuous segment between 30 seconds and 5 minutes long
    • Click on Save changes
  • Click the Save button to publish your post changes
  • Once you’ve published your changes, we’ll automatically generate an audio clip for your post — this may take a few minutes, depending on the file size
  • You can click the Share icon to share your video and audio clips directly to select socials or download them to share across social platforms
Who can listen to these audio previews/clips?

Audio previews/clips are public and can be listened to on your Patreon page or any social media platform where you share them.

Enable audio RSS feeds for my members

Patreon provides a built-in RSS feed so members can listen to your podcast in their favorite podcast apps, such as Apple Podcasts, Castro, or Overcast. This article explains how RSS works, how to enable it, and how to ensure your episodes appear in members’ feeds.

What is RSS?

RSS (Really Simple Syndication) is a feed format used by most podcast apps. When you enable RSS on Patreon, each member gets a private link with episodes they have access to. They can copy this link and add it to their favorite app to keep listening outside of Patreon.

How to enable RSS for your podcast

You can enable RSS when creating a new podcast in your Podcast and audio settings. During setup, you’ll fill out key podcast information — these details are shared through your RSS feed and displayed in podcast apps.

Here’s what gets included in your RSS feed, and what each field means:

  • Cover Artwork: The image that will appear as your podcast thumbnail on apps. We recommend a square image sized 3000x3000 px
  • Title: The name of your show — choose something clear and easy to search for
  • Description: A short summary that helps potential listeners understand what your podcast is about
  • Author Name: This will show up as the creator or host name in podcast directories
  • Author Email: This address will be visible in your RSS feed and may be used by listeners or podcast platforms to contact you. We recommend using an email you feel comfortable sharing publicly.
  • Podcast Type:
    • Episodic: Listeners can jump into any episode — newer episodes appear first in apps
    • Serial: Best for narrative or story-driven shows meant to be heard in order — apps will list from oldest to newest
  • Explicit Content: Toggle this on if your show includes strong language or explicit topics. Learn more about Podcast explicit content
  • Category: Helps listeners discover your podcast when browsing directories
  • Copyright: You can include the copyright year(s), your name, and (if applicable) your company
  • Language: The primary language spoken in your podcast

After filling in your details, you’ll reach the Distribution settings, where you can choose to enable syncing with Spotify and Apple Podcasts. In the RSS section, make sure the Members-only RSS feed is enabled. Keeping this enabled allows members to access your podcast in their preferred app using a private RSS link.

You’ll also find your public RSS link here, which allows you to distribute your public podcast episodes in any podcast app directly from Patreon. Learn more about it in our guide, Get started with Public RSS on Patreon.

Want help on how to create a podcast? Check our complete step-by-step guide on how to Set up a podcast on Patreon.

If you have an existing podcast, you can enable or double-check your RSS settings by going to Your account , and then Settings. In the Creator settings section, select Podcasts and audio, then click on your show and select Distribution. Just make sure the Members-only RSS feed is toggled on.

How to add episodes to your RSS feed

Episodes will appear in a member’s RSS feed when they’re published as an Audio or Video post and added to a podcast with RSS enabled.

You can add episodes to a podcast:

When creating a new post (New episode)

  • Create a new Audio or Video post and toggle Add to podcast to select the podcast show you want the episode to appear in

From your Library (Moving existing episodes)

You can also add existing episodes to a podcast from your Library:

  • On Desktop, select Creator studio in the left-side navigation menu, then click on Library from the sub-menu. Select the episodes you want to move, then click Edit > Edit podcast or season, and choose the podcast
  • If you’ve filtered by a specific podcast: click Add episodes > Move episodes in the top-right corner

The podcast must have RSS enabled in its Distribution settings — otherwise, episodes won’t appear in members’ feeds.

Which posts will show up in an audio RSS feed?

Your members’ private RSS feeds will include all audio and video posts with the Podcast setting toggled on. Here’s a breakdown of what will and won’t appear in the RSS feed:

Included:
  • Audio or video posts added to a podcast with RSS enabled
    • If you post both audio and video versions of your podcast, you should now only post video, and we’ll extract the audio
  • Audio or video posts added to a podcast and marked for sale. Fans who purchase the post will receive the audio in their RSS feed
Not included:
  • Posts with video/audio file attachments instead of direct audio or video uploads
  • Posts with links to third-party audio or video hosting sites (e.g., SoundCloud, Vimeo, etc)
  • Audio or video sold as digital products in your shop (digital products are not included in the RSS feed)

Where members find their RSS feed

Members can easily find their private RSS links in:

  • An email when they join your membership
  • On your creator page, by clicking on the Podcast icon below your profile, or under Membership > Listen on other podcast apps
  • The Collections tab on your creator page
  • On the Patreon app, via the More menu on your page

Share your podcast on Spotify

In addition to RSS, you can enable the Spotify integration to let your members listen on Spotify:

  • Members can connect their Patreon and Spotify accounts to unlock episodes directly in the Spotify app
  • Your paid content stays hidden from non-members but helps attract new listeners
  • If you also offer a free version of your podcast on Spotify, you can use Synced Feeds to combine the two versions into a single, seamless experience. Learn more about Delivering podcasts on Spotify

FAQ

  • Yes! If you upload a video post and add it to a podcast, we’ll automatically extract the audio and include it in the RSS feed.
  • Once a member’s access ends, their feed will stop updating. They may still see previously cached content in their podcast app.
  • Yes. You can choose who sees each episode by setting access when you publish your post. RSS feeds reflect each member’s access level.
  • No. Posts created and sold through Commerce are not included in your podcast RSS feed
  • Sharing a private RSS link with others is a violation of our Terms of Service. We monitor RSS usage for unusual activity, such as a single link being accessed from multiple devices or podcast apps beyond what’s typical for one member.
  • If we detect that a member has shared their link, the affected RSS link will be automatically reset, so anyone else using it loses access. If this happens a second time, the member suspected of sharing their link will have their comment and DM privileges suspended for 7 days. Continued or repeated violations may lead to further action by our Trust & Safety team to protect your content.
  • Email Patreon Support with the RSS link and where it was shared. Include the member’s name or URL if possible

Get started with Public RSS on Patreon

Public RSS lets you distribute your public podcast episodes directly to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and other directories, all from Patreon. In this guide, you’ll learn how to move your public podcast episodes into Patreon, set up your new Public RSS feed, add audio previews to your public feed, check your Spotify integration, and redirect your old Public RSS feed. By the end, you’ll have a fully working public podcast feed hosted on Patreon and ready to share.

Why use Public RSS

  • Manage all podcast distribution in one place
  • Eliminate third-party hosting costs
  • Promote previews of your paid episodes in your public feed

⚠️ Note: Dynamic ad insertion is not supported at this time.

How to set up a public RSS

Follow these five steps to migrate your public episodes and get your feed ready to share.

Step 1: Import your public episodes to your Patreon show
  • On Desktop, click on Your account from the bottom-left corner and then select Settings
  • In the Creator settings section, select Podcasts and audio
  • Select your show and click Import & sync
  • Click on Import my podcast
  • Locate and paste an RSS link from your host that includes all episodes of your show, and then click Continue
    • Most podcast hosting platforms provide your RSS feed URL within their settings or dashboard
    • Please note that only audio posts will be imported
  • Adjust your Import settings
    • You can choose to either Save as draft in Library or Publish automatically for your episodes
    • Select the audience for your episodes — You can change this for each episode before publishing
  • Click Done
  • You will be asked to verify your email as part of the migration process
  • Confirm the code and click Next
  • Once we import your episodes, all episodes will be saved as drafts in your Library. You’ll receive an email when they’re ready for review
Step 2: Manually update access (if needed)
  • From your Library, click on the Podcast dropdown menu
  • Select the show you want to update access for
  • Select the episodes and click Edit access
  • Click Edit in the top-right corner of your Library, select Edit access
  • Set visibility to Public and toggle on Hide from paid members
Step 3: Confirm your feed setup
  • In Settings > Podcast and audio, click on your show
  • Go to Distribution
  • Click on RSS
  • Copy the link in the Public RSS feed section and test it in a browser
  • Adjust items in your Library if anything looks off
Optional: Add previews to your public feed

Previews are toggled on by default for audio files over 30 seconds long, and you can always enable public audio previews for posts where you previously disabled them.

  • In your Library, click the episode title
  • In the settings sidebar, enable Audio preview for the post
  • Select a timestamp from your episode or upload an audio file of your choosing as a preview (Learn more about Customizing Audio Previews)
  • By default, your preview will be visible to non-members. To disable, toggle off Add preview to podcast feed for non-members in the post editor
Step 4: Check Spotify setup

What to know about the Spotify integration and Synced Feeds

When you enable the Spotify integration for a Patreon show, a new, discoverable show is automatically created on Spotify.

  • Members can listen to the episodes they have access to, and non-members will see locked episodes with an upsell to join your Patreon
  • Any public episodes added to this show will also appear in the Patreon-exclusive version of the show on Spotify
  • If you’ve selected Hide from paid members for an episode, that episode will not be included in the Spotify show for your members
  • The Public RSS feed for this show will include all public episodes and any previews you’ve added.

If you’ve set up Spotify Synced Feeds, you may need to use episode pairing to avoid duplicates in your merged feed on Spotify. This is especially important if a newly added public episode duplicates one already included in your existing public show on Spotify. Learn more about Spotify Synced Feeds for Patreon creators.

Step 5: Redirect your old RSS feed
  • In your previous host, set up a 301 redirect to your new Patreon Public RSS feed
  • In Apple Podcasts Connect and Spotify for Creators, check if the feed has updated
  • If not, update it manually

⚠️ Important: Setting up a 301 redirect is permanent.

Next steps

  • Share your new public RSS link everywhere you promote your show
  • Use previews to convert free listeners into paying members

Getting started with podcasting

Whether you’re launching a brand new podcast or bringing over episodes from another platform, Patreon gives you flexible tools to host, organize, and share your podcast with fans.

This article will help you choose the right approach for your podcast and link you to the step-by-step guides you need.

Looking for tips from a fellow Patreon podcaster? Joe Fisher from Midnight Burger shares out tips that have helped him grow. Whether you’re newer or a seasoned podcaster, this mini-course has something to offer. Currently, Patreon for Creators is only available in English.

Setting up your podcast

The first step to podcasting on Patreon is setting up your podcast show in your Podcast and audio settings—check out our step-by-step guide to creating a podcast on Patreon.

Already hosting your podcast elsewhere? Here are a couple of ways to get started on Patreon:

  • Migrate from an external host: Permanently move your podcast to Patreon and manage all your episodes directly on the platform moving forward
  • Sync your existing feed: Keep creating and managing your episodes on your current hosting platform, while distributing them through Patreon.

Decide where members can listen

Once your show is set up, your members can listen in a few different ways:

  • On Patreon: Fans can listen to episodes directly on Patreon, both on desktop and on mobile app
  • On other podcast apps via a private RSS link. Learn more about Enabling RSS and sharing your episodes
  • On Spotify, if you choose to enable the integration. This lets paying members listen on the Spotify app. Learn more about Delivering podcasts with Spotify
  • You can merge your public and Patreon feeds into one seamless experience using Spotify Synced Feeds to drive discovery and membership growth
  • If you host your public episodes on Patreon, you can also share your public RSS on Apple Podcasts, so anyone can listen to your free Patreon episodes

Organize and manage your podcast

You can create a single podcast show or multiple shows to keep your content organized. Patreon gives you tools to:

  • Create and publish new episodes
  • Move episodes between podcasts
  • Manage your podcast titles, descriptions, and settings at any time

For step-by-step instructions on creating, publishing, and managing podcasts, check out: Create a podcast on Patreon

Share your podcast with fans

When a member joins your page, they get access to your episodes based on their membership tier. They’ll also receive a private RSS link they can use in their favorite podcast app.

If your members run into issues with their RSS link, they can follow a few simple steps to resolve it. Check out our troubleshooting guide for common RSS problems

Podcast explicit content

You can mark your show, an individual episode, or both as explicit. These settings determine how your show and episode pages are displayed to listeners.

Within certain podcast players, if you mark your show as explicit, all episodes will display the explicit label unless they’re specifically marked as not explicit. If you don’t mark your show as explicit but mark one or more episodes as explicit, the explicit label is also displayed on the show page — You can learn more here.

To better understand what qualifies as explicit content, please refer to Apple podcast content guidelines.

Availability of podcast content can vary depending on the country or region. For example, you can learn more about how Apple Podcasts presents content worldwide.

Podcasting: Migrating Audio from an External Host

Podcast importing lets you bring your existing RSS feed from an external host to Patreon. Once imported, you can manage and update your podcast episodes directly on Patreon, making it easier to share content with your fans. This article will guide you through the process of migrating your podcast to Patreon, whether you’re creating a new show or adding episodes to an existing one.

Who is Podcast Migration For?

Podcast migration is best for creators who want to import their full back catalog once and manage episodes directly on Patreon going forward.

It’s ideal if you:

  • Want to bring your back catalog to Patreon all at once: Save time by transferring previously published episodes in bulk. This is perfect if you plan to manually upload or manage future episodes directly on Patreon
  • Are moving away from an external host: If you’re fully transitioning off another RSS host, migration lets you bring everything over and manage your content natively on Patreon for a seamless experience
  • Are new to Patreon and want a clean start: Already host a podcast elsewhere? Migrating helps you transfer your existing episodes so you can start engaging fans right away

How to Migrate Episodes

If you already have a podcast hosted elsewhere with an RSS feed, you can migrate your feed to Patreon. This makes it easy to transfer your existing episodes and start sharing your content with fans on Patreon.

- On Desktop, click on Your account from the bottom-left corner and then select Settings
- In the Creator settings section, select [Podcasts and audio](https://www.patreon.com/settings-creator/audio)
- Click on the New podcast button
- You'll be asked to confirm your podcast information. Only description and copyright details are optional; the rest must be completed to continue. Once you're done, click on Continue
- You'll be prompted to Sync your feed, then select Not now
- Click on Import & sync, and choose Import my podcast
- Locate and paste an RSS link from your host that includes all episodes of your show, and then click Continue
    - Most hosting platforms provide your RSS feed under Settings, Sharing, or Distribution
    - Please note that only audio posts will be imported
- Adjust your Import settings
    - You can choose to either Save as draft in Library or Publish automatically for your episodes
    - Select the audience for your episodes — You can change this for each episode before publishing
- Click Done
- You will be asked to verify your email as part of the import process
- Confirm the code and click Next
- You can choose where members can listen to your podcast. The [Patreon RSS](https://support.patreon.com/hc/en-us/articles/213557023-Enable-audio-RSS-feeds-for-my-members) will be turned on by default — this ensures your episodes appear in members' RSS feeds. If you're using Patreon RSS, you can also turn on Spotify integration and enable [Synced Feeds](https://support.patreon.com/hc/en-us/articles/35332949768717-Spotify-Synced-Feeds-for-Patreon-creators), which allows your members to listen to your paid episodes on Spotify, and non-members will have the option to join your Patreon to unlock your exclusive episodes
- Once we import your episodes, they will be saved as drafts in your [Library](https://www.patreon.com/library). You'll receive an email when they're ready for review
- On Desktop, click on Your account from the bottom-left corner and then select Settings
- In the Creator settings section, select [Podcasts and audio](https://www.patreon.com/settings-creator/audio)
- Select a podcast from the list
- Click on Import & sync, then select Import my podcast
- Locate and paste an RSS link from your host that includes all episodes of your show, and then click Continue
    - Most podcast hosting platforms provide your RSS feed URL within their settings or dashboard
    - Please note that only audio posts will be imported
- Adjust your Import settings
    - You can choose to either Save as draft in Library or Publish automatically for your episodes
    - Select the audience for your episodes — You can change this for each episode before publishing
- Click Done
- You will be asked to verify your email as part of the migration process
- Confirm the code and click Next
- Once we import your episodes, all episodes will be saved as drafts in your [Library](https://www.patreon.com/library). You'll receive an email when they're ready for review

Review and Publish Your Episodes

Once the migration begins, you’ll be redirected to the Drafts tab in the Library, where you can track its progress. If you’re migrating a large number of episodes, it may take a few minutes to start. After the migration is complete, refresh the page to view your imported episodes.

We aim to bring over all the information from your original hosting provider, including Tier and Release Date where applicable. You can review each draft individually by clicking on it to confirm the data was imported correctly and update details such as the description, title, or any other details if needed.

When you’re satisfied with the drafts, you can bulk select them from the Library page and click Publish.

Published episodes will retain their original publish dates, ensuring they appear in the correct order in fans’ libraries and RSS feeds. Fans will not receive notifications when these episodes are published.

Make sure you have RSS feed enabled for your members so your episodes appear in their RSS apps. If you’re using Patreon RSS, you can also turn on the Spotify integration, which allows non-members to join directly on Spotify to unlock episodes

FAQ

  • Migrating is a one-time import of your existing back catalog. It’s ideal if you want to bring over past episodes in one go and start publishing directly on Patreon moving forward.
  • Syncing keeps your podcast connected to your original host. New episodes are automatically imported to Patreon as you publish them, and any changes you make are reflected on Patreon. Learn more about Syncing an existing feed to Patreon.
  • We’ve made the decision with Acast to discontinue our integration as of May 30th, 2025.
  • If you’re currently managing your Patreon podcast with Acast RSS, you can use the Importing feature to migrate your episodes to Patreon’s native RSS. This allows you to manage episodes directly on Patreon and enables Spotify integration for your podcast.
  • You can find instructions on how to migrate from Acast RSS to Patreon RSS here. This article also outlines the reasoning behind this change, what we’re building in the coming year, and the next steps you can take as a creator to ensure that your members’ access to your podcast and RSS feed is uninterrupted.
  • No, any episodes you import to Patreon will continue to exist on their original platform, and their reviews will remain intact. Importing to Patreon does not affect your podcast’s presence on other services.
  • No, we do not import analytics or listener data from your existing platform. Metrics such as total listens, geographic audience distribution, and other insights will start fresh on Patreon.
  • Yes, you can set access permissions for imported episodes just like any other post on Patreon. You can choose which membership tiers have access, allowing you to control who can listen.

RSS feed security & protection

RSS Feed Security & Protection

Patreon’s RSS feature allows members to listen to a creator’s audio podcast using their preferred podcast app, without needing to log in to Patreon via our app or mobile web. This makes it easier for fans to enjoy your content while keeping it secure.

That said, sharing a custom RSS link with others to give free access to member-only content is a violation of our Terms of Service.

How RSS Links Work

  • Private RSS links are unique to each member
  • Each feed contains the member’s information, so only registered members with an active pledge can use it
  • If a pledge becomes inactive, the feed stops working until the pledge is renewed

Protecting Your Work

We monitor how many devices and/or podcast apps are using each RSS link. If usage numbers are higher than usual, it may indicate that a member is sharing their link with others.

To safeguard your content:

  • We automatically reset any RSS link that appears to be shared, so anyone else using it loses access
  • If this happens a second time, the member suspected of sharing their link will have their comment and DM privileges suspended for 7 days
  • Continued unusual activity will prompt our Trust and Safety team to take further action to protect your work

Currently, Patreon does not support passwords as a second security layer on the RSS feed. Many podcast apps do not support this feature, and those that do often require openly sharing your account password, which can create security risks. Some apps also cache feed information to make it easier for members to access a podcast later, which could unintentionally share a member’s RSS feed.

Reporting Shared RSS Links

If you discover that a member is sharing their custom RSS link, please email Patreon Support with the following information:

  • The member’s name and email (or URL to their Patreon account). If that’s not possible, provide the RSS link and where it was shared
  • A link to where you found the shared RSS feed

Set up a podcast on Patreon

You can create one or more podcast shows on Patreon, each with its own unique RSS feed. This guide walks you through how to create and manage podcast shows directly on Patreon, whether you’re just getting started or organizing multiple series.

How to create a podcast

  • On Desktop, click on Your account from the bottom-left corner and then select Settings
  • In the Creator settings section, select Podcasts and audio
  • Click on the New podcast button
  • You’ll be prompted to Sync your feed, then select Not now. If you host your podcast elsewhere, you can also Migrate from another platform and/or Sync with another platform. If you want to go that route, check their dedicated guides instead
  • Fill in your podcast details. The podcast settings include information used on both Patreon and for your RSS feed:
    • Cover Artwork: Upload your podcast cover image. Recommended size: 3000x3000 px (square image)
    • Title: Choose a clear, descriptive title that’s easy for listeners to search for
    • Description: Briefly describe your podcast content
    • Author Name: This will appear as the creator’s name on podcast platforms
    • Author Email: Enter the email address associated with your podcast. This email will be visible in the RSS feed. It’s recommended to use an email where listeners can send questions and comments
    • Podcast Type:
      • Episodic: Other podcast apps will update this show with the most recent episode shown first, but fans can enjoy episodes in any order. The Patreon feed won’t change
      • Serial: Other podcast apps will update this show with the most recent episode shown at the end. Choose this option when you want fans to enjoy your podcast in the order it’s published. Existing episodes will be assigned a number based on the publish date. The Patreon feed won’t change
    • Explicit Content: Toggle this on if your podcast contains explicit language. Podcasts with explicit content may not appear in all regions. Learn more about Podcast explicit content here.
    • Category: Select the category that best describes your podcast. This helps listeners find your show
    • Copyright: Enter the copyright details, including the active years, owner’s name, and company name (if applicable)
    • Language: Select the language your podcast is in
  • Click Continue
  • Click on Distribution to choose how members can listen:
    • On Patreon: By default, fans can listen to episodes directly on Patreon, both on desktop and on the mobile app
    • On Spotify: If you choose to enable the integration, fans can listen in the Spotify app. Learn more about how to Share your podcast on Spotify. You can also merge your public and Patreon feeds into a single, seamless experience with Spotify Synced Feeds to drive discovery and membership growth
    • If you host your public episodes on Patreon, you can also share your public RSS on Apple Podcasts, so anyone can listen to your free Patreon episodes
    • Other podcast apps: Via private RSS link. Learn more about how to Enable audio RSS
  • Click Done

Set up multiple podcasts

A combined feed, or a super-feed, is one RSS feed that brings together episodes from all of your podcast shows on Patreon. If you’re creating more than one podcast show, you can split your content into separate themes or series, each with its own feed.

Key things to know
  • Each new show has its own RSS feed
  • Your original podcast remains its own show — it doesn’t turn into the combined feed
  • Existing members will see the combined feed by default when adding to podcast apps, however, this is not yet supported in Spotify
  • You can manage episodes individually and assign them to specific podcasts
Steps to create multiple podcasts
  • Create a new podcast following the steps from the How to create a podcast section above
  • After creating your new shows, you’ll see a combined feed appear that includes all shows, and your original show will remain
  • To move episodes into your new podcasts, use your Library – An episode can only belong to one podcast show at a time
Inform your fans

Let your audience know about the new shows and where to find them. Example message:

“We’re using Patreon’s multiple podcast feature to better organize our content! You can now subscribe to separate feeds based on the shows you love most. If you have any issues accessing episodes, let us know!”

Add and manage your episodes

Once your podcast show is set up, you can start adding new episodes by creating an audio or video post. Each post can be assigned to a specific podcast show, and it will appear in your members’ RSS feeds based on your access settings.

If you upload a video file, Patreon will automatically extract the audio and include it in your podcast’s RSS feed.

Add a new episode
  • On Desktop, click on Create from the left-side navigation menu
  • Select either an Audio or Video post type — both formats can be distributed via RSS
  • Upload a video or audio file
    • If you upload a video file, Patreon will automatically generate an audio-only version for your RSS feed
    • To ensure your file meets Patreon’s technical requirements, click Media Guidelines in the top left corner of the upload screen
  • Add an Episode title (required)
  • Add a description if you’d like — this will appear as episode notes in RSS and is a great way to give listeners extra context
  • Select Add to podcast and choose the podcast show you want to add the episode to from the drop-down menu
  • You can choose No podcast if you don’t want the post to be added to a podcast and shared via RSS
  • Fill in optional episode settings:
    • Add an episode number and/or season
    • Select the episode type: Full, Trailer, or Bonus
    • Select whether your content is Explicit. Learn more about Explicit content for podcasts
  • Click Next, complete the rest of your post details, and then click Publish

You can also add new episodes directly from your Library by following the steps below:

  • From your Library, click on the Podcast dropdown menu
  • Select the show you want to add new episodes to
  • Click Add episodes in the top-right corner and choose New episode from the sub-menu
  • The post editor will open, then follow the steps from the Add a new episode section above
Move episodes between podcasts

Quickly reorganize your content by assigning episodes to a different podcast show or season. You can do this from your Library, whether you’re moving episodes individually or by podcast.

By episode

Best if you want to handpick individual episodes across different shows

  • Go to your Library from the left sidebar
  • Select the episodes you want to move
  • Click Edit > Edit podcast or season to assign episodes

By podcast

Best if you’re organizing a podcast at once

  • From your Library, click on the Podcast dropdown menu
  • Select the show you want to add move episodes to
  • Click Add episodes in the top-right corner, then choose Move episodes – An episode can only belong to one podcast show at a time
Edit or delete episodes

Update episode details, change access or pricing, or remove episodes entirely, all from your Library:

  • Edit episode details: Click More next to the episode and select Edit post
  • Edit price: If you selected to Sell this post in the Audience settings of the post, click Edit in the top-right corner of your Library, select Edit price, then set your desired price. Learn more about Selling your posts and collections
  • Delete episodes: Select the episodes and click Delete in the top-right corner

Update your podcast settings

You can return to your Podcast and audio settings anytime to update how your podcast looks, where it’s distributed, or to remove a podcast you no longer need.

  • On Desktop, click on Your account from the bottom-left corner and then select Settings
  • In the Creator settings section, select Podcasts and audio
  • Click on the show you want to update
  • Click on Settings to update your show’s title, cover image, description, and more
  • When you’re done, click Save

To adjust your distribution settings, select Distribution, and toggle the Spotify integration on/off, enable/disable the RSS feed, or enable/disable the option to let anyone listen to episodes on Apple Podcasts.

Delete a podcast

If you delete a podcast, episodes will remain published on Patreon as posts, but they’ll no longer be included in a podcast RSS feed.

  • On Desktop, click on Your account from the bottom-left corner and then select Settings
  • In the Creator settings section, select Podcasts and audio
  • Click on the show you want to delete
  • Click on Settings
  • Scroll down and click on the Delete your podcast toggle
  • Click on Delete
  • A pop-up will open, and if you’d like to also delete all episodes in this podcast, mark the checkbox
  • Confirm deletion by clicking on Delete podcast — This change cannot be undone

Member experience

  • Members can easily find their private RSS links in:
    • An email when they join your membership
    • The Podcast icon at the top of your creator page, just below your profile image
    • The Membership section of your page, under Listen in other podcast apps
    • The Collections tab on your creator page
  • If you distribute your episodes through Spotify, members can choose to listen on Spotify or use other podcast apps (via RSS). They also have the option to connect their Spotify accounts for quick access.
  • Based on their selection, a list of your available shows will appear, allowing them to add shows to Spotify or copy their RSS link to use in their preferred podcast app.
  • Members can access their private RSS links by visiting the creator’s homepage, tapping More at the top, and selecting Add to podcast app.
  • From there, members can choose their preferred podcast app (including Spotify) or manually copy the RSS link. Depending on what they select, they’ll be redirected to a list of all your shows available for that option.

Share my audio files with members

This article will take you through the steps of uploading audio and attaching audio files to any of your posts.

How to upload audio posts

You can upload audio files directly to Patreon from your device. These uploads will show up as an audio player. The uploaded audio will also populate in members’ RSS feeds if you enable audio RSS for your members.

Here’s how to upload audio for a post:
  • Click + from the left-hand navigation
    • If you also sell digital products, you’ll need to select Post from the drop-down list
  • Select Audio at the top of the post editor, then drag and drop your audio file or browse your computer to upload it
  • Add a title to your post (this is required). You can also start typing the description of your post (optional)
  • To customize your player box thumbnail, click the player box image and upload your own artwork
  • If you’re a podcaster, you can use the Add to podcast option to include this post in your RSS podcast feed, making it available to listeners on their favorite platforms. Learn more about Enabling audio RSS feeds for your members
  • You can schedule your audio as a drop, allowing fans to experience the content together with real-time chats. To enable this feature, make sure the Make this a drop toggle is turned on. Learn more about scheduling Drops
  • You can organize your work by adding Tags or adding your post to a Collection to help fans find more of what they want
  • Click Next to add additional publishing options like Post access, Preview settings and Fan activity
  • When you create an audio post by uploading an audio file from your device, you may be able to turn on audio previews for your post. Learn more about enabling and customizing audio previews.
  • On desktop, you can preview your post before publishing or scheduling your post by clicking the View Post button
Audio file specs
  • File upload size must be 2 GB or less
  • File attachments must be 5 GB or less
  • File formats: .aac, .mp3, .m4a, .mp4, .mpeg, .ogg, .wma, .wav, .x-m4a, .x-wav

By default, members can click the More on your audio posts to download audio files.

How to remove the download link on your audio post

The ability for members to download files from your audio posts is enabled by default, however, you can disable this feature at any point. To disable audio file downloads, go to the Posts and products settings of your Page builder, scroll down to the Audio Settings, and uncheck the box.

To learn more about your audio link settings, please visit hide download links from audio posts.

How to make an audio post with an embed URL

If you’ve enabled custom RSS links for members, audio posts uploaded with a URL (e.g., Soundcloud) will not populate on members’ feeds – only audio files uploaded directly to posts are hosted on members’ private feeds. The section above will help you with uploading an audio file directly.

You can link to audio players hosted on sites like Soundcloud via the link field. Follow these steps to share your hosted audio with members.

Here’s how to make an audio post with an embed URL:

Make sure you follow this guide while in your creator profile. You can switch to your creator profile by clicking on your name in the bottom-left corner of the home screen and selecting your Creator profile from the menu

  • Click on + from the left-hand navigation
  • Select Audio
  • Click on the Embed URL link
    • If you do not see this option, make sure the Make this a drop toggle is turned off. When this feature is enabled, you can only upload audio posts from your device. For more details on scheduling Drops, refer to our Drops guide
  • Enter your URL in the textbox field. An audio player will populate
  • The artwork on your audio player is dictated by whatever artwork you’ve uploaded to the third-party audio host. You cannot change the thumbnail artwork directly from Patreon
  • You can organize your work by adding Tags or adding your post to a Collection to help fans find more of what they want
  • On desktop, you can preview your post before publishing or scheduling your post by clicking the View Post button

We use embed.ly for embedded audio players. You can test your URL to ensure that your player will work. Add your URL in the field and click the arrow button. If you find an error in the type field, your URL will not post properly.

Attaching an audio file to any post

You can add audio file attachments to any post, no matter the featured media type.

What audio file types can I attach to posts?

Your audio file must be 5 GB or less, and in one of the following file formats: .aac, .mp3, .mp4, .m4a, .x-m4a, .mpeg, .ogg, .wma, .wav, and .x-wav files.

To attach your audio file, use the Upload button near the bottom of the post creator/editor. You’ll know your attachment is ready to post when the upload arrow disappears.

Your attachment will show as a link at the bottom of your published post.

If you have custom RSS feeds enabled for your members not all audio posts will populate in your members’ RSS feeds. You can learn more about how to Enable audio RSS feeds for members.

How do I post for certain members only?

You can set post access by creating/editing a post under Who can see this post? You can set your post access to:

  • Public: Anyone can access your post — Free and paid members, as well as non-members, whether logged in or not
  • All members: All free and paid members will be able to access your post. Non-members will see the content as locked
  • Paid members only: Everyone with a paid membership, regardless of tier, can access the post
  • Free members only: Only free members can access your post. Paid members won’t see these posts in their feeds, but the post will still be visible for non-members, locked and with an option to Join for Free to access the content
  • Selected tiers: You can manually choose which membership tiers have access
  • For purchase only: When you sell a post, you can choose the audience to be For purchase only. This means it does not have to be associated with a tier to sell, and both new fans and paid members can purchase that post

If you’re a per-creation creator, you cannot simultaneously charge members and make a post for specific tiers. You can find more information about how Posts work a little differently for you in the following article: How per creation billing works.

Share your podcast on Spotify

As a podcaster on Patreon, you can share your episodes directly to Spotify, giving fans a seamless listening experience and helping new audiences discover your show.

Whether you’re launching your first podcast or already building your audience, the Spotify integration makes it easy to manage distribution for your podcast(s) from your Patreon.

Before you start, make sure the Add to podcast option is turned on for any audio or video post you want to share through RSS. This setting is required for your episodes to appear on Spotify → Enable audio RSS feed for my members.

What you’ll learn

In this article, you’ll learn how to:

  • Connect your Patreon podcast to Spotify
  • Share both public and member-only episodes
  • Manage access and visibility across your posts
  • Use Synced Feeds to combine free and paid episodes

Learn how creator Midnight Burger doubled their Patreon earnings by turning on Spotify Synced Feeds here! Currently, Patreon for Creators is only available in English.

Before you start

Before connecting to Spotify, you’ll first need a podcast set up on Patreon. You don’t need a Spotify account to complete this setup, only a creator account on Patreon. If you haven’t created a podcast yet, learn how in Create and manage podcasts on Patreon.

💡 Tip: Use a desktop browser for setup.

Find your Distribution options
  • On desktop, click on Your account from the bottom-left corner, select Settings, then open Podcast and audio
  • Click the podcast you want to connect
  • Select the Distribution card

The Distribution page lets you choose how members can listen to your podcast, across three channels:

  • Spotify — with three options: let members listen to exclusive episodes, let anyone listen to public episodes, or combine both into one show
  • Apple Podcasts — share your public episodes to Apple Podcasts and other podcast apps
  • RSS — find links to your public and member-only RSS feeds

Let members listen to your exclusive episodes on Spotify

This connects your member-only episodes to Spotify, so members can link their Patreon accounts and listen there. This includes both public and member-only episodes, depending on the access settings you’ve chosen for each post.

💡 Tip: When you sync with Spotify, only posts with Add to podcast turned on will be shared.

  • On the Distribution page, under Spotify, toggle on Let members listen to exclusive episodes
  • A pop-up will appear — click Continue, review the podcast information that will be shared with Spotify (title, description, cover art, and more), and continue through the prompts
  • Click Sync with Spotify to start syncing your episodes
  • Future audio or video posts with Add to podcast enabled will also sync automatically

Once syncing starts, Patreon will create a new Spotify show for your podcast. If you already have a public show on Spotify, this new show will host your Patreon-exclusive content separately. You don’t need to manually submit your RSS link — once synced, your Patreon-hosted podcast appears automatically on Spotify for your members.

Syncing usually completes within 30 minutes, though large shows can take longer. You can refresh the page to check progress. If you edit or delete episodes on Patreon, those changes will automatically apply to Spotify.

What happens when syncing starts
  • Audio from video posts is automatically extracted and shared with your members on Spotify
  • Only audio and video posts are distributed to Spotify. Shop items and other content types won’t appear there
  • We recommend adding a note in your podcast description to let listeners know that available episodes depend on their membership tier

Let anyone listen to your public episodes on Spotify

If you host public episodes on Patreon, you can share them to Spotify so anyone can listen — and share previews of your exclusive episodes to turn more listeners into members. On the Distribution page, under Spotify, select Let anyone listen to public episodes and follow the steps:

  • Log in to Spotify for Creators — Open Spotify for Creators
  • Add your public episodes to Spotify — in Spotify for Creators, go to Add a new show → Find an existing show → Somewhere else, then copy and paste the link Patreon provides to verify you own the show
  • Share your Spotify show link — in Spotify for Creators, copy your public show link from your Settings, paste it back into Patreon, and we’ll add it to your Patreon page

Combine your exclusive and public episodes (Synced Feeds)

Synced Feeds combines your member-only and public episodes into one Spotify show, to help promote your exclusive episodes to non-members. When activated, non-members see your exclusive content as a padlock with a Bonus tag, prompting them to link their Patreon and join your membership.

💡 Tip: Synced Feeds isn’t available for creators who host their public episodes on Spotify for Creators, and can only be activated and managed on the Spotify for Creators website (not the mobile app).

On the Distribution page, under Spotify, select Combine your exclusive and public episodes and follow the steps:

  • Connect your member-only episodes to Spotify — turn on Let members listen to exclusive episodes (the step above)
  • Connect your public episodes to Spotify — if you host public episodes on Patreon and they’re not on Spotify yet, set that up now; if you host them elsewhere, use the RSS link from your host to verify you own the show on Spotify
  • Combine all episodes into a single feed — in Spotify for Creators (on web), select your public (free) show from the list on the left, go to Episodes → Synced Feeds, and approve or manually select episode pairs

For more detail, visit our guide to Spotify Synced Feeds for Patreon creators.

Manage your episodes

Once your podcast is synced with Spotify, your episodes on Patreon will be mirrored on your Spotify page. What’s visible on Spotify depends on how you set access for each post on Patreon:

  • Only audio and video posts with Add to podcast enabled are shared to Spotify
  • Any edits or deletions you make to those posts on Patreon are automatically applied on Spotify
  • Access settings on Patreon determine who can listen on Spotify

FAQ

  • In order to make your podcast available on Spotify, Spotify needs the information necessary to create and populate a page for your podcast on Spotify.
  • To that end, when you sync your podcast with Spotify, you are sending to Spotify your podcast title, description, cover artwork, author name, public author email address, and all of your existing episodes on Patreon, including the text for those posts.
  • You are also choosing to share all of your future audio posts with Spotify, including the text for those posts.
  • For paid members
  • After members link their accounts to Spotify, your posts will show as unlocked for them according to the tier they are in. The tier permission is done at the post level on Patreon.
  • Feel free to refer to Managing access to your posts to learn more about setting post access.
  • If you set your posts to Everyone, everyone can listen to your content on Spotify, regardless of whether they have a membership or a Patreon account.
  • For non-members
  • If you set up the Spotify integration, your Patreon episodes will be distributed to a new Spotify page that hosts all of the Patreon-exclusive content. Only members can enjoy these episodes on Spotify.
  • When you activate Synced Feeds, non-members will see your content as a padlock with a Bonus tag, prompting the listener to link their Patreon to Spotify and sign up for a membership. This can be a great way to promote your Patreon to a wider audience!
  • Yes, members will need to link their Patreon accounts to access your episodes on Spotify. They will be able to do this on Spotify after you’ve turned on Let members listen to exclusive episodes in your Distribution settings.
  • Members will only have access to the podcast episodes that are available on their tier. Learn more about how your members can listen to your content on Spotify.
  • You don’t need a Spotify for Creators account to let members listen to your exclusive episodes. You will need one to share your public episodes or to combine your feeds with Synced Feeds.
  • In your podcast’s Distribution page, under Spotify, toggle off Let members listen to exclusive episodes. After the change, all your Patreon-exclusive episodes will no longer show up on Spotify.
  • Only audio/video posts with the Add to podcast setting enabled in the post editor will be available to listen to on Spotify
  • Yes, you will be able to turn on the Spotify integration even if you’re not on a paid Patreon plan.
  • To manage which audio/video posts are available on Spotify, you can adjust the Add to podcast setting for each individual post. By turning off this option in the post editor, the episode will be removed from your members’ RSS feed and your Spotify page.
