  • Any analytics data related to Patreon-exclusive episodes that fans listen to on Spotify will be available on Spotify for Creators if you claim your Spotify page. Learn more about Linking and promoting your paid podcast.
  • If the episodes are locked on Patreon, that will also be the case on Spotify. Once their membership term ends, members no longer have access to paid episodes on Spotify. This is also true if a member cancels or their payment method declines.
  • When a member cancels, access will be revoked according to the billing model you’ve chosen for your Patreon page:
    • If monthly (non-charge upfront) or per creation, members immediately lose access to the paid episodes
    • If charge upfront or subscription billing, access to paid episodes will be revoked at the end of a member’s final billing cycle
    • If the member is on an annual membership, access to paid episodes will be revoked when their yearly membership ends
  • You can check if the member’s payment is in good standing and if they are in the correct membership option to unlock Spotify content by going to your Relationship manager.
  • If you’ve verified the above and they continue to run into difficulties, feel free to send them the following article: Listen to Patreon exclusive audios on Spotify. The article FAQ includes troubleshooting for different issues that may arise.
  • It’s important to note that only audio or video posts that have Add to podcast enabled are mirrored on Spotify; other types of posts won’t be visible there.

Spotify Synced Feeds for Patreon creators

If you host a paid podcast on Patreon and offer a free version on Spotify, Synced Feeds allows you to merge them into a seamless listening experience. This feature makes it easier for listeners to discover your content while ensuring paid members can access their exclusive episodes—all in one place.

Before you begin syncing your feeds, please make sure you have an existing show in your Podcasting and Audio settings on Patreon and that Spotify distribution is enabled. You’ll need access to your Spotify for Creators dashboard and to be logged in to the account for your show.

For common FAQs and to learn more about how Synced Feeds works, check out Spotify’s Synced Feeds article.

Prefer video? Watch how to enable Synced Feeds and connect your public Spotify show with your paid Patreon feed so listeners see the right episodes in one place.

What is Synced Feeds?

If you host a paid podcast on Patreon and offer a free version on Spotify, they typically appear as separate shows. This can make it harder for listeners to find your content and limit visibility for your paid offerings. Synced Feeds helps by allowing you to:

  • Combine your free and paid podcast feeds into one Spotify page
  • Automatically match episodes between your free and paid versions
  • Show different content based on the listener’s status:
    • Non-subscribers: see all free episodes, locked bonus content, and subtle prompts to upgrade to your paid subscription
    • Paid subscribers: see all premium content, including bonus episodes and any free episodes that weren’t duplicated in the paid feed

This setup ensures free and paid listeners get the right experience while encouraging free listeners to upgrade.

Who Can Use Synced Feeds?

Synced Feeds is designed for creators who offer both free and paid versions of their podcast. If you’re a Patreon creator, here’s what you need to be eligible:

  • Host your paid podcast on Patreon and distribute it to Spotify
  • Claim both your free and paid podcasts in Spotify for Creators using the same Spotify account
  • Don’t host your podcasts with Spotify for Podcasters—both your free and paid shows must be hosted elsewhere and distributed to Spotify

How to Activate Synced Feeds

Learn how creator Midnight Burger doubled their Patreon earnings by turning on Spotify Synced Feeds here! Currently, Patreon for Creators is only available in English.

  • On Desktop, click on Your account from the bottom-left corner and then select Settings
  • In the Creator settings section, select Podcasts and audio
  • Select the show you want to activate Synced Feeds
  • Click Distribution
  • Turn on the toggle to Let members listen to exclusive episodes, if it isn’t already
    • A message will appear stating that the Initial sync to Spotify is in progress — Your podcast will be synced with Spotify and might take some time to appear
    • Make sure both your free and paid podcast versions are distributed to Spotify
  • After, click on Combine your exclusive and public episodes and follow the instructions

On Spotify:

  • Log in to Spotify for Creators on a web browser (this feature isn’t available on mobile)
  • If you don’t already have a podcast on Spotify, open the dropdown in the upper right-hand corner of the dashboard by clicking your account image and selecting Add a new show
  • Select Find an existing show > Somewhere else and paste the link copied from Patreon into the RSS feed link
  • Once your show is added, select your free podcast from the list on the left. You must select your free show to access the Synced Feeds onboarding flow
  • Go to Episodes > Synced Feeds
  • Click Learn More and follow the on-screen steps to activate it

Once enabled, Spotify will start matching episodes between your free and paid feeds.

Managing Episode Pairs

You must select your free show in Spotify for Creators to manage Synced Feeds.

Approve suggested episode pairs:
  • Go to Episodes> Synced Feeds> Pending
  • Select the episodes you want to approve
  • Click Approve Pairs
Edit existing pairs:
  • Go to Episodes> Synced Feeds> Approved
  • Click the edit icon next to a pair
  • Find the correct episodes and click Confirm
Manually add a new pair:
  • Go to Episodes> Synced Feeds> Approved
  • Click Add Pair
  • Find the correct episodes and click Add pair

Changes may take some time to appear on Spotify.

Once your feeds are linked, you can manage synced episodes via Episodes > Synced Feeds in your Spotify for Creators dashboard. There, you can approve suggested episode pairs and ensure your paid and free content is properly aligned.

Editing Your Subscriber Benefits

Your subscriber benefits are displayed on your podcast’s Spotify page, helping potential subscribers see what they’ll get. To update them:

  • Log in to Spotify for Creators
  • Select your free podcast
  • Go to Settings > Synced Feeds
  • Update your benefits and click Save

Turning Off Synced Feeds

If you decide to disable Synced Feeds:

  • Log in to Spotify for Creators
  • Select your free podcast
  • Go to Settings > Synced Feeds and click Turn Off

Once turned off, your free and paid podcasts will revert to their original, separate feeds on Spotify. If you reactivate Synced Feeds later, you’ll need to set up your episode pairs from scratch.

Sync an Existing Feed to Patreon

You can automatically sync podcast episodes from your existing host to Patreon. This is useful if you publish free episodes elsewhere and paid ones on Patreon—syncing lets you show all your episodes in one place. Visitors can sample your work before subscribing, and members can access everything easily.

Looking to move your full back catalog to Patreon in one go instead? That’s a one-time import — see Migrating audio from an external host.

Key Things to Know

  • Your podcast stays hosted and distributed through your hosting platform
  • This is an ongoing sync, not a one-time migration. Once you sync your podcast, Patreon will continuously check for new episodes on your original hosting platform
  • New episodes will automatically sync to Patreon. You can choose whether they’re published right away or saved as drafts in your Library for review before publishing
  • Only audio posts will be synced — video posts in your RSS feed won’t be imported

Syncing vs. importing: Syncing keeps an ongoing connection to your host, so new episodes keep flowing into Patreon automatically. Importing is a one-time move of your existing episodes. Both start from the same place on your podcast — this article covers syncing; for a one-time import, see Migrating audio from an external host.

How to sync your podcast

💡 Tip: Use the desktop web experience for setup.

  • Click on Your account → Settings → Podcast and audio, then either:
    • Click + New podcast to create one — after filling in your details and clicking Continue, you’ll see Bring your public episodes to Patreon. Click Continue to sync (or Not now to start fresh — you can set up syncing later)
    • Or open an existing podcast and select the Import & sync card. The first time, you’ll be asked “I would like to…” — choose Sync my podcast (choosing Import my podcast instead starts a one-time import)
  • On the Find your podcast screen, search for your public show by typing its name, or paste your RSS feed URL
    • Please note that only audio posts will be imported
    • Most hosting platforms provide your RSS feed under Settings, Sharing, or Distribution — it’s usually the same feed your listeners use on Spotify and other apps
  • Patreon will verify that you own the show. Select your podcast and click Continue
  • Choose your Sync settings (you can adjust these later, and change access for individual episodes):
    • After syncing episodes… choose Save as draft in Library (review before publishing) or Publish automatically
    • Who can access these episodes? — for example, Paid members only. You can change this for each episode before publishing
    • Send notifications — members are notified based on their notification settings. This doesn’t apply to the episodes synced during initial setup
  • Once you’re done, your episodes will start syncing

Make sure you have RSS feed enabled for your members so your episodes appear in their RSS apps. If you’re using Patreon RSS, you can also turn on the Spotify integration and enable Synced Feeds, which lets members listen to your paid episodes on Spotify and gives non-members the option to join your Patreon to unlock your exclusive episodes.

Once you start syncing, any episodes you’ve already published will be synced first. You can track the progress in your Library. When syncing is complete, you’ll receive both a notification and an email confirmation. From then on, you’ll get a notification and an email each time a synced episode is successfully published or added to your drafts.

Manage and publish your synced episodes

Your podcast’s episodes appear on its page under Episodes, split into Published and Drafts tabs. You can also track progress in your Library. If you’re syncing a large number of episodes, it may take a few minutes to start — refresh the page once it’s complete to view your synced episodes.

You can take several actions—like updating access settings, editing titles, and publishing episodes—depending on the sync option you selected:

If you chose Save as drafts in Library:

Episodes will appear in the Drafts tab. From here you can:

  • Click on a draft to review its details and confirm everything synced correctly
  • Edit who can see your episodes by selecting multiple episodes and clicking Edit access
  • Click Publish to publish selected episodes when you’re ready
If you chose Publish automatically:

Episodes will appear in the Posts tab once published and will be available to your fans on Patreon. From here, you can:

  • Click on an episode to check details like the title, access settings, or pricing (if applicable)
  • Edit who can see your episodes by selecting multiple episodes and clicking Edit access
  • Move episodes to a different podcast or season by selecting them and clicking Edit

If you want to update things like audio or description, make changes to those episodes on the original platform—those updates will be synced to Patreon automatically.

Published episodes keep their original publish dates, so they’ll appear in the correct order for your fans. Whether fans receive notifications depends on your notification settings.

Update your sync settings

You can update your sync settings at any time. This is useful if you want to change how episodes are handled, adjust who gets access, or pause syncing.

  • Click on Your account → Settings → Podcast and audio
  • Open the podcast you synced and go to its Import & sync settings

From your Sync settings, you can:

  • Switch between Publish synced episodes immediately and Save synced episodes as drafts and publish manually
  • Update who can access these episodes (for example, Paid members only). You can change this for each episode before publishing
  • Choose whether to send notifications when new episodes are published
  • Sync now to manually trigger a sync — changes sync automatically every hour, but this pulls updates right away
  • Pause syncing to temporarily stop importing new episodes, or Stop syncing to end it altogether

Changes made here will apply to all existing and future synced episodes. Want to make changes to individual episodes? You can always edit them directly in your Library.

FAQ

  • Syncing keeps your podcast connected to your original host. New episodes are automatically brought into Patreon as you publish them, and any changes you make are reflected on Patreon.
  • Importing is a one-time move of your existing back catalog. It’s ideal if you want to bring over past episodes in one go and start publishing directly on Patreon moving forward. Learn more about migrating audio from an external host.
  • Yes, you can pause syncing in your Podcast and audio settings at any time.
    • No new episodes will be imported from your podcast host
    • Already-synced episodes will remain in your Library and won’t be affected
    • You can still edit, publish, or manage any previously synced episodes as usual
    • Syncing will resume where it left off if you decide to turn it back on later
    • Edits made to episodes on your external host while syncing is paused won’t appear on Patreon
  • No, we do not import analytics or listener data from your existing platform. Metrics such as total listens, geographic audience distribution, and other insights will start fresh on Patreon.
  • Yes, you can set access permissions for synced episodes just like any other post on Patreon. You can choose which membership tiers have access, allowing you to control who can listen.
  • No, you have control over this. When publishing a free episode, you can choose to hide it from paying members to avoid cluttering their feeds. This helps ensure your paid content stays front and center for subscribers.
  • Yes. When you sync your free episodes to Patreon, members can receive a combined feed that includes both free and paid episodes. By default, anyone already subscribed to your paid feed will automatically receive this unified feed—no extra setup required.

Troubleshooting common RSS errors with members

RSS links rely on 3rd party apps, so members may run into a few hiccups while trying to listen to your podcast. Below is a list of the common errors and how Patreon’s product support team troubleshoots them with members.

Common RSS errors and resolutions

If new episodes are no longer appearing or updating in their podcast app
  • Uninstall and reinstall your podcast app
  • Unsubscribe and resubscribe using the same custom RSS link that appears in your Membership section of the creator’s page
  • Refresh the feed on your podcast app. Many apps utilize the pull-down feature to refresh the feed or provide a button to refresh
Not finding the RSS link under Membership when it should be there?

They should try refreshing their page, clearing cache, or accessing the Membership tab using an incognito browser.

If troubleshooting steps don’t work

We recommend trying a different podcast app or RSS feed reader to subscribe, as not all RSS apps support every RSS link. To find out which ones work the best, you can review our article about how to use your custom audio RSS link. If this still doesn’t work, let us know, as it may be a problem with the feed itself.

Where do members copy and paste their RSS link?

Instructions on how to do this are on this guide on how to use your custom audio RSS.

RSS troubleshooting in the Patreon App

These are the general troubleshooting steps if your member is having issues listening to the episodes within the Patreon App.

  • Power off and then restart your device
  • Log out of your account on the Patreon app
  • Uninstall and then reinstall the Patreon app (latest versions linked below):
    • Patreon app for iOS
    • Patreon app for Android
  • Log back into the Patreon app
  • Check for and install any software updates available for your device

If you’re in an area with lower reception, try connecting to WiFi, which could result in some improvement.

Creators: Posting on Patreon

Bulk editing posts

With bulk editing, you can make changes to multiple posts simultaneously, saving you time and effort. This guide will show you how to use your Library page to easily update who can see your posts, add or delete tags, sell or delete multiple posts, and—if you’re a podcaster—organize episodes into seasons, all from one place

Bulk editing is currently only available on desktop.

Duplicate post drafts

To reuse a post format, go to the Library. Click More next to the draft you’d like to duplicate and then select Duplicate as draft. This is useful if you don’t want to rewrite your post from scratch again.

Edit tier access

Follow the steps below to update access for multiple posts:

  • On Desktop, select Creator studio from the left navigation
  • Click on Library to be taken to the Posts tab by default
    • To edit a Draft instead, select the Drafts tab from the top menu
  • Use the Filter or type in the Search box to locate specific posts. You can also sort posts by clicking on Title, Publish date (for published posts), or Last edited date (for drafts)
  • Checkmark the posts you want to edit
    • To select all posts, click the checkbox at the top. Click it again to unselect all
  • Once you have your selection, click Edit
  • Select Edit access
  • Choose who can view the selected posts
  • Once this is done, click Update
  • A message will appear, notifying you that your update will replace the existing settings. Click Confirm and update to apply the changes

Move episodes between podcasts

If you have a podcast and want to edit which show or season your episodes belong to, you can do this quickly from your Library.

You can move episodes individually or by podcast:

By episode

Best if you want to handpick individual episodes across different shows

  • On Desktop, select Creator studio from the left navigation
  • Click your Library to be taken to the Posts tab by default
  • Use the Filter to sort by Podcast episodes or shows, or the Search box to locate specific episodes — podcast episodes have the Podcast icon under the Post type column
  • Select the episodes you want to move
  • Click Edit > Edit podcast or season to assign episodes
By podcast

Best if you’re organizing a podcast at once

  • From Creator studio in the left navigation, open your Library and filter by a specific podcast
  • Click Add episodes in the top-right corner, then choose Move episodes

An episode can only belong to one podcast show at a time.

Edit Price

You can use the library feature to sell multiple posts at once. You can learn more about Selling posts and collections here.

  • On Desktop, select Creator studio from the left navigation
  • Click your Library to be taken to the Posts tab by default
    • You can only sell published posts
  • Use the Filter or type in the Search box to locate specific posts. You can also sort posts by clicking on Title and/or Publish date
  • Checkmark the posts you want to sell
    • To select all posts, click the checkbox at the top. Click it again to unselect all
  • Once you have your selection, click Edit
  • Select Edit price
  • Set the price for your posts and agree to the terms
  • Click Next
  • Confirm the changes

Edit tags

Follow the steps below to manage your post tags in bulk by adding or deleting tags across multiple posts:

  • On Desktop, select Creator studio from the left navigation
  • Click your Library to be taken to the Posts tab by default
    • To edit tags from a Draft instead, select the Drafts tab from the top menu
  • Use the Filter or type in the Search box to locate specific posts. You can also sort posts by clicking on Title, Publish date (for published posts), or Last edited date (for drafts)
  • Checkmark the posts you want to edit
    • To select all posts, click the checkbox at the top. Click it again to unselect all
  • Once you have your selection, click Edit
  • Choose either Add tags or Delete tags, depending on your needs
    • Add tags: Write the tags you want, and click Add for each tag or hit Enter
    • Delete tags: A list of your existing tags will show up. Click the X next to the ones you want to delete
  • Click Save

Delete posts

Follow the steps below to delete multiple posts:

  • On Desktop, select Creator studio from the left navigation
  • Click your Library to be taken to the Posts tab by default
    • To delete from a Draft instead, select the Drafts tab from the top menu
  • Use the Filter or type in the Search box to locate specific posts. You can also sort posts by Title, Publish date (for published posts), or Last edited date (for drafts)
  • Checkmark the posts you want to delete
    • To select all posts, click the checkbox at the top. Click it again to unselect all
  • Once you have your selection, click Delete
  • A message will appear, notifying you of the number of posts that will be deleted. It will also remind you that this action can’t be undone. Click Delete to confirm and proceed

Can I backdate my posts?

Yes! You can now organize your posts in the exact order you want them to appear on your members’ feeds by backdating your posts (i.e., Setting your post’s publication dates to the past). This tool is especially useful for sharing content that didn’t get posted on time or simply making sure your posts are presented in the order you prefer, ensuring your members see your content as intended.

How to backdate your posts

When creating a new post
- Click Create from the left navigation and select Post
- Add a title to your post (this is required)
- Depending on the type of post you want to create, use the options at the top of the editor.
- You can immediately start typing anything you’d like. This can be a description, an update, or something you want to share with your audience
- (Optional) Attach files to your post if you’d like to share downloadable content with your members.
- If you upload Audio or Video, you can:
    - Turn on the Add to podcast option to distribute your content through your members’ RSS feeds, allowing fans to listen to your content on their favorite platforms. Learn more about [enabling RSS feeds for your members](https://support.patreon.com/hc/en-us/articles/213557023-Enable-audio-RSS-feeds-for-my-members)
    - Schedule posts as a drop, letting fans experience content together with real-time chats. Ensure the Make this a drop toggle is turned on. Note that Drops are currently only available to creators in the [All Audiences](https://support.patreon.com/hc/articles/8304008537741-Categorizing-your-Patreon) category — Learn more about in our [Drops guide](https://support.patreon.com/hc/articles/23852353339917-Drops-Early-access)
- In the right side editor, toggle the Set publish date option and select your publish date and time
- If you don’t want to notify members, go to the Email and notifications section in the right-side editor, and toggle off Allow members to be notified when this post is published
- Click the Publish button at the top of the page, and you're all set!
- Tap Create from the bottom menu and select Post
- The post editor will open, then add a title to your post (this is required)
- Depending on the type of post you want to create, use the options at the top of the editor.
- You can immediately start typing anything you’d like. This can be a description, an update, or something you want to share with your audience
- Tap Settings in the top menu
- Tap Publish date, and toggle Set publish date
- Select your publish date and time
- Tap Publish in the top right corner to confirm
When editing a published post
- Select Creator studio from the left navigation and click [Library](https://www.patreon.com/library)
- In the [Posts](https://www.patreon.com/posts/published) tab, you can find all your published and scheduled posts
- Scheduled posts will be at the top of the list, and include “Scheduled” below the Publish date — Locate the post you want to edit and click on it
- The Post editor will open, and you'll be able to make any necessary changes
- If you want to adjust the release date, go to Set publish date and change the publish date and time
- Click the Update button to save your changes
- Tap Profile on the bottom menu
- Tap Manage posts
- Tap the post you want to edit — Scheduled posts will be at the top and include text above that reads: “Scheduled for [date] at [time]”
    - Tapping on the scheduled post of your choice will allow you to continue editing that post, including the date and time of publishing
- To adjust the date, first tap on Settings in the top menu
- In the Publish date option, toggle Set publish date and adjust the publish date and time
- Tap the Save button to confirm the changes

Comment settings

This article will help you manage comment settings for your Patreon posts and Quips, including who can comment and how to filter out potentially harmful comments.

Comment access

Comment access is controlled at the post level. You can set who can comment when creating or editing any Post or Quip.

The default for new public posts is Anyone can comment, but you can adjust this before publishing. This does not apply to paid-access posts, which keep their existing comment settings. Your choice will be saved as your default for future posts.

Existing posts keep their previous comment settings. You can update the comment settings on any existing post at any time through the post editor.

You can change comment access for your posts by following these instructions:

  • Comment access for posts is managed directly in the post editor.
    • Click on Create in the left-side navigation menu and select Post, or open an existing post to edit it
    • In the Post editor, go to the Settings in the right-side menu
    • Navigate to the More settings section and choose to Allow comments from the available options:
      • Anyone with access: Anyone with a Patreon account can comment on this post
      • All members: Only members (free and paid) can comment
      • Paid members: Only paid members can comment
      • No one: Disable comments for this post
    • Click Publish when you’re done
  • Comment access for posts is managed directly in the post editor.
    • Tap Create in the bottom menu and select Post, or open an existing post to edit it
    • In the post editor, tap Settings from the top menu
    • Navigate to the More settings section and choose to Allow comments from the available options:
      • Anyone with access: Anyone with a Patreon account can comment on this post
      • All members: Only members (free and paid) can comment
      • Paid members: Only paid members can comment
      • No one: Disable comments for this post
    • Tap Publish when you’re done
  • Comment access for Quips is set directly in the Quip editor.
    • Start creating a Quip on Desktop or the App
    • Look for the Public setting above the keyboard (app) or in the bottom menu (desktop)
    • Choose from the available options:
      • Anyone can reply: Anyone with a Patreon account can comment on this post
      • All members: Only members (free and paid) can comment
      • Paid members: Only paid members can comment
      • No one: Disable comments for this Quip
    • Select Share when you’re done
Who can see comments?

Comment visibility depends on the comment settings you choose for each post. Only members with comment access can add a comment.

  • Anyone can reply: Anyone with a Patreon account can view and comment on the post
  • All members: Both free and paid members can view and comment on posts they have access to
  • Paid members: Both free and paid members can view comments, but only paid members can add comments
  • No one: Hides the comment section for all members on that post

Fans who have not yet joined your Patreon will not see the comment section on public posts until they do.

Disabling comments

You can disable or enable comments on any post individually through the Post editor, using the comment settings options above.

When editing a post, navigate to Settings in the right-side menu, and in the Allow comments from section, set it to No one to turn off comments. Changes apply to that post only and don’t affect other posts.

To disable comments on all posts, either new or published, go to the Page settings and in the Comment access section, select turn off comments. This will hide existing comments on all of your posts.

Bulk editing comment settings

You can update comment settings for multiple posts at once on Desktop. Here’s how:

  • On Desktop, select Creator studio in the left-side navigation menu
  • Click on Library from the sub-menu
  • Select the Posts tab
  • Check the boxes next to the posts you want to update
  • Click Edit in the menu bar on the left
  • Select Edit commenting
  • Toggle Allow comments on or off for the selected posts

This also works for drafts by following the same steps and selecting your drafts from the Posts tab.

Please note that bulk editing comment settings is not available for Quips.

What happens when I disable comments for a post?

Members will see a note indicating that comments have been disabled for that post. If members have already added comments on a post and you later disable comments, they’ll see the same note. However, you’ll still be able to see past comments.

Comment Auto-moderation

Comment filtering automatically hides most common types of spam and harmful comments, including threats and hate speech, made by free members who don’t meet our Community Guidelines, before it reaches your community.

The automated moderation is enabled by default for creators who have allowed comments, and you can adjust the level of filtering you’d like for your posts and Quips.

Please note that comment filtering applies exclusively to free members and can be adjusted only on Desktop.

Here’s how to adjust the level of filtering:

  • On Desktop, select Creator studio in the left-side navigation menu and go to your Dashboard
  • Click on Moderation Hub from the sub-menu
  • Go to the Auto-moderation tab
  • In the Comment Auto-moderation section, choose between:
    • Off: Our spam filter remains on, but all other comments will be shown
    • On: We will filter out harmful and spammy comments, but there is a chance that some comments are mistakenly hidden or left up
  • Changes are automatically saved

To report a creator or member for a guidelines violation:

  • Log in to your Patreon account and go to their Patreon page
  • From there, select More to present the option to report them
  • You can also find the reporting tool on any creator’s post, member’s comment, or message by clicking More and selecting Report this content

If you’d like to block a member, please see our guide on Everything you need to know about blocking another user.

Allow media in comments (Early access)

In addition to Comment access and Comment Auto-moderation, your Page Settings include an option to allow your members to attach images to their comments.

This is an early access feature, rolling out automatically to a limited number of creator communities — there’s nothing you need to do to request it. If you have this enabled, the Allow media in comments toggle is turned on by default, and you’ll find it in the same Page Settings section as your other comment settings.

Turning this off only affects new comments going forward — any images members have already added to comments will remain visible.

For now, this only applies to comments made through the Patreon mobile app.

FAQ

  • By default, all new public posts are set to Anyone with access. You can change this in the post editor before publishing. Once you adjust the setting, it will be saved as your default for future posts. When publishing a paid post, you may be prompted to update your comment access, depending on your post audience. Select a new option to continue.
  • No. Existing posts keep their comment settings as before. If you want to update the comment settings on an older post, you can do so by opening it in the post editor and adjusting the Comment access setting.
  • Comment access can be set to anyone with access, all members, paid members, or no one. It is not currently possible to restrict comment access to specific tiers.
  • You’ll be able to see auto-moderated comments, but they will not be visible to anyone else.
  • Yes. You’ll see a message that the comment has been filtered because it may be spammy or harmful to your community, and you’ll be able to expose the comment to see it yourself. Only you and the commenter can see the content of the comment.
  • Yes, filtered comments will count toward the comment total for posts.
  • Yes, it applies to both posts and Quips. You can adjust your filtering level in your Desktop creator view by going to Page Settings, then scrolling down to the Comment Auto-moderation.
  • If you’ve enabled comments for a post, and the member should have comment access, there are a couple of reasons why they are unable to add a comment:
    • Our team is checking their account to keep Patreon safe
    • They may have posted too many comments recently
    • They may be suspended
  • You can tell the member to retry later, and feel free to share our member commenting help article for members.

Control Text Previews for Member Email Notifications

Get more members engaging with your text posts! You can now control how your new text posts are shown in email notifications for your members.

By default, email notifications for text posts include a short preview of the post, encouraging members to visit your site or app for the full content. If preferred, you can change the settings to include the entire post in the emails. Either way, you’re in charge of how your content is shared. Read on to learn more.

How it works

When creating a text post on Desktop, go to the Settings menu on the right side to find the Emails and notifications controls. In the Email options for members with access section, you can select to Show preview only or Show full post. This allows you to choose whether members will see the full content of your text post directly in their email notifications or need to visit your page to read the full post.

Show preview only is currently selected by default. This means that when you create a new text post and don’t change this option, the notification email sent to members for that post will be preview-only. Choosing Show full post means the entire post text is shown instead of just a preview when members receive an email notification for that post.

Once you change this option, the preference will be saved as the default for future posts, and you can change it each time you create a new text post.

How does this look for members

When Show preview only is selected, members will be shown a short preview of your text post in their email, prompting them to visit the app or website to read the full version. Check below an example of what this looks like for your members:

Members who don’t receive the full version of text posts will be more likely to engage with the app or Patreon website, where they can take additional actions such as liking, commenting, or viewing more posts.

Drops

Drops are currently only available to creators in the All Audiences category.

This article provides instructions on how Drops work and how your members experience a drop. For frequently asked questions, please refer to Drops FAQ.

What you need to know about Drops

Drops give creators a way to provide shared experiences for their members right on Patreon, complete with a countdown and live chat.

When a creator drops their latest video or audio release:

  • They build hype with members with a countdown to the first release
  • Their members can watch or listen together and have conversations about the release right in the live chat

How to schedule a drop

  • On Desktop, select Create from the left navigation and select Post
  • Choose your media type: Audio or Video
  • From the right-hand side of the page, make sure the Make this a Drop toggle is on
  • If ready, upload your audio or video file. Alternatively, you can schedule a drop before your content is ready and upload it later by navigating to your posts in the Library
    • You can schedule your drop before your content is ready to upload. We recommend uploading your final content 24 hours before the drop time. If you are not able to upload the final content 2 hours before the drop time, our system will automatically move the drop to drafts
    • For video posts, you can edit the thumbnail — This is what we show your members starting at 2 minutes before the scheduled live drop and post-release
  • Add a title (required) and description (optional)
  • If desired, add your drop to a collection and/or add tags to help you organize your work
  • Select the date and time of the drop under Make this a drop
  • You can also add a cover image for your drop. This is what we show your members when the drop is published until 2 minutes before the drop time
  • Under Audience, select All members if you want the drop to be available to all your members or Paid Access if you want only paid members to be able to access the content.
    • Under More options for Paid Access, you can select which tiers can view this drop.
    • At this time, Drops are available for All members, Paid members only, or Selected tiers
  • If you want, you can set an audio or video preview that will be shared after the live drop
  • When you’re finished, select Schedule drop

Once your drop is scheduled, you can promote it on Patreon itself (e.g. a separate post or in Chats) and/or your socials (e.g. Instagram).

Note that all drops should abide by Patreon’s Community Guidelines, which act as the guardrails detailing the sorts of behaviors that are permitted and prohibited on Patreon.

Drops can only contain audio or video files. If you attach a different file type (i.e. PDF), you will not be able to post the drop.

How to edit a drop

Once a drop is scheduled, it will appear in your Library and can be edited at any time. To edit a drop, follow the steps below:

  • On Desktop, select Creator studio from the left navigation
  • Click your Library to be taken to your Posts
  • Use the Filter or type in the Search box to locate specific drops. You can also sort it by clicking on Title or Publish date
  • Easily identify drops by looking for Scheduled drop beneath the Publish date or by the icon beneath Post Type
  • Click the menu button in the top right corner of the drop. Then click on Edit post to make changes
  • After making the necessary edits to your drop, click Update to save the changes

How to delete a drop

You can delete your drops at any time from the Library. Please note that deleting a drop is permanent and will also result in the deletion of any comments and reactions to that drop.

  • On Desktop, select Creator studio from the left navigation
  • Click your Library to be taken to your Posts
  • Use the Filter or type in the Search box to locate specific drops. You can also sort it by clicking on Title or Publish date
  • Easily identify drops by looking for Scheduled Drop beneath the Publish date or by the icon beneath Post Type
  • Checkmark the drop(s) you want to delete
  • Once you have your selection, click Delete
  • A message will appear, notifying you of the number of posts that will be deleted. It will also remind you that this action cannot be undone. Click Delete post to confirm and proceed

Member experience

Creators can choose to drop to All members, Paid members only, or Selected tiers. Members who don’t have access to your drops will see the drop as locked, and they’ll be nudged to Join to unlock.

The different phases of the member experience described below are available on both the Patreon app and the web.

Pre-release

Once it is 7 days or less before the drop release, your members will see the preview of the drop, including your selected cover image and a countdown on both their homepage and when they click through to your page.

Your members can engage with the drop before its release by clicking on I’m interested—This action allows them to receive reminders about the drop and notifications for any comments you post before the release. They can also participate by commenting, viewing others’ comments, and reacting to them. These features are available on both the web and the Patreon app.

24 hours before the drop, the content will be featured at the top of your page to build anticipation and excitement. 2 minutes before the drop, all members will receive a push notification, letting them know your drop will go live. At this point, they can Join the drop, see the number of people who have also joined, and participate in the live conversation. When there are 10 seconds left, they’ll see a countdown until the content is released.

Live Drop

During a live drop, members can Join the drop and watch or listen, comment, and react in real-time directly underneath the drop content. Members who tapped I’m interested will receive a push notification, letting them know the drop is live.

As a creator, you can also join the live drop and engage in conversations with your community. While it’s not required, participating in the live drop is a fantastic way to connect with your fans on Patreon, making the experience exciting and engaging for everyone.

Post-release

After a drop finishes, your members will continue to have access to watch or listen, read existing comments, and react and comment themselves indefinitely, just like any other post on your Patreon.

Your drop will continue to be highlighted on your page for 24 hours after the drop, ensuring that your content remains visible and keeps your audience engaged. After 24 hours, the drop will appear alongside all of your other posts, in its place chronologically.

Looking for suggestions or helpful tips for upcoming Drops? Check out our article for Helpful tips for your Drops.

Editing your published posts

This article will take you through easily making changes to your posts by visiting your Library on Desktop, or visiting your Patreon on the iOS and Android App. When editing an already published post, be sure to save your post to go live with your edits.

How to edit posts

- Select Creator Studio from the left navigation
- Click on your [Library](https://www.patreon.com/posts/published) to be taken to the Posts tab by default
- Within the Posts tab or Drafts tab, you can:
    - Search for posts by name
    - Sort by Title and/or Publish date
    - Filter by post type, podcast, audience, tags or publish date - click the button to Apply your filter selections
- Checkmark the posts you want to edit
    - Click the Edit button to edit access, price, tags, and edit commenting
    - Click the Delete button to permanently delete the posts
- Depending on what you've selected, a pop-up will appear, and once you're done, click the Update or Save button to confirm your edits
- You can make additional changes to your post by clicking the menu , where you can View, Edit, Duplicate as draft, or Delete your post. Note that Duplicate as draft is only available on desktop
- If you select Edit, the editor will open letting you remove and upload new files, make changes to your post title or post body text, and add or remove the post from collections
- You'll see a Settings sidebar on the right, with controls for audience, collections, drops, scheduling, previews, comment access, and tags. Learn more about Post settings
- Tap on Profile on the bottom menu
- Tap Manage posts
- The Posts screen is where you can find your scheduled and published posts; in-progress posts live in the Drafts screen
- Swipe left on a post to quickly Edit or Delete it
- When you tap a scheduled post, you'll land directly on the post editor to make changes
- Tap the Settings at the top to open your post settings — here you'll find controls for audience, collections, comment access, tags, and more. Learn more about Post settings
- Tap Save. After this, you can choose whether to notify your members about the changes

Bulk editing posts

Bulk editing is currently only available on desktop and mobile web.

  • Select Creator studio from the left navigation
  • Click on your Library to be taken to the Posts tab by default
  • Within the Posts tab or Drafts tab, you can:
    • Search for posts by name
    • Sort by Title and/or Publish date
  • Checkmark the posts you want to edit
    • To select all posts, click the checkbox at the top. Click it again to unselect all
  • Once you have your selected posts, you can:
    • Click the Edit button to Edit access, Edit price, Edit tags or Edit commenting
    • Click the Delete button to permanently delete the posts
  • Click the Update or Save button to confirm your edits

If you use per-creation billing (Legacy) and you’ve checked the option to charge members for a post and delete that post within the same month, any pending member bills will be deleted. In this case, members won’t be charged if you delete your post within the same month it was created. It’s not possible to retroactively bill members for posts you’ve published as unpaid.

Flexible previews (Draggable paywall)

When creating a post on desktop with Paid access selected, you’ll see a draggable paywall in the body of your post. This lets you control which inline content — text, images, video, and audio inserted into your post body — is visible before and after the paywall.

How it works

  • All inline content above the paywall is free to anyone and will be visible to everyone
  • All inline content below the paywall is locked unless you have paid access (paid member or one-time purchase)
  • Attachments added to the post can’t be opened or downloaded unless you have paid access (paid member or one-time purchase)

The paywall only applies to inline content in the post body. Your header media visibility is controlled separately by your Audience settings — for example, you can have a paid post with a locked header video, while text and inline images above the paywall in the body remain free to everyone. Learn more about Setting posts access for your Patreon audience.

How to add a paywall to your post

  • Select Create from the left navigation and select Post
  • In the post settings on the right, select Paid access
  • Start typing and you’ll see a draggable paywall appear in the body of your post
  • Drag it to the position where you want paid content to begin
  • Everything above the paywall will be visible to everyone — everything below will be locked

You can also insert a paywall while drafting a public post, which will turn it into a paid post. Click the + icon on a new line and select Paywall, then drag it to your desired position.

Helpful tips for your drops

This guide offers tips and ideas to get started on your upcoming Drops, so you can make the most out of this feature. If you need help scheduling and managing your drops, check out our Drops guide instead.

Potential use cases for your upcoming drop

  • Recurring content: Weekly/bi-weekly/monthly podcast or vodcast episode, weekly Q&A, latest instructional video
  • Special content: Special podcast or vodcast episode (e.g., notable guest, recording from an in-person tour, etc.), latest single from your new album, comedy special

Tips as you get started

  • Strategize: Think through your upcoming content calendar to determine what could work well as a drop for your members
  • Plan: Schedule your drop at least 24-48 hours in advance to give your members a heads up and build buzz. Choose a day and time that works well for most of your audience
  • Promote: Pre-release, encourage your members to join the upcoming drop on and off platform
  • Engage: During the live drop, jump in the conversation to directly connect with your members, see their commentary on your latest work and get ideas for upcoming drops
  • Test and learn: Test an approach and incorporate your learnings into your future strategy

Additional helpful reminders

  • You can schedule a drop before your final content is ready to build excitement with your members. We suggest uploading your content 24 hours before the time of the drop
  • We recommend including a custom cover image so that the drop post is more visually engaging, which can help draw more interest from your members to join the live drop
  • Note that all drops should abide by Patreon’s Community Guidelines, which act as the guardrails detailing the sorts of behaviors that are permitted and prohibited on Patreon

How do I limit processing time for my videos?

If you’re looking to upload videos on Patreon, it’s important to know that while Patreon accepts most modern video formats and CODECs, certain types of videos might need a bit of tweaking to make sure they’re optimized for uploading.

This guide will walk you through the steps to standardize your content and help speed up the processing time when uploading videos on Patreon.

You can navigate away from the publishing flow while waiting for a video to process. Simply fill in the post details and publish your video post. The video will process in the background and publish automatically once finished.

You’ll be notified when your post is live. If there are any issues with processing or uploading, we’ll notify you about why it failed so you can make the necessary changes

Standard input specs

Standardizing your videos means ensuring they meet certain input specifications. This can help Patreon process your videos faster and reduce video upload failures.

Standard input has the following attributes:

  • 1080p/2K or smaller
  • H.264 video CODEC
  • 8Mbps or below (hard cap at 16Mbps)
  • AAC audio CODEC

Any format used outside the mentioned above is not ideal and may result in extremely slow upload times.

How to create standard input (mobile)

Most mobile devices capture H.264 8-bit 4:2:0 video by default. Here are the main things to watch out for:

  • Ensure that the total file bitrate is below 8 Mbps
  • Ensure the output file uses SDR (standard dynamic range) imaging. Some newer devices capture video in HDR (High Dynamic Range), which requires 10-bit 422 color and must be re-encoded by Patreon Video to support most devices
  • Ensure the output file is smaller than 1080p (1920x1080) or 2K (2048x1152). Some cameras shoot 4K video, which is currently converted down to 1080p when using Patreon Video
  • If possible, choose a keyframe interval of 5s or so, but certainly between 2 and 10 seconds, and enable closed-GOP encoding. (If you don’t see these options in your app or camera, it’s probably the default already)

iPhone camera

When you go to your iPhone settings (as of iOS 17.4.1) and navigate to Camera Formats, you can choose how your videos are captured.

Selecting High Efficiency will capture Video in HEVC (h.265) format which is non-standard. Instead, Video capture on iPhones should select Most Compatible to ensure that video is taken in h.264 codec which will make processing times faster on Patreon’s end.

Non-standard input

Patreon works fine with video outside of the standard input specs. However, because other videos cannot be easily streamed to many modern devices, Patreon must perform an initial encoding operation on non-standard input to create a mezzanine file. This means that non-standard input will be slower to ingest.

How do I notify my members when I edit a post?

If you’re making changes to a published post and want to notify members with an updated version of the post, you can do so with a simple click of the mouse.

To turn on the post-edit notification:

- Select Creator studio from the left navigation, then click your [Library](https://www.patreon.com/posts/published) to be taken to the Posts tab by default
- Within the Posts tab, you can:
    - Search for posts by name
    - Sort by Title and/or Publish date
    - Filter by post type, audience, or tags — click the button to Apply your filter selections
- Click the menu [icon] button in the top-right corner of the post, then click Edit post to make changes
- Click Next at the bottom-right corner of the screen
- Toggle on the Notify members that you edited this post option
    - You can leave this option turned off if you don't want to notify your members that you updated your post
- Click the Save button
- Tap your Profile on the bottom menu
- Tap Manage posts
- Find the post you want to edit and tap it to open it
- Tap the more and select Edit
- While on the post, tap at the top
- Go to Email and notifications and toggle on the Notify members that you edited this post option
    - You can leave this option turned off if you don't want to notify your members that you updated your post
- Tap Save

Members who have email notifications for new posts enabled will receive an email with the updated post.

How do I resolve issues with video posts?

We know how frustrating it can be when you’re finally ready to share your work, only to have technical issues. We’re here to help with our recommendations for resolving common issues that creators write into our team with.

“Video unavailable” for mobile

If members are reporting receiving the message, “Video unavailable” for your YouTube videos in the Patreon app, it’s likely because there is music in your video that YouTube has licensed for you.

YouTube adds licenses to videos that contain licensed music. Doing this allows YouTube to keep your video up, and not remove the videos for licensing violations. This also means the videos will not play in embeds such as our Patreon iOS app.

Note: members using Android devices will not run into this issue. Android opens YouTube videos in the YouTube app, so there’s no issue with embedding.

Can I fix this?

You can remove the licensing limitation from your video by muting the portion of your video with the claimed song. Learn more about muting portions of your video, by clicking on this link for Google’s resource.

Privacy settings for YouTube

If you’re using YouTube as your 3rd party hosting site, there are a few settings you can enable to ensure that members can view your videos on desktop, and on the Patreon app.

With YouTube, we recommend publishing your video as Unlisted. Additionally, there are a couple of YouTube default Advanced settings that you’ll want to keep as-is (below):

  • Keep the License and rights ownership field on the default Standard YouTube License. If you change this, your videos will not play on Desktop or on the app for members.
  • In the Distribution options setting be sure to leave Allow embedding checked.

As quick tool, your YouTube video advanced settings should be like this:

Note: If you’re finding that your video is “Unavailable” on the app in particular, you’ll want to double check your licensing on YouTube. YouTube may add additional copyright licensing to a video that uses music from different artists. This license prevents embedded players within apps from playing these videos outside of their own app or website. You can learn more about music in videos hosted by YouTube, by clicking on the YouTube guide here.

Privacy settings for Vimeo

When editing the privacy settings for your videos on Vimeo, there are few things we recommend doing to ensure that your videos play for your members when viewed on desktop, and the Patreon app.

  1. In the Who can watch? field, we recommend selecting either: Anyone, or People with the private link. If you select any of the other options in the Who can watch field, be sure to whitelist the domain patreon.com, so that embedded videos can be played. Read through #2 for more details.

  2. In the Where can this be embedded? field of your Vimeo privacy settings. We recommend allowing embedding Anywhere.

If you pay for Vimeo, you may also have the option to whitelist your video only for patreon.com. To do this, select the option to allow embedding on Specific domains, you’ll want to add www.patreon.com as a domain (click on the + plus sign to add it).

Here’s what will populate once you’ve given patreon.com permission to embed your video. Once added, it will populate under the field where you can remove the permission by clicking the “x” next to patreon.com.

How do I set up an early access post?

Early access posts let you share work with your members before making it public on Patreon.

Early access isn’t available in the Patreon app post editor. To schedule one, use Patreon on desktop or mobile web. See the FAQ below for a mobile workaround.

Creating an early access post

  • Click +
  • Draft your post as you usually would
  • If uploading video or audio, make sure Make this a drop is turned off (otherwise you won’t be able to set early access). Learn more about drops
  • In the settings, select Paid access and set which tiers you’d like to have early access to the post
  • Click More options
  • Toggle on the Offer early access option and set the date and time that the post will become public (must be 24 hours in the future)
  • Go back and customize the rest of your post’s settings: emails and notifications, adding the post to a new or existing collection, setting a publish date if you are scheduling your post, and adjusting comment settings or tags (under More settings)

Notifications

You can toggle email notifications on or off by clicking into the Email and notifications option in the post settings. If you’ve enabled email and notifications:

  • Members with post email notifications enabled will receive an email when the early access post goes live (if they have access)
  • When the post becomes available to everyone, followers and other members will also get an email notification (if enabled)

FAQ

  • Early access posts can only go from certain tiers/all members access to available to everyone.
  • You can release an early access post to the public ahead of the scheduled date and time by visiting your Library from the left navigation menu. In your library, select the post you want to make public > click Edit > choose Edit access > set the access to Public > click Next > confirm your change.
  • Once you make an early access post visible to everyone, you won’t be able to make the post early access again. So be sure that you’re ready to have the post accessible to everyone.
  • If you’d like to set up an early access post and are creating your post on the go, you can create your post on the Mobile web version (i.e. Chrome, or Firefox) of Patreon to schedule your early access post. Alternatively, draft your post in the app (we’ll autosave your edits), and revisit your post to add early access on Desktop or Mobile web at a later time. Learn more about scheduling your posts.
  • While there is no set way to create recurring early access posts, you can duplicate a pre-existing early access post with the settings you want by going to the Library . You can then click More next to the post you want to duplicate and select Duplicate as draft.

How do I size images for Patreon posts?

This article will detail Patreon’s recommendations for sizing images so that they display best for your fans.

You can upload images with any dimensions you’d like. We optimize your images for the web and for different devices. What follows are simply our recommendations. Do what works best for your work!

Image sizes and ratios

Below are our recommended image sizes to best display your work on members’ devices. It’s fine if your images are larger than the dimensions listed, but we highly recommend keeping the ratios listed. Keep in mind that we will optimize them for your members’ feeds and devices. Your post feed displays images in a 16:9 ratio, so for the cleanest look, size your post images to 1920×1080 px.

Keep it consistent

For each of the ratio groupings above, we recommend using the same image size for visual consistency. For example, if you’re using a 1:1 ratio for your ‘Profile Image,’ it would be beneficial to also use a 1:1 ratio for your ‘Digital Product Hero Image’ and ‘Collection Cover Image,’ and ideally, maintain a consistent image size like 1024 x 1024 px across all of them.

Exploring ratios

While we recommend sizing your post images (gallery and inline) to 1920 by 1080 px, there are some tried and tested ratios that are great for apps and the web. Keep in mind that any ratio other than 16:9 will be letterboxed (padded with empty space) in the post feed, though these formats are ideal for full-screen views or alternative displays. Because you can upload larger format images, we have included a larger version of each ratio – just know that on any screen, it’ll show no wider than ~1080px in the feed.

Resizing by inches rather than pixels

It’s best practice to size your images by pixels if you’re saving for the web, but if you prefer saving images by inches, there is an often-used formula for converting from pixels to inches. In order to do this, you’ll need to have the DPI (or resolution) of your image.

Once you know your image DPI, use the following formula: Divide the pixel dimensions by the resolution
