iOS In-App purchase fees

Except for US customers who are purchasing memberships (see below), Apple requires that all digital purchases (including memberships and digital goods) made through the Patreon iOS app use their in-app purchase system, which comes with a 30% fee on the prices of these sales. Patreon doesn’t charge any additional payment processing fees on iOS transactions, but our platform fee still applies.

  • One-time purchases
  • In January 2024, we began gradually rolling out iOS in-app purchases for Commerce. Learn more by visiting the iOS in-app purchases for Commerce
  • Memberships
  • In November 2024, we began rolling out Apple’s in-app purchase system for new memberships. Learn more by visiting how iOS in-app purchases work on Patreon
  • U.S. customers
  • Due to ongoing legal developments, iOS users in the United States do not have to use Apple’s in-app purchase (IAP) flow. Instead, they have the option to complete purchases directly through Patreon’s mobile web checkout and are not subject to the 30% IAP fee. This experience reflects the outcome of the Epic v. Apple ruling, which prohibits Apple from blocking alternative payment methods

What is the Founders plan?

In May 2019, we first introduced new creator plans and fees. Creators who joined before this date were placed on a discounted founders-only plan, 5%, that gave them the same features as when they first joined without any additional costs. This enabled creators to keep the features they were used to without having to pay more, plus a few extra features that were not previously available.

If you joined Patreon before May 7, 2019, and haven’t since made disqualifying changes to your creator page, like unpublishing it or changing your plan or currency, you’re on the Founders plan.

What’s New with Patreon Plans

Six years later, Patreon has expanded beyond just subscriptions to include media hosting, community, and discovery. We’re releasing even more tools to help creators grow and engage with their biggest fans more directly, including better discovery to help creators grow, and rolling out livestreaming to more creators.

For the creators who have been with us on this journey, we wanted to honor your commitment and the massive role you have played in our transformation. We also wanted to minimize any impact on your business, which is why prices were not increased for you or anyone with a published Patreon page that launched on or before August 4, 2025.

In August 2025, we updated pricing to a standard 10% platform plan, plus applicable taxes, and standardized payment processing rates for new creators who published their creator page after August 4, 2025.

If you published your creator page by August 4, 2025, and it hasn’t been unpublished since, you’re on a legacy platform plan. If you unpublish your page (or Patreon does), your account will move to the standard 10% platform plan, and standard payment rates will apply.

What to expect with iOS in-app purchases

All creators are now using subscription billing. If your account was still on a legacy billing model on November 1, 2026, we switched it automatically and emailed you when the switch was complete.

Key details depending on your previous billing model:

  • Per-creation: If you haven’t resumed billing yet, it stays paused until you review your new tier prices. Learn how to resume billing
  • First-of-the-month: Your existing members are still billed on the 1st of each month. New members are billed on the date they join

In August 2024, we let you know that Apple is requiring Patreon to use its in-app purchase system for all future membership and product purchases made in the iOS app. To comply with Apple’s in-app purchase requirements, some Patreon functionality may work differently for memberships purchased in the iOS app. Patreon began rolling out iOS in-app purchases in November 2024.

Key Impacts

  • Payout Delay: iOS in-app funds have a 75-day pending period due to Apple’s processing time
  • Earnings: Creators can view a breakdown of revenue by platform and see pending vs. settled funds
  • Pricing: iOS in-app pricing may be higher to account for Apple’s fees, except for tiers with physical goods. Pricing for U.S. based fans may not appear higher if they select web checkout
  • Unpublishing: If you unpublish your Patreon page, iOS in-app memberships will be canceled (no automatic refunds); pausing is recommended to maintain these memberships
  • Refunds: Fans who joined via iOS in-app must request refunds through Apple at reportaproblem.apple.com, but creators can still issue other refunds via the Audience Manager
  • Custom Amounts: Fans cannot set a custom membership amount when editing their membership in the iOS app; this is still possible on Web and Android

For iOS users in the U.S.: Fans in the U.S. may have the option to complete their purchase through Patreon’s mobile web checkout instead of using Apple’s in-app purchase flow. Purchases completed on the mobile web are not subject to Apple’s App Store fee.

Payout delay

The iOS in-app purchase system requires a 75-day pending period while Apple processes and makes the funds available for payout. Patreon cannot expedite Apple’s processing timeline. Funds from iOS in-app purchases will appear as pending on your account until Apple has settled the transaction.

Learn more about paying out your balance.

Earnings insights

You’re able to view a breakdown of your monthly revenue, comparing income from transactions made in the iOS app, web browser, or Android app. Additionally, you’ll see a breakdown of your monthly earnings, including pending funds due to Apple’s payout delay and settled funds already deposited into your payout.

Pricing a tier

When pricing a tier on the tier edit screen, you will see a preview of what the price will be when viewed in the iOS app. Depending on the choice you have selected for how to account for Apple’s fees, the price may be higher in the iOS app or the same. This preview allows you to see the price that will be displayed for each individual tier. Please note that any fan in the U.S. will see your original tier pricing first, and will only see the higher tier price if they choose Apple’s in-app purchase system over the default web checkout flow, which doesn’t include Apple’s fee.

Please note: Tiers that utilize structured tier benefits may be exempt from the iOS in-app fee if they include physical goods, such as merch, commissions (delivered by mail) or other tangible goods. The increased offset price will not be included in these tiers when viewed in the iOS app, keeping the same price as on the Web and Android.

Visit our Advanced Sales Tax Settings article to learn more.

Annual memberships

Currently, annual memberships are not supported in the iOS app. Creators can still offer annual memberships on Web and Android. We are working to support annual memberships in the iOS app as a fast follow.

Payout delay

The iOS in-app purchase system requires a 75-day pending period while Apple processes and makes the funds available for payout. Patreon cannot expedite Apple’s processing timeline. Funds from iOS in-app purchases will appear as pending on your account until Apple has settled the transaction.

Learn more about paying out your balance.

Unpublishing your Patreon

Unpublishing your Patreon will remove active memberships for fans who joined through iOS in-app purchases. If you’d like to take a break, we recommend pausing your membership for a month at a time.

If you unpublish your page, all memberships made on iOS in-app purchasing will be canceled without automatic refunds. Memberships created on Web, Android, or iOS prior to the rollout of in-app purchasing will be paused rather than canceled. Since unpublishing your Patreon can impact your ability to republish with your same audience, we recommend pausing your page for up to 60 days so that you don’t lose your iOS memberships processed with Apple’s in-app purchasing system.

Learn more about pausing your membership.

Refunding members

Fans who joined through iOS in-app purchases should request a refund through Apple at reportaproblem.apple.com. Theicon next to a purchase indicates whether the purchase was made with iOS in-app purchases. As a creator, you can still issue refunds for fans through your Audience relationship manager and Sales tab.

Apple ultimately decides whether to approve a refund request on transactions made through in-app purchases. You can find Apple’s guide to requesting a refund here.

Refunding fans who joined on Web or Android

You can continue to issue refunds from their Patreon balance to fans who joined on the Web or Android. Read more about how refunds work.

Custom membership amount

At rollout, fans will not be able to create a custom pledge amount when they edit their membership through the iOS app. This also means that memberships made via in-app purchasing cannot be edited to a custom amount.

Fans will still be able to create and edit their memberships to a custom amount on the Web and Android.

Creators: Sell your work on Patreon

Discounts FAQ

This guide covers the most frequently asked questions about discounts on Patreon. If you’re looking for details on how to set up or manage your discounts, please check out our Managing discounts help center article.

  • At the moment, discounts are only redeemable for new paid members to your Patreon. Here are additional eligibility details to keep in mind:
    • Free members are fully eligible to redeem discounts
    • Canceled paid members whose access hasn’t run out yet aren’t eligible until their current access period ends
    • Members on an active free trial or with a gift membership aren’t eligible, as these count as paid memberships
    • Members who have previously used a discount are still eligible, since there is no per-user limit, only the overall code usage limit set by the creator
  • No, discounts are only applied for the first month or the first year, depending on what you choose to set up. Fans can only redeem the code once.
  • Yes! You can set up product discount codes alongside your membership discounts. Product discounts can apply to items in your shop, and these can be used independently of membership discounts.
  • You can set up multiple product or membership discount codes at a time, but only one sale can be publicly shown at a time. There is a waiting period of 7 days in between public sales.
  • Your fans can still add your discount code during checkout, which will override the free trial. If you have a public sale shown, the free trial option will not show up.
  • Membership Discounts:
    • Public discounts can remain visible for up to 31 days.
    • Individual discount codes can be active for up to 180 days.
  • Product Discounts:
    • There is no time limit for how long a product discount can remain active.
  • Please note that when setting up a new sale, the discount can last for up to 31 days, and the end date can’t be changed afterward. If you’re using promo codes, they can be active for up to 180 days, and you can edit the end date later. Discounts can be stopped at any time.
  • For membership discounts:
    • Minimum discount: There is a minimum discount amount of 5%.
    • Maximum discount: There is a maximum discount amount of 90%.
    • There is also a minimum transaction amount of $0.50 regardless of the discount. So if your tier price is $1 and you set a 90% discount, it will still be transacted as $0.50.
  • For product discounts:
    • Minimum discount: There is a minimum discount amount of 5%.
    • Maximum discount: There is a maximum discount amount of 50%.
    • There is also a minimum transaction amount of $3 regardless of the discount. So if your item is priced at $3.25 and you set a 50% discount, the customer will receive a $0.25 discount and pay $3, as the minimum for USD items is $3.
  • If you have Autopilot turned on, membership discounts can be complementary. With membership discounts, you can run more targeted or time-bound discounts, while Autopilot can continue running in the background automating offers and converting new paid members you might not have had before.
  • No, they can only redeem one discount during checkout. If you’re running a discount publicly displayed on your page, the best offer will be automatically added during checkout. They can also change the discount code to another one they have access to at checkout.
  • For membership discounts, each unique code can be redeemed multiple times as long as it is currently active and the fan redeeming it does not have an active paid membership to you.
  • For product discounts, customers may use a unique code for multiple purchases while it is active.
  • For membership payments, there is also a minimum transaction amount of $0.50 regardless of the discount. So if your tier price is $1 and you set a 90% discount, it will still be transacted as $0.50.
  • For products, there is a minimum transaction of $3 (in local currency). Any discounts that would make a product lower than $3 will be applied only up until the price reaches $3.

Managing customers

This article guides you on managing customers when selling media as one-time purchases. For more information on how to sell media, refer to our guide on Selling one-time purchases on Patreon.

Located in the Audience section of your account, the Sales tab provides valuable insights into your customers’ purchase history and payment status. Continue reading to learn how to make the most of this tool for managing your customers effectively.

Viewing Sales

Here’s how to easily locate and access customer transactions:

  • On Desktop, click Creator studio from the left-side navigation
  • Click on Audience
  • Select the Sales tab from the top menu
  • By clicking on the search bar, you can search by order ID, customer, or product

Within Sales, you’ll find essential information about each transaction, including:

  • The item purchased
  • The date purchased
  • Status (complete vs. refunded)
  • Total amount paid

You can also export your customer details and transaction information by clicking the Download CSV button.

By clicking on the customer’s name from the list, it’ll open the Order details side panel. This is where you can find more details about an individual customer and their order.

Customer management

Refunding purchases

Since Patreon provides a platform for members to pay creators directly, in most cases, Patreon will not refund on behalf of creators. This means that creators can issue refunds at their discretion.

Please note that funds from digital sales will appear as pending for up to 7 days before they are available for withdrawal. Funds must be available to withdraw in order to be used for refunding customers or members.

As long as you have the funds available to withdraw in your balance, you can cover customer refund requests. Here’s how:

  • On Desktop, click Creator studio from the left-side navigation
  • Go to Audience
  • Select the Sales tab from the top menu
  • Search for the customer you want to refund, either by using the search bar or by going through the list of customers
  • Click on the customer’s name to open a side panel with their order details
  • Click on the Issue refund button

Please keep in mind that refunds may take 7-10 business days to process and cannot be undone.

As soon as you refund a product, it will be removed from the customer’s purchases, and they will immediately lose access to the content.

Refunds can be processed within 90 days of the original transaction as long as you have a Patreon balance to cover the refunded amount. You can read more about refunds in Patreon’s refund policy.

Messaging customers

You can directly message your customers to help with troubleshooting your items and communicating about refunds. Follow these steps to message your customers:

  • On Desktop, click Creator studio from the left-side navigation
  • Go to Audience
  • Select the Sales tab from the top menu
  • Click the name of the customer you want to message. This will open an Order details side panel
  • Select the Arrow icon in front of the customer’s name
  • Type up your message and click the Send button. When you send a message to a customer, it creates a message thread where you can find your conversation with that individual

FAQ

  • The Order details panel is where you can find information about a customer and their order. It includes important details like your customer’s transaction history.
  • To access this panel, follow the steps below:
    • On Desktop, click Creator studio from the left-side navigation
    • Go to Audience
    • Select the Sales tab from the top menu
    • Click on the customer’s name. This will open a side panel with the Order details
    • In that panel, select More next to the customer’s name.
    • Click on View transaction history
  • You may notice that the total amount paid by the customer might be higher than the price of the item. This is because we are required by law to apply sales tax to purchases made in certain jurisdictions. You can see a breakdown of where we’re collecting sales tax from customers and what those tax rates are in the following article: Sales Tax on Patreon.
  • Yes, you will have the option to message all your customers using the Patreon messaging system.
  • Patreon should be a safe space for all creators to share their work. If you feel a customer is being problematic or making you uncomfortable, you have the option to block them:
    • On Desktop, click Creator studio from the left-side navigation
    • Go to Audience
    • Select the Sales tab from the top menu
    • Click on the customer’s name. This will open an Order details side panel
    • Click More and select Block user
  • Please note that blocking a customer will also block any accounts connected to the same payment method used, blocking any other accounts they might have. They won’t be able to purchase from you or become a member.
  • Any members that you’ve blocked from joining your Patreon will not be able to purchase work you sell as one-time purchases.

Managing discounts

This guide explains how to create, manage, and track both discounts for your shop and membership. If you’re looking for frequently asked questions, please check out our Discounts FAQ.

Discounts Overview

Discount codes are a powerful tool to grow your Patreon. Whether you’re looking to boost product sales or drive more sign-ups to your membership, discounts can help you engage your audience and offer exclusive deals.

On Patreon, there are two types of discounts:

  • Product Discounts – Discounts applied to digital products in your shop, encouraging sales by offering special deals
  • Membership Discounts – Promotions designed to attract new paid members by offering discounts on the first month or year of membership tiers
What you need to know about discount codes:
  • Discount codes can be shared with fans on and off Patreon
  • You can create and run multiple discount codes for your entire store, select products, or membership tiers
  • While multiple codes can be active, fans can apply only one discount code per product or membership at checkout — discounts don’t stack
  • For product discounts, if the code reduces the product price below the minimum, customers will receive a partial discount. The minimum price will be displayed when you create your product
  • You can add discount codes to both existing products and products saved as drafts
  • Membership discounts are available for any tier but only apply to new members during their first month or first year of membership — the full price will apply for subsequent billing cycles
  • If you are running a public sale for membership discounts, only one discount can be publicly displayed on your page at a time
  • Public membership discounts can remain visible for up to 31 days, and individual membership discount codes can be active for up to 180 days. There is no time limit for how long a product discount can remain active

Set up a Membership Discount

  • Select Creator studio from the left navigation, then click Promotions
  • Select the Discounts page at the top, where you can view your current and past promotions
  • Click the Add discount button to create a new discount
  • If you’re selling digital products, you can choose between Membership Discount or Shop Discount. If you’re not selling digital products, you’ll proceed directly to the Membership Discount flow
  • Complete the discount code form with the following:
    • Name: Only visible to you as the creator
    • Code: Click the generate option to get an auto-generated code, or type in your own custom code with at least three characters
    • Valid for: Choose if this discount applies to their first month, first year, or both. If annual memberships aren’t on, you’ll default to monthly
    • Discount amount: Choose a discount amount between 5–90%
    • Applies to: Your code can apply to all your tiers or selected tiers
    • Display this discount publicly on your Patreon: Toggling this on will automatically show this discounted rate to anyone except existing paid members. You can only display one discount publicly at a time and must wait 7 days between each active public discount
    • Start date & time: Set the date you’d like your code/public sale to become active
    • End date & time: You’ll need to set an end date for your discount. Please note that the discount duration cannot exceed 180 days. You can also edit the date later or stop a discount at any time
  • Once you’ve filled out the discount form, click Create code
  • You can share this code with fans on and off Patreon to be applied at checkout — anyone with the discount code can use it at checkout. If the code was shared with a small group, people outside of the group can still use it if it’s shared around

When you set up an annual discount, the percentage off will be from your annual price, which may already be discounted depending on how you set up your annual membership. Keep this in mind as you create your discounts.

Set up a product discount

You can add discount codes to existing and future products.

Existing products
  • Select Creator studio from the left navigation, then click Promotions and select the Discounts tab
  • You’ll land on the Discounts page
  • Click the Add button
  • A pop-up will appear, and you can select from three different options: Run a sale, Offer an early bird discount, or Create a promo code
  • After, complete the discount code form with the following:
    • Name: only visible to you as the creator
    • Code: click the generate option to get an auto-generated code, or type in your own custom code with at least three characters
    • Discount amount: your code can apply a set discount amount or a percentage of the product price (max 50%)
    • Applies to: your code can apply to your entire shop or to select products in your shop
    • Start date & time: set the date you’d like your code to become active
    • End date & time: add an expiration date for your discount code
      • Please note that when setting up a new sale, the discount can last for up to 31 days, and the end date can’t be changed afterward. If you’re using promo codes, they can be active for up to 180 days, and you can edit the end date later. Discounts can be stopped at any time
    • For the Offer an early bird discount option, you can also define a discount limit of how many fans can apply this discount
  • Once you’ve filled out the discount form, click on Create code
  • You can share this code with fans on and off Patreon to be applied at checkout
New products
  • Select Create from the left navigation
  • Choose the Product option
  • Set your digital product title, prices, description, and upload your work
  • To add a discount, go to More options in the right-side menu below Sell this post
  • Scroll down to Discounts and then select the desired alternative
  • Select from three different options: Run a sale, Offer an early bird discount, or Create a promo code
    • You can apply as many discount codes as you’d like to a product, and customers can redeem one applicable code at checkout. This can be useful if you want to promote on different platforms — you can measure code usage to determine where customers are coming from
    • Please note that when setting up a new sale, the discount can last for up to 31 days, and the end date can’t be changed afterward. If you’re using promo codes, they can be active for up to 180 days, and you can edit the end date later. Discounts can be stopped at any time
  • Fill out the form and click Create code if you’re adding a new discount

Managing and editing discount codes

To edit, duplicate, or end a promotion, select Creator studio from the left navigation, then click Promotions.

Editing product discounts

Once you’ve created a discount code, you can edit aspects of your discount by selecting Creator studio from the left navigation, clicking Promotions, then clicking the more menu, and choosing Edit.

Here’s what you can edit depending on your code’s status:

Status

Can change

Cannot change

Scheduled: if the start date has not occurred yet

Change any aspect of the code.

Active: if the code has already started, and there is no end date, or the end date has not yet occurred

  • Change the display name
  • Change what the code applies to
  • Move the end date up (to now) or further out

Important: For a public sale that’s already active, the only thing you can change is its name.

  • Change the start date
  • The code itself
  • The discount amount or configuration (i.e., percentage or fixed amount)

Expired: if the start and end date are both in the past

You can no longer make changes to the code

End promotion

To delete a product discount, select Creator studio from the left navigation, then click Promotions. Once you’ve landed on the Discounts tab, click the more menu and select End promotion. When you end a promotion, its status will update to Expired, and you’ll have the option to Delete it. Please be aware that once a member redeems a discount code, you’ll be able to end it, but you can no longer delete the discount code.

Tracking discount code redemption

You can track the redemption of your discount codes and see who used them.

Promotions tab

On the Discounts page, you’ll see your active and expired sales, plus how many times your code has been redeemed. You can click on each one to see more information.

Once you click in, you can click View Details under redemptions to see who redeemed your code.

Sales tab (Product Discounts Only)

Select Creator studio from the left navigation, click Audience, and then the Sales tab to view a list of all the customers who have redeemed a discount code — by searching for the discount code, or by clicking the View details button in the expanded view of a discount in the Promotions tab.

What customers see

For membership discounts

There are two ways fans can redeem a membership discount:

  • Using a Discount Code: Fans can enter the discount code during checkout by clicking the Discount code section in the Order Summary
  • Public Sale: If you are running a public sale, the original price of the membership will be crossed out, showing the new discounted monthly price
For product discounts

When customers check out, they can apply the discount by clicking on the Discount code section in the Order summary.

Partial Discounts

Customers will receive a partial discount if your discount code makes your product’s price less than the minimum. For example, if your item is $3.25 and you set a 50% discount for your entire shop, a customer will receive a $0.25 discount and pay $3 since the minimum for USD items is $3. The minimum for your currency will be listed when you create your product. Partial discounts ensure that prices don’t drop below the minimum threshold for your currency.

How discount codes are applied on the iOS app

Discounts are applied to the list price you set before any price increases are made to account for Apple’s App Store fees.

For example, if you offer a 10% discount on a $5 item (priced at $7.50 on iOS), it will be $4.50 on web and Android and $6.50 on iOS.

Visit our Apple in-app purchases page to learn more.

Selling one-time purchases on Patreon

Whether you’re a musician, illustrator, writer, or video creator, you can sell your digital work directly to fans. From full videos and podcast episodes to collections of your best work, your membership or exclusive media can be available as one-time purchases through your Shop tab.

It’s free to get started. You’ll only see fees applied when you earn, and we’ve built tools to help you track sales and grow over time.

Commerce is available to Adult/18+ creators on subscription billing. Digital products must comply with our guidelines for Public Previews. Learn more about feature access for Adult/18+ creators.

All work sold through Shops must comply with our Community Guidelines.

What you can sell

You can sell posts, digital products, and collections:

  • Digital products (text, audio, video, image, attachments)
  • Posts (these can be posts for paid members or for purchase only)
  • Collections (groups of posts, like mini-series or themed bundles)
Supported file types:
  • Video: .mov, .mp4, .m4a, .mpeg, .ogg
  • Audio: .mp3, .mp4, .m4a, .wav, .aac, .ogg
  • Image: .gif, .jpeg, .png,
  • Attachment file types: .epub, .doc, .rtf, .txt, .zip, .7-Zip, .stl, .3mf

You can view the full list of supported file formats here.

Want ideas for selling beyond membership? Check out “Increase your earnings with one-time purchases” on Patreon for Creators. Currently, Patreon for Creators is only available in English.

How to post your work for sale

There are two pathways to post your work for sale in your Shop.

  • Click Create > Post
  • Click Create > Product

Both options will take you to the posting editor, where you can:

  • Add a title, write details about what you’re posting, and set your price (between $3 and $5,000 USD)
  • Make the posting available to members (as well as for sale) or for purchase only
  • Edit your preview
  • Publish your posting to your Shop

Posting a collection for sale

You can set a collection for sale when you first create it, or anytime afterward.

- On Desktop, select Creator studio in the left-side navigation menu
- Click on Dashboard from the sub-menu
- Go to your [Collections](https://www.patreon.com/c/user/collections) tab
- Click Create collection or select an existing collection
    - If you're creating a collection: Add a title (required) and description (optional)
    - If you're selecting an existing collection: Click on the Collection, then select Edit
- Toggle on the Sell this collection option
- Set a price (minimum $3)
- Choose:
    - Posts to include
    - Layout: Grid or list
    - Preview (image, audio, or video – 984×554 px recommended)
- Click Save — your collection will be listed in your [Shop](https://www.patreon.com/c/user/shop)
- On Desktop, select Creator studio in the left-side navigation menu
- Click on [Library](https://www.patreon.com/posts/published)
- Check the boxes next to the works you want to sell
- Click Edit price, then set your price and agree to the terms
- Click Next, then Confirm

Note: Collections must include at least one post to appear in your Shop.

Fees that apply to sales

There’s no fee to post products for sale — fees are only applied to successfully processed payments.

For creators:

Fee

Details

Platform fee

Standard 10% platform fee for successfully processed sales

Note: Creators who started selling digital products before August 4, 2025, may be subject to a legacy platform fee instead of the standard fee, depending on your platform plan settings.

Learn more about it in our Creator fees overview.

Payment processing fee

Varies by currency (e.g., 2.9% + $0.30 USD)

Sales tax on fees

May apply based on your location

Payout fee

Based on your withdrawal method and currency

For fans:

Fee

Details

iOS app store fee*

30% of the sale price (Apple’s fee), depending on the creator’s account settings

Currency conversion

Sales tax

May apply based on the customer’s location

  • iOS in-app purchases for one-time purchases are currently available in select countries. Visit our iOS in-app purchases: country & currency page for more information about where iOS in-app purchases are currently supported. Fans who are not located in one of the currently supported countries can still view products on the iOS app but are unable to purchase products on that platform.

Managing your Shop

You can make changes to work you’re selling in your Shop at any time — even after they’ve been purchased.

  • Edit the title, files, price, and description
  • Stop selling or unpublish to hide the product from your Shop (existing buyers keep access)
  • Delete to remove the posting entirely (removes access; refunds optional)
How to manage your one-time purchase
- Go to the [Shop tab](https://www.patreon.com/user/shop) on your page
- Click More next to the posting you want to manage
- Choose:
    - Edit to update details
    - Stop selling to remove it from your Shop
    - Delete to remove it entirely — If you want to fully delete a single post that you've posted, you can click the Edit option to delete the post from your Patreon
- Tap your Profile in the right corner of the bottom menu
- Select View page
- Go to the Shop tab
- Tap More in the product you'd like to make changes
- Select Edit — if you want to fully delete a single post that you've posted, after selecting Edit, tap on the post Settings and select Delete post to remove it from your Patreon

What fans see

You can use the Preview feature to see how the public views your posting on your page.

Featuring products in your shop

You can feature up to three products at the top of your Shop to drive attention from your fans. Featuring products is a great way to showcase your most popular or new items and encourage sales.

To feature a product:
  • Go to the Shop tab on your page
  • Click on More next to your posting
  • Select Highlight in shop

Your featured products will appear prominently at the top of your Shop, helping fans discover your best offerings quickly.

The after-purchase experience

When someone buys access to a post or collection, the content unlocks immediately. Buyers can access their purchases anytime from the Purchases tab — no membership required.

You can continue to edit, add to, or remove content after posting it for sale. Buyers will see any updates, even if changes are made after their purchase. If you remove content, consider offering refunds or notifying affected fans.

Track and grow

Head to Insights > Shop to view your earnings by product and see your top-selling items. Sales data updates every 4 hours.

To see who’s buying your work, go to Audience > Sales. Click a buyer’s name to view their purchase history — including full details if their activity goes back more than three months.

Payout timing

Once funds are available for payout, you can manually withdraw your balance immediately, or if you have automatic payouts enabled, your funds will be paid out on the 5th of each month.

Platform

Pending funds

Web & Android

Up to 7 days

iOS

Up to 75 days (Apple delay)

When you withdraw funds, a payout fee will be deducted from the payout amount.

Refunding a customer

Funds must be available in your balance to issue a refund. You can issue refunds for up to 90 days after a purchase. Once refunded, the customer immediately loses access to the product.

Refunds typically take 5–7 business days to process and can’t be undone.

How to issue a refund:
  • On Desktop, select Creator studio in the left-side navigation menu
  • Click on Audience from the sub-menu
  • Select the Sales tab
  • Search for the customer or find them in the list
  • Click their name to view the order details
  • Select Issue refund

If you’re deleting a product, you’ll be prompted to:

  • Refund all customers who purchased it
  • Or select individual purchases to refund
iOS in-app Purchase Refunds

Refunds for iOS in-app purchases can be handled in two ways:

  • Through Patreon: Issue the refund as usual (if funds are available)
  • Through Apple: Customers can request a refund at reportaproblem.apple.com. Apple handles the process and communicates directly with the customer. If approved, the full amount is returned to their Apple account — Apple will process refunds within 60 days of the purchase taking place

Selling posts and collections FAQ

This article addresses frequently asked questions about this feature. If you want a detailed guide on how to sell posts and collections work, please visit Selling one-time purchases on Patreon.

Tips for selling posts and collections

This article will share some tips as you get started selling posts and collections and how to think about it as part of your overall Patreon strategy.

If you’re looking for detailed instructions on how to set this up, please refer to our Selling posts and collections guide.

Key tips to get started

Start with something you feel good about
  • Begin by selling content that you know your fans already love or are eagerly anticipating. For example, you could sell a popular series, playlist, or course. You can also consider bundling related content into a collection and offering it as a one-time purchase
  • Not sure where to start? Head to your Insights page and check the Posts tab to see which posts have received the most engagement. This can help you identify the content your fans are most interested in.
Price based on what your goal is
  • Pricing can vary depending on your objectives and the nature of the content. Here are a few strategies:
  • If the content is exclusive or larger in size, consider setting a higher price point. For instance, collections with multiple posts could be priced higher due to their added value
  • Compare the price of your content to your membership tiers. If your goal is to provide a more accessible entry point, you might price the content at the same level or lower than your tier pricing
  • Don’t hesitate to adjust your pricing strategy over time based on fan feedback and sales performance
Promote it to your fans and free members

Promotion is crucial for letting your audience know they can purchase your work without committing to a membership. Here are some ways to promote your sales:

  • An easy way to notify your free members is by publishing a free member only post about your latest work for sale. Read more about Setting audience access for your posts
    • For example, we’ve seen creators share a free member only post highlighting “Now you can purchase access to individual posts for sale without a recurring membership. If you like what you see, you can always upgrade your membership to unlock more of my work.” As a reminder, nothing changes for your paid members who already have access
  • You can also share similar language across your social media pointing fans to your Patreon page, or share a Promo card linking directly to your post for sale for a more visual effect. Learn more about Sharing your posts to your social platforms

Creators: Taxes on Patreon

About Advanced Sales Tax Settings

This article is a reference guide for all things VAT/GST, and Sales Tax settings-related.

If you’re curious about which locations are impacted by sales tax, feel free to read through our article: Patreon’s Sales Tax Requirements

Throughout this article, when we say ‘sales tax’, we also mean VAT, GST, and other similar taxes.

General information about Advanced Sales Tax Settings

Sales Tax Settings live within each tier you’ve created. Head to your Membership tab and click the Edit tier button for each tier to access Sales Tax Settings.

We built these tax settings to give creators more control over how sales tax and other similar taxes around the world, such as VAT or GST, are applied to your membership. Using these settings you can give us further detail on what benefits you offer and how much we should value those things for sales tax purposes.

Why is this important? Not all benefits are taxable in all regions and taxation depends on your benefits and how these are offered. These details from you will allow us to charge tax only where necessary.

If you don’t use the settings to define your benefits and/or assign values to these, we will apply sales tax to pledges from your members in required locations based on a bundle approach. This may result in higher taxes being applied to your sales.

Tax laws change frequently, and Patreon is constantly working to keep up with those changes to meet our obligations in the most creator-first way possible. Learn more about required tax locations in this help article: Patreon’s Sales Tax Requirements.

About Listing your Benefits

Not all benefits are taxable in all regions. By giving us more detail about the unique benefits you’re offering, you allow us to be more accurate about applying tax only where required. The settings allow you to choose from common benefit types or create a custom benefit if what you offer is not listed. When you’re finished with this step, we’ll have a clean, organized, and detailed list of what you’re offering in each of your tiers in our database to make it possible for us to charge sales tax more accurately for your unique membership. You can update this at any time and our sales tax logic will update along with it.

Listing “General Support” as a benefit — IMPORTANT!

If your members are at all motivated by the idea of supporting your work, without wanting the benefits or content you provide, you can account for that fact in your tax settings. Pledges with the purpose of support are not taxable in some regions, but tax law cannot be applied based on your members’ intentions. We can only apply tax law according to whether or not a member is receiving something taxable in return for their pledge and the value assigned to each thing. If your members in one or more of your tiers receive no benefits, you should add General Support as the relevant benefit. That way we can consider those pledges to be support-motivated and we may be able to not apply sales tax to them.

About Adjusting benefit value, using percentages

Adjusting benefit value is a way for you to tell us the relative value of the benefits in each of your tiers. Once you’ve done this, we’ll be able to apply sales tax more specifically only to the benefits which should be subject to tax. And we will know what portion of a given pledge should be taxed. For example, if you have a tier that includes both digital content and a sticker, you can adjust the benefit value setting to tell us that the sticker makes up 10% of the value of that tier. Then, in places where the sticker is taxable, but not digital content, we can apply tax to just 10% of the pledge amount. If we don’t have these percentages set by you, we will have to apply sales tax to 100% of each pledge, in all locations where sales tax applies.

Value can be challenging to determine. It can be about more than just the wholesale cost of an item. Think about why your members participate in your membership. A t-shirt is a commodity, but wearing your t-shirt may also be about the member demonstrating their overall support for your creations. Your podcasts aren’t just about the file itself, but how the member can engage in the community by discussing the episode and shaping future content as well.

Some benefits are one-time gifts or giveaways. Set those to 0% value

If, as part of a tier subscription, you offer any reward benefits that members only get once after they join, or after a certain number of months, that should be considered a giveaway or thank you gift, like the tote bag you get if you support a public radio station. You can list that benefit, but set it at 0% value so it is not generally considered taxable on its own.

Accessing and Using the Settings

If you’ve already defined your tiers, pricing, and the benefits that you’re delivering to members, and it’s working for you, you don’t need to change anything in order to prepare for sales tax. All you need to do is use the Advanced Sales Tax settings to tell us what benefits you are offering and how to value those benefits for sales tax purposes.

Where do I find the Advanced Sales Tax Settings? Advanced Sales Tax Settings are located within each individual tier you’ve created. Head to your Membership tab and click Edit tier for each tier to access and use your tax settings.

Using the Advanced Sales Tax Settings

You can use the steps below to customize your tax settings:

  • Select Creator studio from the left navigation — you’ll land on your Dashboard.
  • From there, on your page, go to your Membership tab and click the Edit tier button for your first tier — follow these instructions, save your work, and repeat with all of your other tiers
  • Click into the Advanced section of the tier editor
  • List ALL of the benefits for this tier using the List your benefits drop-down menu. If you don’t have the List your benefits drop-down, click the Add benefit button. You can also choose Custom benefit if what you offer isn’t listed
  • In the Adjust benefit value section, tell us how much each benefit is worth. You’ll need at least two benefits listed for any tier before you can access the Adjust benefit value settings. If you only have one benefit in a tier, it can only equal 100% of the tier value. Please note that if you manually adjust the benefit values for each benefit, they must equal 100%
  • Don’t forget to click the Save button when you’re done!
  • Repeat the above steps on each of your tiers. If your higher tiers include benefits from your lower tiers, you’ll need to list them out each time on every tier

Advanced Sales Tax Settings FAQ

  • More practically, a helpful way to think about this may be to consider what you would charge for the benefit if the tier consisted of nothing but that benefit. In other words, if you have a $10 tier made up of an extra podcast, recurring merch and access to a poll, imagine what you would charge for each one of those components if they were listed individually as three separate items on a menu. Would you charge $3 a month for the extra podcast episode? $2/month for the poll access? If so, it seems reasonable to assume that the remaining $5/month should go towards recurring merch. In that case, you’d set the values at 30% for the podcast episode, 20% for poll access, and 50% for recurring merch. If there is only a single thing in a tier, such as a shoutout, then 100% of the value of that tier will be the shoutout.

  • As a company, we can only use the information which you have provided, so we trust Creators to be honest and act in good faith when engaging with the tools.
  • You are thus responsible for ensuring that all of your benefits are properly categorized using good faith efforts and to the best of your ability using the available tools. We also rely on the fact that you will provide accurate information when you are engaging with the tier tools, sales tax weighting tools and, generally, when listing and categorizing benefits transferred within membership tiers and offerings.
  • As long as you’ve filled out the settings accurately and to the best of your ability, we should be able to show proof that we are collecting sales tax correctly on your pledges.
  • If you have any doubts about using the tax tools, please reach out for support.

Other Sales Tax Questions

  • Tax amounts can change for a number of reasons. It may be that you updated your tier settings and the taxable items in the tier were assigned a new value. It may be that the members moved locations. A state could have clarified a ruling or enacted a law relating to something (like digital streaming) which to that point they had not ruled as being taxable or nontaxable. Or it may just be that the actual tax rate changed in the local jurisdiction (which happens frequently).
  • Please review your tiers to ensure your benefits accurately reflect what you are providing to members to the best of your ability. If your tier is only for members to support you and they are not paying directly for any physical or digital goods or services or any other benefit you offer, you can choose the “General support” benefit in your tier. If you have more than one benefit, you can use the tax weighting feature in the tier to tell us how much to value each benefit.
  • We understand that creators don’t always have a regular cadence for providing benefits. In this case, we recommend using the Benefit Value feature and giving the merchandise benefit a lower value. If the merchandise is really a give-away for support, you can give it a 0% value to ensure it is not taxed in locations that don’t tax give-aways.
  • In locales where Patreon is liable for tax collections, Patreon will have to decide whether a discount for sales tax collected is appropriate. This will depend on the reasons for which tax was applied and whether this may have been applied in error. If you believe tax should not be applied on the pledge by a certain fan, ensure the fan has set their accurate location in their member settings. Encourage the member to contact Patreon support and we can assist them in their sales tax concerns.
  • Unfortunately, our system does not currently support this. However, please contact us if you would like more information.
  • Maybe, depending on your circumstances. First, to be clear, this is in regards to sales tax filings. (Everyone always needs to file income tax returns.) The entity required to collect tax and submit a sales tax filing depends on the rules applicable in tax jurisdiction i.e., usually the fan location and essentially whether that location requires or allows a marketplace to take on such obligations. In most jurisdictions where Patreon is requested to take charge of the tax collection obligations creators will not be required to comply with the tax for the relevant sales. This may however also depend on your tax registration status and activities you have in the relevant location. Please consult with your tax advisor for specific details regarding your tax obligations.
  • No, it is not being reported on your 1099K.

About Tax Identification Numbers (TINs)

A Tax Identification Number (TIN) is a number assigned to individuals/businesses to identify them for income tax purposes. TINs can be called different things in different countries, but generally everyone is assigned a TIN by the authorities in their country of birth and/or residence.

What’s the difference between a TIN and a VAT/GST id?

Please note that a Tax Identification Number (TIN) differs from a Value-added Tax (VAT) registration number (also known as a GST number in some regions). While most creators are generally assigned a TIN by their country of residence, a VAT/GST number is not typically required. VAT/GST numbers are assigned only to individuals or entities actively engaged in business who have met the threshold for VAT/GST registration, which varies by jurisdiction.

If you do have a VAT/GST number, you can include it in the tax form - but it is not a required field.

I have more than one Tax Identification Number (TIN). How do I add all TINs?

When completing the “Non-US Citizen Tax Form” (individuals) or the “Non-US Entity Tax Form” (entities), you can provide us with multiple TINs. For each individual TIN, please select the country of issuance and provide the number. Please refer to the above table for the expected format for TINs in all of the EU Member States.

Please see below for confirmation of the expected format of TINs in your country, along with what it is known locally as .

Our tax forms can only be submitted if the TIN is provided in the correct format. Please note that when providing us with your TIN on the tax form, you should exclude any characters such as “-” or “/”.
