Is my personal tax information secure on Patreon?

When submitting your W-9, Patreon will check the information against the IRS database to ensure accuracy.

Real-Time TIN Verification makes it possible to proactively validate your information and check individual data against the IRS TIN matching database, Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) list, and Death Master File (DMF) as you submit your form. (This is done in real-time, and thus we will let you know if there is a mismatch or problem with the submission.)

All information provided is secure. We encrypt your forms with 2048bit RSA encryption.

Each time you want to update your W-9, you will have to submit an entirely new form.

If you have additional tax questions, please feel free to read through our US Creator Frequently Asked Questions guide or reach out to a local tax professional for further assistance.

Taxes on creator fees

Changes to pricing and applicable taxes starting on August 4, 2025. Existing creators will not see any increase

We’re consolidating our platform plans into a standard 10% platform plan + applicable taxes, and standardizing payment processing fees for all new creators who publish their page after August 4, 2025.

Get the details about this change and what to expect as an existing or new creator by visiting our guide on the upcoming pricing changes.

Depending on your location and business status, Patreon may be required to apply sales tax/VAT to the service fees it charges creators. These tax obligations are based on local laws, including how intermediary platforms are treated, the type of service, and whether any exemptions apply in your jurisdiction.

Which countries will Patreon apply tax on fees on?

Patreon may have obligations to collect tax on fees in certain US and non-US locations, which are generally aligned with those where underlying sales are also subject to tax. The taxes that apply to your fees depend on your location, business status, and local tax laws. Refer to our article, Patreon’s Sales Tax Requirements, for details regarding relevant locations.

How will tax apply and be collected?

Indirect taxes on creator fees are generally expected to apply per the rates and rules in the Creator’s location. Head over to our article Patreon’s Sales Tax Requirements, for information on tax rates that apply in various locations.

  • In the United States, where tax is applicable depending on the state, Patreon will generally add such tax
  • In non-US jurisdictions, the person liable to account for the tax will, in most cases, depend on the business status of the Creator. In these cases, Patreon will only need to collect tax where the Creator does not provide sufficient valid proof that they are a business customer according to the local rules

Where you provide Patreon with a valid VAT ID, and Patreon does not charge VAT on its fees to you, it will be your responsibility to assess whether you should account for VAT on services acquired from Patreon. Also, note that in certain countries (e.g., South Africa, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia) Patreon will generally charge VAT irrespective of your VAT ID registration status. Irrespective, we encourage you to add your relevant VAT ID to your account to enable overall tax document and compliance obligations.

What do I need to do as a creator?

Application of tax and related tax compliance obligations will depend on the location of the Creator and, often, in non-US locations, on Creator’s business status. For the most accurate application of tax, add the required location details in your Patreon account, as well as your relevant VAT ID in the available box of the W8 form included in the Tax section of your Patreon account.

For information on how to add your VAT ID to the W8 form and a list of relevant VAT IDs, please refer to our Help Center article Providing your VAT ID number. When you are providing your VAT ID, we suggest you review and confirm your business legal address in the same form, which will be our first point of reference for location details in the application of tax. Note also that we expect the VAT ID you share will match the location details provided.

In the absence of a valid VAT ID, Patreon may need to charge VAT/GST to non-US creators. VAT/GST thus charged may not be recoverable for a Creator; please consult with your local tax advisor in this regard.

Want to learn more about how Patreon approaches payments and tax? View the video “Funny you should ask: Reading & answering some of your biggest questions on payments” on Patreon for Creators. Currently, Patreon for Creators is only available in English.

How is tax calculated?

Where applicable, sales taxes or VAT will be applied on top of the fees charged to a Creator. For example, a Creator located in Australia makes a sale of digital content to a member in the US. The sale to the member is for $10, and the Creator has not provided Patreon with a valid tax registration number.

Purchase payment amount

$10.00

Creator fee (5%)

$0.50

GST at 10% applicable to fee (charged by Patreon and remitted to the relevant tax authority)

$0.05

Cash to Creator

$9.45

Tax will be applied at the time of each member transaction when fees are assessed and retained by Patreon. Taxes thus charged will be separately shown in your creator earnings dashboard.

*In this article (and generally on the Patreon platform), any reference to VAT includes reference to Value-Added Tax (“VAT”), Goods and Services Tax (“GST”), Harmonized Sales Tax (“HST”), and any other similar tax or indirect tax imposed in non-US jurisdictions, as relevant. Sales and use tax (“sales tax” or “SUT”) refers to sales taxes applicable in the United States. Together VAT and sales tax will be referred to as indirect taxes or transaction taxes.

US Creator: Frequently Asked Tax Questions

Let’s face it: taxes can be a lot – while we can’t offer specific advice on how to file your taxes, we’ve compiled this list of frequently asked questions from other creators to help you navigate this tax season with more ease.

  • In many jurisdictions, the money you receive from your members and customers is considered taxable income.
  • There are many types of taxpayers, from corporations to individuals, and how each is taxed is, unfortunately, beyond the scope of this document. That said, the IRS considers gross income to mean “all income from whatever source derived,” which can include payments made to you from your members or purchases from customers if you are selling digital products.
  • Most, if not all, creators will have expenses that offset some or all of that income. Further, if you are a legally recognized not-for-profit (for example, a USA 501(C)(3) charity), then you might not owe tax on your Patreon income. A local tax advisor would know for sure, so we encourage you to contact one for additional information. Learn more about being a non-profit creator here: Can non-profits use Patreon?
  • Depending on location, Patreon may need to withhold income tax from your earnings earned on Patreon. See, for example, our Mexican VAT & Income Taxes page. You can see your gross earnings and any income tax withheld amounts by visiting the Documents page of your Payouts section. In addition, for any tax withholdings, Patreon usually issues withholding certificates which should provide information and support for your relevant tax compliance. Patreon may have sales tax and VAT obligations related to the service fees it charges to its creators. This obligation usually depends on the local tax laws applicable to a creator’s jurisdiction. As a general rule, where applicable, all fees will be subject to tax unless an exemption or exception is found to be relevant in a particular location, for a particular fee, and/or for a particular scenario. Any taxes charged on top of your fees will be broken out in your Earning Dashboard.
  • Additionally, in several locations, we are obligated to add, collect, and remit sales tax and VAT in relation to some payments you receive, but those funds are not calculated in your gross earnings overview. In specific jurisdictions, Patreon is required to share the VAT payment obligations with you through a withhold VAT mechanism. In these situations, VAT is collected on amounts charged to fans and Patreon withholds part of this VAT to pay in its own name, and shares the rest of the collected VAT with you for you to remit directly to the relevant tax authorities. See our Mexican VAT & Income Taxes page. You should be able to see VAT collected, paid, withheld and passed on to you in your Earning Dashboard.
  • The IRS released a tax estimator that may be helpful to you as you plan for the US tax season.
  • Patreon may have sales tax and VAT obligations related to the service fees it charges to its creators. This obligation usually depends on the local tax laws applicable to a creator’s jurisdiction. As a general rule, where applicable, all fees will be subject to tax unless an exemption or exception is found to be relevant in a particular location, for a particular fee, and/or for a particular scenario. Any taxes charged on top of your fees will be broken out in your earnings dash.
  • Per IRS guidance FAQ FS-2023-06 issued March 2023, in order to calculate your gross earnings, we take the total amount of processed payments from your members on a gross basis before refunds and without regard to any adjustments for credits, cash equivalents, discount amounts, fees, refunded amounts, or any other amounts.
  • Your gross earnings for a given year if reportable (Forms 1099-K are issued once you hit certain thresholds) will be available on the Documents page of your Payouts section.
  • The W-9 form is used in a wide range of payment situations. Taxpayers commonly fill out a W-9 when working as a freelancer or independent contractor rather than an employee. The purpose of collecting the W-9 form is to record your tax identification number, along with your name and address, so that Patreon can notify the IRS of the amount earned in a calendar year if required.
  • Patreon requires creators who meet certain earnings thresholds to complete the W-9 form to generate a 1099-K – please review the section below to find out if you meet those earnings thresholds.
  • To complete a W-9 form for your Patreon, follow the directions below:
    • On Desktop, click on Your account from the bottom-left corner and then select Settings
    • In the Creator settings section, click on Billing and Payouts from the sub-menu
    • Go to the Tax settings section at the bottom of the page
    • Fill out W-9 form button to access an electronic W-9 form
  • For detailed instructions on how to complete your W-9 form, we recommend reviewing the IRS instructions for completing your W-9.
  • Form 1099-K is an IRS information return used to report certain payment transactions to improve voluntary tax compliance. It is wholly informational in nature; there is nothing on the form you could not otherwise find in the dashboards.
  • Whether or not you’ll receive a 1099-K from Patreon depends on your earnings. Review the current earnings thresholds to know if you should expect one from us: Will I receive a 1099 form?
  • A Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) is an identification number used by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) to administer tax laws. It is issued either by the Social Security Administration (SSA) or the IRS. The SSA issues a Social Security Number (SSN), whereas the IRS issues all other TINs.
  • When submitting your W-9, Patreon will check the information against the IRS database to ensure accuracy.
  • Real-Time TIN Verification makes it possible to proactively validate your information and check individual data against the IRS TIN matching database, Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) list, and Death Master File (DMF) as you submit your form. (This is done in real-time, and thus we will let you know immediately if there is a mismatch or problem with the submission.)
  • All information provided is secure. We encrypt your forms with 2048bit RSA encryption. Each time you want to update your W-9, you will have to submit an entirely new form, as we do not surface previous information considered sensitive.
  • Probably! It depends on the jurisdiction, but we are handling tax in Canada, Europe, the US, the UK, and many other places. If we do, there’s nothing you need to do or worry about. We’ll calculate and add the tax due on top of the member/customer payment, collect it, and remit it to the taxing authority of the member/customer directly. Find a list of places where this is the case here: Where is Patreon collecting tax, and what are the tax rates?
  • I have not paid US taxes, I don’t earn income from services performed in the US nor do I live or own anything in the US.
    • If you are a US citizen you should fill out a W-9 regardless of where you are currently sitting. Your income from Patreon may be subject to 1099 reporting.
    • If you are not a US citizen, and you are not in the US, generally you will fill out a W-8BEN if you are an individual and a W-8BEN-E if you are an entity. Please refer to the W-8BEN form for more instructions, here: Instructions for Form W-8BEN. While this is a US form, the purpose is to evidence non-US citizenship for tax purposes.
  • ID Type
  • Definition
  • SSN
  • For USA creators who are individuals/persons — your Social Security Number
  • EIN
  • Employer Identification Number
  • ITIN
  • Individual Taxpayer Identification Number
  • ATIN
  • Taxpayer Identification Number for Pending U.S. Adoptions
  • PTIN

Will I receive a 1099-K form?

You will only receive a Form 1099-K from Patreon if you are in the United States (or if you’re a US citizen living abroad) and reach the following threshold for the 2025 calendar year.

As per IRS guidance released July 2025, applicable reporting thresholds for 2025 calendar year earnings will be as follows:

US STATE

EARNINGS

All US States and territories

$20K+ USD in a calendar year

Arkansas

$2,500+ USD in a calendar year

Illinois

$1,000+ USD in a calendar year

New Jersey

District of Columbia

$600+ USD in a calendar year

Massachusetts

Maryland

Mississippi

Virginia

Vermont

Oregon

Any earnings

Only those meeting the above thresholds will receive a Form 1099-K from Patreon.

As per IRS guidance issued in March 2023 (FAQ FS-2023-06), the Form 1099-K reports gross earnings before fees and refunds. As such, be sure to account for these expenses and any other expenses incurred during your year as a Creator on your tax return.

It’s worth stressing that Patreon cannot provide tax advice, so please consult a tax professional. Be sure to report all income to the relevant tax authorities, regardless of whether you receive a Form 1099-K.

If you have multiple accounts on Patreon that use the same tax TIN (SSN or EIN), each account will receive its own form. To find your 1099-K, you need to log into each of your Patreon accounts for your statement(s). If you cannot locate it, send us a note by clicking the Email Patreon Support button below. It’s possible that we were unable to link multiple accounts owned by the same person and thus may not be aware of a threshold being met. Have no fear! We can always generate a form (or other proof of income if necessary).

While we proactively reach out to payment processors to prevent double reporting, some creators may receive a 1099-K from elsewhere that includes the payouts they have received from Patreon. Make sure that you do not double-report this income! Also, as always, please consult with a tax professional for specific tax advice.

Where can I access my 1099-K form?

You can access your 1099-K by visiting your Payouts Documents tab.

Will I get a 1099-K if I have multiple Patreon pages?

Patreon will provide one 1099-K per page, not per taxable identity. For example, if you have two pages with the same tax information on your W-9 and one of your pages met the earnings threshold, we’ll generate a 1099-K for both pages individually and report the earnings of each page individually.

I unlaunched my creator page, how do I access my digital 1099-K form?

If you’ve reached the earnings thresholds for a 1099-K, but have unlaunched your creator page, you can access your form with the steps below:

  • Log in to your Patreon account
  • Click on the option to finish your page from the menu — don’t worry, clicking this won’t relaunch your page; it will only take you to the creator page editor
  • Once you are on that page, replace the browser URL with the following link: patreon.com
  • In the Income tax section, click the Download button for the year you’d like to download your 1099-K for

Creators: Tiers and Benefits

Add Merch for Membership to your tiers

Merch for Memberships is only available to creators who are already using it. If you don’t see the Merch tab in your page settings, this feature isn’t available for your page.

Merch for membership is available to monthly billing creators on our Pro and Premium platform plans. This service allows creators to offer a merchandise item as a benefit on a tier, helping you reward your members even more. We take care of everything for you.

How do I include Merch on my tiers?

  • While logged in to your creator account, navigate to your page editor and click on the Merch link from your editor menubar
  • Click on the Create New Merch button to get started
  • Let us know if you want to create a loyalty merch program where members receive merch every 3 months for a year, or a one time merch item where members receive merch once, after three payments
  • Select the merch item you’d like to personalize. You can choose from a Sticker, Poster, Mug, T-shirt, Hoodie, or Tote bag. Depending on which item you select, we will recommend the minimum tier price based on the cost associated with producing and shipping the item. Learn more about merch earning schedules, here: When will my members earn merch?
  • Now, you can start customizing your exclusive merch! Upload the artwork you want printed on your merch item and choose how you’d like to place the artwork on your item
  • Now, click the Continue button
  • Add a short description that describes the merch item and then select the tier(s) you want to include this in. You can choose as many tiers as you would like. Then click the Review button
  • Once you’ve confirmed that everything is exactly the way you want it to be, hit Publish merch button to complete and add to your tiers

Things to know about creating merch

  • For best results, we’ve included templates that you can download and use to make sure your artwork fits the dimensions of your selected merch item
  • Using the in-product design preview tool, you can choose the size of artwork and how much space it will take up on the merch item
  • Once you’ve placed the image of your artwork on the item, we recommend you save the image by clicking on “View full size” and downloading the image to use in promotion of the item on socials
  • You will have the option to order proof of the item once you finish this process

What happens after I include Merch in my tiers?

After you publish your item, you can request a high-resolution preview from a real human designer as well as physical proof of the item.

If you need to edit or tweak something about the design, you can still do this as long as your item is produced.

The members in your merch tiers will receive an email announcing that you have included merch in the tiers that they are pledged to. If you’d like to let members on non-merch tiers know that you are now offering merch, you can let them know by sending them a bulk message filtered by tier or posting on your creator page. Learn to do this in this guide on How to direct message members.

All current and new members will receive your exclusive merch after 3 successful consecutive pledges. This does not apply retroactively to previous pledges, only going forward.

Please note: Tiers that utilize structured tier benefits may be exempt from the iOS in-app fee if they include physical goods, such as merch, commissions (delivered by mail) or other tangible goods. The increased offset price will not be included in these tiers when viewed in the iOS app, keeping the same price as on the Web and Android.

Visit our Advanced Sales Tax Settings article to learn more.

Be sure to ask your members to update their shipping address! We ship globally and you can find out where in this full list of countries we ship to.

Additional questions about Merch for membership

  • Your members will receive their exclusive merch after 3 successful pledges. For example, if they pledge on March 9, they will be eligible to receive their merch benefit after their June pledge processes successfully. This does not apply to retroactive successful pledges.
  • Once your member is eligible for merch, they will receive an email notification letting them know this. Then when the item ships, they will receive another email containing a tracking number that they can use to track shipment.
  • Please let us know or have them contact us and we’ll be happy to review if they are eligible for a replacement based on our policy.
  • If you’ve already got designs made, you can check out and use our Design guidelines and templates for your merch items to make the process seamless.

Adding Promo codes as a benefit to tiers

Promo codes are a lightweight way to instantly add value to new and existing tiers — it’s a simple way to deliver a code for discounts to your off-platform online store without the worry of how your members will access it.

Add a promo code to a tier

You can add a promo code to new and existing tiers you create from the Membership page. To add a promo code as a benefit, follow the steps below:

  • Select Creator studio from the left navigation
  • While on your page, click your Membership tab
  • Find the tier you want and click the Edit tier button
  • Click the Add benefit button, then click Browse recommended benefits to open a list of our benefit recommendations
  • You’ll find the one-time recommended benefit, Promo code — click the Add button for a promo code
  • Create your promo code and link to your site
  • Click the Save button
  • Click the Save tier button to add the promo code to your tier

Once you’ve saved your promo code, potential members will find the discount listed in the tier description.

Delivery of my new promo code

After you’ve added a promo code as a benefit to a tier, we get to work on making sure your members can enjoy their new perk! Here are the different ways members can access your promo code:

Welcome note

After confirming their membership with you, new members will find their promo code benefit in your welcome note to them.

Email

We’ll include your promo code in the welcome email we send new members, showing them all of the great benefits they’ve just unlocked.

My membership tab

The My membership tab is your members’ central hub for benefits you offer — once you add a promo code to a tier, we’ll add it to the My membership section for eligible members.

Existing members

If you’ve selected the option to notify eligible members about this new benefit, we’ll send an email to existing members showing them their newly added perk.

How do I remove a promo code?

How to remove a promo code from a tier

To fully delete a promo code benefit from benefits you track, it must be assigned as a benefit to a tier you are editing. If you’ve removed your promo code from all tiers, you’ll want to temporarily add it back so that you can delete it fully.

You can easily remove a promo code from a tier by heading to your Membership tab and following these steps:

  • Click the Edit tier button option in the upper right corner of the tier
  • Click the X button on the corner of your promo code
  • Confirm that you’d like to remove your promo code by clicking the OK button
  • Click the Save tier button to make the change

Once removed, we will stop tracking that promo code benefit for that tier moving forward. You can find a history of deleted benefits from your benefits page.

FAQ

  • If you have an e-commerce or merch site where you sell goods (outside of Patreon), promo codes are a great perk to give members. You can offer discounts to live events and concerts or share passwords to unlock access to your other websites.
  • Not at the moment. You can trigger an email sent to eligible members by manually updating the code each month.
  • We don’t have a way of tracking this on our end, but you can likely use your online store analytics to gain insight into member use of your promo code. If the code is unique to Patreon, you’ll be able to find exactly how many times that code has been used!
  • We recommend monitoring your online store for unusual promo code usage — if you do spot something fishy, you can always update the code in your tier editor and discontinue the code on your online store.
  • Yes! You can change and update promo codes from your tier editor. If you change anything about the promo code, we’ll automatically send an email to update your members.
  • Yes, they’ll receive the welcome note and receive an email as a new member of that tier.

Adjusting Benefit Value for Sales Tax

If a tier has multiple benefits, you can use this feature in the Advanced section of the tier editor to assign a value to each benefit. Then, in locations where tax law allows Patreon to calculate tax for each benefit individually, we can apply tax to just the portion of the pledge that covers a taxable benefit. Since not all benefits are taxable in all patron locations, using this feature may reduce the amount of the pledge that is taxable.

Value can be challenging to determine, so we’ve put together a few examples based on common benefits that many creators offer. These settings are not available to patrons, so they don’t have access to how you have set your benefit values.

Please note that these are just a small set of examples. You have the ability to customize your tax settings in any way you deem fit, based on the benefits you are offering. For more details on sales tax settings, please visit this help center article: About Advanced Sales Tax Settings

Best practices for increasing your tier prices

This article is for you if:

  • You use either our Charge Upfront, Monthly, or Per Creation billing model and want to increase your tier pricing
  • You use our Subscription billing model and want to increase your tier pricing beyond the $20 increase limit when using the repricing tool

If you have Subscription billing, you can raise your tier price by up to $20 more than the original price directly from your Membership tab — it only takes a few clicks.

If you want to raise a tier’s price beyond that $20 limit and you already have members on it, you’ll need to create a new tier with the updated price and phase out the old one. This guide helps you plan that switch so it goes smoothly for you and your members.

Looking to rethink your tiers or pricing? Check out how one creator’s tier “glow up” doubled their earnings on Patreon for Creators. Currently, Patreon for Creators is only available in English.

Communicate changes with your members

A smooth transition starts with clear communication. A few tips for letting your members know about an upcoming price change:

  • Give them a heads-up about a month before the next billing cycle, right after the current month’s payments have processed
  • Announce it anywhere your members are likely to see it. Making a post is a reliable way to make sure everyone has access to the information
  • Consider running a poll or a survey to get their input. It’s a good way to involve members and gauge how they feel about the change
  • Explain why you’re making the change and how it benefits them. Share a clear timeline for when the old tier goes away and the new one opens up

Here’s a quick template for letting members know about a new tier price and guiding them to switch:

The “Limited-time bonus alert” line below is optional — only include it if you’re offering something extra for members who join before the deadline.

Hi lovely members,

I’m so excited to announce my new [NEW TIER] tier. It’ll be available to join starting March 1st. [FORMER TIER] will stop accepting new members on March 10th and will be deleted entirely on March 25th, so be sure to pick a new tier before then.

Limited-time bonus alert.

Join [NEW TIER] by March 25th and get a limited edition sticker!

If you’re still in [FORMER TIER] when it’s deleted, you’ll still be my member, but you’ll show up as No tier and won’t have the same access as you do now.

Here’s how to pick a new tier: How to change your tier. Questions? Drop them in the comments.

Create your new tier

Once you’ve gathered member feedback, you’re ready to build the new tier at the updated price. The steps below are for desktop.

  • Select Creator studio from the left navigation
  • On your page, click your Membership tab
  • Scroll down and click + Add tier
  • Click Save. A tier name and price are all you need to save it, you can fill in the rest later
  • Once it’s saved, hide the tier from your page: click Edit tier, scroll down, and click Unpublish. This keeps members from joining before it’s ready

Pro tip: let a promotion do the work. A discount, free trial, or gift gets you that same “now’s the moment” energy without adding extra benefits to fulfill. They all live in your Promotions tab.

Give your new tier access to posts

Before you publish a new tier, make sure it has access to everything you’ve already posted. Right now, adding back-catalog access for a new tier is a manual step. If your posts are set to All members or Paid members only, any new tier automatically gets access, no extra work needed.

If you’ve set post access to Selected tiers, you’ll need to add your new tier to those posts yourself so members don’t lose access to anything. Good news: Bulk editing lets you update many posts at once, so you won’t be doing this one by one.

Bulk editing is currently only available on desktop.

To update access to your posts:
  • Select Creator studio from the left navigation
  • Click your Library
  • You’ll land on the Posts tab, where you’ll find your published posts and drops
  • Use the filter or search box to find specific posts. You can also sort by Title, Publish date, Last edited date, or Price (for posts sold as a one-time purchase)
  • Check the posts you want to edit
  • Click Edit
  • Select Edit access
  • Choose the tier you want to grant access to
  • Click Update
  • You’ll see a message noting this replaces the existing settings. Click Confirm and update to apply the change

We’ve also put together a full guide: Bulk editing your posts

Unpublish the old tier

Unpublishing is usually the safer move here. It disappears from your tier options so no new members can join, while anyone already in it sees no change and can stay until they switch or cancel on their own time.

You can still post specifically for members in an unpublished tier, which is a nice way to keep them in the loop and nudge them toward switching.

Once your new tier is ready, here’s how to unpublish the old one:

  • Select Creator studio from the left navigation
  • On your page, click your Membership tab
  • Find the tier and click Edit next to it
  • Scroll to the bottom and click More
  • Select Unpublish tier, then confirm

Unpublishing removes the tier from your page so no new members can join, but it stays active for anyone already subscribed, gifted a subscription, or on a free trial, and you can republish it anytime. You’ll know it worked when you see Unpublished at [DATE] next to that tier.

There’s no rush here — tiers can stay unpublished indefinitely, so it’s worth waiting until everyone has switched or canceled before deleting one. If members are slow to move, a friendly reminder through a post or a private message usually does the trick.

To check which tier a member is in, search their email or profile name. You can also point them to How to change your tier.

Delete the tier

We advise against deleting a tier that still has members on it. Unpublish it instead.

Before you delete a tier:
  • Once it’s deleted, it can’t be recovered
  • Members who haven’t switched out will keep paying the old tier’s price. They won’t have a tier, and since they aren’t Custom pledge members either, they won’t show up under No tier. Find them in your Relationship manager using the All tiers filter
  • Deleting a tier doesn’t cancel a member’s payment. To stop future payments, members need to cancel their membership
  • If you offer annual memberships and this tier has active annual members, unpublish it instead so no new members can join. They’ve already paid for the year
To delete a tier:
  • Select Creator studio from the left navigation
  • On your page, click your Membership tab
  • Find the tier and click Edit next to it
  • Scroll to the bottom and click More
  • Select Delete, then confirm. This can’t be undone, so double-check your list before you do

Choosing the right Merch program for your Membership

Merch for Memberships is only available to creators who are already using it. If you don’t see the Merch tab in your page settings, this feature isn’t available for your page.

There are so many ways you can offer merch benefits to your members. In this article, we’ll discuss different Merch programs you can offer - from limited-time merch drops to monthly merch clubs and everything in between!

While deciding which merch program is right for you, you might find a few of our other resources helpful. For details on when current and new members will earn merch, visit our guide on members’ earning period.

You can also learn more about how to delete or retire your merch items in this guide on managing your merch items.

Recurring Merch programs

Loyalty programs

We think our loyalty program feature is best to offer Merch to your members. A loyalty program delivers four items you select to a member over the first year of their pledge.

Receiving a new merch delivery every three months that they pledge gives each member ongoing value that makes it easy for them to stick around. Even better, since every member earns the four items on their own schedule after they sign up, you can be sure that everyone gets a consistent, excellent experience without any extra scheduling or tracking effort from you. To make the most of your loyalty program, consider placing less expensive items earlier in the program and more expensive items at the end.

Seasonal recurring merch

What if you don’t want your members to earn recurring merch on individual schedules and instead want to promote the same merch product to all your members at strategic times of the year? One example may be seasonal merch drops for spring, summer, fall, and winter. You can offer this to your members with some ongoing action from you.

To start this program, simply publish a single merch item to your tiers before March starts (the beginning of spring in the Northern Hemisphere), then at the end of May, retire that item and replace it with a new item for summer. Repeat this process again at the end of August and October, and your members who pledge for the whole year will earn all four items. When you end each item, ensure that you retire the item instead of deleting it so members receive the merch they’re due.

Seasonal recurring merch can be a great way to drive ongoing buzz about your membership. And best of all, members are still required to pledge for three months to receive the item, so you don’t have to worry about members signing up and then leaving.

Monthly merch clubs

Maybe you’re interested in starting a Poster of the Month or Sticker of the Month club? To offer this program to your members, simply publish a new item at the end of every month while also retiring the item from the previous month based on their billing anniversary. members will earn a new item monthly, starting three months after they pledge, based on their billing date. Be sure to create a new item every time you want your members to earn something — if you only edit the design of an item, members will only earn that item once with the latest design.

Other Merch programs

Merch welcome gift

Not sure where to start? A welcome gift is the simplest way to add Merch to your membership. Simply publish a one-time delivery item to your tiers, and every member will earn the item once, three months after they start their pledge. Want to update your design? You can edit it at any time without changing your members’ progress.

Limited-time merch drop

A limited-time merch drop can be a fantastic way to encourage members to join your membership. To offer limited-time merch, simply choose the one-time delivery option, publish the item to your tiers, and then retire the item from your tiers when you are ready to end the offering.

members who pledge while the item is on your tiers will be eligible to earn it, and as always, they are required to pledge for three months to earn the item. Be sure to promote to your members before you publish your merch drop, and also let them know when the offering is about to end!

Loot boxes

Merch bundles or loot boxes can be an exciting way to earn swag. Unfortunately, we aren’t currently able to pack multiple merch items into a single delivery. We also aren’t able to randomize which items a member receives. However, members can earn multiple Merch items at the same time!

If your tier is priced high enough to allow it, you can add multiple merch items to any tier, and the member will earn all the items together. Earning multiple items at once can be combined with any of the programs mentioned here except loyalty programs.

Creator Coins as a Membership Benefit

As of October 2021, creators on Patreon can offer social tokens, or creator coins, as a membership benefit for their patrons. Below are answers to some of the most common creator questions about this. This Help Center article will be updated as additional resources become available.

Would my coins be developed, issued, and/or stored on Patreon?

On Patreon, creators can offer the coins as a membership benefit for patrons. Patreon is not the developer, issuer, or distributor of the coins, and cannot change the supply of the coins.

How might creators develop their own creator coins?

There are a number of third party companies that creators can work with to develop, issue, and store their own coins. It could be available to supporters off-platform, too. Creators can elect for their coins to unlock special perks for patrons like exclusive merchandise, passes to a show or livestream, access to an exclusive Discord community, and more.

Will my coins be exclusively available to my patrons?

Patreon does not require you to keep the coins exclusive to patrons on Patreon, but if you want to make it exclusive to patrons on Patreon, you can.

Is developing creator coins mandatory?

No. The decision as to whether you would like to offer creator coins is opt-in, totally up to individual creators. The idea is to allow creators to have new options in the types of benefits they can provide to patrons, not to force you to provide this type of benefit.

How are creator coins held by patrons?

Coins can be held by a third party company on behalf of your patrons or by the patrons themselves in a non-custodial wallet (where custody of a user’s funds are 100% in the user’s control).

Does Patreon offer cryptocurrency as a means of payout?

No. Patreon’s payout process remains the same, and Patreon continues to disallow partial payments such as coupons, gift cards, or incentives to purchase cryptocurrency. The policy around creator coins as a membership benefit is strictly a new type of benefit creators can pursue if they so choose.

Are creator coins tradable or redeemable for USD or other fiat currency on Patreon?

No.

Where can I read Patreon’s guidelines with respect to creator coins?

Check out our Benefits Guidelines.

I have additional questions about Patreon’s guidelines related to creator coins.

We welcome additional questions! You can email Guidelines@Patreon.com.

Deleting benefits from tiers

You can only delete benefits while they are connected to a tier. If you are trying to clear the clutter from your Benefits page, you will first need to add the benefit back to a tier in order to permanently remove the benefit from tracking.

To remove a benefit from a tier:

  • While logged in to your creator account, click on the My Page button from the left sidebar navigation if you aren’t already there
  • While on your page, click on the Page controls or “…” button
  • Then, click on the Edit Tiers link from the submenu
  • Click the Edit tier button at the upper right corner of the tier you want to remove the benefit from
  • In the benefits section, you’ll find a list of current benefits for that tier. Click the X to remove a benefit
  • Click the Save tier button to finalize your benefit removal

When you remove a benefit from one tier, we will not remove the benefit from all of your tiers. If you’d like to fully delete a benefit, please remove the benefit from each tier individually.

Design guidelines and templates for your merch items

Merch for Memberships is only available to creators who are already using it. If you don’t see the Merch tab in your page settings, this feature isn’t available for your page.

If you already have the designs made for your merch items, we have a number of guidelines and templates to make things easier for you! Below are the specifications for adding your artwork.

Image quality

Artwork should be at least 150 DPI, and the file format should be JPG or PNG. For artwork with a transparent background, use a PNG file. For designs that do not require transparency, use a JPEG file.

Color profile

Save your file to the RGB color profile, or convert CMYK art to RGB before uploading. Do not use transparent colors. Colors that have less than 100% opacity may not print correctly. Use solid colors for all elements of your design.

Design templates

We have design templates you can use to make sure your artwork prints exactly as you want it to. You can download a template for the following merch items:

  • Download Mug template
  • Download Sticker template
  • Download Mini Print template
  • Download Poster template
  • Download Organic Tote Bag template

Ending a merch item

Merch for Memberships is only available to creators who are already using it. If you don’t see the Merch tab in your page settings, this feature isn’t available for your page.

You can end a merch item or loyalty program by clicking on the trash or delete item button beside an item in the Your Merch section of the Merch tab. Once selected, you’ll have the option of either deleting or retiring your merch item. You can delete items that you retire later on.

  • Retiring a merch item
  • Deleting a merch item

Retiring a merch item

Retiring a merch benefit immediately removes the item from your page, and no new members will be eligible to receive this merch. However, members who are making progress towards earning this benefit will still be eligible to receive their items. So, retiring merch is a way to remove a merch item from your page while still delivering the value to members already earning the merch item.

You can only retire a single merch item, not an entire loyalty program.

Deleting a merch item

Deleting a merch item or loyalty program immediately removes the item from your page, and no new members will be eligible to receive this merch. members who are currently earning this merch item but have not yet become eligible also will not receive the item. If you choose to delete an item, we recommend giving those members a heads up that they will not receive the merch benefit.

Free Trials FAQ

Please note that you must be enrolled in subscription billing to offer free trials.

All creators still using legacy billing will be required to switch to subscription billing by November 1, 2026. If you’d like one-to-one assistance during this transition, you must contact Support via your settings by September 30th, 2026.

Subscription billing offers a more predictable model for you and your members, and unlocks features like Autopilot, Gifting, Discounts, and Tier Repricing.

How it works

Free trials let potential members try out your membership for a 7-day trial period before they’re charged.

  • Choose your tier(s). You can offer a 7-day trial for any or all of your tiers. We recommend starting free trials with your most popular tier
  • Free trial members get all the benefits of their tier, including past posts (but not Merch). They’ll provide a payment method at subscription, but won’t be charged until the end of their trial period
    • Please note that you won’t see earnings for a free trial tier until members are charged at the end of their trial period
  • See how free trials help you grow. You can see which of your members joined through a free trial in Relationship manager and how many converted into paying members at the end of their trial in Insights

Free trial members are included in your active member count for the duration of their trial period. You can find a breakdown of free-trial members by using the paid status filter in your Relationship Manager or by visiting your Membership Insights dashboard.

Who can enable free trials?

Creators who use Subscription billing can enable Free trials. Creators whose work is categorized as Adult content must complete ID verification before Free trials are available to them.

If you have questions about your eligibility, contact our support team.

Enabling free trials

You can enable free trials for any or all of your tiers directly from your Dashboard by following the steps below:

  • From the left-side menu, click Creator Studio
  • Click Dashboard
  • Select Membership
  • Navigate to the Paid membership tiers section and find the tier you want to enable Free trials
  • From the bottom-right corner of the tier, click Edit
  • Scroll down and toggle on Free trials
  • Click Save to apply the changes
  • Repeat for any additional tiers

You can turn off free trials for new visitors at any time. If you disable the free trial option, existing members currently on a trial will complete their remaining trial period. Be sure to promote your free trial alongside any promotion of your membership to encourage fans to join.

FAQ

  • Free trials are available to people who have never subscribed to you before. Members are allowed one free trial per account and form of payment to each creator.
  • Former members won’t have the option to start a free trial — they’ll only have the option to join and pay upfront for a tier with a free trial.
  • Free trials are only available to creators on subscription billing.
  • Visitors to your page will see Start free trial instead of Join now on your chosen trial tier(s). Anyone joining a free trial tier will automatically start on a free trial.
  • At checkout, they will need to enter a payment method but won’t be charged anything until the trial ends. They will then have immediate access to all the benefits in their tier, including past posts.
  • Free trial members will also receive a confirmation and welcome email (with the tier’s welcome note if you have one), just as paying members do.
  • You will also receive the new member notification email, which will specify that the member is on a free trial.
  • At the end of the trial period, the member’s payment method will be charged for a full month and again monthly on that same date unless they cancel. They will receive an email confirming their payment and the standard welcome email from you.
  • If a member decides to cancel their free trial, they can still enjoy all the membership benefits until the trial period ends.
  • If they sign up again after canceling, they’ll have to pay the membership amount for whichever membership tier they choose. This applies whether they rejoin the same tier or a different one. The new membership starts immediately upon rejoining, and the previous free trial ends.
  • You can filter by a member’s free trial status in the Relationship manager and message them accordingly. You can also see an overview of your free trial members in your Membership Insights dashboard.
  • To see how your free trials are performing, visit Insights. Free trial members are included in your New member count for the duration of their trial. If a member cancel before the trial ends, they will show as cancelled. In the Free trial activity section you can check how many free trials were started, completed, converted into a paying member, or cancelled within a selected time period. Please note that some started trials may still be in progress and aren’t yet eligible to be counted as converted.
  • Free trial members will not count in your New member count until they’ve been charged for their first payment.
  • To turn off a free trial for a tier, visit your Membership tab to edit the tier and toggle off free trials. New members will no longer be able to join via a free trial. Members with an existing free trial will finish out the remainder of their trial period.
  • All free trials turn into monthly subscriptions at the end of the trial period. Members who wish to become annual members will need to edit their membership in their Active memberships tab.
  • Custom pledging is not supported on free trials.
  • Members on tiers that offer Merch for Membership will not start earning toward merch rewards until their first payment.
  • Your integrations and webhooks will be given access to free trials just like paid members. Each integration may be different in how access is granted and removed.
  • For Discord, members will be granted appropriate roles for access based on tier eligibility. If they cancel, they will have their roles removed accordingly.
  • Yes. However, members who join tiers with free trials will only be eligible for a Special Offer if they become a paid member at the end of their trial.
  • We recently rolled out Apple’s in-app purchasing requirements to Patreon’s iOS mobile app, which currently does not support free trials on this system. We are working to support free trials in the iOS app as a fast follow. Fans can start a free trial on web, mobile web, and Android.

Get members’ shipping addresses

You can add a shipping address requirement as you create your tiers, or add this requirement to existing Tiers at any time.

Creating a new Tier? We show you how to make a tier

How do I add a shipping address requirement to an existing tier?

When you edit a Tier to request shipping addresses, only new members will be prompted to enter their shipping address. To make sure that existing members know to add this information, you can send those members a note and request they update their membership to include their address.

  • While logged in to your creator account, click on the My Page button from the left sidebar navigation if you aren’t already on this page
  • Click on the Page controls “…” button
  • Click on the Edit Tiers link from the submenu
  • Select the Edit tier link to the right of the tier you are editing
  • Scroll down, expand the Advanced section, and select the checkbox in the Shipping address field, to request this from members during membership confirmation
  • Click the Save tier button!

We won’t alert existing members to this change, so once you’ve added the Shipping address request to your Tier, it’s a good idea to message existing members. Let them know you’re collecting members’ shipping addresses and why. Feel free to link members to this article to update their membership: How do I change my shipping address?

Gifting memberships to your fans (creator to fan gifts)

Gifting complimentary memberships to fans is a great way to expand your community, thank loyal fans who aren’t yet members, entice fans to try out Patreon before committing, or thank collaborators. This feature is available for all creators who are on subscription billing.

This article covers how creators can gift complimentary memberships to fans. For resources on how fans can gift memberships to other fans, see this article.

Key things to know about gifting

  • Existing members can redeem gifted memberships without disrupting their current subscription
  • Gifting is currently available to all creators who are on subscription billing
  • You can gift between 1-12 months of membership to up to 1000 people per link (or any lower cap you set). If you offer annual memberships, gifts of 1 year of membership will be at the discounted annual membership price
  • You can gift published tiers with no tier limits
  • Fans can redeem their gift on desktop or mobile web. Mobile app redemption is not yet available
Gifted Membership Scenarios

Use the toggles below to explore common scenarios and see how gifted memberships affect access and billing:

  • Let’s say someone who is already a member of a creator in their entry-level tier is gifted a membership to the same creator, at the same tier. In this case, the gift will apply as soon as it’s redeemed, and the paid period pauses.
  • For example:
    • Original Billing Date: 15th of every month.
    • Gift Redemption Date: 25th.
    • Gift Coverage Period: 25th to the 25th of the following month.
    • Remaining Paid Access: 20 days left on the original subscription when the Gift was redeemed, which runs immediately after the Gift period ends.
    • Next Billing Cycle: Starts after the remaining 20 days are finished (on the 15th).
    • Specific Access Period (Gift + Remaining Days): Paid access runs from the 25th (end of gift) to the 14th (the day before the original billing date).
  • Someone who is already a member of a creator in their entry-level tier is gifted a membership to the same creator at the higher tier. In this case, the gift will apply as soon as it’s redeemed, granting access to the high-tier benefits immediately and pausing the paid period.
  • For example:
    • Original Billing Date: 15th of every month
    • Gift Redemption Date: 25th
    • Gift Coverage Period: 25th to the 25th of the following month
    • Remaining Paid Access: If the member doesn’t upgrade, they will drop back to their prior tier when the gift period ends and will still have 20 days of paid access left on the original subscription when the Gift was redeemed, which runs immediately after the Gift period ends.
    • Next Billing Cycle: Starts after the remaining 20 days are finished (on the 15th).
    • Specific Access Period (Gift + Remaining Days): Paid access runs from the 25th (end of gift) to the 14th (the day before the original billing date).
  • Someone who is already a member of a creator at the middle-tier is gifted a membership to the same creator at a lower tier. In this case, the gift will apply as soon as it’s redeemed, granting access to the tier benefits immediately and pausing the paid period.
  • For example:
    • Original Billing Date: 15th of every month
    • Gift Redemption Date: 25th
    • Gift Coverage Period: 25th to the 25th of the following month
    • Remaining Paid Access: If the member doesn’t upgrade, they will revert to their prior tier when the gift period ends and will still have 20 days of paid access left on the original subscription when the Gift was redeemed, which runs immediately after the Gift period ends.
    • Next Billing Cycle: Starts after the remaining 20 days are finished (on the 15th).
    • Specific Access Period (Gift + Remaining Days): Paid access runs from the 25th (end of gift) to the 14th (the day before the original billing date).
  • When a member cancels a Gift before the gifting period ends, they lose access right away. If a paid membership exists, billing resumes immediately, using the remaining days of paid access from the original subscription when the Gift was redeemed.
  • You can only have one gifted membership per tier at a time. If you try to redeem a second gift for the same creator, regardless of tier, you’ll receive an error message. You can either wait for the current gift to expire or cancel it in Membership Settings.

Please note: merchandise rewards are not earned through gifted memberships. Only memberships with an attached payment to the member account are currently eligible to earn Patreon merchandise rewards. This rule also applies to regular merchandise items: a member will not begin earning merchandise rewards until their account makes its own payment.

How gifting works

As a creator, you can gift between 1–12 months of membership. Gifts can be redeemed by new fans, free members, canceled members, or existing paid members. Each gift link can be redeemed by up to 1000 fans or fewer, depending on the limit you set.

Who can create a gift?
  • You are using subscription billing. Visit your Billing settings to check your billing type
  • If you create 18+ content, you’ll have to complete Age Verification. Learn more about the Age Verification process here
  • You have a published paid tier that doesn’t have limited spots

Creating a gift

To create a gift as a creator, follow the steps below while using a desktop.

  • Select Creator studio from the left navigation, then open your Promotions page
  • Click on the Gifts tab from the top menu
  • Click on the Add a gift button if it’s the first time you’re creating a gift, or click on the +Add button at the top right of the page if you have existing gifts
  • Enter the following fields:
    • Title: Name your campaign for your own reference. This isn’t shown publicly
    • Tier: Decide which tier you’d like to gift. (Note unpublished tiers and tiers with limited spots are currently unavailable to gift)
    • Length: Choose between 1 – 12 months
    • Redemption limits: Up to 1000 people can claim a gift for each link
    • Start/end date: You must have a start date, which can be scheduled in the future. The end date is optional. If you choose to set one, the gift can no longer be redeemed after your specified date
  • After you create the gift link, you can share it by selecting the copy icon in the table view of all gifts or clicking on the three dots … and selecting Share gift link

Managing gifts

Editing gifts

You can edit existing gifts at any time by navigating to your Gifts tab, clicking on the three dots … and selecting Edit.

If your gift link has not gone live yet, you can edit the following fields:

  • Title
  • Length
  • How many people can claim
  • Personalized message
  • Promotion start and end date

If your gift link is already active, you can edit the following fields:

  • Title
  • Personalized message
  • Promotion end date
    • To immediately end a gift redemption period, just edit the end date to a date in the past.
Seeing fans who have redeemed a gift

Under the Gift tab in your Promotions page, you can see who redeemed a gift, and when their gift period expires.

You can find more information in your Relationship manager (via Creator studio → Audience), where you can see the following details:

  • Which members have redeemed a gift and are actively in their gifted membership period. To see this, select the Gifted by you filter. Members who are actively in a gifted membership will also have a gift box icon next to their Current Tier.
  • A member’s history of gift redemption even if they’ve upgraded to a paid membership or have canceled. To see this, click on their profile from your Relationship manager

To see which gifted members are eligible for benefits in a specific month, use the Benefits tab.

Insights about gift redemption

You can find insights about gift redemption under the Gift tab in your Promotions page. Click on a gift link to see the number of redemptions, and the number of gifted members who stayed on as paying members after their gift period ended.

In your Insights section, gifted members will be counted as paid members for the duration of their gift period.

How fans can redeem your gift

Fans can follow the gift link you share to redeem your gift. If they don’t have an account yet, they’ll be prompted to sign up before redeeming their gift. At redemption, they can opt out of staying connected as a free member after their gift period ends.

Fans who are redeeming a gift from creators of 18+ content must confirm they are over 18 years of age to access the page.

About fan-purchased gifts

In addition to gifting memberships directly, creators may also receive gifted memberships purchased by fans. Fans can choose to:

  • Gift access to someone they personally know (friends and family), or
  • Gift a membership for you to share with members of your community (currently in Beta with a small group of creators)

If your creator page is included in the Community gifting Beta, fans will see the option to purchase a community gift directly from your page (at patreon.com/[creatorURL]/gift). You’ll receive an email notification when a community gift is purchased, and you’ll be able to share those gifted memberships with your audience in any way you choose, such as posts, direct messages, or social media.

Key things to know:

  • These gifts are non-renewable and valid for 90 days from the date of purchase
  • Creators can distribute community gifts at their discretion. You can find your community gifts in your Gift tab within Promotions. There will be a community gifts table with gift links displayed
  • Fans can purchase multiple community gift links for redemption
  • Creators can see who purchased a community gift, but recipients will only see the gifter’s name if it was shared publicly

This feature is currently available only to a small group of creators. If you’re part of the beta, this gifting option is automatically available on your creator page.

Fans can convert their gift into a paid membership

Fans can continue to receive access to paid benefits by converting their gift into a paid membership. They can do this any time during the gifted period by visiting Memberships, selecting Extend membership, and adding their payment information to opt into a paid membership. They won’t be charged until their gifted membership ends.

How do I pay for merch?

Merch for Memberships is only available to creators who are already using it. If you don’t see the Merch tab in your page settings, this feature isn’t available for your page.

How the merch fee and billing works

When does the 3% fee to use Merch start?

You will begin paying the additional 3% fee immediately upon signing up for Merch. This 3% fee applies to your total monthly earnings on Patreon.

When will I be billed for shipping merch?

You will be billed for the cost of a merch item whenever a member earns the item and the order to ship that item is successfully processed. You can learn more about when members earn their merch in this guide.

Most Merch orders are processed once per day. If an order to ship an item cannot be processed (often due to a problem with a member’s address), we will not charge you for that item. We will attempt to retry an unsuccessful order for up to 100 days after an item has been earned. You can find your merch fulfillment bill in your earnings dashboard.

Do I need to enter a credit card to pay for merch?

Nope! You will pay for the merch items with your Patreon balance.

I’m seeing a warning when I try to withdraw my account balance. What does that mean?

Because the merch you offer is funded from your account balance, withdrawing your account balance can delay merch shipments. Merch orders are processed after a member has been successfully billed for the month. If you withdraw your entire account balance, there is a risk that you could delay a merch shipment until more funds arrive in your account.

How does this warning calculate how much merch is waiting to be shipped?

Any Merch for Membership items that have been earned by members in the last 100 days but have not yet shipped will be included in this number. If an item does not ship successfully we keep attempting to ship the item for 100 days after it is earned, so the number of items that have been earned but not shipped may seem higher than expected. You can explore these items at any time by visiting your Benefits page. There are a few reasons that an item can be earned but not yet shipped:

  • Orders have not been processed since the item was earned (see the above schedule)
  • There has not been enough account balance to pay for the item when orders have been processed
  • The member has not entered a valid shipping address
  • The member has not entered a valid size selection (if the item requires one)

These factors, as well as how long ago an item was earned, are helpful to consider when deciding whether to withdraw your account balance. Recently-earned items that have a valid shipping address attached are ready to ship and would likely be delayed by withdrawing your account balance. Orders that are missing a valid shipping address or size selection cannot be shipped and are less likely to be delayed by withdrawing your account balance. However, Patreon automatically reminds members to update their shipping address whenever we are unable to ship an item to them, so these orders could be updated by the member with a shipping address at any time. Items earned more recently are more likely to have their shipping address and size selection updated by members, and items that were earned less recently are less likely to be updated.

How do I learn what I’ve already paid for the merch items?

In your Earnings Dashboard, you can find a monthly breakdown of the merch items paid for as well as the Patreon platform fee.

Estimating how much your merch will cost

How can I estimate how much I’ll owe?

We help you out with estimation when creating your merch item, but there are other things you might want to estimate for. Note: You will only be charged for merch items that have been shipped.

When creating your items, we estimate the cost of your merch items by multiplying the number of current members in the assigned tier (at that time) by the cost of the item. Most creators pay less than this estimate because not all of their members enter a shipping address and/or size preference. We will email your members to remind them to enter their information, and you can also encourage them to update their information in their memberships.

If you are publishing a one-time merch item, your members must pledge for 3 consecutive payments before they become eligible for merch and the merch ships. If you are launching a merch loyalty program, your members will earn merch after, 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. You can learn more about when members typically earn merch here. You can expect to pay for merch sent to be sent to existing members between 2 and 4 months after a merch item is added to a tier, depending on what time during the month you add merch to that tier and whether you charge your members for each month up front.

You can check for eligible members in Benefit Tracker and in the monthly merch email we send you:

Why did I send more/fewer items than I expected?

Creators using Merch for Membership frequently send and pay for fewer merch items to their existing members than expected. Here are a few reasons why:

  • There are fewer members pledging to your tier now than when you created your merch (i.e. members have stopped their membership),
  • Some members have chosen to opt-out of receiving physical goods from that tier
  • Many members have not added a valid shipping address or selected a size for their merch item. members must have a valid address associated with their account to receive merch.

You can easily identify which of your members need to add or update their shipping addresses in your Benefits page. We recommend sending messages and making posts to your Merch tiers to remind your members to update their shipping address and size preferences.

How to adjust your membership tier prices

All creators are now using subscription billing. If your account was still on a legacy billing model on November 1, 2026, we switched it automatically and emailed you when the switch was complete.

Key details depending on your previous billing model:

  • Per-creation: If you haven’t resumed billing yet, it stays paused until you review your new tier prices. Learn how to resume billing
  • First-of-the-month: Your existing members are still billed on the 1st of each month. New members are billed on the date they join

As your offerings evolve, you may decide to adjust the prices of your tiers to better reflect what you share with members. This guide walks you through the process of changing tier prices, provides insights on how changes affect members, and highlights best practices to ensure a smooth transition.

Please note: If your tier includes merchandise, you must remove all merch items before changing the tier’s price. This prevents errors and ensures your price update is applied correctly.

What you need to know before getting started

  • Eligibility: You can reprice tiers with existing members if you’re using the Subscription Billing model. Check your billing model in your payout settings to confirm eligibility
  • Device-specific pricing: Members who join through iOS in-app purchases will remain at their original price, as Apple doesn’t allow Patreon’s pricing tool to adjust these payments.
  • Free trials: Tiers with free trials cannot currently have their prices updated (this feature is coming soon)
  • Billing model: First-of-month billing users must switch to Subscription Billing in payout settings to enable tier repricing

How to change the price of your tier

Before updating your tier price, go to the tier’s merch settings and remove all associated merch items. Once the merch is removed, you can proceed to adjust your tier’s price.

  • Select Creator studio from the left navigation to open your Dashboard
  • From your page, navigate to the Membership tab
  • Select the tier you want to edit the price for and click Edit tier
  • In the Monthly price section, select the Edit price button
  • A pop-up will open, then enter the New monthly price (you can increase it by up to $20 or lower it to any amount)
  • Adjust the settings of Who should the new price apply to by selecting one of the two options:
    • New members only - Your existing members will keep their current price
    • All members - The new price will apply immediately for new members, and existing members will change price in their next renewal
  • Once you fill in the new price and select who it should apply to, click on the Confirm update button
  • Carefully review the pop-up confirmation and click Apply new price to save changes

Existing members in the tier are automatically notified when the price of their membership changes. The notification includes details about when the new price will take effect. All renewals for the next 31 days will be at the old price, so existing members aren’t charged the new price right away. Your members will receive an email informing them that their tier price will change after 31 days and that their next bill will reflect the new price.

Troubleshooting: If you try to change your tier price while merch is still attached, the update may fail or behave unexpectedly. Always remove merchandise first, then update your tier price, and finally re-add any merch items if needed.

Looking to rethink your tiers or pricing? Check out “Podcaster Lara Schoenhals on simplifying her tiers and overdelivering” on Patreon for Creators. Currently, Patreon for Creators is only available in English.

Key considerations for tier repricing

Price adjustment limit

  • You can raise your tier price by up to $20. This cap ensures that price changes remain reasonable for your members (e.g., if your current tier price is $5, you can increase it to up to $25) If you need to increase beyond this, create a new tier and encourage members to switch
  • You can decrease tier prices without limit, but we don’t recommend setting tiers below $3

You can learn more about Best practices for increasing your tier prices

Price lock period

  • After changing a tier’s price, it is locked for 31 days to notify members. During this period:
    • Renewals are billed at the old price
    • New members pay the updated price
    • Benefits, titles, and descriptions can still be edited
  • Once this 31-day period is over, renewals will be billed at the new tier price, and if necessary, you may adjust the price again
  • We do not recommend changing the price of a single tier multiple times during consecutive months, as it may lead to an increase in cancellations from your members

Impact on membership renewals

If you keep existing members on the old price, their future renewals will not be impacted, and they will continue to pay their original price.

  • Monthly members: Price updates take effect one renewal cycle after the change
    • For example, if you change your tier price on September 3 and an existing member’s renewal is on September 5, they will still pay the old price on September 5, as it falls within the 31-day Price Lock Period. Their next renewal on October 5 will reflect the updated price
  • Annual memberships: Updates depend on their renewal date relative to the price lock period
    • For example, if you change your tier price on September 3 and an annual member’s renewal date is October 1, their renewal will remain at the old price because it falls within the 31-day Price Lock Period
    • If an annual member’s renewal date is not within 31 days of when you change your tier price, the new price will be in effect when they renew.
      • For example, if you change your tier price on September 3 and an annual member’s renewal date is October 5, their renewal will reflect the new price. Annual members receive an additional payment reminder two weeks before their renewal, providing extra notice of the price change

Existing members who subscribed via iOS in-app purchases will retain their original tier price. This limitation is due to Apple’s requirements, which don’t support Patreon’s pricing adjustment tools.

Email notifications sent to members

Once you confirm any price changes, your paid members will automatically receive an email from Patreon letting them know their membership price will change, the updated amount, and when this change will take effect.

Note: If you keep existing members at the old price, they will not receive an email notification when you change the price for new members.

Here are some examples of the emails Patreon sends to members:

  • Hello [Member name],
  • The price of your recurring subscription to [Tier Name] from [Creator Name] was recently changed to [$Y new price]. Just like any independent business, creators may adjust prices to account for increased costs or other changed circumstances.
  • What this means for you
  • Your upcoming renewal on [Member’s Next Charge Date] will be at the previous price of [$X old price]. Your renewals starting on [Member’s Subsequent Next Charge Date] will be at the new price of [$Y new price], unless you cancel before that date here. Otherwise, your monthly subscription will continue renewing automatically and you’ll be notified in advance of any further price changes.
  • You can review the benefits included with your membership here.
  • Thank you for subscribing to [Creator Name] and supporting their creativity on Patreon!
  • Patreon
  • Hello [Member name],
  • The price of your recurring subscription to [Tier Name] from [Creator Name] was recently changed to [$Y new price]. Just like any independent business, creators may adjust prices to account for increased costs or other changed circumstances.
  • What this means for you
  • This update goes into effect 1 month from today on [Today + 1 month] for all existing members. This means your upcoming annual renewal on [Member’s Next Charge Date] will be based off the previous tier price of [$X old price]. Any subsequent renewals starting on [Member’s Subsequent Next Charge Date] will be based off the new tier price of [$Y new price], unless you cancel before that date here. Otherwise, your annual subscription will continue renewing automatically and you’ll be notified in advance of any further price changes.
  • You can review the benefits included with your membership here.
  • Thank you for subscribing to [Creator Name] and supporting their creativity on Patreon!
  • Patreon
  • Hello [Member name],
  • The price of your recurring subscription to [Tier Name] from [Creator Name] was recently changed to [$Y new price]. Just like any independent business, creators may adjust prices to account for increased costs or other changed circumstances.

  • This update goes into effect 1 month from today on [Today + 1 month] for all existing members. This means your annual membership renewal on [Member’s Next Charge Date] will be at the new rate of [$Y new price]/month for the upcoming year unless you cancel before that date here. Otherwise, your annual subscription will continue renewing automatically and you’ll be notified in advance of any further price changes.

  • Thank you for subscribing to [Creator Name] and supporting their creativity on Patreon!
