Their membership will continue renewing automatically, and we’ll notify them in advance of any further price changes.

All notifications related to price changes are sent directly from Patreon. However, we encourage you to personally reach out to your members to explain the changes and any new value added to the membership as part of the change. Creators who create a post or send a message to existing members detailing any additional exciting things included with tier price changes are more likely to retain members.

Updating your tiers ensures that your prices reflect your current membership offerings. For additional tips, explore Patreon for Creators for more guides and best practices.

How to edit your membership tiers

This guide explains how to manage and update your membership tiers, including editing tier details, pricing strategies, and member transitions.

Check in with yourself on a regular basis

Are you burnt out? Try to think about what is valuable to your members and what will be sustainable for you. Patreon for Creators is full of great articles to support you through your membership journey, including, How to structure your membership and price your benefits.

Editing your tier

  • Select Creator studio from the left navigation to open your Dashboard
  • From your page, click on your Membership tab
  • Scroll down and click on the Edit tier link on the tier you’d like to edit

At the top of the tier editor, you can change the tier name, description, and benefits. If you have Subscription billing, adjusting your tier prices can be done quickly and easily for increases up to $20 more than the original amount.

Change your tier image by selecting the ‘Remove image’ button (marked by an X icon) near the current image.

Click on the Advanced section to change the following:
  • Increase, or decrease the member limit for a tier
  • Add, or remove a shipping requirement
  • Change, or remove Discord roles

Whether you’re making a minor change to your description or completely relaunching a tier, be sure to scroll down and click the Save tier button to save your changes.

Looking to rethink your tiers or pricing? Check out “10 quick tips for setting up or optimizing your membership tiers” on Patreon for Creators. Currently, Patreon for Creators is only available in English.

Pricing tiers

If you have Subscription billing, adjusting your tier prices can be done quickly and easily for increases up to $20 more than the original price. Learn more about Changing the price of your tiers and how it impacts your existing members.

You won’t be able to change the price of a tier that has a Free trial enabled just yet. This will be coming soon.

For adjustments over $20, or if you’re not using Subscription billing, consider creating a new tier at the desired price point and encourage your members to switch. Communication is key when updating your pricing. We recommend following our Best Practices for Increasing Your Tier Prices to ensure a smooth transition.

New tiers you create will automatically get access to any posts you’ve published for Paid members only.

Giving your new tier access to posts

You can give your new tier access to past posts by visiting your Library via Creator studio.

  • Select Creator studio from the left navigation, then click your Library — you’ll land on your Posts page where you can:
    • Search for posts by name
    • Sort by Title and/or Publish date
    • Filter by post type, audience, or tags — click the button to Apply your filter selections
  • Checkmark the posts you want to edit
    • To select all posts, click the checkbox at the top. Click it again to unselect all
  • Click the Edit button
  • Click on Edit access
  • From the dropdown menu, choose Selected tiers
  • Checkmark the new tier that you want to give access to your selected posts
  • Click the Next button
  • Click the Confirm update button to save your edits

FAQ

  • Note: We advise against deleting tiers if you still have existing members on those tiers.
  • When a tier is deleted, existing members from that tier will still be billed their membership amount. While they’ll retain access to content available to Paid members only, they won’t have access to content for Selected tiers. These members aren’t categorized as Custom pledge members either. As a result, they won’t appear if you search for them using the No tier filter in the Relationship manager. However, you can locate them by using the All tiers filter instead
  • Another important point to consider is that when a new tier is created, members from the deleted tier won’t automatically transition to the new one as it changes their billing and benefit selections. Members need to change this on their end to be included in anything new. They can edit their payment by following these steps: Editing your membership.
  • Yes, repricing tiers for existing members who joined on web, mobile web, or Android is available for creators on our Subscription Billing model. Existing members who subscribed via iOS in-app purchases will remain at their original tier price. This limitation is due to Apple’s requirements, which don’t support Patreon’s pricing adjustment tools.
  • If you’re considering updating the price for your existing tiers, you can learn more about Changing the price of your tier.
  • You can check your billing model from your account settings.
  • Not at the moment. Only members can edit their membership tier, so you won’t be able to move members from “no benefit” to a tier on your end.
  • Feel free to pass along this article from our Help Center to guide members through selecting a new tier: How do I edit my membership?
  • You can use the filters in your Relationship manager to access a list of who’s not currently in a tier.
  • To do this select the following from your Relationship manager > click the Filters button > select No tier > click the Apply filters button
  • Check if you have an extra character in the field where only numbers are allowed (like $.) Try removing any extra characters and saving again.

Limit member spots in your tier

When creating or editing your tier, you can limit the number of available member spots to keep a tier exclusive or give you more control over the number of benefits you’ll need to fulfill.

To learn more about creating and editing tiers, visit our guide on How to set up paid tiers and benefits.

To set a member tier limit, follow these steps:

  • While on your creator view, click on Dashboard from the left sidebar navigation
  • Click on the Membership tab on your page
  • Click the Edit button for an existing tier or click on the Add tier button to start with a fresh tier
  • Scroll down and click on Advanced tier settings
  • In the Tier Settings section, click on the Limit the number of members who can join this tier option
  • Enter the number of members you’ll permit in the tier
  • Click the Save button to confirm your changes

Only limit tiers if the benefits are difficult to deliver to a large number of members — once a tier is full, new members won’t be able to join, which could mean missing out on potential members.

What if a member’s payment fails?

We regularly retry failed membership payments and notify members when a payment hasn’t gone through, allowing them to resolve the issue. Members whose payment retries repeatedly fail for ~30 days will be converted to free members. This way, you’ll be able to stay connected with them while also opening up space in limited-spot tiers. We will continue to show the member as Active in Insights for the time we are retrying the payment. If they become a free member, they’ll also show up as a paid cancelled member.

Managing your merch items

Merch for Memberships is only available to creators who are already using it. If you don’t see the Merch tab in your page settings, this feature isn’t available for your page.

Once you’ve created your merch items, you’ll be able to access, edit, and end those items directly from the Merch tab.

This article will explain what you will find on the merch tab and what actions you can take with your items.

Accessing your merch items

To access a list of items you offer, log in and head to the Merch tab link of your page editor. You’ll find a historical list of your merch items.

Here’s more information on what these columns and statuses mean:
  • Item: the type of merch item
  • Description: the description you set when you created your merch. You can edit this description by clicking the pencil icon.
    • Active: this item is live and visible to patrons and fans on your Patreon page. Patrons may be actively earning this item.
    • Deleted: this item has been deleted. It is not visible on your page, and no patrons can receive the item.
    • Retired: this item has been retired.
  • Published: the date you first published the merch item, and the date it was deleted or retired
  • Tiers: the tier(s) your merch item is assigned to. You can edit these by clicking the pencil icon.

Editing an item

You can edit an item’s description, the tiers it’s assigned to, and the artwork by clicking the Edit item link or the pencil icon to the right of an item.

Once you make your changes to your merch item, you must review the details in order to save the item and update it.

Can I order a sample of my new item?

Yes! Email merch@patreon.com to order a sample of your revised item.

When will my patrons receive my merch?

If you’ve added this item to any new tiers, patrons of those tiers will begin their earnings progress when you click the Publish merch button.

Patrons of tiers that already included this item will continue their previous earnings progress without any changes.

Editing the item design or description does not affect when patrons earn merch. Any new orders sent to patrons after you edit your design will use the new design. Learn more about how patrons earn merch in this guide.

Ending an item

You can end your merch item by clicking on the delete item button (which is also a trash bin icon) to the right of a merch item on your Merch tab. You have the option of either deleting or retiring your merch item. To learn more check out our guide on Ending a merch item.

Managing a loyalty program

You can access the list of items included in your loyalty program, edit your loyalty program, and end your loyalty program from your Merch tab.

Editing a loyalty program’s tiers

You can edit the tiers a loyalty program is assigned to by pressing on the Edit item link (which is also a pencil icon). If you change the tiers you assign your program to, the earning timelines for all four items in the program will be affected. For a detailed guide on editing your merch items, please visit our help center article on editing a merch item.

Editing a loyalty program’s artwork

You can edit or add artwork for any of the items in a program at any time by pressing the Edit item link/pencil icon. Changing artwork does not change patrons’ earnings progress.

What does Artwork required mean?

To make things easy for you, we only require you to upload artwork for the first item in your program when you publish a new loyalty program. If at least one item is still missing artwork, you will find the Artwork required status in your Merch tab. The Artwork required and Artwork overdue statuses do not contain precise information on when your patrons will earn merch — they are just reminders we show you to help keep things on track. You can add the required artwork by editing your loyalty program.

What does Artwork overdue mean?

We recommend you upload artwork for each item in time for any patrons who might have been pledging when you published the item to earn it without any delays.

We calculate the date when artwork is “due” for each item by determining the earliest time that the item was added to any of your tiers, then adding the length of time that it would take for a patron already pledging to that tier to earn the item.

For example, if you publish a loyalty program on May 15th, then the artwork for your 6 month item will be “due” on November 1st, which is when existing patrons in that tier would earn the item.

If you add a loyalty program to different tiers at different times, we will always calculate the artwork due date based on the date it was added to the first tier.

What happens when my artwork is overdue?

If a patron has earned an item but that item has no artwork available we will not be able to ship the item, which is why it’s important to upload your artwork before this date.

If no patrons are pledging to a tier when the loyalty program is added, then the calculated artwork due date may be too early. To learn the current status of which patrons have earned your merch, and if any may be blocked by missing artwork, please visit your Benefits page.

Ending a loyalty program

Ending a loyalty program works the same as ending an item — all items in the program will be affected. For detailed steps on how to do this, please visit our Ending an item help article.

Navigating Global Tariff Changes as a Creator on Patreon

A quick guide to what’s changing, who it affects, and how to prepare.

Starting August 29, 2025, the United States is ending its de minimis exemption — a policy that previously allowed international shipments valued under $800 to enter the U.S. duty-free and without full customs processing. This change means all physical goods shipped to fans in the U.S. from outside the country will now be subject to customs duties and import processing.

Below is a guide to help you understand what’s happening and how to prepare.

Who this change may affect

You may be impacted if you:

  • Ship physical rewards from outside the U.S. to fans in the U.S.
  • Use international fulfillment services (including most shipping companies)
  • Import materials like packaging, merchandise, printed goods, or stickers

Digital rewards (downloads, videos, access to media) are not affected by these changes.

How to adapt

There’s no one-size-fits-all approach, but here are a few practical ways creators are adjusting:

  • Use U.S.-based fulfillment providers: Services like Printful, ShipBob, Easyship, and Printify can store or ship products from within the U.S., helping you avoid cross-border duties and delays.
  • Ask your shipping provider about DDP: If you still plan to ship internationally, talk to your carrier about Delivered Duty Paid (DDP) shipping. This allows you to pay customs duties in advance, which helps prevent surprise delivery fees or delays for fans.
  • Consider switching to digital rewards: Digital offerings like PDFs, wallpapers, tutorials, or zines avoid international shipping entirely and aren’t subject to customs duties. Visit our Help Center to learn about updates to selling digital products and selling one-time purchases on Patreon.

Adjusting your pricing if needed

If your shipping, materials, or fulfillment costs are going up, it may be time to review your pricing. Patreon provides tools to adjust your tier pricing smoothly and transparently. You can:

  • Apply new prices to future fans only
  • Decide whether to update pricing for current fans
  • Notify fans 31 days in advance of any changes

Being transparent about why prices are changing — and reminding fans of the value they receive — can reduce confusion or cancellations.

Wondering how much your costs might go up? Some vendors may notify you about price changes, but not all will. If you’d like to ballpark what kind of increase you might face, public resources like TariffCheck.org and PassportGlobal’s U.S. Tariff Summary offer approximate tariff rates by country. These tools can help you estimate the additional cost on imported goods, though rates may continue to change over time.

Communicating with your fans

If you make changes to how you ship or price your rewards, keeping fans informed can go a long way in maintaining trust. You can update your tier descriptions, share a post, or include a note in your monthly update.

Example message: “U.S. customs rules are changing starting August 29. If you’re based in the U.S. and receive physical rewards from me, there may be delivery delays or new import fees. I’ll keep you updated and do my best to minimize any issues.”

Staying informed

We’re closely monitoring how this change impacts creators on Patreon — especially those who rely on physical rewards or international fulfillment. While we don’t manage shipping directly, we’re actively listening to creator feedback and exploring ways to make it easier to navigate changes like this.

FAQ

  • It allowed shipments under $800 USD to enter the U.S. without duties or customs paperwork. That rule ends for all countries on August 29, 2025.
  • Tariffs are taxes on goods imported into a country. They vary by product and country of origin and are usually a percentage of the item’s value.
  • Any creator who sends physical goods to fans in the U.S. from outside the country — whether directly or through an international fulfillment partner.
  • No. These changes only apply to physical goods. Digital files and access-based media are unaffected.
  • It depends on your carrier:
    • Postal carriers (e.g., USPS, Canada Post): Fans may be asked to pay fees at delivery (Delivered Duty Unpaid).
    • Express carriers (e.g., UPS, FedEx, DHL): You may be able to pay duties up front using Delivered Duty Paid (DDP) shipping.
  • Their package may be delayed, returned, or discarded. You might also be billed for the return. DDP shipping helps avoid this risk.
  • Yes, but only with clear communication. If you want to change which countries you ship to, you’ll need to update your reward tier description accordingly and follow through on any promised rewards. Creators cannot silently stop fulfilling rewards to certain regions.
  • If you’d like to remove shipping to a specific region (like the U.S.) or restructure your tiers, consider updating the tier description and using our tier pricing tools to make those changes transparent to fans. You might choose to:
    • Adjust pricing for tiers with physical rewards
    • Create a new tier with updated shipping availability
    • Clarify that your current tiers are only available to regions you still support
  • If you have questions about your rewards, fulfillment setup, or tier pricing, contact our Creator Support team. We’re here to help.

Set up the Discourse integration with my Patreon page

Discourse is a powerful tool that makes it easy to run and manage a member-only community forum. Patreon has an integration with Discourse that automatically adds/removes members based on their membership access.

How do I set up my Discourse account?

Go to Discourse.org and click on the blue Try it FREE link. Then, select a plan for your 14-day trial and set up your account by entering the following information

  • Email address
  • Subdomain or domain – If you don’t self-host your own domain, select the box next to “I need a temporary domain” and enter the subdomain you’d like to use; If you host your own domain, you can use that as well, and it will be free
  • Community name (you can change this later)

You’ll receive an email from Discourse asking you to confirm your email address. Follow the instructions in the email to confirm your account.

After you confirm your email address, you’ll be taken to Discourse, where you’ll follow the steps below to set up your community. Follow the on-screen steps and select Next after you complete each step.

Items to complete:
  • Choose a language
  • Add a community name: You can always edit this in the future
  • Add a description for your community: This is like your “elevator pitch” and will be the first thing that new arrivals to your community will read
  • Set your access: You can choose whether your community is public or private. If you choose public, everyone can access your forum even if they are not logged in. If you choose Private, only logged-in users can find your forum. You can create private categories for your members. You can also enable the option to invite people to your community. Please note that if you do this, you will have to send the invites to each person on your end
  • Contact information: This includes the email address for the person in charge of this community, a general contact web page (for example, your website or Patreon page), and the user from which automated messages are sent
  • Organization information: If you have a company, please enter your company name, governing law, and city for disputes; If you don’t have a company, you can skip this step
  • Theme: Select the color theme, logos, icons, homepage format, and emoji style you prefer for your community.
  • Invite staff: If you have other individuals on your team who need to moderate the community, you can invite them during this time as well.

When you’re done, you’ll be taken to a page that says “Your Discourse is Ready!” Select Done, then you’ll be taken to your Community page.

How to set up the Discourse integration with Patreon

Now that you’ve set up your community, you will need to connect it to Patreon.

  • To start, select the burger menu in the top right corner, then select Admin > Plugins
  • Scroll down, then select the settings icon next to “Discourse-Patreon” – Keep this tab open, since you will return to it in a few steps
  • In a separate browser window, enter the following URL: patreon.com
  • Click the Create Client button and fill out the required fields
  • Set App Name to Patreon Discourse Plugin – You’ll also enter your Redirect URI. To get your Redirect URI, go back to the browser window with Discourse open and copy your Discourse URL with subdomain (https://yoursubdomain.trydiscourse.com)
  • Paste this URL into the Redirect URIs field, then add/auth/patreon/callback so that the entire redirect URI displays like this: yoursubdomain.trydiscourse.com
  • Then click the Create Client button to find your App name and client ID, then select the down-arrow icon to open up a menu that displays all of your client info
  • Now copy and paste your client info back into your Discourse plugin settings – You’ll be switching back and forth between the browser windows with Discourse and Patreon open, so you may want to keep them side by side
  • Copy and paste the following from the Patreon client page into the corresponding Discourse fields:
    • Patreon Client ID
    • Patreon Client Secret
    • Patreon Creator Access Token
    • Patreon Creator Refresh Token
  • Select the green arrow next to each field to save
  • Now, navigate to this URL: yoursubdomain.trydiscourse.com, then select “Update Patreon Data and Sync Groups.” A pop-up will appear and confirm that new data has been downloaded
  • Refresh the page and select OK

How do my members join Discourse?

To check how a member would join your Discourse forum, follow the steps below:

  • Open an incognito tab, paste your Discourse community URL, and select the With Patreon button to log in using your Patreon credentials.
  • Enter your login information and select Allow when you are taken to the OAuth window. If your member doesn’t have a Discourse account, they will be asked to create one at this point.
  • Your member will then be taken to your Discourse community homepage.

Setting up a Special Offer

Special Offers is being retired. You won’t be able to create new Special Offers moving forward.

If you have one running now, it’ll run through its end date exactly as planned, members who joined through it keep everything they signed up for, and you’ll keep access to benefits tracking for any past offers. Nothing gets lost in the switch.

Want to run something similar going forward? Let a promotion do the work. A discount, free trial, or gift gets you that same “now’s the moment” energy without adding extra benefits to fulfill. They all live in your Promotions tab.

Tier highlighting

You can choose from a couple of options to highlight your tiers on your creator page. The “Earnings potential” option has been selected to start. You can switch to highlighting options or turn this off by going to your Membership tab settings. Read on to see our list of FAQ.

Tier highlighting is currently only available for creators who have more than 1 tier.

How to turn on Tier highlighting

  • Select Creator studio from the left navigation to open your Dashboard
  • From your page, go to your Membership tab
  • Select Settings next to Paid Membership Tiers
  • Toggle on Enable tier highlighting
How will tier highlighting look on my page?

A default option has been selected to start and will appear on your tier using your chosen brand colors. Tier highlighting is automatically shown on your public-facing tier page (pictured below):

Where can I adjust or turn off tier highlighting?

There are two available options for tier highlighting:

  • Earnings potential: is the tier that is predicted to increase your earnings. This will appear on your page with the label “You may like,” or it can appear as “Most popular” if your most popular tier gives you the best chance at earnings potential
  • Most popular: where your most popular tier (most members) is highlighted. This will appear on your page with the label “Most popular”
  • Your choice: is the tier that you want to personally recommend to users. This will appear as Recommended by creator. Simply select the tier in your settings after selecting Your choice
FAQ
  • Tier highlighting allows you to draw attention to a specific tier, encouraging more visitors to become members by helping them decide which tier to join.
  • Yes, you can choose your tier to highlight!
  • The highlighting label will use your default creator page colors. You cannot change the copy on the label.
  • A tier has been selected by observing your “Most popular” tier performance against another tier and predicting which one would help increase your earnings.
  • For some creators, the most popular tier is the predicted tier that would best increase your earnings.
  • Your most popular tier may be a tier that is below the fold, meaning it is positioned on the lower half of the page and is only visible when members click to expand your tier offerings. Visitors can expand your tiers to review the highlighted most popular tier.
  • Tier highlighting is currently only available for creators with more than 1 tier. We will be building out more functionalities for tier highlighting in the future.

Track delivery with Benefits features

This article covers the Benefit Tracker alongside the Benefit Eligibility Status tool. As we continue to enhance our Benefits features, if you find the Benefit Eligibility Status tool in the Benefits tab, refer to our article on tracking your members’ benefit eligibility status for updated guidance.

If you haven’t made any tiers or added any benefits to your tiers, we recommend that you first read through our article on How to set up paid tiers and benefits. Once you’ve added benefits to your tiers, you can start to track them.

Patreon’s benefit tools help you:

  • Track benefit eligibility: See how many members, both new and existing, have successfully paid and should receive benefits this month
  • Monitor upcoming renewals: See how many members haven’t been charged yet but have a renewal scheduled before the end of the month
  • Track delivery: Mark benefits complete as you deliver them to each member
  • Take action: Export a list or message specific groups of members

These tools support your workflow whether you deliver benefits as members are charged or wait until billing is complete for the month.

Please note that gifted members don’t currently appear in the Benefits Tracker. Only members with an active payment attached to their account appear in your benefits tracking.

Check who’s eligible for benefits

The Benefit Eligibility Status shows which members are eligible to receive benefits for the month. By default, it shows monthly and annual members who’ve already paid for the current month.

View eligible members
  • On Desktop, select Creator studio in the left-side navigation menu
  • Click Audience from the sub-menu to open your Relationship manager
  • Click the Benefit Eligibility Status button
  • To narrow your results, filter by membership tier (optional)
  • Click View to see members who are eligible for benefits this month

You can also switch the view to the previous month and download a CSV list of eligible members. This is especially helpful if you deliver benefits after all payments are processed or at the end of the month.

For example, if you’re a creator who delivers benefits once a month, this tool can help you stay organized. If you want to deliver your benefit on the first of May, you can use the benefit delivery tool to pull a list of everyone who paid in April.

Member groups

The tool also groups members by their payment and renewal status, so you can better understand where they are in the billing cycle and plan your benefit delivery accordingly:

  • New members: Joined this month or rejoined after canceling
  • Continuing members: Ongoing monthly or annual members
  • Eligible soon: Members with renewals scheduled before the end of the month who haven’t been charged yet

Use Eligible soon to track upcoming renewals and plan ahead for how many members you may need to deliver benefits to, or how much income you should expect to receive throughout the month.

Download a list or message members

After clicking View on the current month or any of the additional breakdowns, you’ll see a list of filtered members based on your selected preferences. You can download a CSV or Message members directly. Just select one or more members from the list, then choose the action you want. These options give you the flexibility to communicate with your members or fulfill benefits in a way that best suits your workflow.

Add tracking to a benefit

  • On Desktop, click Creator studio from the left sidebar navigation
  • Select Audience
  • Go to the Benefits tab – benefits that you’ve added to your tiers will be listed here
  • If you’re not tracking your benefits yet, you’ll see a section of Benefits not tracked, then click on the Add tracking button right next to the benefit
  • You’ll be asked how often members receive this benefit – choose from one-time or monthly, and click on the Add tracking button to confirm it
Check delivery status

Your benefits table includes a benefit title column and a status column:

  • If you’ve completed delivering benefits to all eligible members, the status will show you the number of members completed and have a green checkmark
  • If there are some members who are still owed a benefit, the status will show the number of members with a “due” status
Member benefit list

Click on a benefit to get a list of members who are due this benefit. The highest tier you offer this benefit and the delivery frequency (i.e., on a monthly or one-time basis) will be listed under the benefit name.

Here, you’ll find your members’ names, shipping addresses (if you’ve asked for this), pledge amount, and the benefit due date. You can mark individual members as complete using the Mark Complete feature. If you do big batch benefit deliveries, mark the entire member list complete by clicking the Mark # Complete button.

Click into the Completed section of a benefit for a list of members to whom you’ve delivered this benefit.

Want more information on a particular member? Click on a member’s name to go directly to your Relationship manager.

From your Relationship manager, you can message your member, review payment history, check their Discord handle, and any notes you may keep about them (i.e., prefers my illustration postcards over my photo postcards).

For more details, visit our guide on Relationship manager.

Annual members

If you have members paying you annually, they’ll appear on benefits lists as soon as their membership year starts. They will show up for all monthly recurring benefits associated with the tier they join; however, their year of membership will be paid in full on the date they joined.

You can learn about what to expect if you are in our annual membership beta here: Annual memberships creator overview.

Subscription billing

With subscription billing, there are a couple of ways that you can choose to deliver benefits to members:

  • You can deliver benefits to all members who are active at the time you’re processing benefits
  • You can also deliver benefits at the start of each month to any member who has paid throughout the previous month

For example, if you typically mail a sticker on the 5th of each month to members who have paid by the 1st, you can mail the sticker on September 5 to all members who had a successful payment in August. On October 5, mail the September sticker to all members who made a successful payment in September.

All creators are now using subscription billing. If your account was still on a legacy billing model on November 1, 2026, we switched it automatically and emailed you when the switch was complete.

Key details depending on your previous billing model:

  • Per-creation: If you haven’t resumed billing yet, it stays paused until you review your new tier prices. Learn how to resume billing
  • First-of-the-month: Your existing members are still billed on the 1st of each month. New members are billed on the date they join

Track your members’ benefit eligibility status

Looking for the Benefit Tracker? Benefit Tracker is being retired and replaced by the new Benefit Eligibility Status tool. Check the guide on Track delivery with Benefits features for the former experience.

The Benefit Eligibility Status tool helps you identify members who have successfully paid and may be owed a benefit. You can review eligibility history month by month, making it easier to deliver recurring benefits.

It shows members eligible for benefits that month (including annual-paying members, gifted members, and monthly members who paid), but it doesn’t track delivery, so you can’t mark members as complete. To keep a record of what you’ve delivered, download and save the CSV for each month you fulfill.

The tool is available to creators on subscription billing, and you can find it on a dedicated page in the Benefits tab. If you haven’t created paid tiers or added benefits yet, see How to set up paid tiers and benefits.

Access your benefit eligibility list

  • On Desktop, click Creator studio in the left-side navigation menu
  • Select Audience
  • Go to the Benefits tab
  • Choose the tier and the month you want to review

September 2026 is the first month with complete eligibility data. August 2026 may contain partial data. Earlier history is still being added, so the months available may vary by creator. Check the Month dropdown to see which months are available for your account.

Filter by tier

Open the Tier dropdown to view members from a specific tier. This helps you focus on members associated with the benefit you’re preparing to deliver.

Select a different tier when you’re ready to review another group of members.

Choose an eligibility period

Open the Month dropdown and select the month that matches your benefit-delivery schedule.

For example:

  • If you deliver benefits monthly, select the month you’re fulfilling.
  • If you deliver benefits quarterly, review each relevant month before preparing your delivery.
    • A member who paid in each of those months appears in each month’s list, so remove duplicates before sending a one-time benefit.
  • If you deliver benefits after the end of each month, select the previous month to review members who successfully paid during that period.

The current period may continue to change as additional member payments are processed. The count at the top of the page shows how many members are eligible so far and how many are expected based on upcoming renewals.

Export your list

Download your eligibility list as a CSV file to use for mailing labels, fulfillment services, or your own records.

  • Choose the tier and month you want to export.
  • Select Download CSV. You’ll find it at the top of the member list, next to the Message button.
  • You’ll receive an email with the file. You can open it in any spreadsheet app.

Your filters apply to the export, so the file only includes the members shown in your list. Along with the member details shown in the list, the file includes Eligibility Tier and Eligibility Month columns. These show the tier each member held in the selected month, which may be different from their current tier.

To export another tier or month, change your filters and download again.

Messaging members

You can send a message to the members in your eligibility list without leaving the Benefits tab. For example, you can let members know a benefit is on its way, share a link or code for a digital benefit, or remind them to update their shipping address.

  • Choose the tier and month for the members you want to reach.
  • Select Message. You’ll find it at the top of the member list, next to the Download CSV button.
  • Write your message and send it.

Your message is sent to members in the filtered list who can receive messages from you. You can message current or former paid members. The recipient count may be lower than the eligibility count. Free-only members aren’t eligible for direct messaging. Each member receives it as a direct message in their Patreon inbox. Before sending, check your tier and month filters to make sure you’re reaching the right members.

Understanding who appears in the list

The list includes:

  • Monthly members who successfully paid during the selected month
  • Annual members during their paid annual term
  • Gifted members during their gift period

The list doesn’t include free members, members on a free trial, or people who made a one-time purchase without joining a paid tier. These don’t include tier benefits.

If a member was charged for the current month and then changed tiers during the month, they appear once for each tier they held. If they haven’t been charged for the current month and upgraded, they will appear only once for the upgraded tier. They’re still counted only once in the total at the top of the page.

Annual members

Annual members pay for their membership term upfront. They appear in the list for each month of their active annual term, even though they aren’t charged every month.

For more information about annual memberships, see Annual memberships creator overview.

Deliver benefits with subscription billing

With subscription billing, members renew on different dates throughout the month. You don’t necessarily need to deliver benefits separately on every member’s billing date.

Instead, choose a delivery schedule that works for you and use the eligibility tool to identify members who successfully paid during the relevant period.

For example, you can:

  • Deliver benefits weekly.
  • Deliver benefits twice a month.
  • Deliver benefits after the end of each month.
  • Review several months when delivering quarterly or less frequently.

Example: You have a monthly delivery, and you normally mail a sticker on the fifth of each month. On November 5, you can select October and export the list of members who successfully paid during October. On December 5, select November and repeat the process. This lets you continue delivering in monthly batches even though members may renew on different dates.

Troubleshoot missing members

If a member you expected to see isn’t listed:

  • Confirm that you selected the correct month
  • Check whether the member is in a tier associated with the benefit
  • Review the member’s payment status in Relationship manager. If a payment is still pending or declined, the member won’t appear until it’s successfully processed
  • Check whether the member has a free membership or is on a free trial. These members aren’t included
  • Eligibility history starts in August 2026. Lists for August 2026 may be incomplete, and earlier months aren’t available
  • If the member was in a tier you’ve since deleted, the list may show “No tier” for them. The CSV export shows the correct tier name

For more information about an individual member, select their name to open their record in Relationship manager.

September 2026 is the first month with complete eligibility data, and August 2026 may be incomplete. Earlier history is still being added and may not yet be available for your account. Use the Month dropdown to check which months you can review.

What tiers should I put my merch on?

Merch for Memberships is only available to creators who are already using it. If you don’t see the Merch tab in your page settings, this feature isn’t available for your page.

When assigning or adding merch to your membership tiers, you may have some questions about where to place the items or how to ensure you won’t lose any money in this process. Here are some of your most frequently asked questions.

What tiers should I put my merch on?

The most important consideration when adding merch to your tiers is the cost of each item. To help you with this decision, we offer recommended tier prices for each item as well as minimum tier prices. Based on the tier you choose, you’ll see our recommended tier price, the minimum tier price, and the estimated earnings per member.

For most creators, we recommend placing a loyalty program or only one merch item on each tier, to help all of your items stand out.

Why am I restricted from assigning merch to certain tiers?

We want to make Merch easy and safe to use for every creator on Patreon. As a way to protect your business, we do not allow merch to be added to a tier if the combined cost of all merch on that tier exceeds the total pledge value from a member after 3 months on that tier.

When adding a loyalty program to a tier, the most expensive item in the set is used to determine the price of the loyalty program. At this time loyalty programs cannot be added to a tier that contains any other merch items.

I want to publish a Merch item but don’t have a tier at the right price. What can I do?

You may want to consider creating a new tier for that merch item. For example, if you want to offer a hoodie but don’t already have a tier that costs enough, you can create a new $35 tier (recommended) or $11 tier (minimum). Many creators will create a higher-priced tier ($75+) and limit the number of members that can pledge to it. This way you can create exclusivity in your highest tier and offer valuable and exclusive benefits.

Can I bundle multiple merch items on a single tier?

Yes! As long as the combined cost of the items is less than the total pledge value of a member after 3 months on that tier, you can add as many items as you like. At this time multiple items are sent individually, and cannot be combined into a single shipment. Loyalty programs cannot be added to a tier that contains any other merch items.

How much will it cost me to add merch to a tier?

You can expect to pay for each item that is sent to a member on each tier, including existing members. The listed price for each item includes tax and shipping to anywhere in the world (learn which countries you can send merch to in this article). The total cost to use Merch will vary depending on how many members you have, the cost of the items you publish, and how many of your members have entered valid shipping addresses.

You can learn more about how and when you’ll pay for your merch items in this guide on paying for merch.

Please note: Tiers that utilize structured tier benefits may be exempt from the iOS in-app fee if they include physical goods, such as merch, commissions (delivered by mail) or other tangible goods. The increased offset price will not be included in these tiers when viewed in the iOS app, keeping the same price as on the Web and Android.

Visit our Advanced Sales Tax Settings article to learn more.

When will my members earn merch?

Merch for Memberships is only available to creators who are already using it. If you don’t see the Merch tab in your page settings, this feature isn’t available for your page.

So you’ve just set up merch benefits through Patreon for the first time — this article will explain how and when members earn their merch benefits.

How members earn merch

Members earn merch when they meet two requirements:

  • Joined a tier that contains a merch item
  • Made a required number of consecutive payments in that tier. The number of payments depends on the type of merch program you offer the item in (3 months or loyalty program)

Both new and existing members earn progress toward a merch item by making successful monthly payments after the item is added to their tier. Each successful payment counts as one month of progress.

To continue earning toward the item, the member must remain actively subscribed to a tier that includes the merch item and make uninterrupted payments. If a payment fails, the member cancels their membership, or switches to a tier that doesn’t include the item, any progress toward that merch item is lost. If the member later rejoins a qualifying tier, their progress restarts from the beginning.

Only memberships with payments made directly from the member’s account are eligible to earn merchandise rewards. Progress does not begin until the member’s account successfully makes a payment. Please note that merchandise rewards cannot be earned through gifted memberships.

What may interrupt earning progress

Certain events can interrupt progress toward earning merch and reset it. These events include:

  • Refunds
  • Billing pauses
  • Failed or declined payments
  • Temporary removal of the merchandise item from the tier
  • Any other disruption to a member’s paid access to the qualifying tier

Once billing resumes without any interruptions on a tier that offers the item, the member will start accumulating progress again from the beginning.

Real-life scenarios

Let’s look at some examples to understand when members typically earn merch. For this example, we’ll use a merch program that delivers an item once every 3 months.

  • If a creator who charges members up front adds a merch item to a tier on May 15th, existing members will have their next payment made after May 15th count toward their merch item. For example, a member whose billing anniversary was the 20th would make their first eligible payment on May 20th. On June 20th, that member would process their second payment towards earning that merch item. On July 20th, the member would earn the merch item. If a new member joins on July 15th, they will be charged immediately upon signup and earn their first payment towards their merch item. The new member would earn their second payment towards their merch item on August 15th and then earn the merch item on September 15th.
  • If a creator who charges members upfront adds a merch item to a tier on May 15th, existing members will have their next payment (June 1st) count toward their merch item. On July 1st, those members would process their second payment towards earning that merch item. On August 1st, members would earn the merch item. If a new member joins on July 15th, they would be charged immediately upon signup and earn their first payment towards their merch item. The new member would earn their second payment towards their merch item on August 1st and then earn the merch item on September 1st.
  • Suppose a creator who does not charge members upfront adds a merch item to a tier on May 15th. In that case, existing members with a valid membership in that tier will earn their first payment towards that merch item on June 1st, eventually earning the item on August 1st. A new member who joins on July 15th would earn their merch item on October 1st.

As a reminder, you can always find what benefits your members have earned, including Merch for Membership benefits, on your Benefits page.

FAQ

  • Typically, existing members will earn their merch item on their third successful charge after the merch is added. Previous payments do not count toward a member earning merch.
  • No, editing the design of a merch item won’t impact a member’s progress toward earning it.
  • If you’ve removed an item or loyalty program from any tiers, members will stop all earnings progress for those tiers.
  • If you’ve added an item or loyalty program to any new tiers, members of those new tiers will begin earning the items when you click the Publish merch button. You can find when you added each item or loyalty program to each tier on your merch tab.

Creators: Using Patreon

Add an image to your About section

To add a photo to your About section, you’ll need to upload the image you want to use to an image-hosting website like Imgur or PostImage.

Here’s how to add an image to your Patreon About section:

  • Open the photo you want to use on an image-hosting website of your choice and copy the image URL. Make sure you copy the direct link to the image and not the embed code
  • Go to your Dashboard
  • Click on the three dots (…) button next to Page details
  • You’ll land on the Basics section
  • Scroll down to About your page
  • In the Bio, click the Insert image link icon from the About section. You can click the </> icon or HTML link if you prefer to add the link directly to the HTML of your About section. You’ll receive a preview of your image in the About section editor
  • Be sure to scroll up to select the Save changes button

Connect a custom domain to your Patreon

Custom domains are only available on the new creator page. If you haven’t switched yet, you’ll need to update your creator page before you can access this feature. Learn more about your updated creator page.

Index: Custom Domain Setup Guides by Domain Provider

We have step-by-step guides for the most popular domain providers:

  • Porkbun
  • GoDaddy
  • Hover
  • Network solutions (Domain.com)
  • Squarespace
  • Cloudflare
  • Namecheap

If your provider isn’t listed, don’t worry — the steps are very similar. Check your provider’s Help Center for how to:

  • Add a TXT record
  • Add a CNAME record
  • Add an ALIAS/ANAME or A record (for root domains)

How custom domains work

A custom domain lets you replace your Patreon URL (patreon.com/yourname) with a branded link like yourname.com or members.yourname.com. This makes your page easier to share, helps fans recognize and trust your brand, and gives your Patreon a more professional, cohesive presence — while Patreon still powers everything behind the scenes.

Strategically, there are two options you might want to explore for your domain:

  • Custom branding: Use your main website (yourname.com) if you want your membership to be the center of your online presence.
  • Matching your existing brand ecosystem: Use a subdomain like membership.yourname.com to tie your Patreon into your existing site and brand identity.

Once your domain is connected and verified, we’ll automatically secure it with HTTPS so fans can safely visit your page.

Things to know

  • You’ll set this up by editing DNS records at your domain provider (like GoDaddy, Porkbun, etc.)
  • You can connect either a subdomain (recommended, e.g. members.yourname.com or www.yourname.com) or your root (apex) domain (yourname.com)
  • Changing DNS for your Patreon connection won’t affect email (MX records) or other non-web settings — as long as you only update the records Patreon shows.
  • Only one custom domain can be connected to your Patreon page at a time.

Before you begin

  • Make sure you own a domain and can edit its DNS records through your provider
  • Decide whether you want to connect a subdomain or your root domain
  • Sign in to your creator account on Patreon (desktop recommended)

💡 Not sure what terms like CNAME or A record mean? You’ll find quick definitions in the Glossary at the end of this article

Quick overview of the setup

  • In Patreon: Enter your domain and take note of the DNS records we generate
  • At your domain provider: Add the provided DNS records to your domain’s DNS settings
  • Patreon verifies your setup: Once the records are found, we automatically issue an SSL certificate for your domain
  • After 24h, your page goes live: All fans can now visit your Patreon at your custom domain

How to set up a custom domain (step-by-step guide)

Step 1: Add your domain on Patreon
  • On desktop, select Creator studio from the left navigation — you’ll land on your Dashboard
  • From your page, click More and select Page details
  • In the Basics tab, go to the Use your own domain section and click the Add a domain button
  • A pop-up will appear with a text box for you to enter your desired domain (e.g. members.yourname.com or yourname.com)
  • Click the Next button
  • Patreon will display the DNS records you need to add at your domain provider (CNAME, A, TXT records for routing)
Step 2: Add DNS records at your provider

Now that Patreon has given you the records, log in to your domain provider (like GoDaddy, Porkbun, etc.) and open the DNS editor. Depending on your provider, this might be called DNS settings, Zone editor, or Advanced DNS.

Add the given DNS records in your DNS editor. This will be some combination of A, AAAA, CNAME and TXT records. Use the details provided in Patreon settings.

Important: Each line shown in your Patreon DNS instructions must be added as its own DNS record in your provider’s DNS settings. If we show 3 rows, you must create 3 separate DNS records — one per row. Do not combine multiple rows into a single record.

Copy and paste these records exactly as shown. The values displayed in your Patreon settings are the source of truth and may be unique to your domain.

Step 3: Verify and activate
  • After you’ve added the DNS records at your provider, return to Page details → Basics tab → Your domains in Patreon
  • Click the Refresh button to get the latest verification status. The status of your domain will update once we detect the correct records and have successfully issued a SSL certificate on your behalf. This status update may take up to 24 hours.
  • Once verified, it’ll take 24 hours for your domain to become your primary/canonical URL. DNS changes can take up to 24 hours to update for all visitors to your domain. We suggest that you only begin to share your domain after this 24-hour period.

Redirects & canonical URL

  • Your original patreon.com/creatorname link will keep working. Once your custom domain is active, anyone visiting your Patreon link will be automatically redirected to your new domain
  • Depending on what you chose as your domain, you may see Redirecting domains in addition to your primary domain. The redirecting domains will redirect to your primary URL
  • Visiting custom domains will not deep link to the mobile app and will always open in your mobile browser. From there, you can choose to open the Patreon app.

Troubleshooting

When you add a custom domain, you’ll first see the status as Pending in your Custom domain settings. This is normal while DNS updates spread across the internet. Most connections resolve within minutes, but it can take up to 24–48 hours.

If the status doesn’t change from pending or switches to an error state, here are the most common issues and how to fix them:

If the status doesn’t update, or switches to an error, here are the messages you might see:

  • Patreon can’t detect the DNS records for your domain
    • This usually means you haven’t added the records yet at your provider, or the changes haven’t propagated.
    • Double-check that you added both the TXT (verification) and routing records exactly as shown in Patreon
    • If you just updated your DNS, give it more time — it can take up to 24–48 hours to appear
    • DNS updates can take up to 24–48 hours
    • Confirm the TXT record matches exactly (no extra spaces or quotes)
    • Check that the Host/Name field matches what Patreon shows (e.g. _patreon or _patreon.members)
    • Some providers auto-append your domain. If that’s the case, enter just members (not members.yourname.com)
    • Remove any old A or CNAME records for the same host — you should only have one routing record per host
    • If you’re using a root (apex) domain, confirm you used the ALIAS/ANAME or A records provided by Patreon, not leftover values from a past website host
  • Some issues don’t appear in Patreon — you might notice them instead in your browser, email, or registrar account.
    • SSL is only issued after both verification and routing succeed
    • Check for restrictive CAA records at your provider. If present, add Patreon’s certificate authority as shown in-product, or remove the restrictive entries
    • This happens when only one part of your domain is connected
    • Add a second connection for the missing version (apex or subdomain), or set up a DNS redirect at your provider. Follow instructions in Step 2 above.
    • Choose a canonical URL in Patreon to avoid duplicate content
    • Connecting a domain shouldn’t affect email, but it can happen if there was a mistake made while editing DNS records.
    • Double-check that your MX records are still present
    • If they were overwritten, restore your email provider’s MX records or contact your email provider’s support
    • If verification fails with DNSSEC turned on, check that your DS records are valid after making DNS changes
    • Broken DNSSEC will prevent verification

Limitations

  • You can connect only one custom domain per creator page. (A subdomain and a root/apex domain count as two separate domains.)
  • Multi-domain setups aren’t supported. Contact Support if you think this applies to you.
  • Patreon uses a CDN (content delivery network) to keep your page fast. This means changes to your content may be cached briefly, but updates will still appear close to real time
  • Some country-level domains (ccTLDs, like .de or .uk) have special DNS rules. If you’re using one of these, you may need extra help from your domain provider to complete setup
  • Once you point a subdomain (like members.yourname.com) to Patreon, only Patreon-hosted pages can live there. You can’t serve other content on the same subdomain

Disconnect or change your domain

You can disconnect your custom domain at any time. When you do, your page will automatically fall back to your original patreon.com/creatorname link, so fans will still be able to reach you.

To disconnect your domain
  • Select Creator studio from the left navigation — you’ll land on your Dashboard. From your page, select More and choose Page details
  • In the Basics tab, scroll to the Custom domain section
  • Find your active domain and click more > Disconnect domain
  • Select Disconnect

Your Patreon will no longer be accessible on this domain. You’ll need to revert your DNS records in your domain provider settings.

To connect a new domain

After disconnecting, you can add a different domain by following the steps in Connect a custom domain to your Patreon page.

Glossary

Not sure about some of the terms in this guide? Here are quick definitions in plain language to help you out. You don’t need to memorize them — just use this section as a reference while you set up your domain.

  • A record → Connects your domain to an IP address (used for root/apex domains if CNAME isn’t allowed)
  • CNAME record → Connects one domain name to another (used for subdomains like members.yourname.com)
  • TXT record → A text record often used to prove ownership of your domain (Patreon uses this for verification).
  • Apex/root domain → Your main domain, like yourname.com (without www or another subdomain).
  • Subdomain → A prefix added to your domain, like www.yourname.com or members.yourname.com

Connect your Cloudflare domain to your Patreon page

If you registered your domain with Cloudflare Registrar, or if you manage your DNS records through Cloudflare, you can connect it to your Patreon page. Once connected, your fans will see your Cloudflare domain (like yourname.com or members.yourname.com) instead of patreon.com/yourname.

You’ll need to have already registered your domain and pointed it to Cloudflare’s nameservers. Once connected, Patreon will still host your page, but your fans will visit it using your Cloudflare domain.

Add your domain to Patreon

Changing your Patreon URL to a custom domain will not affect your existing members or messages. We suggest letting your members know before changing your URL so they can update any bookmarks.

Here’s how to change your Patreon URL to a custom domain:

  • In Patreon, go to Dashboard in the left sidebar menu
  • In the Home tab, click the … menu next to the Edit page button and select Page details
  • In the Basics tab, scroll to the Custom domain section and click Add a domain
  • Enter your domain (for example members.yourname.com or yourname.com)
  • Patreon will display the DNS records you need to add at Cloudflare — a TXT record for verification, plus either CNAME, ALIAS/ANAME, or A records for routing

Add DNS records at Cloudflare

  • Log into your Cloudflare account

  • Select the domain you want to use

  • Go to the DNS tab on the left sidebar — this opens the DNS Records section, where you can view and edit your records

  • First, review your existing DNS records:

    • Delete any records that match the type you plan to add (for example, old A, CNAME, or ALIAS records) so you don’t have duplicates or conflicts
    • Records labeled MX or TXT don’t affect your Patreon setup and can stay as they are
    • If this domain has been used before, there may be additional records you’ll need to remove. For guidance on configuring an existing domain, check with your domain provider’s setup instructions

  • In that same DNS Records section, click Add record and enter the records exactly as shown in Patreon

    • TXT record (verification): Name: _patreon.members (or as shown in Patreon), Content: the TXT value shown in Patreon
    • CNAME record (routing): Name: members, Content: the target shown in Patreon (e.g. custom.patreon-domains.com)
    • TXT record (verification): Name: _patreon, Content: the TXT value shown in Patreon
    • Routing record → either:
      • ALIAS/ANAME → point to Patreon’s host
      • A records → point to the IPs shown in Patreon
    • 👉 For your root (apex) domain, use @ in the Name field in Cloudflare

For your redirecting domain, enter www in the Name field in Cloudflare.

Important for Cloudflare users

  • Remove or replace any existing A, CNAME, or ALIAS records for the same host to avoid conflicts
  • Set the Proxy status to DNS only for all Patreon records. Note that Cloudflare automatically sets all new records to Proxied, so you’ll need to click the toggle to switch it before saving. Leaving it set to Proxied will prevent Patreon’s SSL certificate from issuing, and your domain won’t connect correctly
  • Leave TTL set to Auto

Verify on Patreon

  • Return to Page details → Basics tab → Custom domain in Patreon
  • Patreon will detect your records, verify your domain, and activate the connection. The settings will reflect as “Connected” in green once successful

Once verified, we’ll issue an SSL certificate automatically.

Most connections resolve within minutes, but DNS updates can take up to 24–48 hours. If your domain doesn’t connect after this time, check the Troubleshooting section in the main custom domain guide for common fixes.

Disconnect or update your domain

To disconnect from Patreon:
  • Go to Dashboard → Home tab → … menu → Page details
  • In the Basics tab, scroll to the Custom domain section
  • Find your active domain and click (…) more > Disconnect domain
  • Select Disconnect to confirm

Once disconnected, your page will fall back to your original patreon.com/creatorname link.

To update DNS in Cloudflare (optional):

This step is only needed if you want to use the domain for something else (like a website or email service).

  • Log into your Cloudflare account
  • Select your domain and go to the DNS tab
  • Locate the TXT and routing records you added for Patreon
  • Delete them (trash icon) or edit/replace as needed
  • Save your changes

After saving, your domain’s DNS will no longer point to Patreon.

Add your domain to Patreon

  • Click the Next button

Update DNS records in Domain.com

  • Log in to your Domain.com account

  • Select Domains in the left-side menu

  • Select the domain name you want to adjust (If you only have one domain, you will be taken directly to the Domain Details page)

  • On the domain page, go down to the Advanced Tools section

  • Click Manage close to Advanced DNS Records. A pop-up may appear, click Continue

  • You’ll land on the DNS Management page. First, remove a few existing records from your domain settings. Delete any records with the category Alias or CNAME. Records labeled MX or TXT don’t affect your Patreon setup and can stay as they are.

    • If this domain has been used before, there may be additional records you’ll need to remove. For guidance on configuring an existing domain, check with your domain provider’s setup instructions

  • In Network Solutions DNS editor, click Add Record and insert the DNS records exactly as shown in Patreon. Be sure to select the correct category in the Type drop-down menu, matching A record with A record, AAAA with AAAA, and so on. Leave TTL at the default

  • Paste the number from Patreon in the “Value” section, and then select the Add button

    • You need to add every single type/value into the domain provider
    • For the CNAME value in your Redirecting domain, be sure to add “www” in the “Name” section in Network Solutions

  • Once you’ve entered all of the values from Patreon into Network Solutions, you’re all set. You may need to wait up to 24 hours before they are officially connected, but you can head back to Patreon and click “Refresh” next to your domain to check the updated status

    • TXT record (verification) → Host: _patreon.members (or as shown in Patreon)

Update DNS records in GoDaddy

Now you have to copy the DNS records into the provider’s account:

  • Sign in to your GoDaddy Domain Portfolio

  • Select the domain you want to connect to access the Domain Settings page

  • Select DNS to view your DNS records

  • Check your existing DNS records for any records that conflict with the ones shown in Patreon

    • If an existing A or CNAME record uses the same host as a record Patreon asks you to add, delete the existing record before adding the new one
    • You don’t need to delete other DNS records that don’t conflict with the records shown in Patreon

  • Select Add New Record and choose the record type shown in Patreon from the Type menu

  • Enter the DNS record exactly as shown in Patreon:

    • Name: Enter the host or name shown in Patreon
    • Value: Enter the corresponding value shown in Patreon
    • TTL: Leave this at the default setting

  • Select Add More Records if you need to enter additional DNS records, and repeat the steps above for every record shown in Patreon

  • Select Save to add the record. If you added multiple records at the same time, select Save All Records

  • Once you’ve entered all of the values from Patreon into GoDaddy, you’re all set. Head back to Patreon and click Refresh next to your domain to check the updated status

    • TXT record (verification) → Host: _patreon.members (or as shown in Patreon)
    • CNAME record (routing) → Host: members, Answer / Value: the target shown in Patreon (e.g. custom.patreon-domains.com)
    • TXT record (verification) → Host: _patreon

Here’s how to connect your Squarespace domain to Patreon:

Add DNS records in Squarespace

Follow these steps to add your DNS records in Squarespace:

  • Log in to your Squarespace account
  • From the top navigation, go to Domains, if you’re not already there, and select the domain you want to connect
  • In the left sidebar, click DNS → DNS Settings
  • Review your existing DNS records:
    • Delete any records that match the type you plan to add (for example, old A or CNAME records) so you don’t have duplicates or conflicts
    • Records labeled MX or TXT don’t affect your Patreon setup and can stay as they are
    • If this domain has been used before, there may be additional records you’ll need to remove. For guidance on configuring an existing domain, check with your domain provider’s setup instructions
  • Go to the Custom Records section, select the Add Record button, and enter the records shown in Patreon exactly as displayed
  • In Squarespace DNS editor, add the DNS records exactly as shown in Patreon. Be sure to select the correct category in the Type drop-down menu up top, matching A record with A record, AAAA with AAAA, and so on. Leave TTL at the default. Then select the Save button

You need to add every single type/value into the domain provider

For A records (if using your root domain):
  • Host: @
  • IP Address: enter the IPs shown in Patreon
For CNAME records (if using a subdomain):
  • Host: your subdomain name (e.g. members)
  • Alias Data: the target shown in Patreon
For redirecting domains (optional):
  • Host: www
  • Alias Data: the target URL provided by Patreon

Once you’ve entered all of the values from Patreon into Squarespace, you’re all set. You may need to wait up to 24 hours before they are officially connected, but you can head back to Patreon and click Refresh next to your domain to check the updated status.

Verify your connection in Patreon

After saving your DNS changes:

  • Return to Page details → Basics tab → Custom domain in Patreon
  • Patreon will automatically check your records and verify the connection
  • Once verified, you’ll see a green Connected status
  • Patreon will issue an SSL certificate automatically for your domain

Most connections resolve within minutes, but DNS changes can take up to 24–48 hours to fully propagate.

Disconnect or update your domain

To disconnect from Patreon:

If you ever want to disconnect your Squarespace domain from Patreon:

  • Go to Dashboard → Home tab → “…” menu → Page details
  • In the Basics tab, scroll to the Custom domain section
  • Find your active domain and click (…) More → Disconnect domain
  • Confirm by selecting Disconnect

Once disconnected, your page will revert to your original patreon.com/creatorname URL.

If you’d like to reuse your Squarespace domain for another purpose, you can go back to DNS Settings in Squarespace and delete or replace the Patreon-related records.

To update DNS in Squarespace (optional)

This step is only needed if you want to use the domain for something else (like a website or email service)

  • Sign in to your Squarespace Domain Portfolio
  • From the top navigation, go to Domains, if you’re not already there, and select the domain you want to connect
  • In the left sidebar, click DNS → DNS Settings
  • Go to the Custom Records section, find the record you want to delete, and select the icon
  • A pop-up will open asking to confirm the deletion of the selected DNS records, click Delete button

Connect your Namecheap domain to your Patreon page

If you bought your domain through Namecheap, you can connect it to your Patreon page so fans can visit you at a branded URL (like yourname.com or members.yourname.com) instead of patreon.com/yourname.

You’ll need to have already registered your domain with Namecheap and be using Namecheap’s DNS (BasicDNS, PremiumDNS, or FreeDNS). Once connected, Patreon will still power your page behind the scenes, but your fans will see your Namecheap domain in the URL.

Add your domain to Patreon

Changing your Patreon URL to a custom domain will not affect your existing members or messages. We suggest letting your members know before changing your URL so they can update any bookmarks.

Here’s how to change your Patreon URL to a custom domain:

  • In Patreon, go to Dashboard in the left sidebar menu
  • In the Home tab, click the … menu next to the Edit page button and select Page details
  • In the Basics tab, scroll to the Custom domain section and click Add a domain
  • Enter your domain (for example members.yourname.com or yourname.com)
  • A table will display the DNS records you need to add at Namecheap — a TXT record for verification, plus either CNAME, ALIAS/ANAME, or A records for routing

Add DNS records at Namecheap

  • Log in to your Namecheap account

  • Go to Domain List and click Manage next to your domain

  • Select the Advanced DNS tab — this opens the Host Records section, where you can view, edit, and add DNS records

  • Review your existing records first:

    • Delete any records that match the type you plan to add (for example, old A or CNAME records) so you don’t have duplicates or conflicts
    • Records labeled MX or TXT don’t affect your Patreon setup and can stay as they are
    • If this domain has been used before, there may be additional records you’ll need to remove. For guidance on configuring an existing domain, check with your domain provider’s setup instructions

  • In the Host Records section, add the new records exactly as shown in Patreon:

    • Match each record type correctly (A with A, CNAME with CNAME, etc.)
    • If a record with the same host/type already exists, replace it

  • For your redirecting domain, enter www in the Host field in Namecheap

  • Leave the TTL as the default value and don’t forget to click Save All Changes to confirm your updates

    • TXT record (verification): Host: _patreon.members (or as shown in Patreon)
    • CNAME record (routing): Host: members, Answer / Value: the target shown in Patreon (e.g. custom.patreon-domains.com)
    • TXT record (verification): Host: @
    • Routing record → either:
      • ALIAS/ANAME → point to Patreon’s host
      • A records → point to the IPs shown in Patreon
    • 👉 For your root (apex) domain, enter @ in the Host field in Namecheap

Verify on Patreon

  • Return to Page details → Basics tab → Custom domain in Patreon
  • Patreon will detect your records, verify your domain, and activate the connection. The settings will reflect as “Connected” in green once successful

Once verified, we’ll issue an SSL certificate automatically.

Most connections resolve within minutes, but DNS updates can take up to 24–48 hours. If your domain doesn’t connect after this time, check the Troubleshooting section in the main custom domain guide for common fixes.

Disconnect or update your domain

To disconnect from Patreon:
  • Go to Dashboard → Home tab → … menu → Page details
  • In the Basics tab, scroll to the Custom domain section
  • Find your active domain and click (…) more > Disconnect domain
  • Select Disconnect to confirm

Once disconnected, your page will fall back to your original patreon.com/creatorname link.

To update DNS in Namecheap (optional):

This step is only needed if you want to use the domain for something else (like a website or email service).

  • Log into your Namecheap account
  • Go to Domain List → Manage → Advanced DNS
  • Under Host Records, locate the records you added for Patreon:
    • TXT record ( _patreon or _patreon.members)
    • CNAME record (for subdomain, e.g. members)
    • ALIAS/ANAME or A records (for apex domain)
  • Delete them (trash icon) or edit/replace as needed, then click Save All Changes to confirm

After saving, your domain’s DNS will no longer point to Patreon.

Connect your Porkbun domain to your Patreon page

If you bought your domain through Porkbun, you can connect it to your Patreon page so fans can visit you at a branded URL (like yourname.com or members.yourname.com) instead of patreon.com/yourname.

You’ll need to have already registered your domain with Porkbun. Once connected, Patreon will still power your page behind the scenes, but your fans will see your Porkbun domain in the URL.

Add your domain to Patreon

Changing your Patreon URL to a custom domain will not affect your existing members or messages. We suggest letting your members know before changing your URL so they can update any bookmarks.

Here’s how to change your Patreon URL to a custom domain:

  • In Patreon, go to Dashboard in the left sidebar menu
  • In the Home tab, click the … menu next to the Edit page button and select Page details
  • In the Basics tab, scroll to the Custom domain section and click Add a domain
  • Enter your domain (for example members.yourname.com or yourname.com)
  • A table will display the DNS records you need to add at Porkbun — a TXT record for verification, plus either CNAME, ALIAS/ANAME, or A records for routing

Add DNS records at Porkbun

  • Log into your Porkbun account

  • Go to Account → Domain Management

  • Find your domain and click Details → DNS Records (or use the quick DNS link)

  • Click the edit (pencil icon) next to DNS Records

  • First, remove a few existing records from your domain settings. Delete any records with the category Alias or CNAME. Records labeled MX or TXT don’t affect your Patreon setup and can stay as they are.

    • If this domain has been used before, there may be additional records you’ll need to remove. For guidance on configuring an existing domain, check with your domain provider’s setup instructions

  • In Porkbun’s DNS editor, add the DNS records exactly as shown in Patreon. Be sure to select the correct category in the Type drop down menu up top, matching A record with A record, AAAA with AAAA, and so on. Leave TTL at the default (600 seconds / 10 minutes)

  • Paste the number from Patreon in the Value section, leaving Host blank for anything associated with your Primary domain, and then select the Add button

    • You need to add every single type/value into the domain provider in both your Primary and Redirecting domains

  • For the CNAME value in your Redirecting domain, be sure to add www in the Host section in Porkbun

  • Once you’ve entered all of the values from Patreon into Porkbun, you’re all set. You may need to wait up to 24 hours before they are officially connected, but you can head back to Patreon and click Refresh next to your domain to check the updated status

    • TXT record (verification): Host: _patreon.members (or as shown in Patreon)
    • CNAME record (routing): Host: members, Answer / Value: the target shown in Patreon (e.g. custom.patreon-domains.com)
    • TXT record (verification): Host: _patreon
    • Routing record → either:
      • ALIAS/ANAME → point to Patreon’s host
      • A records → point to the IPs shown in Patreon
    • 👉 For your root (apex) domain, leave the Host field blank in Porkbun

Important for Porkbun users

  • Porkbun often pre-populates DNS with default records pointing to pixie.porkbun.com or uixie.porkbun.com. Delete or replace these if they conflict with your Patreon records
  • If a record with the same host/type already exists, replace it
  • Always click the green Save button after adding or editing a record
  • Leave TTL at the default (600 seconds / 10 minutes)

Verify on Patreon

  • Return to Page details → Basics tab → Custom domain in Patreon
  • Patreon will detect your records, verify your domain, and activate the connection. The settings will reflect as “Connected” in green once successful

Once verified, we’ll issue an SSL certificate automatically.

Most connections resolve within minutes, but DNS updates can take up to 24–48 hours. If your domain doesn’t connect after this time, check the Troubleshooting section in the main custom domain guide for common fixes.

Disconnect or update your domain

To disconnect from Patreon:
  • Go to Dashboard → Home tab → … menu → Page details
