What is Discord? (Creator)

Discord is a voice and text chat app where you and your members can connect to build the community you envision. Our Discord integration syncs your Discord server roles with your Patreon tiers to grant members exclusive access.

Discord integration is available to all launched Patreon creators in good standing.

Discord created a Beginner’s Guide to Discord with a ton of information and tips as you get started.

Glossary of Discord terms

Discord has a specific vocabulary. Below are some terms they use and we use when describing Discord and Patreon’s integration. Please note the definitions below are taken directly from Discord’s resources and will be updated if changed by Discord.

Server: Servers are the spaces on Discord. They are made by specific communities and friend groups. The vast majority of servers are small and invitation-only. Some larger servers are public. Any user can start a new server for free and invite their friends to it.

Channel: Discord servers are organized into text and voice channels, which are usually dedicated to specific topics and can have different rules.

  • In text channels, users can post messages, upload files, and share images for others to see at any time.
  • In voice channels, users can connect through a voice or video call in real-time, and can share their screen with their friends - we call this Go Live.

Roles: Roles are a way of designating who is who in your server. You can keep channels within your server exclusive to certain roles (for example, your highest-paying members get their own private channel). Roles can have their own set of server and channel-specific permissions (see below).

Permissions: Permissions allow users to have specific privileges and functions in a server. Some permissions can be as basic as allowing users the ability to add reactions to messages while other permissions grant users more administrative actions. These permissions are based on the roles assigned to users in a server and permissions can be assigned per role on both the server level and channel level. Learn more about permissions from Discord, here: Setting up Permissions

DMs and GDMs: Users can send private messages to other users as a direct message (DM), as well as start a voice or video call. Most DMs are one-on-one conversations, but users have the option to invite up to nine others to the conversation to create a private group DM (GDM), with a maximum size of ten people. Group DMs are not public and require an invite from someone in the group to join.

Go Live: users can share their screen with other people who are on a server or a DM with them. You can disable this for certain roles and disable it for others using role permissions.

How can I use Discord?

Give members access to your private world with our Discord integration. Discord is a versatile community-building app with a thousand and one ways you can utilize it. Here are just a few ways you can use Discord to add benefits to your membership:

Access to private member-only channels

You can give members special access to locked channels. Here is how you can create a super-secret channel just for members:

  • Log into your Discord server
  • Click on the “+” icon next to one of your existing text channels
  • Type in the new channel name and select the option for a Private Channel
  • Choose the role(s) that will have a VIP pass to access this channel
  • Finally, click Create
Hang out with your members with a Voice channel

With Discord, you can create voice channels where members can have conversations in real-time. You can also video call individual members that you’ve had direct messages.

FAQ

  • Discord is free to use! All you have to do is create an account: Create your Discord account.
  • Many creators self-moderate their servers while they’re getting started. You can pin “Server rules” in a specific channel that you direct all new members to. As your community grows and becomes more active, you’ll start to recognize users who naturally regulate channels — those are the people you can reach out to and ask if they’d like to help moderate your server.
  • Discord has created a resource for learning about server moderation. It also breaks down how to set up a channel and permissions you can customize: Discord Moderator Academy

General: Content policy and guidelines

Access to Patreon’s features and products for Adult/18+ creators

We’re committed to supporting all Patreon creators in building their creative businesses and connecting with their biggest fans. We’re safely expanding access to more products and features for more creators on Patreon, including those that make Adult/18+ work. We will update this page as additional products and features are made available.

All Adult/18+ creators must be ID-verified and age-verified to be on Patreon and to use Patreon’s features. Check the Guidelines for Adult/18+ creators’ age verification.

Features Currently Accessible to Adult/18+ Creators

Media Types
  • Text Posts: Fully accessible
  • Newsletters: Fully accessible. Newsletters cannot include video content, consistent with other video restrictions that apply to Adult/18+ creators
  • Image Posts: Fully accessible. However, image and media previews are blurred with increased opacity for 18+ content
  • Third-party video hosting: Patreon Video is not available to Adult/18+ creators. Creators can link to external platforms (e.g., YouTube, Vimeo) to host their content
  • Attachments and File Types: Fully accessible
Autopilot
  • Available for Adult/18+ creators
Memberships
  • Adult/18+ creators can offer free and paid memberships to fans who are 18 or older
  • You can choose how prominently to display the Join for free option on your Patreon — Learn more in our guide on How free memberships can help grow your community
  • 18+ content must be kept behind a paid subscription wall, even if your free members are 18 or older
Free Trials
  • Adult/18+ creators can offer Free Trials for paid tiers
Payments
  • Web & Android Payments: Adult/18+ creators can accept payments on mobile and web browsers
Community Chats
  • Available to Adult/18+ creators
Search and Explore
  • Fans who are 18 and older can update their member settings to discover Adult/18+ creators through Patreon’s search and explore tools — Learn more about how to Find creators on Patreon
Discount Codes
  • Adult/18+ creators can offer discounts to their members as long as the members are over the age of 18
  • Creators must be on subscription billing to be eligible for this feature — Learn more about Managing discounts
Gifting
  • Adult/18+ creators can access creator-to-fan and fan-to-fan gifting
  • Recipients must be over the age of 18 years old to redeem the gift for an Adult/18+ page — Learn more about Gifting memberships to your fans (creator to fan gifts)
Commerce & One-Time Purchases
  • Adult/18+ creators can sell digital products (including posts and collections) as one-time purchases — Learn more about Selling posts and collections
  • Creators must be on subscription billing to be eligible for this feature
  • Creators’ digital products must additionally comply with our guidelines for public previews — Check our guide on Understanding Public Previews and Commerce guidelines for adult/18+ creators

How we roll out products

Patreon ensures that we roll out features to all creators in a way that ensures we are compliant with legal, payment, and platform policies. We gradually roll out products to ensure the product is working for creators as designed to minimize disruption.

Age Verification: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Below you’ll find some of the common questions we’ve received about Age Verification requirements for Adult/18+ creators from our payment processing partners. We will add additional answers to any other common questions that emerge.

About the requirement and who needs to do it

  • Payment processors like Mastercard and Visa require Patreon to have all creators sharing sexually explicit creations or creations that include nudity verify that they are over the age of 18. Patreon relies on this payments infrastructure to accept digital pledge payments and enable creators to earn on Patreon.
  • This payment processor requirement applies to creators in the Adult/18+ category.
  • Yes, you are eligible to recategorize from “Adult/18+” to “Safe for All Audiences,” which opts you out of Age Verification. Here’s how you can do that.
  • Yes, if you remove every piece of sexually explicit content or nudity on your page, you are eligible to recategorize from “Adult/18+” to “Safe for All Audiences,” which opts you out of Age Verification. Again, here’s how you can do that.
  • You are responsible for obtaining the written consent of any real humans who participate in works on your Patreon. You should use this consent form template to do so and retain all participant consent documentation indefinitely. Upon request from a payment partner, Patreon may ask you to provide this documentation, which would then be shared with the requesting payment partner to demonstrate compliance with their rules.

The Age Verification process

  • You’ll first be asked to select your country — the process differs for some countries, including South Korea (see below). The majority of creators will then submit a government-issued identification showing full name, birthdate, and photo (like a license, passport, or national ID), and you’ll submit photos of that document to a third party we detail below. You’ll also snap a photo of yourself in that moment (in other words, a selfie), that will be matched to the photo from the ID to confirm it’s you. We expect the process to take approximately 3-5 minutes to complete.
  • Due to South Korea’s Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA), we’re no longer able to accept ID documents that contain a Resident Registration Number (RRN). South Korean creators verify using Digital ID Verification instead — a quick check through your mobile carrier or credit card provider. This method doesn’t require a selfie or a document upload.
  • You’ve shared lots of ideas for how we can prioritize inclusivity throughout this process. With that in mind, we’ve developed a list of alternative (non-government-issued) IDs we accept. If you do not have a government-issued ID, you might be eligible to use alternative IDs.
  • You are eligible to use alternative IDs if you do not have a government-issued ID or if you have a serious privacy concern about using your government-issued ID.
  • Every alternative (non-government-issued) ID document you submit must:
    • Be written in English, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French, or Italian.
    • Be a photo or scanned copy that presents clearly and without glare, with all four corners visible and font large enough to read.
    • (If an expiration date is listed), be valid as of the date the document is submitted.
    • Show the exact same name* as those on the other submitted documents.
  • To learn more, please check our Guidelines for Adult/18+ creators age verifying with alternative (non-government-issued) IDs.
  • We have prepared a broad list of documents that you may use to verify with an alternative ID if you do not have a government-issued ID. Collectively, the documents you submit must show your full name, date of birth, and photo. All documents must show the same name, or else official name change paperwork must also be provided.
  • If your address is out of date please update it. Accurate location data is required for tax information reporting in some jurisdictions, and inaccurate addresses can result in inaccurate reporting and/or inaccurate sales tax/VAT application. You can update your address in your tax form.
  • We’ve enlisted a third-party vendor specialized in identity verification. And yes, it’s able to accommodate the vast majority of languages for the convenience of Patreon creators.
  • Creators let us know that maximizing the number of supportable languages and countries was important to you. Stripe is a little bit more limited on those fronts, whereas now we are enabled to make life easier for creators by supporting nearly every country, language, and form of government-issued identification.
  • We are leveraging ID verification product meaning that your information will be processed end-to-end by a third-party vendor, but you don’t have to leave Patreon’s website to complete the process. You’ll be able to begin the process from a desktop browser, mobile browser, or from within our iOS and Android apps. However, your progress will not be carried over if you attempt to switch between devices in the middle of the process. Verification only takes a few minutes to complete, so we expect most creators to be able to finish the process once they get started.

Additional FAQ

  • Creator privacy is incredibly important to us, and we made sure to select a vendor that specializes in identification verification, which has received multiple information security certifications such as ISO/IEC 27001:2013, PCI DSS, and SOC2 Type 2.
  • Patreon will not use the information you provide during verification to update any of the public information on your account or campaign. We will never publicly share or sell personal information.
  • If you’re submitting a government-issued ID, please ensure that you are submitting a clear picture of the complete document. If you’d prefer to redact your address from the government-issued ID you are submitting for verification, please reach out to us.
  • We recognize that asking for identification is deeply sensitive and personal, and that not everyone uses their legal or birth names in their daily lives. The option mentioned above [by which you can submit alternative IDs], may be a good path for you. We will never publicly share the name from the identification you submit.

Miscellaneous

  • If your new page is Adult/18+ and will feature sexually explicit content or nudity, then yes, you’ll complete the verification process again. We are unable to transfer verification status or verified information from one account to another.

Appendix to creator Privacy Promise

This appendix forms part of the Data Processing Agreement - Creator Privacy Promise. Please refer to the main document for full context and definitions.

ANNEX I

A. LIST OF PARTIES
Data exporter(s):
  • Name: Patreon, Inc.
  • Address: 600 Townsend Street, Suite 500, San Francisco, CA 94103, USA
  • Contact person’s name, position and contact details: Patreon Privacy Team, privacy@patreon.com
  • Activities relevant to the data transferred under these Clauses: Patreon enables Creators (as defined with the Creator Privacy Promise) to start an offering by directly connecting with their biggest fans and turning them into free or paying members of the Creator’s community, or one time purchasers of Creator offering(s).
  • Role (controller/processor): Controller
Data importer(s):
  • Name: Creators on Patreon’s platform
  • Address: The address provided by the Creator in their Patreon account settings.
  • Contact person’s name, position and contact details: The name and contact details provided by the Creator in their Patreon account settings.
  • Activities relevant to the data transferred under these Clauses: Provision of offerings, membership benefits, content, and communications to Members (as defined in the Creator Privacy Promise).
  • Signature and date: These Clauses take effect the moment a Creator creates a Patreon account.
  • Role (controller/processor): Processor
B. DESCRIPTION OF TRANSFER
Categories of data subjects whose personal data is transferred:

The category of the data subjects are website users who sign up for both free and paid memberships, or make a one time purchase, on Patreon.

Categories of personal data transferred:

The personal data transferred is determined by the data exporter and may include: purchase information, including, but not limited to, amount, start date, and end date, and contact information, including, but not limited to, username, email address, and shipping address.

Sensitive data transferred (if applicable) and applied restrictions or safeguards:

By default, no special categories of personal data are transferred. Should the nature of the data importer’s services involve the processing of special categories of data, the data importer must apply strict access controls, purpose limitation, and enhanced security measures appropriate to the risk. Any such processing requires explicit consent from the data exporter and the data subject.

The frequency of the transfer:

Continuous, for as long as data importer holds Member Data (as defined in the Privacy Promise).

Nature of the processing:

The processing activities include the collection, recording, organization, storage, retrieval, use, and disclosure of personal data for the purposes of managing memberships, communicating with Members, and delivering membership benefits.

Purpose(s) of the data transfer and further processing:

To enable the data importer (Creator) to fulfill their obligations to their Members, including:

  • Providing access to content
  • Delivering physical or digital goods and benefits
  • Communicating updates and messages to Members
  • Managing the membership relationship
The period for which the personal data will be retained:

Data importer will not retain any of the personal data for longer than is necessary to provide Membership Services. Upon the termination of such services for any individual Member, or upon the instruction of the data exporter, the data importer shall, at the election of the data exporter, securely destroy or return to the data exporter all personal data related to that Member. The data importer shall certify to the data exporter that it has done so upon request.

For transfers to (sub-) processors, also specify subject matter, nature and duration of the processing:

The data exporter does not authorize the data importer to engage any sub-processors for the processing of personal data under these Clauses, except to share with any third party listed on Patreon’s App Directory at patreon.com, as updated from time to time, solely as necessary to provide Membership Services.

C. COMPETENT SUPERVISORY AUTHORITY

The competent supervisory authority is the Comissão Nacional de Proteção de Dados (CNPD) of Portugal.

ANNEX II

TECHNICAL AND ORGANISATIONAL MEASURES INCLUDING TECHNICAL AND ORGANISATIONAL MEASURES TO ENSURE THE SECURITY OF THE DATA

The data importer shall implement and maintain, at a minimum, the following technical and organizational measures to ensure the security of the personal data:

Measures of pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data:
  • Personal data shall be encrypted in transit using strong, industry-standard protocols (e.g., TLS 1.2 or higher).
  • Personal data shall be encrypted at rest using strong encryption standards (e.g., AES-256).
Measures for ensuring ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems and services:
  • A formal information security policy shall be maintained and reviewed annually.
  • Access to personal data is restricted on a “need-to-know” basis, using role-based access controls.
  • All personnel with access to personal data are subject to binding confidentiality agreements.
Measures for ensuring the ability to restore the availability and access to personal data in a timely manner in the event of a physical or technical incident:
  • Regular backups of personal data are performed and stored in a secure, separate location.
  • A disaster recovery and business continuity plan is in place and tested regularly to ensure timely restoration of data and services.
Processes for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of technical and organisational measures in order to ensure the security of the processing:
  • Regular vulnerability scans and penetration tests of systems processing personal data are conducted.
  • Security measures are reviewed and updated in response to new threats or vulnerabilities.
Measures for user identification and authorisation:
  • Unique user IDs are assigned to each individual with access to personal data.
  • Strong password policies are enforced, and the use of multi-factor authentication (MFA) is required for access to systems containing personal data.
Measures for the protection of data during transmission:
  • All data transfers over public networks are encrypted using secure protocols (e.g., TLS/SSL).
Measures for ensuring physical security of locations at which personal data are processed:
  • Where data is processed on-premises, physical access controls (e.g., locks, access cards) are implemented. For cloud-based processing, the data importer relies on the physical security measures of the cloud provider (e.g., AWS, Google Cloud), which are subject to independent security audits (e.g., SOC 2, ISO 27001).
Measures for ensuring events logging:
  • Logs of access to and actions performed on personal data are maintained and reviewed regularly for security incidents.
Measures for ensuring data minimisation:
  • The data importer shall only process personal data that is adequate, relevant, and limited to what is necessary for the agreed-upon purposes.
Measures for ensuring limited data retention:
  • A data retention policy is in place to ensure personal data is not retained for longer than necessary and is securely deleted upon the end of the retention period.

ANNEX III

LIST OF SUB-PROCESSORS

The data exporter has not blanketly authorized the use of any sub-processors by the data importer. The data importer is prohibited from engaging any third party to process personal data on its behalf under these Clauses, except to share with any third party listed on Patreon’s App Directory at patreon.com, as updated from time to time, solely as necessary to provide Membership Services.

Are there any age restrictions?

If you want to create a Patreon account, you need to be at least 13. If you want to become a member of a creator or provide membership as a creator, you must be at least 18 years old or have permission from a parent or guardian.

As we welcome people over the age of 13, we employ stricter measures to ensure their safety that ultimately translates to a zero-tolerance policy for sexualizing underaged individuals on Patreon. Part of this commitment to ensure the safety of underaged creators is our reporting partnership with National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC).

If you are a parent or guardian of a creator who is under 18 years old, you may want to consider the following ways that you can take a more proactive approach towards controlling your child’s experience on Patreon:

  • If your child plans on making a creator page on Patreon, we encourage you, as their parent or guardian, to reach out to the Trust and Safety team to establish an ongoing relationship with us.
    • Doing this early on will allow us to have eyes on your child’s account and advise both you and your child in situations that may be difficult to navigate.
  • You may consider supervising your child’s activity on their account or even administering their account on their behalf.
    • Doing so will allow you to have greater control over what your child is exposed to on Patreon.
  • If you would rather have your child independently manage their own account, you should still consider monitoring the comments and messages that other users are sending to their page.
    • If you come across bullying or anything inappropriate, please block the person and send us a note.

Beta testing and early access program eligibility

We are constantly experimenting with product features to improve Patreon. This may take the form of beta testing or early access to new features and iterations of existing features. We may use a different set of criteria to determine who is eligible to participate in testing and early access for each product or feature. As explained in Patreon’s Terms of Use, access to beta testing and early access is not guaranteed, and Patreon may enable and disable these beta, test, or early access features at our discretion.

Fan Profiles (Beta)

Fan profiles just got an upgrade! This beta gives fans access to a new look and feel for their existing fan profile, including more customization options and a new activity tab where your public posts, likes, and comments are visible to everyone.

Please note: Content on your activity tab is always publicly visible, even if you have disabled your full public profile setting. When your full public profile setting is disabled, your activity tab will still be displayed in this beta version of fan profiles.

This upgraded fan profile is currently available to a limited group of fans, and features and functionality, including related settings, may change before it becomes available to everyone.

Can I be anonymous?

While there’s no way to be completely anonymous to creators you support and Patreon, you can use aliases in certain situations to protect your privacy from other users.

What account details do my creators have access to?

When you are a member of a creator, we provide the following information to them:

  • Your username (also displayed for anyone who lands on your profile)
  • Email address
  • Membership level

How to protect your privacy

We recommend you do 2 things:

  • Use a non-descriptive email address
  • Use an alias as your profile name

You can change both of these things by doing the following:

  • Click Your account , then Settings
  • You can change your name and the email address associated with your Patreon account, which is also used for logging in
  • Click the Save button to finalize your changes

Be mindful that your profile is public. You can read more about what is publicly displayed on your profile in the following article: Your Public Patreon Profile

You can read through our privacy policy for more details regarding what information we collect and the privacy of your account.

Consent form for participants in Adult/18+ works

Payment processing partners require Patreon to ensure that creators in the Adult/18+ category obtain written consent from real humans who participate in their creative works by being featured visually. To meet this requirement, Adult/18+ creators whose works visually feature real human participants other than themselves should document participant consent using the template below, which Patreon translated into 18 languages for convenience.

Note: This requirement does not apply to Adult/18+ creators whose creative works feature themselves alone, or to creators of Adult/18+ works that do not feature real people (e.g. animators, game developers, writers).

This participant consent template was updated as of May 2024 to meet the latest payment processor requirements. To ensure continued compliance with all requirements, Adult/18+ creators should use this template to document participant consent from May 2024 onward. Adult/18+ creators do not need to use this form to obtain retroactive consent from participants in past creative works, but should retain whatever form of consent documentation they did obtain at the time.

Adult/18+ creators should retain all participant consent documentation indefinitely. Upon request from a payment partner, Patreon may ask Adult/18+ creators to provide this documentation, which would then be shared with the requesting payment partner to demonstrate compliance with their rules.

Creator is not delivering benefits

Patreon doesn’t have direct management of benefits a creator may offer, however, we’re sharing our tips on what to do if your creator isn’t delivering what you had expected or if they are delivering subpar or corrupted digital products.

Get the details

We recommend doing a read-through of your creator’s “About section” or your specific membership in the My membership tab on the creator’s page.

There may be details about the creator’s timeline of creation/delivery. Most creators try to put that information front and center in their About section for fans considering membership.

Send the creator a message

If you’ve read through your creator’s page to see the benefit timeline, but things aren’t matching up, send a note to your creator to ask what the delay might be. There may be a perfectly good reason as to why their benefit delivery is delayed, or something may have gone wrong with the delivery. Reaching out to your creator is a great way to get to the bottom of it!

Visit this guide for sending your creator a message.

Request a refund from the creator

If you’ve waited long enough and would prefer to not receive the benefit at all, send the creator a note requesting a refund for your membership payment. Here are our best practices for requesting a refund from your creator.

Please note that there is no guarantee that the creator will issue your refund.

Cancel your membership

If you are not getting what you expected, we highly recommend cancelling your membership with the creator, which will ensure no future payments are processed.

Read through our cancellation article for step by step directions on how to cancel.

I think the creator is going against Patreon’s terms

Please refer to our Terms of Use and Community Guidelines before reporting a creator to our team.

If you believe that a creator is going against our Terms of Use or Community Guidelines, you can report the creator to our Trust & Safety team. Follow the steps outlined in this article to formally report a creator.

Data Processing Agreement - Creator Privacy Promise

Date: May 27, 2026

Patreon empowers creators on our platform (“Creators”, “You”) to start an offering by directly connecting with their biggest fans and turning them into free or paying members of your community, or one time purchasers of your offering(s) (“Members”).

To facilitate this direct connection with Members and enable Your offering(s)’ rewards and obligations to be fulfilled, Patreon provides some personal data of Members (“Member Data”) to Creators. Creators then process Member Data in order to provide Members any and all products, services, or updates as part of that Creator’s offering(s) on Patreon (collectively known as “Membership Services”). All Creators agree to this Data Processing Agreement (“Privacy Promise”) to ensure that Creators respect the privacy rights of Members when processing Member Data.

This Privacy Promise is between Patreon and Creators, taking effect from the moment a Patreon account is created and applies exclusively to the Member Data collected by Patreon and provided to Creators for the purpose of running an offering or business with Patreon.

This Privacy Promise is an extension of Patreon’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy and will outline certain requirements for Creators to process Member Data during and beyond their relationship with Patreon.

I. Definitions.

  • “Data Protection Legislation” means all applicable laws relating to privacy and the processing of personal data that may exist in any relevant jurisdiction, including, where applicable, the guidance and codes of practice issued by the supervisory authorities. Data Protection Legislation includes, but is not limited to, European Directives 95/46/EC and 2002/58/EC (as amended by Directive 2009/136/EC) and any legislation and/or regulation implementing or made pursuant to them, or which amends, replaces, re-enacts or consolidates any of them, including the General Data Protection Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), UK Data Protection Act 2018, Brazilian Data Protection Law (LGPD) (As amended by Law No. 13,853/2019), and U.S. state privacy laws, including the California Consumer Privacy Act 2018 Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.100 et seq.
  • “Good Industry Practice” means exercising the same skill, expertise, and judgement and using facilities and resources of a similar quality as would be expected from a person who: (a) is skilled and experienced in providing the services in question, seeking in good faith to comply with his contractual obligations and seeking to avoid liability arising under any duty of care that might reasonably apply; (b) takes all proper and reasonable care and is diligent in performing his obligations; and (c) complies with the Data Protection Legislation.
  • The terms “data controller”, “data processor”, “service provider”, “subprocessor”, “data subject”, “personal data”, “processing”, and “appropriate technical and organizational measures” shall be interpreted in accordance with Directive 95/46/EC, or other applicable Data Protection Legislation, in the relevant jurisdiction.

II. Scope.

The parties agree that Patreon is a data controller and that Creator is a data processor or service provider, as applicable, in relation to Member Data that Creator processes in the course of providing Membership Services. The subject matter of the data processing, the types of personal data processed, and the categories of data subjects will be defined by, and/or limited to, those necessary to carry out the Membership Services. The subject matter, duration, nature, and purpose of the processing of the personal data as well as the type of personal data and categories of data subjects covered by this Privacy Promise are as follows:

  • The subject matter of the data processing is Member Data.
  • The duration of the processing is for as long as Creator holds Member Data.
  • The nature and purpose of the processing under this Privacy Promise is limited to a Creator’s fulfillment of Membership Services to the Member.
  • The type of personal data covered by this agreement is purchase information, including, but not limited to, amount, start date, and end date, and contact information, including, but not limited to, username, email address, and shipping address.
  • The category of the data subjects are website and mobile app users who sign up for both free and paid memberships, or make a one time purchase, on Patreon.

III. Data Protection.

Creator shall adhere to the following requirements:

  • Processing as Instructed. Creators will process Member Data only in accordance with Patreon’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, and this Privacy Promise and only in compliance with Data Protection Legislation. The nature and purpose of the processing shall be limited to that necessary to carry out such instructions, and not for Creator’s own purposes, or for any other purpose except as required by law. If Creator is required by law to process the personal data for any other purpose, Creator will inform Member of such requirement prior to the processing unless prohibited by law from doing so.
  • Extent of Processing. Creator will process the personal data only to the extent, and in such manner, as is necessary for the provision of Membership Services.
  • International Data Transfer.
    • Transfer between parties: To the extent the Member Data is transferred from a country deemed to provide an adequate level of protection under Data Protection Legislation to a country not deemed as providing adequate protection, the parties will rely on Module Two (controller to processor) of the then-current standard contractual clauses (SCCs) for the transfer of Personal Data or other transfer mechanisms as provided for by Data Protection Legislation, which are incorporated herein by reference. The information required by the Annexes of the SCCs is set forth in Appendix 1 to this Privacy Promise.
    • No onward transfers: Creator will not transfer or authorize the transfer of Data to countries outside the European Economic Area (EEA) or jurisdictions not deemed to provide an adequate level of protection under Data Protection Legislation, without the prior consent of Patreon. To the extent that Patreon approves an onward transfer, Creator will ensure that such transfers are made in compliance with applicable cross-border data transfer laws. In particular, Creator must rely on the then-current standard SCCs for the transfer of Personal Data or other transfer mechanisms as provided for by Data Protection Legislation.
  • Appropriate Technical and Organizational Measures. Creator will implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational measures designed to protect the personal data against unauthorized or unlawful processing and against accidental loss, destruction, damage, theft, alteration, or disclosure. The measures shall be appropriate to the harm which might result from any unauthorized or unlawful processing, accidental loss, destruction, damage, or theft of the personal data and having regard to the nature of the personal data which is to be protected and as a minimum shall be in accordance with the Data Protection Legislation and Good Industry Practice.
  • Transfer to Third Parties. Creator will not give access to, sell, share, or transfer any personal data to any third party (including any affiliates, group companies or subcontractors) without the prior consent of Patreon, with Patreon’s prior consent granted to share with any third party listed on Patreon’s App Directory at patreon.com, as updated from time to time, solely as necessary to provide Membership Services. Creator must also ensure the reliability and competence of such third parties, its employees or agents who may have access to the personal data processed in the provision of Membership Services, and must ensure that the third party is subject to provisions protecting Member Data which are equivalent to those in this Privacy Promise and Patreon’s Terms of Service and as are required by applicable Data Protection Legislation.
  • Reliability and Competence of Creator Personnel. Creator will take reasonable steps to ensure the reliability and competence of any Creator personnel who have access to Member Data. Creator will ensure that all Creator personnel required to access the personal data are informed of the confidential nature of the personal data and comply with the obligations set out in this Privacy Promise.
  • Acknowledgement of Data Protection Legislation and Assistance. Creator will take all reasonable steps to assist Patreon in complying with applicable Data Protection Legislation. For example, Creator will promptly inform Patreon in writing if it receives: (i) a request from a data subject concerning any personal data; or (ii) a complaint, communication, or request relating to Member’s obligations under Data Protection Legislation.
  • Destruction or Return of Property Upon Membership Services Completion or Upon Leaving Patreon’s Platform. Creator will not retain any of the personal data for longer than is necessary to provide Membership Services. At the end of Membership Services, upon Patreon’s request, or upon Member’s request, Creator will securely destroy or return (at Member’s election) the personal data to Member. If Creator leaves Patreon’s platform, Creator will securely destroy personal data in accordance with this Privacy Promise and will have no further rights to process Member Data.
  • Loss or Security Breach. If Creator becomes aware of any accidental, unauthorized or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, or disclosure of, or access to Member Data processed by Creator in the course of providing Membership Services, it will do the following:
    • Provide notice to Patreon. Creator shall promptly and without undue delay notify Patreon and provide Patreon with: a detailed description of the loss or security breach; the type of data that was the subject of the loss or security breach; the identity of each affected person if known, and the steps Creator has taken or will take in order to mitigate and remediate such security breach, in each case as promptly as such information can be collected or otherwise becomes available (as well as periodic updates to this information and any other information Patreon may reasonably request relating to the loss or security breach); and
    • Investigate the matter promptly. Creator shall promptly take action, at its own expense, to investigate the loss or security breach and to identify, prevent and mitigate the effects of the loss or security breach and to carry out appropriate recovery actions to remedy the loss or security breach.
  • Compliance with Data Protection Legislation. Creator shall comply at all times with and assist Patreon in complying with its applicable obligations under Data Protection Legislation. Creator shall provide reasonable information requested by Patreon to demonstrate compliance with the obligations set out in this Privacy Promise. Creator will notify Patreon immediately if, in Creator’s opinion, an instruction for the processing of personal data given by Patreon violates any country’s data privacy legislation.

For the Appendix to this Privacy Promise, including the list of parties, description of transfer, and technical and organizational measures, please visit Appendix to the Creator Privacy Promise.

EU Digital Services Act

Patreon is a safe space for shared art and community between creators and their most passionate fans. We’re proud that 280,000 creators and growing worldwide trust us with their businesses, and we’re committed to ensuring the platform remains a safe and rewarding destination for the millions who visit it.

Patreon’s Terms of Use, including our Community Guidelines and Benefit Guidelines, are in place to make sure Patreon is welcoming to all creators and their fans. We are mindful that these policies — and how we enforce them — can impact creators’ livelihoods and creative freedom. We go to great lengths to enforce our policies fairly and consistently. For more information on how Patreon addresses illegal, harmful, or violative works, please review our Transparency Report for 2023.

The Digital Services Act (DSA) is a legal framework in the European Union (EU) that is intended to help harmonize rules and regulations governing such content moderation activity.

Number of Patreon Accounts in the EU

For the period of January 1, 2026 through June 30, 2026, Patreon had an average of 3,106,493 monthly active logged-in accounts in the EU, including an average of 34,741 monthly active logged-in accounts of creators who are earning money on Patreon

Legal Representative and Single Point of Contact for Relevant Authorities under the DSA

Patreon, Inc. has designated Patreon Portugal as its DSA legal representative. For DSA purposes, Patreon Inc. falls under the jurisdiction of Portugal.

You can contact the Patreon DSA legal representative at dsa-poc@patreon.com or at:

Patreon Portugal

Rua Augusto Rosa nº 79

4000-098

Porto, Portugal

The email address dsa-poc@patreon.com also functions as the electronic point of contact for Member States’ authorities, the European Commission, and the Board for Digital Services. Preferred language for communications: English and Portuguese.

If you are submitting a request for user information, please also review the additional information and follow the associated instructions here.

Please note that the dsa-poc@patreon.com email address is for use only by the European Commission, EU Member States’ authorities, and the European Board for Digital Services. Emails sent to this email address that are not from relevant authorities under the DSA will in principle not be read.

If you are an EU-based user or certified trusted flagger, you may report content that you think violates Patreon’s policies, including content that you believe is unlawful in the EU, as explained here. For remaining queries and requests from EU users, please visit our contact us page.

Flagged and hidden posts

At Patreon, we bring a creator-first mindset to the tools and processes we build to uphold our Community Guidelines and keep the platform safe. Our Content Moderation team can now flag or hide specific posts that need correction, allowing creators to fix posts while keeping their page up and running.

My post has been flagged

A post may be flagged if it might violate our Community Guidelines. Creators will be notified about flagged posts in 4 different places:

  • Email notification
  • Mobile push notification (if enabled)
  • Notification tab on desktop and mobile web
  • Notification on the post in question
How long will I have to correct my flagged post?

Once a post has been flagged, creators have 72 hours to fix the post so that it follows our Community Guidelines. After 72 hours, the post will be hidden. Read the section below to learn more about hidden posts.

How do I fix my post so it’s within Patreon’s Community Guidelines?

To fix a flagged post, click on the flagged post notification to review the specific policy reason that your post was flagged. You’ll have 72 hours to make edits to your post and to send the edited version to our Content Moderation team for review. Once you’ve corrected the post, click the Save and submit for review button. Our Moderation team will review your post changes within two business days.

If your edits are accepted, the post will stay up, and you’ll have completed the review process. If your post still needs work to be within our guidelines, the post will be hidden while you work to fix it. We’ll send you notifications (email, push notification, and notification tab) if your post has been hidden. Learn more in the section on hidden posts below.

I need help with fixing my post

Our Moderation team is available to support you if you have any questions or need help fixing your post. Click the Contact us button, and our team will be in touch with you.

My post has been hidden

A post may be hidden if it violates our Community Guidelines or was flagged but not corrected within 72 hours. Hidden posts are not visible to patrons or the public when they visit a creator’s page. Hidden posts are accessible to the creator via the Hidden tab of their Managed posts page. The Hidden tab will only appear if a creator has hidden posts that violate our Community Guidelines.

Will I be notified when a post is hidden?

If a post of yours has been hidden, we’ll notify you through email, push notifications (if enabled), and the notification tab on desktop or mobile web.

How long do I have to fix my post?

We recommend correcting any Community Guidelines violations as soon as possible to avoid disrupting your patrons’ access to your posts. However, there is no time limit on when you can fix a hidden post.

How do I fix my post, so that it’s within Patreon’s Community Guidelines?

Here’s how to review and correct any hidden posts:

  • Visit your Hidden posts tab — if you don’t have any hidden posts, the Hidden tab will not appear
  • Select the post you want to fix and review the specific policy reason provided at the top of the post editor — you can expand each section for additional context on the issues found with the post
  • You can review our Community Guidelines for clarity on what is within and outside of our guidelines
  • Once you’ve made the necessary changes to your post, click the Save and submit for review button
  • Our Moderation team will review your changes. If the edits are accepted, the post will become visible again. If more work needs to be done, you’ll receive an email with further details
I need help with fixing my hidden post

If you have questions or need help correcting your post, our Moderation team is available to support you. Simply click the Contact us button, and our team will be in touch with you.

I have a question about my flagged or hidden post

If you have any questions about why your post was flagged or hidden or if you need help with fixing your post, please feel free to contact our Moderation team. Here’s how to get in touch with the team:

Visit the post editor for your flagged or hidden post

  • At the top of the post editor, click the Contact us button
  • Type your question in the text field and click the Submit button
  • Our Moderation team will follow up with you through email. Be sure to check your inbox that is linked to your Patreon account for the next steps

Please note that the Contact us button will not be available if you’ve already submitted changes. You can submit a ticket through our Help Center if you have questions or need support.

FAQ

  • A post may be flagged or hidden if it contains Community Guidelines violations. If you click into a flag or hidden post notification, we’ll tell you what needs to be addressed to fix your post.
  • Feel free to review our Community Guidelines for any clarification on why your post may have been flagged or hidden.
  • If you have any questions or need any help with fixing your post, you can click the Contact us button on your flagged or hidden post. A member of our Moderation team will reach out via email to support you further.
  • Hidden or flagged posts do not impact your ability to interact with your patrons or post new content. In most cases, flagged and hidden posts will not impact your payouts either — you can still pay your balance out as you normally do.
  • If you charge per creation, and a post you intended to charge for is hidden before the 1st of the month, we will not process payments for that post. This will not impact any other posts you may have intended to charge for as long as they are not hidden for Community Guidelines violation(s).
  • It’s important to note that other posts will not be flagged or hidden unless they also contain Community Guidelines violations.
  • You can make changes to the flagged or hidden post according to the policy reason shown when you edit the post. If you see no other way of fixing your post, you have the option to delete the post.
  • What if I don’t take any action at all?
  • If you do not make edits or take action to bring your post within guidelines, your post will be hidden indefinitely.
  • No, only the specific flagged post will be hidden. If the rest of your page is within guidelines, your page and other content will still be accessible by your patrons.
  • Context is very important when considering how violations may impact an account. We will continue to try to educate creators to help them understand how a rule has been broken and how to remedy the issue. In cases where the violation is particularly bad, or we see multiple instances of violating content, we may take further action, such as suspending or removing their account. In the most extreme cases, we may ban a creator from using Patreon.
  • It’s also important to note that all moderation decisions can be appealed, so if you feel that the decision was incorrect, you can let us know.
  • If you’ve had violations in the past and want clarity on the Community Guidelines, please don’t hesitate to reach out to our Moderation team by Selecting “I have a question about Community Guidelines” on this form, and a Trust & Safety teammate will be happy to help you.
  • Our Moderation team will contact you by email. Be sure to check your inbox for the email address you have linked to your account. You can check which email you have on your account in your account Basics settings.

Guidance around our off-Patreon activity policy

Patreon is committed to fostering a safe and supportive space for creators and their audiences. To protect our community and uphold our Community Guidelines, this policy outlines standards for behavior that extend beyond Patreon’s platform.

Engaging in certain harmful activities off-platform can impact our members and the integrity of Patreon itself. By defining these boundaries, we aim to prevent misuse, keep our community safe, and encourage positive interactions between creators and their fans. Attempts to direct, coerce, lure, or otherwise lead people from Patreon to third-party websites or experiences are strictly prohibited unless otherwise stated. If Patreon determines an account is being used to engage in prohibited off-platform activity, we may take action, which could include penalizing, suspending, or removing violating accounts.

Prohibited Off-Platform Activities

These prohibited activities fall into three broad categories: Scams, General Platform Abuse, and Commerce.

1. Scams

The following scams are strictly prohibited, whether they occur on Patreon or through off-platform engagement:

  • Financial scams including any attempt to request payment outside of Patreon’s payment ecosystem
  • Romance scams including encouraging or luring individuals to engage with dating apps, services, or messaging platforms
  • Payment system circumvention including any attempt to bypass Patreon’s payment tools to avoid fees or taxes
2. General Platform Abuse

Misusing Patreon to engage in prohibited activities off-platform, including:

  • Directing people off-site to engage in any activity prohibited by Patreon’s Community Guidelines, such as recruiting for dangerous organizations, organizing hateful or illegal activities, or offering prohibited products or services
  • Obscuring behavior to avoid detection, including using Patreon as a front account to funnel payments to off-platform websites engaged in prohibited activities
  • Exploiting Patreon as a lead generation platform for external services, such as directing fans to an Amazon storefront to avoid Patreon fees or farming followers for TikTok or Instagram accounts
  • Sharing links to private, closed, or password-protected messenger apps or chat threads.
  • Requesting personal contact information from Patreon users, including email addresses, phone numbers, or direct messaging usernames
3. Commerce

For the safety of our community, any product, service, or benefit sold or offered on Patreon must have a listing that clearly describes the item being sold, including how it will be accessed, downloaded, or delivered. Failure to comply may result in content removal or additional enforcement actions.

Permitted Off-Platform Activities

While some external activity is restricted, the following uses are allowed:

  • Existing Discord integrations for fan communication
  • Links to public social media pages (not behind paywalls or password protected), including:
    • Instagram
    • TikTok
    • Facebook & Facebook Groups
  • Non-native video and audio hosting: 18+ creators cannot use Patreon Native Video, but they can link to external platforms to host their content. Permitted sites include:
    • Vimeo
    • YouTube
    • OnlyFans
    • Podcasting sites/aggregators (more integrations to come)
  • Games, game mods, and other content must comply with Patreon’s Commerce Guidelines, including providing a clear description of the content and how it will be accessed, downloaded, or delivered

Enforcement & Future Considerations

Patreon will continue refining and expanding this policy based on emerging trends and community needs. Regular updates will be communicated through the Creator Policy Engagement Program to ensure that creators remain informed and have opportunities to provide feedback. For further details, please refer to our Community Guidelines.

Guidelines for Adult/18+ creators age verifying with alternative (non government-issued) IDs

We strongly encourage Adult/18+ creators with access to a government-issued ID to make use of our secure verification process available in your Notifications page, which only takes a few minutes. Approval wait times for the verification of alternative (non government-issued) IDs may take many months depending on volume.

South Korea: South Korean creators verify using Digital ID Verification instead of an ID document — a quick check through your mobile carrier or credit card provider, with no document upload or selfie required. This is different from the alternative (non-government-issued) ID process described in this article, which is not available as a substitute for South Korean creators. If Digital ID Verification isn’t working for you, please contact support.

Every alternative (non-government-issued) ID document you submit must:

  • Be written in English, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French or Italian.
  • Be a photo or scanned copy that presents clearly and without glare, with all four corners visible and font large enough to read.
  • (If an expiration date is listed), be valid as of the date the document is submitted.
  • Show the exact same name* as those on the other submitted documents.

*We understand names may have legally changed in the course of life; those creators should additionally submit notarized paperwork (e.g. marriage certificate, divorce decree, certificate of naturalization showing a new name, a signed court order for a name change) to account for the name differences.

Adult/18+ creators age verifying with alternative (non government-issued) IDs must submit identification documents from each of the following lists, including:

  • One (1) document from List A and
  • Two (2) documents from List B and
  • One (1) document from List C.
List A

Submit one (1) document from this list, which must show both your name and date of birth. The name must match the names on documents from Lists B and C, unless you submit additional documentation attesting to a name change (see above under “All submitted documents must”).

  • Original or certified copy of birth certificate
  • Hospital record of birth
  • Report of birth abroad
  • Federal or State census record
  • Final adoption decree (as adopter or adoptee)
  • Military record
  • Record of naturalization
List B

Submit two (2) documents from this list, both of which must show your name. Do not submit two documents of the exact same type (e.g. two electric bills), but two different documents under the same category (e.g. two utility bills — one electric and one internet) are acceptable. You may mask any information on the documents besides the elements listed below that must remain visible. The names must match the names on documents from Lists A and C, unless you submit additional documentation attesting to a name change (see above under “All submitted documents must”).

  • Social security card or equivalent national ID card. Document must show name, official letterhead, last 4 digits of social security number.
  • Voter ID card. Document must show name, official letterhead of the issuing country or state, issue date, expiration date.
  • Refugee or asylum identity card or certificate. Document must show name, official letterhead of the issuing country or state, issue date, expiration date.
  • Utility bill from within 90 days of submission (e.g. electricity, water, gas, sewage, trash, recycling, internet, phone). Document must show name, official letterhead, state of address.
  • Financial document from within 90 days of submission (e.g. bank statement or credit report). Document must show name, official letterhead, state of address.
  • Tax return from the most recent tax year. Document must show name, official letterhead, state of address.
  • Mortgage, lease or rental agreement. Document must show name, date, state of address.
  • Pay stub or earnings statement. Document must show name, official letterhead, state of address.
  • Insurance policy (e.g. life, health, automotive, home). Document must show name, official letterhead, state of address, issue date, expiration date.
  • Education record (e.g. transcript or diploma from high school or higher education institution). Document must show name, official letterhead, degree earned, date of issue.
List C

Submit a photo of yourself/selfie holding one (1) document from this list, which must show both your name and photo. The name on the photo ID you are holding must match the names on documents from Lists A and B, unless you submit additional documentation attesting to a name change (see Bullet 4 under “All submitted documents must:”).

  • Library card
  • Student ID card
  • Employment ID from an employer
  • Loyalty card
  • Public transportation card
  • Club/organization membership card
  • Debit or credit card

Additional FAQs

  • Patreon currently only accepts alternative (non government-issued) IDs to verify Adult/18+ creators. Non-Adult/18+ creators who have been asked to verify their identity for another reason need to provide a government-issued ID. You can reach out to our support team if you have further questions about your specific case.
  • Alternative (non government-issued) ID verification is available to Adult/18+ creators who do not have a government-issued ID. Additional emails will be sent once we are ready to accept their documents.
  • No. This alternative ID pathway is a separate option for creators worldwide who don’t have any government-issued ID — it doesn’t apply to South Korea’s Digital ID Verification requirement. If Digital ID Verification isn’t working for you, please contact support for help instead of submitting documents from this article.
  • Our submission process will use SendSafely to secure your alternative ID documents and pictures. SendSafely uses end-to-end encryption to protect any and all files and messages you submit. There is no way for SendSafely, or any third party, to decrypt this information. Even if the data is intercepted, stolen or seized, it cannot be read without the proper decryption keys, which are never stored or accessible by SendSafely systems. Furthermore, these documents will only be accessed by members of Patreon’s Trust & Safety team. Once we’ve verified your identity, your documents will be permanently deleted within 14 days.
  • If you are an Adult/18+ creator interested in using the alternative ID process for age verification, reach out to us.

Guidelines for Requesting User Information from Patreon

At Patreon, we are committed to protecting the privacy and safety of our users. We carefully review all requests for user information and disclose data only when legally required or when necessary to prevent imminent harm.

The following guidelines describe how government agencies, legal entities, and other authorized parties should submit requests.

Emergency Requests

Patreon may disclose limited user information on an expedited basis in response to emergency requests involving an imminent threat of death or serious physical harm. Determinations are made at Patreon’s discretion or based on the representations of a recognized law enforcement authority.

To submit an emergency request, please follow these instructions.

Service of Legal Process

All legal requests (e.g., subpoenas, court orders, warrants) must be formally served on Patreon’s designated agent for service of process in the applicable jurisdiction. We do not accept service via email, fax, physical mail, or hand delivery to our offices.

Note: Requests must include sufficient detail to identify the user account(s) at issue—such as username, campaign name, email address, link to patreon page, or payment identifiers.

Patreon is a U.S.-based company and requires foreign legal process to be domesticated through a Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty (MLAT), letters of request, or 28 U.S.C. § 1782 proceedings, as applicable.

Data Preservation Requests

We regularly purge data in accordance with our internal retention policies. If you anticipate a forthcoming request for information, we recommend submitting a preservation request as early as possible.

Preservation requests must:

  • Be submitted in writing to legal@patreon.com; and
  • Include sufficient detail to identify the user account(s) at issue—such as username, campaign name, email address, link to patreon page, or payment identifiers

We may, at our discretion, preserve data for up to 90 days and may extend this period upon receipt of a formal legal request.

User Notification Policy

Unless legally prohibited, Patreon may notify users when their data is requested by an external party. If your agency or entity seeks to delay or prevent user notification, you must include a valid and binding non-disclosure order with your request.

Cost of Reimbursement

To the extent permitted by law, Patreon reserves the right to seek reimbursement for the reasonable costs associated with gathering and producing user data in response to legal process.

If reimbursement is required under applicable law, payment should accompany your request or be made promptly upon invoicing.

Questions?

For general inquiries related to requests for user information, you may contact us at legal@patreon.com. Please note this email is not a channel for service of legal process.

I am being bullied, how can you help?

At Patreon, we empower creators and fans to express themselves, though not at the expense of anyone else’s safety or privacy. Our goal is to build a community where everyone feels welcome and free to share their ideas and creativity. While constructive disagreements can happen, bullying or harassment is unacceptable. If you’re facing or witness harassment or bullying on Patreon, here’s what you can do:

  • Understand Our Guidelines: Visit our Community Guidelines to learn more about our philosophy. In short, safety is our top priority. As our Harassment and Hate Speech policies detail, we promote inclusivity on Patreon. We have zero tolerance for bullying, dogpiling, doxxing, non-consensual intimate imagery, swatting, or the threatening or inciting of violence.
  • Collect Evidence: Collect as much evidence as possible (e.g. screenshots, URLs, etc.). For videos, we recommend including a timestamp indicating where in the footage the harm occurred; including a transcript of the segment, if available, is helpful as well. This sort of documentation is crucial for Patreon’s Trust & Safety Team to assess the situation and take appropriate action.
  • Report the Incident: Once you’ve collected your evidence, submit a report. Reporting helps us keep the community safe. If we confirm that a violation of guidelines has occurred, we will take appropriate action; however, details of our decision may not be shared with you.
  • Limit Communication: While you should limit your communication with the abuser, don’t be afraid to ask them clearly to stop contacting or mentioning you.
  • Block the Abuser: After asking them to stop, block their account if possible. Ignoring attacks can lead bullies to lose interest if they don’t get the reaction they want.
  • Contact Authorities if Threatened: If you fear for your safety at any point, contact local authorities and file a police report.
  • Seek Support: Talk to a friend or someone you trust. You are not alone.

By following these steps, you can help maintain a safe and supportive environment for everyone on Patreon.

I grant Patreon a license to do what with my creations?

A common and entirely legitimate concern sometimes comes up around the license that creators grant Patreon with regards to Patreon’s use of their creations. Specifically, this portion of our Terms:

Patreon is a creator-founded company that understands completely the importance of retaining ownership over your creations. Creators should be downright skeptical of any agreement that seeks to share in or transfer any portion of ownership in your creations. We are definitely not attempting to claim any sort of ownership or control over your creations.

Instead, this section is to ensure that Patreon has all necessary permission to, for example, host, resize, and display creators’ creations worldwide. Like we say in the text, “you keep full ownership over your creations and what you post on Patreon; we are not buying your intellectual property rights or leasing them from you for our gain. We will never try to steal your creations, use them in an exploitative way, or seek to profit off of them by any means other than facilitating memberships and offerings you’ve configured on Patreon.”

The state of copyright law requires us to receive a comprehensive license in order to operate Patreon’s services, including hosting your creations, providing and promoting memberships to your patrons, and enabling community features like post comments. Otherwise, we could risk liability for doing any number of normal things. If you review the terms of use for other hosting sites, you will find very similar licenses.

As to why we have specific parts of the license provision, please see some examples below:

  • royalty-free - you can’t ask us to pay you now or in the future for us having copies of the creations you’ve uploaded to Patreon. Of course, you will be paid for your memberships and other offerings on Patreon.
  • perpetual - once you post a creation on Patreon, we are not liable for infringement if a copy of it remains in our system even after you delete it.
  • irrevocable - you can’t post a creation, then change your mind and ask us to remove all copies of it from our system or face liability for infringement.
  • non-exclusive - this is to ensure you can license your creations to anyone else you want to license them to.
  • sublicensable - we use all kinds of third party services to host creations and operate our services. For example, Amazon Web Services (AWS) hosts most of our data and we need to be able to sublicense the right to host your creations so they are protected from liability.
  • worldwide - Patreon is available in most of the world and so we need to be able to show your creations to patrons around the world.
  • translate - patrons speak many languages, but creations are typically in only a single language. We need to be able to translate your creations to help show them to patrons.
  • copy, reproduce, store - we can make multiple copies of your creations and store them.
  • use, transmit, distribute, perform, publicly display - these cover different steps taken for, and forms of, showing your creations to patrons.
  • prepare derivative works - something as simple as resizing an image may create a derivative work. To functionally run a service like Patreon there are tons of things that we do to slightly alter creations in various ways.
  • display in connection with any name, username, voice, or likeness provided in connection with your creations - this covers us associating you with your creations when they are shown to patrons.

We hope this article allays any fear or concern that that section of our terms may have caused. If you have further questions or concerns, please contact us here.

ID verification troubleshooting tips

If you are having trouble verifying your government ID, please try resubmitting your government ID from your Notifications page using the best practices below:

  • Use only valid, non-expired government-issued identification showing full name, birth date, and photo (like a license, passport, or national ID)
  • If the original government-issued identification does not work, you can also attempt to use another as long as it clearly shows your full name, birth date, and photo
  • If you are using your phone, please make sure you’re using the latest version of the Patreon app and that your device is running the latest software available
  • Alternatively, you can use your preferred browser to submit your ID by going to patreon.com and completing the process there with your webcam (or try using your mobile browser and phone camera)
  • Make sure to take photos in a room with good lighting, and try to avoid any shadows or glare covering parts of your ID document

I’m trying to launch my Patreon. Why is my account under review?

As part of our commitment to providing a safe platform for creators and members, our Trust & Safety team will review your content to ensure it’s within our Community Guidelines before you launch. Learn more about our Community Guidelines.

During the review process, you will not be able to edit or make changes to your Patreon.

After reviewing your content, a member of our Trust & Safety team will inform you whether or not you can launch your Patreon. If some of the content is outside our Community Guidelines, a Trust & Safety representative will work directly with you to update your content to remove anything in violation of our policies. Once your Patreon is within our guidelines, you will be approved to launch.

Once you launch, your membership page will be publicly visible, and you can start making posts and promoting your Patreon.

Learn more about building and launching your Patreon in our guide on how to get started as a creator.

Making sure you are GDPR compliant with Patreon WordPress

Ensuring you are GDPR compliant with Patreon WordPress is fairly simple. Follow the steps below to ensure you’re up-to-date:

  • Make sure you have at least WordPress 4.9.6 running at your site. If not, upgrade it to the latest version.
  • Visit Settings > Privacy section in your WordPress admin.
  • You will find that you can create a privacy policy page, if you haven’t already created one. If you haven’t created a privacy policy page before, just click the Create New Page button to create a privacy policy page automatically.
  • Visit this URL in your website: http://<domain.com>/wp-admin/tools.php?wp-privacy-policy-guide=1
  • Replace domain.com with your website domain. Remember to include a subfolder if your site’s URL is structured like this: domain.com
  • On this page you will find any recommendations from WordPress, or any of the plugins you are using, for adding to your privacy policy. If you haven’t already done this, add any necessary sections to your privacy page. This will ensure any of your plugins, including Patreon WordPress, have higher GDPR compatibility.
  • Scroll down to find the section related to Patreon WordPress, as in “Source: Patreon WordPress”.
  • Click Copy button at the end of this section to copy Patreon WordPress related information, and then paste it to a proper place in your privacy page (either newly created or the existing one you have) and save your privacy page content.

Along with the new GDPR tools in WordPress 4.9.6+, which allow you to export and delete user data as necessary, this makes you GDPR compliant.
