Mid-year 2026 developments from Patreon’s policy team

As part of Patreon’s Creator Policy Engagement Program (CPEP), we regularly share proposed updates to our platform guidelines early and gather input directly from creators to help refine and improve them. Today, we’re happy to share the mid-year 2026 CPEP update.

Join the Policy Team for a livestream next week

Join members of Patreon’s Policy Team, including VP of Trust & Safety Eric Han, for a live policy discussion and Q&A on Thursday, July 16, at 9-10am PT / 12-1pm ET / 4-5pm BST.

RSVP here

This event will take place in English. Can’t make it live? Everyone who RSVPs will receive a link to watch the on-demand recording after the event. At the livestream, the team will walk through each of the below proposed updates in detail.

We’ve heard from creators that you want even more time dedicated to answering your questions, so we’re experimenting with the format this cycle. Rather than opening the floor to live questions asked during the event, we’ll spend that time working through questions submitted in advance via the RSVP form or by emailing CreatorPolicy@Patreon.com ahead of time, so we can get to as many as possible and address them thoroughly. And to make sure any questions that arise during the event itself also get answered, we’re doubling the duration of our Q&A in our Patreon Creator Community Discord server, keeping it open for two weeks instead of one.

Below is a preview of what we’ll be discussing. We hope you can join!

Proposed guidelines updates for creator feedback

The proposals below reflect our ongoing commitment to keeping Patreon’s Community Guidelines clear, accurate, and aligned with how our community and the broader industry think and talk about these issues. Since our last CPEP cycle in December, Patreon announced the launch of its network, so we’re continuing to update our guidelines to address the evolving features and keep pace with the increase in public posts on our platform. These are proposals to be finalized once we’ve previewed them and heard from you.

Hate Speech

We’re proposing updates to the Hate Speech section of Patreon’s Community Guidelines to make our language more precise. That includes expanding our language to better cover the types of hate speech and behaviors we do not permit on Patreon. These updates are not a departure from our existing stance; Patreon has zero tolerance for hate speech, and that is not changing. This is about being clearer and more accurate in how we describe what we prohibit and why. For example, we’re adding language around behaviors like using symbols and coded terminology to promote hateful ideologies, and we’re getting our language up to the standard creators and our peers would expect.

Harassment

The proposed updates to the Harassment section focus on language cleanup and precision — particularly around bullying, sexual harassment, and threats. We’re further clarifying that Patreon takes threats and expressions of harm seriously regardless of whether they are credible, and that targeting someone’s physical safety is never acceptable on our platform. We’re also proposing to add clearer language around bullying and sexual harassment, including language that addresses abuse of Patreon’s social and community features to engage in targeted bullying or unwanted sexual contact. The goal is to update policy language to be crisper, more specific, and more predictable in how it’s applied.

Inauthentic Behavior

We’re proposing updates to the Inauthentic Behavior guidelines section to bring greater precision to this section and better align it with industry best practices. That includes addressing malicious and deceptive behavior: things like phishing, malware distribution, coordinated scam activity, and more. The goal is a section that more accurately captures the behaviors we prohibit and gives creators a clearer picture of what isn’t tolerated on Patreon.

Transparency Report 2026

In April, we published Patreon’s third annual Transparency Report, covering calendar year 2025. It offers a detailed look at how we enforce our policies, respond to legal requests, and uphold platform integrity — and it’s an important part of how we hold ourselves accountable to the creators and fans who rely on Patreon. If you haven’t had a chance to read it, we’d encourage you to.

Advocating for creators in public policy conversations

Patreon’s policy work doesn’t stop at our guidelines. This year, our team has been active in external forums where decisions about the creator economy and internet regulation get made.

In March, Patreon attended Internet Works’ annual Hill Day in Washington, D.C., meeting with congressional offices on issues that directly affect creators and the platforms they build on. Internet Works is a coalition of 28 mid-sized tech companies working to ensure that platforms of our size have a voice in regulatory discussions.

Also in March, Courtney traveled to Dublin for Middle Tech Europe’s annual fly-in, where Patreon and fellow coalition members engaged directly with EU policymakers on the Digital Services Act and related regulatory developments. The EU regulatory landscape has real implications for how Patreon operates globally, and being in those conversations, rather than reacting to the outcomes after the fact, matters.

In June, Patreon took part in the first-ever Creator Economy Showcase on Capitol Hill, hosted by the United States’ Congressional Creators Caucus, co-chaired by Reps. Yvette D. Clarke (D-NY) and Beth Van Duyne (R-TX). Patreon has been a founding supporter of the Caucus since its launch in 2025. We invited multiple creators to attend the showcase and had one of the most popular tables in the room. Courtney attended on Patreon’s behalf alongside three Patreon creators — Sara and Lucinda from Color Class and Miguel from mz4250 — who engaged directly with members of Congress and their staff. Patreon was also asked to contribute a quote to the official congressional press release for the event.

How to share your feedback

We’re excited to hear what you think about these proposed updates, creators; your input is what makes this process work. Here’s how to participate:

  • Join the livestream on July 16: RSVP here to attend live and/or receive the link to the on-demand recording afterward.
  • Join the post-event Q&A in the #policy-qa channel in Patreon’s Creator Community Discord, open for two weeks following the event.
  • Email the Policy Team at CreatorPolicy@Patreon.com.

Thank you for your ongoing feedback and partnership, and hope to see you on July 16!

My creator account has been suspended. What should I do?

Patreon’s Community Guidelines act as the guardrails detailing the sorts of behaviors that are permitted and prohibited on Patreon. As a creator, your account may be suspended by the Trust & Safety team if it features frequent or severe violations of those guidelines.

How will I be notified that my Patreon page has been suspended?

If your creator account is suspended, our Trust & Safety team will send a message to the email address associated with your Patreon account. You will also see a banner at the top of your page when you log in. We encourage you to consult our Community Guidelines to understand the violation(s) on your Patreon.

Can I make other changes to my page in the meantime?

While you work with Trust & Safety to make any changes needed for your suspended page to comply with our guidelines, you retain the ability to edit, create and delete posts, change your benefits, and message your fans. However, during this period, your members will not be notified when you publish a new post and your page will not show up in search.

Should I inform my fans that my page has been suspended?

We recommend that you inform your fans about your account suspension by publishing a new post. You will be unable to send DMs, post comments, or participate in chats while your account is suspended.

What happens to my pledges, my fans and my funds?

While your creator account is suspended, your existing members are not billed, and fans are unable to become new members. When the account suspension is lifted, existing members whose bills were scheduled within the previous seven days are then billed. If the creator under suspension is also a member supporting other creators on Patreon, their member pledges will continue to be processed during the suspension.

Am I able to process a payout while my creator account is suspended?

If your creator account is suspended due to a violation of Patreon’s guidelines, you won’t be able to process a payout.

Can I appeal the Trust & Safety decision?

If you believe that no violation occurred, you can reply to the email notification from Trust & Safety with additional evidence supporting your claim and your case will get another look from a member of the team.

My page has been taken down, what can I do?

Patreon’s Trust & Safety team takes reports of guidelines violations very seriously and treats each case with individual care. Whether you’re a creator or member, if you receive an email from the team that your Patreon account has been removed, you can submit an appeal.

How to submit an appeal

When the Trust & Safety team removes your account, you have six months to appeal that decision. Here is how to file an appeal:

  • Visit the removal appeal form in our Help Center
  • Select My account was removed for a Community Guidelines violation
  • Select the Community Guidelines violation that led to the removal. The violation(s) are always listed in the removal notice you received by email
  • Input the email address associated with your Patreon account that was removed
  • Under Description, detail your reasoning for filing the appeal
  • Attach any supplemental evidence to support your appeal claim
  • Click Submit

What happens to funds in a removed account?

Funds that had not been transferred off the account prior to removal will be placed on hold for up to 28 days while Patreon reviews and makes a decision on the appeal. This ensures that the process is carefully analyzed before any funds are released or further action is taken.

My work is being stolen!

By enabling creators to instantaneously share their work with fans around the world, the modern internet represents a boon for creative professionals and is helping usher in the second renaissance. But quick-and-easy content distribution has its downsides; namely, it’s never been easier to pirate digital creative work.

As a creator, it’s troubling to see your work being used online without your permission. But there are tools and strategies you can deploy to help keep your content safe and under your control.

Start With an Informal Dialogue

When you see your work being used online without your permission, we recommend, as a first step, opening a dialogue to attempt to reach a direct resolution. Not everyone knows about IP laws, and people often share copyrighted material without knowing they’ve done anything wrong. When “piracy” turns out to be an honest mistake, a friendly message identifying yourself as the rights holder and requesting that the content be removed may be enough to solve the problem.

When Diplomacy Fails…

If an informal resolution isn’t possible, it’s time to consider your other options. In the U.S., creators can take advantage of the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (or “DMCA”). The DMCA established a notice-and-takedown procedure, whereby rights holders can contact internet platforms to request pirated content be removed (this is commonly known as a “DMCA takedown request”, or more formally, a “notification of claimed copyright infringement”).

It’s important to note that a compliant DMCA takedown request requires you – the rights holder – to provide your full contact information. The receiving party – the host platform – has no obligation to keep this information confidential, and will often share the takedown request, including your personal information, with the alleged infringer or even the general public. If you’re concerned about sharing your information, consider hiring an agent, such as an attorney, to send the takedown request on your behalf.

Community Building Can Buffer Against Piracy

There are also steps you can take to proactively safeguard your content from piracy. By offering your fans easy, reliable, and meaningful access to your work – for instance, by maintaining a Patreon creator account – you’re disincentivizing theft and incentivizing would-be pirates to become legitimate members.

For information on how to properly set up and manage your Patreon creator account, check out the Help Center resources found here.

Indeed, forming a direct and meaningful connection with your members humanizes you as a creative professional and helps dispel the common myth that piracy is a victimless crime. Offering members a glimpse into your creative process and showing the time and effort you put into your work also demonstrates the inherent value of your creative output and reinforces the idea that your content is worth purchasing.

Protecting Your Work with Private RSS Links (For podcasters)

If you share your work via private RSS links, it’s important to understand Patreon will help safeguard your content. Private RSS links are unique to each member, and we monitor how many devices and/or podcast apps are using the same link. If usage numbers are higher than usual, it may indicate that a member is sharing their link with others.

To protect your work, we automatically reset any link that appears to have been shared by a member, so anyone else using it loses access. If this happens a second time, the member suspected of sharing their link will have their comment and DM privileges suspended for 7 days. Continued unusual activity will prompt our Trust and Safety team to take further action to ensure your content remains secure.

Patreon Experiments

To help creators connect with more fans and grow their membership community, we’re always experimenting and testing new ways for creators, like yourself, to grow their Patreon brand and membership. Much like creativity itself, testing new ideas takes time and repeated versions until we reach a final product. If you’re curious, here’s how we approach experimentation at Patreon.

What are experiments?

An experiment is when we release a product, feature, or design to a subset of our community to see how it affects their experience. By limiting the experience to some, we can compare this experience to our wider community and measure impact, so that we can be sure that what we’re building will help creators grow.

Experiments are part of the core building process at Patreon. They are responsible for informing the data to make decisions when we develop products. We look across the funnel for areas where we can improve- starting with how creators can get more audience to their page, to getting more fans to successfully pledge, helping members discover and activate their benefits, as well as what tools and insights can help maintain a healthy community.

We are always listening to feedback from our creators and experiments are a way for us to test our different approaches to many of the challenges that creators have shared with us. If you’d like to share specific feedback or a product request, you can learn how to do so here.

Who participates in experiments?

Participation in experiments depends on the nature of the experiment and product areas that we are testing. Typically, we randomly select participants to remove bias. We consider a variety of enrollment factors such as the size of the testing group, the time period the experiment is run, and various other audience criteria.

On some occasions, creators will have the opportunity to sign up and participate in experiments that are in the early stages of product development. Creators will be notified of these opportunities either in-product or via email. Be sure to opt-in to receiving communications from Patreon, which you can check to see in your email notification settings here.

How we test

  • Start with principles. Principles serve as a guide for how we set up and conduct experiments, and as an anchor for what values we want to embody.
    • Example: One of our guiding principles is always to be creator first, and so our goals and hypotheses should ladder up.
  • Identify goals. In this case, we want to help turn more page visitors into members, and keep more members subscribing past their first month. Based on past research and data (including the feature request form, community conversations, support tickets, surveys, research studies, and more), we form ideas for how we could achieve just that.
    • Example: We’d like to help video creators get more fans to become members.
  • Form and test hypotheses. A hypothesis is an assumption that we can test.
    • Example: If creators could tease fans with snippets of their video posts, more fans would become members after they preview that content.
  • We then test the hypothesis “in the wild” for a portion of potential members. Throughout the test, we monitor both metrics we want to change (for example, whether there’s an increase in the percentage of visitors to your page who sign up) and related metrics to ensure the test doesn’t have unintended side effects.
  • Review results and observations. Once we’ve collected enough data, we analyze whether we can confidently attribute the results to the specific changes we tested, rather than pure chance. Sometimes the data confirms what we were thinking. Other times, it surprises us with an unexpected insight.
    • Example: How effective are video previews at converting fans to members? How does that differ on-platform vs off-platform? How often do creators promote their video previews?
  • Iterate based on what we’ve learned. If a test is inconclusive or unsuccessful, we’ll refine what we’re testing. We could use a different layout, wording, or color, or go back to the drawing board. If the results look promising, we could expand the test to a wider audience. Once we have confidence that what we’re testing will benefit the majority of creators, we’ll roll it out.

FAQ

  • It varies. Experiment durations depend on the size of the audience required to get unbiased results. We need to run experiments long enough to have confidence in the results and be sure that they are not due to chance. Depending on the product surface areas and audience eligibility, some experiments may take longer to gain traffic than others.
  • Typically, experiment participation is chosen at random and individuals will remain in the experiment to ensure unbiased results. In some scenarios, creators will be invited to participate in the early stages of the experiment which allows for more flexibility.
  • Because we run tests of all kinds every day to constantly iterate our product, not every experiment will notify creators ahead of time. In some cases, we may notify creators based on their participation eligibility to inform them of recommended actions to take ahead of the experiment. Most of the time, creators, fans, and members won’t know that they’re part of an experiment to eliminate bias.
  • If the feedback and insights we receive on the experiment are positive, we’ll make the changes live beyond our testing groups. For any new products, designs, or features, we will notify creators either in-product or via mobile or email notification. Be sure to opt-in to Patreon’s product newsletter, and join our official Patreon Creator Community Discord server to follow our #patreon-announcements channel.

Patreon Page Vanity Policy

At Patreon, we recognize the important role that a unique campaign vanity and page URL plays in a creator’s brand. Vanities help creators engage with their audience, grow their online presence, and drive their creative business forward. This policy outlines how Patreon manages campaign vanities to ensure fairness, consistency, and accountability, while promoting the continued growth of our platform and community.

Disputes and Vanity Reassignments

From time to time, a dispute may arise when a prospective creator seeks to claim a vanity that’s already in use by another creator. In such cases, Patreon will evaluate the situation thoroughly and thoughtfully. If a current creator is actively using a vanity, we will consider their engagement on Patreon and their broader off-platform brand presence in our decision-making. Vanities from inactive or underutilized Patreon accounts may be reassigned, pending our review.

If Patreon determines that reassigning a vanity will benefit the platform and community, we will do so in a way that prioritizes fairness and transparency. We will notify the impacted creator ahead of time. On a case-by-case basis, we will consider additional ways to mitigate harm to a creator’s earnings and community when their vanity has been reassigned.

Our Commitment to Fairness

At Patreon, we are committed to ensuring that vanity assignments are handled fairly, transparently, and in a way that supports the growth of our community. We aim to provide creators with the tools they need to succeed while maintaining a level playing field for all.

If you have any questions or concerns about this policy or your vanity, please don’t hesitate to contact Patreon Product Support for assistance.

Patreon’s refund policy

Overview

Our refund policy outlines how fans who have made purchases through Patreon can seek refunds and how creators should accommodate refund requests.

Fans and creators are responsible for complying with all applicable local laws related to product returns and refunds.

How to request a refund

Purchases made through the web

Fans can go to their Billing History and select the payment they’d like refunded. They must request a refund within 60 days of the original payment. Note that per-creation charges can’t be refunded through Billing History.

If they are outside this window or need a refund for a per-creation charge, they will be directed to contact Patreon Product Support. They should provide documentation showing that products, services, or benefits were not delivered within the agreed-upon timelines. Patreon will investigate the refund claim and determine whether to award or deny the refund. If Patreon finds it in the fan’s favor, the refund amount will be deducted from the creator’s account balance.

Creators may appeal this decision by contacting Patreon Product Support and are encouraged to provide documentation showing that products, services, or benefits were delivered and received by the fan within the agreed-upon timelines.

For the safety of our creators and platform, excessive or fraudulent refund claims may result in denied refunds, Patreon removing account access, or other action. In some instances, it may take up to 28 days for a refund to be issued. Be aware that all decisions on fan refund claims are made at Patreon’s sole discretion.

Purchases made through Apple iOS In-App Purchases (IAP)

For purchases made through Apple’s IAP functionality, fans should request a refund through Apple.

Customers can request a refund from Apple via reportaproblem.apple.com. Apple will handle the refund on the creator’s behalf and communicate with the customer on the status of the refund. If the refund is granted, funds will be issued back to the fan’s Apple account.

If the refund is approved, customers will get a full refund for the entire purchase amount.

How to issue a refund

Creators should accommodate refunds that meet the guidelines found in this policy. For more details, see our dedicated article on How to manage refunds for your fans.

What scenarios qualify for a refund?

The following situations and scenarios may qualify for a refund. The refunded amount includes the purchase price, as well as any fees or taxes collected during the transaction.

General Refund Scenarios:
  • Technical errors caused by Patreon
  • Item not received (creators should clearly state the delivery window for the product, service, or benefit and communicate with the fan if the delivery window needs to be adjusted)
  • Product mismatch (the item received differs significantly and in an easily visible way from the item promised in either appearance, performance, or quality)
  • Creator provided a refund for the prior month, but the fan forgot to cancel the membership
  • Creator suspended/removed from Patreon within a week of receiving a pledge or order
  • Creator violates Patreon’s policies on harassment and abuse of fans
  • Fan blocked before receiving rewards
  • Fan canceled membership renewal, but charge still occurred
  • Fan did not access any content & canceled membership within 48 hours
  • Currency issues (e.g., a Mexican fan who believed a pledge was 399 pesos, not $399 [*creator should state that billing will be in local currency and not USD])
  • Creator and/or fan death
Digital Commerce Refund Scenarios:
  • Creator deletes a product (Buyer loses access to purchased content)
  • Creator deletes a campaign (Buyer loses access to purchased content)
  • Creator Un-Launches Campaign (Buyer sees “product currently unavailable”)
  • Patreon deletes a previously purchased product for violating Patreon’s policies
  • Patreon deletes a campaign with a grace period (Buyers have access during a 28-day grace period, after which they lose access)
  • Patreon immediately deletes a campaign (Buyers immediately lose access to products)
  • Patreon suspends a product (Buyers see “temporarily unavailable” message)
  • Patreon suspends a campaign (Buyers see “temporarily unavailable” message)

What doesn’t qualify for a refund?

The following situations and scenarios do not qualify for a refund:

General
  • Items where the purchase or exchange of a product, service, or benefit happens off of Patreon’s platform
  • Orders that have already been refunded or charged back/disputed by the fan’s or creator’s bank
  • Damage that occurs to items after they are delivered
Digital Commerce
  • Creator switches from 18+ to All Ages
  • Creator Hides Product (Buyer continues to have access to purchased content)

When does Patreon process payments for memberships?

The date and time that your payment processes depend on the billing schedule the creator has selected. Below are the billing dates and times you can expect for each of our billing options:

Creator’s billing schedule

Payment date and time

Subscription billing

Your renewal payment processes on your join date on UTC. Please note that you may be charged up to 24 hours beforehand due to time zone differences.

1st of the month (charge upfront)

Your renewal payment processes on the 1st of each month on PT for the month of access.

1st of the month (non-charge upfront)

Your renewal payment processes on the 1st of each month on PT for any access you had the previous month.

Per creation

You’ll typically pay on the 1st of each month on PT for paid posts published the previous month. If you cancel your membership before the 1st of the month, we’ll trigger your last payment process on that date.

Annual membership

  • If the creator uses subscription billing, your renewal payment will process yearly on your join date on UTC and on that date every year until canceled.
  • If the creator uses 1st of the month (charge upfront) billing, your renewal payment will process yearly on the 1st of the month on PT, a year after the initial join date, and on that date every year until canceled.

Want to learn more about what to expect depending on your creator’s billing schedule? Visit our guide, How membership billing works to learn more.

Payment Processors’ Adult/18+ Requirements: An Overview

Payment Processors’ Adult/18+ Requirements: An Overview

Payment processing partners like Mastercard and Visa have implemented two new requirements for Adult/18+ creators and platforms like Patreon that host Adult/18+ content:

  • Age Verification
  • Consent Documentation
REQUIREMENT 1: AGE VERIFICATION

This is a summary of the Age Verification requirement. For greater detail into the process, including measures we’re taking to ensure privacy, security, and inclusion, check out this frequently asked questions article in our Help Center.

Payment processors require Patreon to verify the identifications of Adult/18+ content creators to ensure the creators are over 18. The requirement specifically applies to creators in the Adult/18+ category (in other words, those whose pages include one or more works containing sexually explicit content or nudity). If you’re in the Adult/18+ category, but your page contains no sexually explicit content or nudity — or if you choose to remove any such content — you are eligible to opt out of Age Verification by recategorizing from “Adult/18+” to “Safe for All Audiences.” Here’s how you can do that.

You can read more about this in the Age Verification FAQ article in our Help Center.

REQUIREMENT 2: CONSENT DOCUMENTATION

Payment processing partners require Patreon to ensure that creators in the Adult/18+ category obtain written consent from real humans who participate in their creative works by being featured visually.

What does securing Consent Documentation entail?

To meet this requirement, Adult/18+ creators whose works visually feature real human participants other than themselves should document participant consent using this template, which Patreon translated into 18 languages for convenience.

Do we have to use the template form provided by Patreon, or will a general one do?

Although you are not required to use this specific template, we developed it to make creators’ lives easier and help you better meet payment partner requirements. If you choose to use a different form, please ensure that it contains at least the same information

Once I document participant consent per the requirement, do I submit the document somewhere or retain it myself?

You should retain all participant consent documentation indefinitely. Upon request from a payment partner, Patreon may ask Adult/18+ creators to provide this documentation, which would then be shared with the requesting payment partner to demonstrate compliance with their rules.

Report content that violates community guidelines

Patreon’s Community Guidelines act as the guardrails detailing the sorts of behaviors that are permitted and prohibited on Patreon. We encourage you to review these guidelines and report any violations you encounter to help keep our community safe. We review and resolve reports within five business days.

To report a creator or member for a guidelines violation:

  • Log in to your Patreon account and go to their Patreon page. From there, find the **more button (“…” 3 dots), which will present the option to report them.
  • You can also find the reporting tool on any creator’s post or member’s comment or message by clicking on the “…” button and selecting Report this content.

Gather and submit as much evidence as possible (e.g. screenshots, URLs, etc.) for the report. For videos, we recommend including a timestamp indicating where in the footage the violation occurred; including a transcript of the segment, if available, is helpful as well. This sort of documentation is crucial for Patreon’s Trust & Safety Team to assess the situation and take action if appropriate.

Note that the evidence you include in your report should be tied directly to the person you are reporting. For example, Patreon would not remove a creator based on the violative action of a fan unless the creator incited that behavior.

If we confirm that a guidelines violation has occurred, we will take appropriate action; however, details of our decision may not be shared with you. If there is evidence of illegal or non-compliant content, it will be removed immediately.

Sanctions Policy

At Patreon, we are committed to upholding global regulatory standards, particularly in adhering to economic sanctions and trade restrictions set forth by authoritative bodies such as the Office of Foreign Assets Control (“OFAC”) within the U.S. Department of the Treasury. As a U.S.-based company with international operations, it is imperative that we ensure compliance with these regulations to maintain ethical and legal integrity.

Regardless of your geographical location, our sanctions policy applies universally to all members. When creating or updating your Patreon account or page, it is essential to provide accurate information about yourself and your country of residence. Failure to do so may lead to the termination of your account or page.

In accordance with our commitment to compliance, we observe restrictions on transactions involving:

  • Certain countries, including Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, and specific regions such as Crimea, the Donetsk People’s Republic (DNR), and Luhansk People’s Republic (LNR), along with any individuals or entities operating or residing therein
  • Individuals or entities listed on sanctions rosters, such as OFAC’s Specially Designated Nationals (“SDN”) List or the Foreign Sanctions Evaders (“FSE”) List

To safeguard our community and ensure adherence to these regulations, we undertake various measures, including:

  • Prohibiting access to Patreon from certain geographic locations
  • Restricting creators from offering benefits originating from sanctioned areas
  • Requesting additional information or actions from users to facilitate compliance

Should we suspect any violation of economic sanctions or trade restrictions, including operating an account from a sanctioned location or benefiting sanctioned entities, we reserve the right to suspend, terminate, or take appropriate action on the account.

Furthermore, it is important to note that different countries may impose additional trade restrictions, and certain items may be subject to export or import prohibitions under international laws. Members engaging in transactions with international parties should familiarize themselves with relevant jurisdictional laws. For legal counsel, consulting a qualified professional is recommended.

Additionally, our payment partners, such as PayPal, Visa, and Mastercard, independently monitor financial transactions for sanctions compliance and may block transactions as part of their own compliance protocols. Please be aware that Patreon does not influence or control the decisions made by these providers.

Given the dynamic nature of economic sanctions and trade restrictions, updates may occur frequently, potentially impacting our ability to engage with members or imposing additional restrictions on benefits. We encourage members to stay informed by referring to relevant resources provided by authoritative bodies, including the US Department of the Treasury, Bureau of Industry and Security at the US Department of Commerce, Department of State, and the European Commission.

For further guidance or inquiries, please do not hesitate to reach out to our Creator Success team. We appreciate your cooperation in maintaining a compliant and responsible community at Patreon.

Security Research & Reporting Security Vulnerabilities

We are committed to protecting the security of members and creators by addressing security issues responsibly and in a timely manner.

If you’re a security expert or researcher and believe you have discovered a security-related issue with Patreon, we appreciate your help in disclosing the issue to us responsibly.

We require that you:

  • Use our Security Policy page for further instructions on how to submit bug reports. Security researchers must include detailed information, along with clear steps, to enable us to reproduce the vulnerability.
  • Give us a reasonable amount of time to respond to the issue before making any information about it public.
  • Refrain from:
    • Accessing or modifying user information without the permission of the account owner.
    • Exposing other users to vulnerabilities. All testing should be done on your own user pages and only between accounts you control. This includes pledging to actual creators. If you need to test the pledging functionality, create a second test account and set it to “creator” status.
  • Act in good faith not to degrade the performance of our services (including denial of service).

Should my campaign be marked Safe for All Audiences or Adult/18+ and how do I recategorize?

We categorize Patreon campaigns as either “Safe for All Audiences” or “Adult/18+” because the payment processors we rely on to get creators paid require this distinction. This article details the differences between these categories and how to request a category change.

Differences Between Categories

The “Adult/18+” category is for pages with one or more works (audio, text, or visual, including depictions of human beings and animations) containing sexually explicit content and/or nudity. To comply with payment processor guidelines, these creators must complete a brief age verification process to ensure they are at least 18 years old.

In contrast, the “Safe for All Audiences” category is for campaigns with no works containing nudity or sexually explicit content. These pages are searchable on Patreon, and these creators do not need to complete the age verification requirement mentioned above.

How to Recategorize

From Safe for All Audiences to Adult/18+

Creators currently categorized as Safe for All Audiences who intend to add one or more works containing sexually explicit content and/or nudity should first follow this process to recategorize as Adult/18+.

  • Log in to Patreon.com and navigate to your Creator Page Editor
  • Click into Page settings from the top menu
  • Scroll to the Adult content section and check the box
From Adult/18+ to Safe for All Audiences

Creators currently categorized as Adult/18+, but whose campaigns contain no sexually explicit content or nudity, may choose to bypass age verification by recategorizing to Safe for All Audiences.

  • Click here to open a ticket with our support team
  • Select I have a question about Community Guidelines (English only) from the dropdown
  • Input the email address associated with your Patreon account
  • From the General Account Questions dropdown, select My account is incorrectly labeled as Adult Content
  • Add a Subject line and Description detailing your circumstances, for example:
    • Subject: Recategorizing my page to Safe for All Audiences
    • Description: My page is currently categorized as Adult/18+, but because it has no works containing nudity or sexually explicit content, I would like to recategorize it as Safe for All Audiences
  • You’ll then hear from a member of the Patreon support team with any next steps.

Spotting & preventing creator impersonation on Patreon

How to recognize scams, protect your fans, & what Patreon is doing to help

What’s happening?

Impersonation scams are common online, and creators can be targets given their direct connection with fans. For example, scammers may create fake member accounts that copy creator names & profile photos. These accounts leave comments on creator posts, often promoting fake giveaways, rewards, or investment opportunities, to trick fans into contacting them off-platform, typically via third-party messaging apps.

What should I watch for as a creator?

Be on the lookout for:

  • Display names or profile photos that resemble yours
  • Comments with messaging like:
    • “You’ve been selected for a giveaway…”
    • “For more guidance and tips…”
    • “For professional guidance to earn you maximum profits…”
    • “Message me on [a third-party messaging app]”

These are not legitimate messages. If you or your fans see something suspicious, don’t respond; report it instead.

What can I do to protect my community?

  • Let your fans know that you will never ask them to contact you via a third-party messaging app or other off-platform/private channels — especially not for giveaways, rewards, or financial offers.
  • Encourage them to report suspicious accounts by:
    • Clicking on the impersonator’s profile photo and using the built-in reporting option
    • Or submitting a report in our Help Center by selecting:
      • “I want to report suspicious activity”
      • “General” for the issue that best describes your situation, then “I want to report a fake/suspicious account”

To help us investigate quickly, please include:

  • The creator’s name being impersonated
  • A link to the post where the suspicious comment appears
  • A copy/paste or screenshot of the comment

Can I limit who comments on my posts?

Yes, you can adjust your page settings to restrict comments to paid members only. However, some scammers may purchase memberships to bypass these limits, so this setting alone may not fully prevent impersonation attempts. To learn more about limiting comments, visit our Comment settings guide

What is Patreon doing to keep my community safe?

We’re actively working to detect & remove impersonators and minimize their impact. Our efforts include:

  • Identifying & removing impersonator accounts
  • Blocking spammy comments & repeat offenders
  • Improving tools to detect impersonation patterns
  • Exploring bulk comment deletion tools & simpler reporting flows

These improvements are ongoing; our priority is making it easier for creators to keep their communities safe.

How do I report or escalate an issue?

If you think someone is impersonating you or scamming your members, please report the post or user directly — or submit a report through our Help Center.

We’re here to help.

Spotting Scam Emails: How to Recognize Suspicious Activity

If you received a suspicious email and aren’t sure if it’s coming from Patreon, here are a couple of ways you can check its legitimacy:

Is it promotional?

If someone offers you a service in exchange for money, it is a scam. We would never ask you to pay us money in exchange for promotional services. Below is an example of a real scam email that has been sent to creators in the past:

Are you being asked for sensitive information?

If you receive an email asking for your tax info, credit card number, or other private information, double-check that the email comes from a Patreon email domain:

  • @email.patreon.com
  • @patreon.com
  • @patreon.zendesk.com
  • @core.patreon.com
  • @info.patreon.com
  • @orders.patreon.com
  • @security.patreon.com
  • @safety.patreon.com
  • @creator.patreon.com
  • @community.patreon.com
  • @live.patreon.com
  • @updates.patreon.com

If the sender does not have a Patreon email address, DO NOT send over your personal information.

If you’re ever unsure if an email you received is a scam, you can start a chat to send us a message — If you’re using a mobile device, scroll down to the bottom of the article to find this button. Please attach a full-screen screenshot of the email you received so we can confirm the legitimacy of the email.

Suspended products

This article serves as a guide for creators selling digital products whose products may be suspended.

To keep Patreon safe for everyone, all products listed in your shop must meet our Community Guidelines and Commerce Guidelines. When products do not meet our guidelines, we may need to suspend them from your shop. This allows creators to keep their page up and running even while their product is in the reform process. Repeated instances of products not meeting our Community Guidelines may result in account suspension or removal.

What happens if my product is suspended?

When you view your shop, products that do not meet our Community Guidelines will be labeled as Suspended (only visible to you). Suspended products are not available for customers to purchase and won’t be available to customers who have already purchased the product. We’ll send you an email notification to the email associated with your Patreon account detailing the next steps.

How long can my product be suspended?

Products that do not meet our Community Guidelines may be suspended indefinitely; however, we encourage you to refer to the email correspondence with our team for detailed next steps.

I have a question about my suspended product

If you have any questions about our Community Guidelines or your specific product, please submit a ticket through our Help Center for additional support.

FAQ

  • A product may be suspended if it does not meet Community Guidelines. Refer to the email we have sent to the email address associated with your Patreon account for detailed next steps about your suspended product.
  • You can review our Community Guidelines for any clarification on why your product may have been suspended.
  • Suspended products do not impact your ability to interact with your customers or list new products. In most cases, suspended products will not impact your payouts either — you can still pay your balance out as you normally do.
  • It’s important to note that other products will not be suspended unless they do not meet Patreon’s Community Guidelines.
  • Suspended posts do not appear in your store and cannot be purchased by new customers. Customers who have already purchased the product will not be able to access it from their Purchases tab.

Suspicious activity on your account

If Patreon detects suspicious activity on your account, your creator balance payouts will be temporarily paused. However, you can continue using Patreon as usual during this review period.

To help keep creators safe, our Trust & Safety team manually reviews accounts when suspicious activity is flagged. During this time, you’ll still be able to post, engage with fans, and receive memberships—only payouts will be restricted. A member of our team will reach out to you directly with more information.

We understand that a payout delay can be disruptive, especially if you rely on those funds. If you need urgent help or believe the review is in error, please contact our Trust & Safety.

Understanding Patreon’s AI policies for Adult/18+ creators

Patreon allows creators to share AI-generated works, with different rules based on whether a page is categorized as Safe for All Audiences or Adult/18+. This distinction ensures compliance with Patreon policies, as well as requirements from payment partners. This article clarifies these policies, focusing specifically on the differences between hyperrealistic and illustrated/animated figures.

AI-generated works on Safe for All Audiences pages

If your account is categorized as Safe for All Audiences, AI-generated depictions of people are permitted as long as they do not contain nudity, sexual activity, or related adult/18+ material. These works must comply with Patreon’s Community Guidelines.

AI-generated works on Adult/18+ pages

TLDR: If your account is categorized as Adult/18+:

  • AI-generated depictions of people that are illustrated/animated are permitted
  • AI-generated hyperrealistic depictions of people are permitted only if the people are real and have documented their explicit consent (see “Age verification and consent documentation” for details)

As a reminder, all works on your page must comply with Patreon’s Sexually Gratifying Works policy and Patreon’s Community Guidelines broadly.

Distinctions between illustrated/animated and hyperrealistic AI

To help Adult/18+ creators distinguish between illustrated/animated and hyperrealistic AI-generated images, below you’ll find visual examples and descriptive characteristics.

What do we mean by “illustrated/animated?”

AI-generated works that are illustrated/animated deviate from reality in terms of visual representation; they present as distinct artistic interpretations rather than having the appearance of real-life photography. In practice, the depicted figures may have characteristics such as:

  • Stylized, exaggerated, or distorted features (e.g., anime-, comic-, or cartoon-style or aesthetics)
  • Flat or painterly appearance (e.g., visible brush strokes, less emphasis on intricate texture details)
What do we mean by “hyperrealistic?”

AI-generated depictions are considered hyperrealistic if the characters are highly detailed and lifelike; the appearance closely mimics a real human. These images typically include:

  • Three-dimensional composition (e.g., high resolution, intricate backgrounds, and foregrounds)
  • Anatomical consistency with a human (e.g., not part-robot or part-animal)
  • Mimicking natural lighting and movement
  • Detailed texture (e.g., visible skin pores, wrinkles, individual eyelashes, lifelike shadows)

As AI technology evolves, Patreon remains committed to ensuring its policies are clear, enforceable, and adaptable to new developments. If you have questions about how these guidelines apply to your works, we encourage you to review Patreon’s full Community Guidelines.

Understanding Patreon’s mobile app age rating

In November 2024, Patreon updated the age rating of its iOS app from 12+ to 17+ and its Android app from Teen to Mature (or the equivalent age rating in your region). Here’s what you need to know about why Patreon made this change, what it means, and answers to frequently asked questions.

We announced in August 2024 that Apple is requiring Patreon to use its in-app purchasing system for all transactions in the iOS app. With this update, Patreon needs to move to a 17+ age rating for the iOS app to help enable creators to be discoverable and able to earn within the app. This change helps creators to continue to earn on Patreon, regardless of their classification. We made this change for our Android app as well to ensure a consistent experience across apps.

What’s Not Changing

Patreon is not changing the types of work that are allowed. Rather, this change better reflects the type of work that we already allow. Similarly, all creators will still be required to follow Patreon’s Community Guidelines, which delineate what is and what is not allowed on Patreon.

What This Update Means

With this update, we’re making Patreon safer. With the mobile age rating updates, we’re aligning our mobile apps with device-level parental control settings. We’re also introducing a new member account setting that allows fans who are 18 and older to customize the visibility of Adult/18+ creators. You can learn more about that setting here.

We’re also expanding product access to more creators, including Adult/18+ classified creators. To learn more about your product access, go here.

FAQ

  • You must be 18 years or older to become a member of a creator that is classified as Adult/18+ or to discover Adult/18+ creators in search and explore.
  • By default, members with no active Adult/18+ memberships will not see Adult/18+ creators in the app. You can change these settings in your member Settings. If you have an active Adult/18+ membership, you will need to cancel the membership to turn off the Adult/18+ visibility toggle.
    • Using a web browser, go to your Settings
    • Scroll down to Adult creators
    • Toggle on the option to See 18+ creators
    • You’ll see a pop-up that asks you to confirm that you are 18 years or older
    • Once you confirm that you’re 18 years or older, you’ll be able to see Adult/18+ creators on Patreon. These creators will be shown with an 18+ badge
  • You may also update your settings when searching for creators:
    • At the top of search results, you’ll see 18+ creators are hidden. Show 18+ creators
    • Tap Show 18+ creators
    • After clicking, you’ll see a pop-up that asks you to confirm that you are over 18 years old
    • Once you confirm that you’re over 18 years old, you’ll be able to see Adult/18+ creators on Patreon. These creators will be shown with a specific 18+ badge

Updating our Hate Speech, Harassment, and Inauthentic Behavior Policies

Patreon’s Creator Policy Engagement Program (CPEP) exists to ensure that the people most impacted by our policies have early visibility into proposed changes and an open line of communication with the Policy Team before policies are finalized.

Earlier this summer, as part of CPEP, we hosted our mid-year Patreon Connect livestream with VP of Trust & Safety Eric Han and Head of Platform Policy Travis Reed. On it, we walked through a new set of proposed updates to Patreon’s Community Guidelines — focused on Hate Speech, Harassment, and Inauthentic Behavior. These changes are now live on our Community Guidelines page.

Here’s a rundown of what’s been updated, plus a look at a few other things happening across the Policy Team this year.

Updates to Hate Speech

Patreon has always had zero tolerance for hate speech. We’ve added more precise language in our Community Guidelines to better clarify the specific types of hate speech that are already prohibited.

Attacking people or groups of people on the basis of race is already treated as hate speech. However we decided to add the word “color” explicitly to the list of characteristics we consider when assessing if something is hate speech to make this more transparent. The full list of characteristics we consider now includes: caste, immigration status, national origin, race, color, ethnicity, religion, disability, serious medical condition, sex, gender identity, or sexual orientation.

We’ve clarified that stereotypes that vilify or incite fear, discrimination, or violence aren’t tolerated.

We expanded language to address hate-based claims of superiority or inferiority, so it’s explicit that claiming a group is inherently inferior or superior based on one or more of the characteristics listed in our Community Guidelines (see full list above) isn’t permitted.

New language was added addressing symbols and coded terminology used to promote hate, including memes, content trends, or coded terms used to promote hate movements or hateful ideas.

These updates were developed in consultation with outside experts, including researchers and NGOs who specialize in hate speech, and we’re grateful for their input.

Updates to Harassment

The Harassment updates are mostly about adding clarity and predictability around bullying, sexual harassment, and threats.

We specified that threats and expressions of harm are not allowed regardless of whether they’re a specific and credible threat.

We reinforced that our community features cannot be used for bullying or unwanted sexual contact, including repetitive unwanted comments or chats, targeted insults, and pages solely dedicated to ridiculing, shaming, or degrading other people.

We’ve separated Sexual Harassment into its own subsection in the policy language, making clear that abusing Patreon’s features to send unwanted or repeated sexual comments isn’t permitted—including but not limited to behaviors like “cyberflashing” and other non-consensual sexual exposure, as well as using abusive sexual language to silence people on the platform.

Updates to Inauthentic Behavior

We’ve made updates to bring more precision to this section and better align it with industry best practices. Now, we more directly address malicious and deceptive behavior like phishing, deceptive redirects, malware distribution, and coordinated scam activity in our Community Guidelines. In response to feedback we heard from creators, we also prohibit joining Patreon with the explicit goal of taking other creators’ works to train AI systems.

We’re really excited about all of these updates and believe they’ll continue to help make Patreon a safe and friendly space for creativity to flourish.

Looking Ahead

For the remainder of this year, we’ll be reviewing our guidelines on Harmful Acts, Violent and Graphic Works, and Hazardous Activities. These sections cover topics like depictions of suicide and self-harm, glorification of violence, and discussions of regulated goods and activities.

To support that work, we’ve engaged with external subject matter experts, and will continue to do so in the months ahead. We’ll likely share updates on these policies in the new year.

Gratitude

A big Thank You! to everyone who joined our mid-year Patreon Connect livestream, submitted questions ahead of time, or weighed in with feedback. Engaging with creators and fans is critical to balancing our policies and holding ourselves accountable.

What are Patreon’s Community Guidelines?

You can consult our Community Guidelines for more details.

If you are ever unsure of whether or not your activity on Patreon is within our Community Guidelines, please Select “I have a question about Community Guidelines” on this form and a Trust & Safety teammate will be happy to help you.

What information do third-party apps receive about my Patreon account?

Overview

When you log in with Patreon on a third-party app or website, they are granted access to information that you choose to share with them. For example, they could ask to be able to find your:

  • Membership amount to their creator page
  • Member profile information

In general, you will be required to allow access in order to use the app, since it relies on that data to function. Not all apps will require all of the above permissions.

How do I revoke account access from a third-party application?

You can revoke or remove an app’s access to your Patreon information at any time in your account settings, in the Logged in with Patreon section of the Connected apps tab.

Revoking (removing) access means that the app will no longer be able to review information about your Patreon account. In order to continue using the app, you will have to log in and grant them permission again. If the app works in the background (like an app that gets a list of your memberships every day, for instance), it will not work until you log back in.

Note: The app may still have the data you shared with them. For details about removing this data, please contact the app provider or visit their privacy policy.

For developers: A list of our API endpoints lives at docs.patreon.com

What to do when a creator is suspended

If a creator you support has been suspended, it means their content is temporarily unavailable while they work with our team to align with Patreon’s Community Guidelines. While suspensions are typically resolved within a few days, the timeline can vary depending on the updates needed. We understand this can be frustrating, and this article is here to help you navigate what this means for your membership, access to content, refunds, and next steps.

What is a suspension?

A suspension means a creator’s content is temporarily hidden because it doesn’t comply with Patreon’s Community Guidelines. Our Trust and Safety team reviews all reports thoroughly and works directly with creators to address the issue. The goal of a suspension is to give creators time to update their content while ensuring Patreon remains a safe and inclusive platform. While we can’t share specific details about a creator’s suspension, rest assured that these decisions are made thoughtfully and without bias.

What happens to my membership while a creator is suspended?

During a suspension, your membership remains active, but you won’t be able to access their content until the page is reinstated. This includes access to posts, videos, and any other perks tied to their Patreon page. Creators are encouraged to message their fans during this time to provide updates on the suspension and their plans for returning.

Will I receive a refund while a creator is suspended?

If your creator has been suspended, you might wonder about refunds for the time their content is unavailable. Refunds are managed directly by the creator, depending on their chosen payment cycle.

To request a refund, we recommend reaching out to the creator directly through Patreon messaging. If you encounter issues or have additional questions, you can also contact our support team for assistance. For more details, check out Patreon’s Refund Policy.

Can I cancel my membership?

Yes, you can cancel your membership at any time. Learn how to do so here. If the creator’s page is reinstated and you’d like to support their updated content, you can choose to renew your membership at any time.

What should I do if I believe the suspension is unfair?

Due to privacy concerns, we are unable to comment on a specific creator’s suspension. Rest assured that we apply our Community Guidelines equally to all creators.

Why wasn’t I notified about the suspension?

Patreon does not notify fans when a creator is suspended. Instead, we work directly with creators to help them update their content and return to the platform as quickly as possible. We encourage creators to keep their fans informed during the suspension and to notify them once their page is reinstated.

Why are similar creators not suspended?

Our Community Guidelines apply equally to all creators. If you believe another creator’s content violates our guidelines, you can report their page for review by following the steps outlined in this article.

Why are my comments disappearing?

Creators have the ability to disable comments on their posts. Learn more about disabled comments.

If a comment you left on a creator’s post has disappeared and you didn’t delete it yourself, there are a few possible reasons why it might have been removed.

Filtered comments

Creators can enable a feature called Comment filtering, which automatically hides comments that may be spammy or potentially harmful to the creator’s community. If you believe that your comments have been mistakenly filtered, you can direct message the creator to see if they can adjust their comment filtering settings.

Community Guidelines violations

Note that all comments should abide by Patreon’s Community Guidelines, which act as the guardrails detailing the sorts of behaviors that are permitted and prohibited on Patreon. Patreon’s Trust & Safety team reserves the right to remove comments that violate those policies.

The creator has disabled comments

Creators can retroactively disable comments. You may notice that comments are disabled on posts you had previously been able to comment on. If you see the message that “comments are disabled for this post,” it means that the creator has since disabled comments. If you see this message for all of the creator’s posts, it means that the creator has disabled comments on all of their posts.

The comment was removed by the creator

It is possible that the creator is moderating the comment section of their posts and determined that your comment should be removed. If you suspect this, you may be able to direct message the creators to learn more about the rules of engagement for their Patreon.

Learn more about direct messaging a creator

Why can’t I view or create adult content in my country?

As our global community of creators and fans continues to grow, we regularly review our Community Guidelines to ensure that they align with the laws and regulations for each region in which we operate.

While Patreon allows for certain categories of adult content on our site, we are unable to host adult content in certain regions where it is prohibited by local law.

What does this mean for me as a fan?

Fans located in a region where Adult/18+ works are regulated by local law will be prevented from supporting or consuming Adult/18+ works on Patreon.

What does this mean for me as a creator?

If you are a creator located in a region that prohibits Adult/18+ works, you will not be allowed to publish Adult/18+ works on Patreon. If your page is found to be in violation of Community Guidelines, our Trust & Safety team will contact you to resolve the matter.

Creators in these regions are required to confirm when creating their Patreon account that their works are not Adult/18+ in nature.

Why Doxing Is Not Allowed on Patreon

Creators and fans are empowered to express themselves on Patreon, though not at the expense of anyone else’s safety or privacy.

Doxxing is a form of harassment in which someone shares an individual’s personally identifiable information (e.g. home address, phone number, bank account information, medical information) online without consent. This abusive act can lead to on- and offline harms against the individual such as stalking, emotional distress, physical harm, job loss, and identity theft.

Patreon prohibits creators and fans on the platform from engaging in or encouraging doxxing.

Fortunately, the vast majority of creators and fans on Patreon don’t try to hurt other people through doxxing or similar abuse. Our Trust & Safety team takes a strong stance in those rare circumstances that someone does participate in doxxing on Patreon, because we know of the real-world harm it can cause.

You can read more about our policies on doxxing and related harms in our Community Guidelines.

Why is my account disabled under fraud suspicion?

There are many reasons why your account might have been flagged as potential fraud. Don’t worry, we are here to help you.

You will receive email notification and will also be alerted when trying to log in. If you believe your account has been disabled in error, please don’t hesitate to contact the Trust and Safety team.

Please be sure to completely answer the questionnaire sent to you by the Trust and Safety team. This includes:

  • Your name:
  • Location:
  • VerifyPayment/Payout Method:
  • Any services used for internet browsing:

When providing your payment/payout details please only provide the last four last digits of your card, this is for the security of your personal information.

General: Login and signup

Accidentally created a second Patreon account? How to fix it

Users sometimes log in with Google or Facebook and unknowingly create a second account. When that happens, you might lose access to member-only content while still being billed on the original account.

Important: We can’t merge accounts or move memberships between them.

What to do (quick steps)

  • Decide which account you’ll keep
  • Use the email on your Patreon receipts or the account where your current memberships live.
  • Log in to the account you won’t keep and delete it
  • Deleting an account immediately cancels any active memberships for that account (as a member or a creator)
  • Log in to the account you’re keeping and continue using that one going forward

Tip for creators: If you have multiple pages, you can unpublish a page instead of deleting your whole account. That way, you can keep your memberships active on your main account.

Before you delete

  • Let your creators know if access may change during the switch
  • Double-check which email you’re deleting to avoid canceling the wrong memberships
  • Use the same log-in method (email + password, or the same Google/Facebook account) from now on to prevent duplicates

How to delete your account

Follow the steps in: Delete your Patreon account

You must be able to access the email on the account you’re deleting.

Need help?

If you can’t access the email on the duplicate account, please complete our account recovery form, and a member of our Product Support team will follow up with you as soon as possible.

How do I change my email address?

You can only change your email to one that isn’t already in use with an existing Patreon account. The change will not stick if you attempt to switch to one that already exists.

How to update your Patreon account email address

  • While logged in, make sure you are on your member profile
  • Click Settings from the left navigation menu, which will take you to the Profiles basics page
  • Enter your new email address and scroll down to click the Save button
  • We’ll send a confirmation email to the new email you updated to. Please confirm with the emailed link to complete your change request
  • Once you’ve confirmed the change, your email has been successfully changed

You can log in with the updated email address. Additionally, all email notifications from us will be sent to your updated email address. If you do not confirm the email change, the change won’t go through. Your previous email will still be listed on your account and should be used for login.

If you can’t log in to your Patreon account or the email account we have on file, please contact our support team for assistance.

How to change my password

To follow the steps in this article, you need to be logged in and switched to your Member view. If you are having issues logging in, please check the Login Help article.

You cannot change your password on the Patreon app. Please visit the Patreon website to change your password.

If you’re already logged in and want to change your password, here’s how:

  • Click on the Account menu button (where your name is at the bottom left corner) and click your Member profile
  • Click on Settings from the left navigation menu
  • Click on the Account tab
  • Under the Login section, enter your old password and a new secure password. Confirm your new password a second time
  • Click the Update password button

If you don’t remember your old password, you need to make sure you log out and use password reset to create a new password. If you don’t log out, it will continue to ask you for your old password.

Please use a strong password with symbols and numbers. Using a password generator and saver like 1Password is a great way to secure your passwords.

If you need further assistance resetting your password, please check the Login help article.

How to set up Two-factor authentication

Two-factor authentication provides added security by requiring a 6-digit code generated by a mobile device to be entered anytime that a user logs in. Two-factor authentication allows users to bypass email device verification.

You cannot set up Two-factor authentication via the Patreon app. Please visit the Patreon website to set up Two-factor authentication.

Turn on two-factor authentication for text

Here’s how to set up two-factor authentication for text:

  • While logged in to your Member profile, click on the Settings button from the left sidebar navigation
  • Click on the Account tab
  • Under Two-factor authentication, click on the Use text message
  • Enter your phone number
  • We’ll provide you with a set of backup Two-factor recovery codes
    • You can use these codes if you lose your device and cannot receive authentication codes. These codes are exactly like a password, so store them in a very secure place, like a password manager
  • Enter the code sent to your phone number
  • Click Continue
  • You’ve now set up Two-factor authentication!

Turn on TOTP two-factor authentication

You’ll need to set up an authenticator app such as Duo or Google Authenticator for the Time-based One Time Password Two-factor authentication (TOTP).

Here’s how to set up TOTP two-factor authentication for an authenticator app:

  • While logged in to your Member profile, click on the Settings button from the left sidebar navigation
  • Click on the Account tab
  • Under Two-factor authentication, click Use authenticator app
  • We’ll provide you with a set of backup Two-factor recovery codes
    • You can use these codes if you lose your device and cannot receive authentication codes. These codes are exactly like a password, so store them in a very secure place, like a password manager
  • Click Ok
  • Use your preferred TOTP authenticator app to scan the QR code
  • Enter the 6-digit code produced by your authenticator app
  • You’ve now set up Two-factor authentication!

Now, when you log in to Patreon, you will be prompted to enter a code from your authenticator app or text, adding another layer of security.

I received an unrecognized device verification request

If you receive a verification email from Patreon and don’t recognize the location, please follow these tips below to keep your account safe.

Change your password

If someone other than you has triggered a device verification request, it means that someone successfully entered your login credentials. If you have an email and password login, you’ll want to change your password as soon as you can to prevent future login attempts from unknown parties.

If you use a third-party login app like Google or Facebook, we recommend that you change your password on that app directly.

Making a strong password
  • Use a combination of at least six numbers, letters, and punctuation marks (like ! and &).
  • It should be different from other passwords you use elsewhere on the internet.
  • Use a service like 1Password
  • Change your password regularly.

If you are unable to log into your account being locked due to security rate limiting, you can change it using the password forgot form: patreon.com

How did someone get your password?

Patreon does not store passwords; we keep the “BCyrpt hash” of a password and check that the password you log in with matches it.

The most common method of access to your password is through one of 3 methods:

  • Password reuse: someone accessed your password for another service that does not store them correctly
  • Phishing: a phishing attack happens when someone tries to trick you into sharing personal information online. Phishing is typically done through email, ads, or on imposter websites that seem similar to ones you already use. For example, you might get an email that seems like it’s from your bank asking you to confirm your bank account number.
  • Malware: while this is rarer, it can happen that malware logs the passwords you are typing into your browser. Check your browser for suspicious add ons or plugins and make sure your browser and operating system are updated.

Tips for keeping your account safe

  • Never give your password out to someone you don’t know or publish it in an email
  • Turn on two-factor authentication login. This feature enables you to bypass device verification by authenticating all login attempts directly from your mobile device. Here are our steps for setting up two-factor authentication login
  • Make sure your email account is secure. Change your password often and use unique passwords. Anyone who can read your email can likely also access your Patreon account.

Login help

Password help

  • To request a password reset:
    • Log out of Patreon using this link: patreon.com/logout, which will log you out automatically. You can reset your password only after you log out. Otherwise, it will ask you for the old password when you attempt to change it in your settings
    • Once logged out, you can request a password reset
    • You’ll receive an email with your reset link – follow the link and enter your new password
  • If you use a password saver, update your saved Patreon password before logging back in.
  • Check your spam folder and filters (e.g., Promotions) for emails from password@patreon.com.
  • Add password@patreon.com to your email contact list, and request another reset link.
  • If you use a private domain, contact your domain host and ask that they add it to your email safe list.
  • If you used Facebook, Google, or Apple sign-in to create your Patreon, you don’t need a password to log in, so you likely won’t have a password.
  • Check the Security section of your other app accounts. If Patreon is listed in the Permissions section, try logging in with that app.
  • You can contact our Support team for further assistance.
  • If you can no longer access your email address and can’t reset your password, contact our Support team. We need to verify your identity before we take any action on your account.

Email help

  • If you need help figuring out which email you used to create your account or the email you are using, go to the password reset page and enter possible email addresses you own. When you get a reset email, it will confirm your login email. If you already know your password, you can ignore the reset and use your email and existing password to log in.
  • Check your Facebook, Google, or Apple app account settings in case you’ve used these third-party login options instead.
  • If you encounter any of these messages when trying to sign in, you may have requested that we disable your account. You can either create an account with an alternate email address or reach out to our Support team, and we’ll help you clear this up.
  • You might only need to access your email address to log in if you need to reset your password or if you are required to verify your device (this usually happens if you don’t have 2-factor enabled). If you are already logged in, you can follow the steps to Change your email, and you should be able to change the email on file.
  • If you need to access your email to log in, you will need to contact our Support team. We’ll verify your identity by asking some security questions before taking any action on your account.

Device verification help

  • We may ask you to verify your device via email for security purposes. If email verification is required, we’ll ask you to check your inbox to verify when you log in.
  • If you’re not receiving our verification emails, please check the following:
    • Add no-reply@patreon.com to your email contact list and try logging in again, which will trigger a resend
      • Google’s instructions for adding a new contact for Gmail
      • And directions to manage your Yahoo email contacts
    • Check your spam folder and filters (e.g., Promotions) for emails from no-reply@patreon.com
      • Here’s how to unmark Spam in Gmail
      • And how to manage your Spam list on Yahoo
    • If you are running email through a private domain, contact your domain host and add no-reply@patreon.com to your email safe list
  • If you still need to receive a device verification link after following these steps, please get in touch with our Support team for further assistance.
  • If you’re receiving an expired link message when you try to verify, here are some measures you can take to retry:
    • Log in using a different web browser
      • If you’re using Firefox, please disable Enhanced Tracking Protection — this feature may block verification for your device
    • Log in again and allow 15 minutes for a new verification link to arrive. If you try logging in during that 15-minute window, it will expire the first verification link
    • Check that you’re using the most recent link we’ve sent you
    • Make sure you’re verifying on the same device you are attempting to access your account on (i.e., verify on your desktop if you want to log in on your desktop)
  • If you have an old email on file or cannot access your email to verify your device, please reach out to our Support team for further assistance. Note that we will need to verify your identity before we can take any action on your account.

SMS 2-factor help

  • If you’re not receiving your 2-factor code or the code isn’t working, please try these tips — try logging in after each:
    • Turn your phone off and on, and reattempt login. This may help push the text through
    • Turn on airplane mode on your mobile device for about 10 seconds. Then turn your phone off and back on
  • If you’re still unable to log in and you haven’t changed phone numbers or carriers, please reach out to our Support team with the following information:
    • A screenshot of the SMS confirmation page (this will generally contain a partial phone number)
    • Your current location
    • The complete phone number, with country code
  • If you no longer have access to the phone number you used for 2-factor authentication, please reach out to our Support team.
  • Make sure to write in using or referencing the email address linked with your Patreon. We’ll verify your identity by asking some security questions before we can take any action.

Authenticator app 2-factor help
