Found a problem with the site

Having an issue with the site?

There are a few troubleshooting steps we recommend that may resolve the issue. Retry your action after each steps. If the issue is resolved after one of the steps, there’s no need to keep troubleshooting.

Step 1: Check for any updates for your browser. While older browser versions may work, it’s best to have the most current versions for better performance of the site. Once updated, reattempt.

You can find a list of supported browse by clicking this link here.

  • You can get the most recent version of Chrome here: chrome.google.com
  • The most recent version of Firefox is here: mozilla.org
  • If you use Safari on your iOS device, only versions 11 and up are supported.

Even if you already use one of these browsers, test things out using a secondary browser.

Step 2: Remove or disable any add-ons, or extensions that didn’t come with your browser originally. Sometimes the added software, including ad-blockers, can negatively impact the site.

Step 3: If the issue persists, reattempt while logged in using an incognito (private) browser. Using an incognito browser window allows the site to function without the influence of added add-ons and extension software.

Step 4: Restart your computer. Be sure to fully power down, and restart your device – simply putting your computer to “sleep” won’t do the trick.

Step 5: Restart your modem and/or router. Once you’re back online, reattempt.

Still encountering the issue?

If you think that there’s a larger issue, or ‘bug’ on the site, send us a note with a screenshot of what’s happening with the inspect console open, and our team will take it from there.

You can open your browser’s inspect console by right-clicking, and selecting inspect from the drop down menu that opens. From here, select console from the top bar. Once the console is open, retry the action you’re having an issue with (i.e. clicking a button, or submitting a payment).

Please take a screenshot of the entire page, including any red error messages. This information will help our team with reproducing, and reporting any issue.

How Patreon uses AI in Support

Our goal regarding AI use is simple: provide clearer answers, quicker replies, and support from a real person who cares about resolving your issue. AI helps us do that — but it does not replace the human side of support. Every message sent from Patreon Product Support is reviewed, edited, and owned by a human member of our Product Support team. Our Product Support team is accountable for the accuracy and quality of what you receive.

Every support conversation has a human behind it. If you are in touch with support through email, rest assured that a real person is handling your case.

How AI Supports You and Our Team

Patreon has many features and workflows, and our knowledge base continues to grow alongside the platform. AI helps us manage that complexity. By handling repetitive tasks, AI gives our team more space to focus on what requires human judgment, care, and context.

You may encounter AI in two places within our support experience:

Our Help Center chatbot

When visiting our Help Center, you may interact with an AI-powered chatbot. The chatbot is designed, maintained, and continuously updated by our technical writing and support teams. It’s built around our publicly available Help Center articles and guides — the same resources our human agents use.

The chatbot can guide you to relevant resources and quickly answer common questions. If your situation requires a human, it can also gather information about your issue and route your request to the right team, so it reaches someone with the right expertise. This reduces back-and-forth and speeds up resolution.

AI inside our support tools

Behind the scenes, we also use AI to help our agents work more efficiently. These tools help our team search our knowledge base more effectively, organize and route incoming tickets, and generate draft responses that agents carefully review and edit before replying.

These tools are still evolving, and we actively monitor their quality. If something doesn’t feel right or if something works especially well, we welcome your feedback.

What To Expect When You Contact Patreon Support

If the chatbot can’t resolve your question, or you prefer to speak with a human, we’ll route your inquiry to the appropriate support team, and a member of our Product Support team will follow up by email. Our Product Support team offers 24/7 support.

Sometimes, support responses may begin with troubleshooting steps that feel basic – that’s intentional. We don’t assume anybody’s experience level with Patreon’s product when they first reach out. These steps resolve a high percentage of issues. Starting with consistent troubleshooting helps us diagnose and resolve more complex cases faster. If you need more clarity or deeper guidance, you can always reply to your existing email thread, and we’ll continue working with you.

How to contact Patreon Product Support

We understand that reaching out for help can sometimes feel frustrating, especially when you’re eager to resolve an issue. At Patreon, we’re committed to providing you with the best support possible, and we’ve designed our email support process to ensure your inquiries are handled efficiently and thoroughly.

How to Contact Us

If your request involves payments, login issues, or questions about our guidelines:

  • Visit the Contact Us page:
    • Start a chat for fast answers to your questions. Anything that can’t be solved in chat will be sent to a member of our Product Support team, who will follow up with you as soon as possible
    • On mobile devices, you can start to scroll to open a chat from any article page
  • What to Expect:
    • Our team aims to reply to all questions as quickly as possible. We answer all requests on a first-come, first-served basis.
    • Please do not send multiple emails for the same issue—this can delay responses. If your issue is resolved before we reply, feel free to update your initial email to let us know.

Why We Use Email Support

To give you the most effective assistance, we focus on email support. This method allows us to:

  • Safely and securely address account-specific questions (like payments or login issues)
  • Maintain a clear and accurate record of your inquiry for follow-ups
  • Ensure your request is reviewed by the right specialist to get it resolved as quickly as possible

While we don’t offer phone support, we strive to make our email process as smooth and responsive as possible.

Helpful Resources While You Wait

While our team works on your request, check our comprehensive resources:

  • Patreon on Patreon: Stay up to date on product and company happenings
  • Patreon for Creators: Explore guides and live sessions to help you grow your page and community
  • Help Center: Browse answers to common questions and solutions to technical issues

Thank You for Your Patience

We’re so grateful to have you as part of the Patreon community. Your understanding and patience allow us to provide thorough, thoughtful support to all creators and fans. Thank you for giving us the opportunity to assist you!

How to erase your Patreon account (Account Deletion)

Deleting your Patreon account is a non-reversible action that erases all your data from the platform. This process can take up to 30 days and is not a substitute for canceling memberships or payments — for this, please check Canceling a membership instead.

To delete a Patreon account, you must submit the account for deletion through our Privacy Center. Keep reading to learn more.

Key things to know before deleting your account:

  • The account deletion process can take up to 30 days — There isn’t a way to speed this up
  • To avoid unwanted charges that can still occur during the deletion process, make sure to cancel all active memberships before submitting your deletion request. Learn more about Canceling a membership
  • Once the deletion process starts, you have 14 days to stop it. We will send follow-up emails that you can respond to if you wish to cancel the data deletion. You can also cancel the deletion process by accessing the Privacy Center and going to your Active requests
  • After 30 days, all your data will be permanently erased. There isn’t a way to reactivate your deleted account or restore the deleted data.

Note for creators: If you no longer want to run a membership but still want to keep your account, consider unpublishing your Patreon and keep your account as member-only. If you no longer wish to receive emails about your creators’ content or announcements from Patreon, you can unsubscribe from notification emails.

Deleting your Patreon account and data

Once the deletion process is complete (after 30 days), all data is permanently erased and cannot be restored. If you wish to return to Patreon, you will need to create a new account.

  • Visit our Privacy policy center and click the Take control button
  • Select the option to Erase your data from our systems If you are not logged in to your Patreon account, you’ll be asked to log in using your Patreon account credentials
  • Click the Allow button so our data deletion partner, Transcend, can view your Patreon account. They must have access to the account to erase it
  • A window will appear asking you to confirm the erasure of your account and data

Once you’ve submitted your account for deletion, it can take up to 30 days for your data to be erased and your account fully deleted. During this time, our data deletion partner, Transcend, will send follow-up emails to your account’s email address about the status of your deletion request.

You have 14 days to stop the deletion process. To cancel, either respond to these follow-up emails or go to the Privacy Center, click on Active Requests, and cancel your request.

I’m not getting emails from Patreon

If you are not receiving emails from Patreon, this article lists the actions we suggest to make sure that our emails reach you.

Check your Spam, Junk, Promotions, and Social folders

It’s possible that our emails are being organized into lesser-used inbox sections.

If you find Patreon emails in your Spam folder, you can unmark those emails as Spam, ensuring that future emails of that type appear in your inbox.

  • Create a Gmail filter so Patreon emails never go to Spam
  • Manage your Spam lists in Yahoo

Add Patreon emails to your inbox contact list

Patreon sends emails from several different addresses, depending on the type of email. Adding the following addresses to your contact list will help make sure that our emails never get lost:

  • no-reply@email.patreon.com (communication from Patreon)
  • no-reply@core.patreon.com (account and transaction emails, such as verification codes, billing, receipts, and payout notices)
  • no-reply@patreon.com (device verification, payment, and other automated emails)
  • password@patreon.com (password reset emails)
  • @creator.patreon.com (creator post emails)
  • message@patreon.com (private message notifications from your creators)
  • guidelines@patreon.com (trust and safety communication)
  • @patreon.zendesk.com (product support communication)

If your email provider lets you add an entire domain to your safe list, add core.patreon.com and creator.patreon.com so that you don’t miss emails from any address we use on those domains.

Here are Google’s instructions for adding a new contact for Gmail and Yahoo’s instructions for managing your email contacts.

Using a private domain? Check with your service provider

Your provider may have additional anti-spam tools running that prevent you from getting messages from us. If so, ask them to add the above addresses to your safe list.

I’m not getting push notifications

If you find that you’re no longer receiving push notifications from the Patreon app, there are a few steps you can take to make sure that you start getting notifications.

To check your notification settings, follow the instructions below:

  • Tap on the Notifications icon from the bottom menu. From this screen, you can see a list of all your in-app notifications, ordered chronologically.
  • Tap on the Settings icon at the top right corner of the notifications screen
  • Check that you have push notifications enabled
  • If push notifications are already enabled, tap the checkmark to disable, and then tap the selection again to re-enable — this should set things right
  • To save, exit your settings using the back arrow
  • You can also check your device’s notification settings for the Patreon app to ensure nothing else is blocking our push notifications

If you follow the instructions above and still don’t receive push notifications, please visit this guide on how to troubleshoot problems on the Patreon app.

Scheduled maintenance

In order to optimize creator and fan experiences, Patreon will sometimes require maintenance which may affect certain features for small periods of time.

For information on upcoming maintenance periods, please be sure to visit our Status Page.

If you have additional questions regarding scheduled maintenance or need assistance, please reach out to us.

Submit a feature request or feedback

Do you have an idea for a new feature or some feedback to submit? We would love to hear it! Simply fill out this form to send us your idea. Any creator can submit feature requests or feedback.

Where do the requests and feedback go?

Directly to our Product team! We review the feedback coming into this form alongside all of the feedback we get from social media, support tickets, and conversations with creators to identify common themes and areas to improve. This is an important step in deciding where we should focus next.

Troubleshoot problems on the Patreon app

Having an issue on the Patreon app?

There are a few troubleshooting steps we recommend trying that may resolve the issue. Follow the instructions below – if you’re the issue persists, please let us know! We’re happy to look into things further.

Step 1: Sign out of the Patreon app, and uninstall the app.

Step 2: Restart your phone.

Step 3: Once your phone is back online, reinstall the Patreon app on your phone.

We resolve bugs with new app releases, so reinstalling the latest version of the app may clear up an issue from a later version that we’ve since fixed.

You’ll find the latest versions of the Patreon app here:

  • Patreon app for iOS
  • Patreon app for Android

Sometimes doing a manual installation (rather than using the update feature) will clear up some issues.

Step 4: Check if you have any software updates available for your device.

Some issues can be introduced by the combination of your app and OS version, so making sure you have the most current versions of both is key.

Step 5: If you’re in an area with lower reception, you can also try connecting to WiFi, which could result in some improvement.

Still running into the same problem?

Click the ‘Email Patreon Support’ button below, and let us know. When you submit your ticket, providing the following information will expedite our investigation:

  • A screenshot of any errors you’re encountering
  • Device type (iPhone, Pixel, Galaxy?)
  • OS version
  • Version of the Patreon app you are using

Members: Being a member

Becoming a free member

This article details what it means to be a free member, what you can expect when you join for free, and how you can upgrade at any time.

Who can join for free?

All fans can join for free if their creator has a free offering listed on their page. Some creators may only show their paid options prominently on their Patreon. You’ll know a creator offers this option if you see a Join for free button on their page.

What can I access when I join for free?

When you join for free, you get updates about a creator’s posts directly to your inbox. Never miss an announcement or content that’s exclusive to Patreon!

Upgrading to a paid membership

Some creators may only offer free membership; however, if your creator does have paid membership offerings, here’s how to upgrade to a paid tier:

- In the left navigation, click Your creators — you'll see your memberships split into Paid and Free. Find the creator under Free and click their name
- Click on the Upgrade button on the creator's Patreon
- Click the Join button for the paid tier you'd like to switch to
- Review your billing date and click the Subscribe now button
- Enjoy the perks of your paid membership!
- In the top-left corner, tap the stacked creator images — you'll see your memberships split into Paid and Free
- Tap the membership from this list to go to the full member view of the creator's Patreon
- Tap on the Upgrade membership button
- Locate the tier you want to upgrade to, tap the Join button, and follow the prompts to make the switch
- Enjoy your paid membership perks!

FAQ

  • When you join for free, the creator will see your email address on their end and your member profile name if you have an account.
  • There’s no commitment to upgrade to a paid membership. You can stay for free as long as the creator offers it and as long as you’d like.
  • There are a few reasons why you might not be able to comment on a post you have access to:
    • Your account email still needs to be verified: To add comments on a post you have access to, you’ll first need to verify your account email.
    • Comments are disabled: Creators can disable post comments.
    • Upgrade to add a comment: The creator has set comment access to Only paid members for Public posts
    • You may have sent too many comments recently: If you sent a lot of comments recently, come back later and try again
  • Learn more about why you might not be able to comment.

Can I have multiple Patreon accounts?

You can have multiple Patreon accounts if you’d prefer to keep different things separate — whether you’re a creator, a fan, or both.

Before creating a second account, it’s worth noting that you can manage both your creator page and your memberships and/or purchases under a single Patreon account and login.

If you are a creator and want multiple people to manage a single page, Team Accounts lets you add collaborators to your existing page.

If you do manage multiple accounts, here are a few things to keep in mind:

  • Accounts must have different email addresses to log in
  • Your accounts are not connected, and information cannot be transferred between them
  • Accounts cannot be merged
  • Email addresses can only be tied to one account, so you can’t reassign an email that’s already in use
  • If you’re a creator with a founder’s account, this founding status does not extend to any new accounts you create

If you’re looking to set up a creator page, check out our Creator Launch Checklist for everything you need to know before publishing your page.

Connecting my social media to Patreon

There are 3 ways you can connect your social media accounts to Patreon:

  • Enabling Facebook login
  • Adding your social media pages on your Patreon creator page
  • Finding creators through your social media connections

How to enable Facebook login

Want an easy one-click log in? Here’s how you can connect your Facebook account to log in to Patreon:

  • While logged in to your Patreon account, hover over your profile avatar to open the user menu
  • Click on the Settings link from the menu on the left
  • Click on the Account tab from the menu bar
  • In the Login section, click on the Connect button for Facebook
  • Log in with your Facebook login credentials, or click continue as… if you’re already logged in to your Facebook account
  • The next time you visit Patreon, just click the Continue with Facebook button

When you connect your Facebook account for login, your current Facebook profile image will become your Patreon profile avatar. Here’s how you can change your profile avatar back if you don’t want your two accounts to have the same image.

How to add social media links to my creator page

You can add a direct link to your social media pages on your Patreon creator page. Patrons can seamlessly switch from your Patreon page to your social media spaces with one click.

Follow these instructions to link your social media pages to Patreon:

  • While logged in to your creator account, click on the My Page button from the left sidebar navigation
  • While on your page, click on the Page controls “…” button and go to Edit Page
  • Click on the Page Settings link from the menu bar
  • Under the Social links, section click on the Connect button next to your social media platform of choice
  • You can log in and click the Allow button to finish verifying the connection
  • If everything went as planned, the Connect button will now read Disconnect

Your page will now display an icon button for the social accounts you’ve linked. They will be located directly under your creator page name.

Find creators through my social media networks

Connecting your social media networks to Patreon allows you to find creators on Patreon through your social media communities.

To find creators you already love, go through the steps below:

  • While logged in to your Patreon account, click on the Find creators button
  • Click on the Find creators button for the network you want to link to
  • Log in with your login credentials for that platform and click the button to continue the verification process
  • Any creators in your social network who have a Patreon linked will populate under the creators we found section

Email import preferences

When a creator has your email address from another platform, they may be able to add you to their Patreon community as a free member. This article explains how this works and how to manage your preferences.

How it works

Depending on your settings, one of the following will happen when a creator has your email address and imports it to Patreon:

  • You’re added automatically — you’ll be added as a free member without any action needed on your part
  • You receive an invitation — you’ll get an email inviting you to join for free, and you can choose whether to accept
  • Nothing happens — creators with your email won’t be able to add you and you won’t be invited

How to manage your preferences

  • Click Personal settings from the left side menu (or Settings if you haven’t combined your profiles yet)
  • Select Privacy from the menu bar
  • Find Email import preferences and click Edit
  • A pop-up will open. Choose your preferred option:
    • Let creators automatically add me as a free member — you’ll be added as a free member if a creator imports your email
    • Send me an invite to join a creator’s Patreon — you’ll receive an invitation email and can decide whether to join
    • Don’t add me as a free member or invite me to join — you won’t be added as a free member or invited
  • Click Save

Default settings

Your default setting depends on your region, which is typically determined by where you were located when you created your account:

  • Outside EU/UK/Brazil — set to “Let creators automatically add me as a free member” by default
  • EU/UK/Brazil — set to “Send me an invite to join a creator’s Patreon” by default

You can change this at any time in your Privacy settings.

Fan email sharing with creators

Patreon wants to ensure fans understand and are able to manage their data-sharing preferences with creators. By default, subscribing to a creator on Patreon automatically shares your email address with them, and this article explains how to adjust this setting and manage the information you share.

How to view and edit email sharing settings

Make sure you’re following the steps below when using a desktop:

  • On Desktop, click Settings from the left-side navigation menu (if you’re also a creator, click Your account in the bottom-left corner and select Settings)
  • Click on Privacy (if you’re also a creator, go to the Account settings section, and click on Privacy)
  • Find the Creator email sharing category
  • If you’d like to view or modify the current status of your email sharing settings, click on the Edit button
  • A pop-up will open, and you’ll be able to see whether your email address is currently being shared with creators you currently subscribe to, and the setting that controls whether your email address is shared with new creators
    • To disable email sharing with new creators you subscribe to in the future, simply turn off the toggle next to Share your email address with new creators
    • If you want to stop sharing your email address with a specific creator you’re already subscribed to, find their name in the list and uncheck the box beside it
    • To stop sharing your email with all creators, turn off the toggle next to Share your email address with new creators and uncheck the boxes beside each of the names of the creators you are already subscribed to. By doing this, you’ll stop sharing your email with all current creators, and it won’t be shared with any new creators you subscribe to in the future, unless you adjust the toggle
  • When you’re done, click Save. Any changes you’ve made will not go into effect unless you do this.

Key impacts of changing email sharing settings

Changing your email sharing settings only affects whether creators can see your email address. It does not change your email notification preferences, including for posts, updates, or other alerts related to those creators. To learn how to adjust these settings, visit the article on managing email notifications.

Keep in mind that some creators may use email addresses to send you specific benefits, like direct updates or exclusive content. If you disable email sharing, you might miss out on these benefits. Make sure your benefits won’t be affected, or that you’re comfortable with that trade-off, before you change this setting.

Your email sharing preferences also don’t affect a creator’s ability to contact you via Patreon’s direct messaging system. The direct messaging system is separate and only on Patreon.

In summary, changing your email sharing settings will not affect:

  • Your email notifications, including about posts, updates, or platform alerts
  • Your shipping address – visit our dedicated article to learn how to update your shipping address
  • Your ability to receive direct messages from creators

What is affected:

  • Whether creators can see your email address on Patreon
  • Your ability to receive benefits by email directly from creators may be affected

FAQ

  • Disabling that toggle will stop your email address from being shared with new creators you subscribe to in the future.
  • No, disabling that toggle will only stop your email address from being shared with new creators you subscribe to in the future. If you want to stop sharing your email with creators you’re already subscribed to, you’ll need to unmark the check boxes beside their names as described above.
  • Yes, you can disable the toggle next to Share your email address with new creators to stop sharing your email address with all new creators in the future by default. If you want to share your email only with specific creators, you can manually select the boxes for the creators you wish to share your email with.
  • If you previously disabled the toggle, turning it on again will cause your email address to resume being shared with the new creators you subscribe to in the future.
  • After changing your settings to stop sharing your email address with a creator, your email address remains visible to that creator on Patreon for a buffer period. Email addresses do not stop being shared immediately upon changing these settings because they may be used for benefit fulfillment.

Find creators on Patreon

This article explains how to find creators on Patreon using the Explore tab. Whether you’re searching for a specific creator or discovering new ones, this guide will help you navigate the Explore tab and use its features to find creators that match your interests.

How to Navigate the Explore Tab

The Explore tab makes it easier to discover creators you’ll enjoy. Creators are grouped into hundreds of different genres and niches based on their content type and descriptions. The Explore tab provides a unique, personalized experience that reflects your memberships, interests, and past activity, so you can easily discover content suited to you.

The Explore tab is accessible across all platforms, Web, iOS, and Android, so you can explore new creators from anywhere, whether on your computer or mobile device.

The Explore tab is divided into various sections to help you find creators based on different factors:

  • Search: Type a creator’s name or topic in the search bar to quickly find what you’re looking for or discover something new
  • Topics: At the top of the page, you’ll see taglines related to your interests. Clicking on them takes you to a page featuring top and trending creators in those topics
  • Recently Visited: This section helps you easily return to creators you’ve recently explored. You can also tap More next to their names to Remove them from history
  • Creators for you: Find other creators based on your memberships
  • Popular this week: Stay updated on what’s popular. This section highlights creators who are currently trending in the community
  • Explore Topics: Browse through a wide variety of topics and genres. From niche interests to broader categories, this section makes it easy to dive into different types of content that might spark your interest
  • New on Patreon: Discover fresh creators who have recently joined the platform. This section showcases up-and-coming talent, giving you a chance to support and follow new creators early in their journey
  • Top creators: Based on your past activity, memberships, and browsing behavior, this section suggests creators that align with your interests. Whether it’s creators you’ve recently viewed or those in similar categories, the Explore tab curates a list of creators just for you

If you’re not interested in a particular creator, simply click More next to their name and select Don’t show again to remove them from your suggestions. You can also choose to Report this creator if you believe their content violates our guidelines.

Discovering Adult/18+ creators on Patreon

Fans can now discover both all audiences creators and Adult/18+ creators on Patreon. To see Adult/18+ creators, you need to be over the age of 18. If you’re over 18 years old, follow these steps to see Adult/18+ creators in the Search and Explore:

  • While logged in on desktop or mobile web, click Your account and then Settings
  • Click Privacy
  • Scroll down to the Adult creators section
  • Toggle on the option to See 18+ creators
  • You’ll see a pop-up that asks you to confirm that you are over 18 years old
  • Once you confirm that you’re over 18 years old, you’ll be able to see Adult/18+ creators in the app. These creators will be shown with a specific 18+ badge.
Viewing Adult/18+ creators while searching

You may also update your settings when searching for creators. Below the search bar, you’ll see a link to Show 18+ creators. When you click on this link, a pop-up will appear asking you to confirm that you are over 18 years old

You can change these settings at any time by going back to your Privacy settings and toggling off the ability to see Adult/18+ creators in the app. If you are already a member of an Adult/18+ creator’s page, then you do not need to update your settings. Adult/18+ creators will show up automatically.

How do I change my name on Patreon?

In this article, we’ll guide you through updating your profile name on Patreon. This will change your display name whenever you publicly comment on a post. Note that although Patreon does permit profanity in creator or fan usernames that don’t violate any other Community Guidelines, username profanity can’t attack another person, ethnicity, or protected group.

Changing your profile name is not available on the Patreon app, so make sure you follow these steps using the desktop or mobile web version.

How do I update my profile name?

Follow the steps below to change your profile name:

  • While logged in, click on Personal settings from the left navigation menu, which will take you to the Basics page
  • Type the name you want to use in the Your name section
  • Once complete, click on the Save button to finalize your change(s)

Your new profile name should start displaying in your Patreon account!

How do I change my profile image?

You cannot change your profile image on the Patreon app. Please visit the Patreon website to update your profile picture.

You can update your profile image anytime you’d like by:

  • While logged into your Patreon account, click on Settings from the left navigation menu
  • Under Basics settings, click on your current profile picture
  • Select your new image. We recommend that images be 1024 px by 1024 px. Image files must be 16 MB or less
  • Click the Save

That’s it! Your new profile image should show up wherever you interact on Patreon.

How do I update my shipping address?

Whether you’ve recently moved, or need to make a small adjustment to your zip code, you can change your shipping address whenever you want.

What we’ll cover:

  • How to add or update your address from your Account Settings
  • How to add or update your address for a specific membership
  • How to remove a shipping address
  • Frequently asked questions

How to add or update your address on your Account Settings

  • While logged into your Patreon account, settings from the left navigation menu list
  • Click on the Account link from the menu
  • In the Shipping address section of the page, you can add a new address or click the Edit button to update your address
  • Select which creators you’d like to share or update your shipping information with at the bottom of the form
  • Note: Only creators who request a shipping address from their patrons, will appear on the list
  • Click the Save button

How to add or update your address for a single membership

  • While logged into your Patreon account, hover over the Pencil Icon on the left navigation menu and Click on the Manage button.
  • Find your creator, and click the Update button under the “Shipping Address” section.
  • You can select from any shipping address already on file, or click the Add a new address option. You can also opt-out of receiving physical benefits by selecting I prefer not to receive benefits through the mail
  • Click the Save button

How to remove an address from your account

Callout: You can only delete addresses that are not linked to any memberships.

  • While logged into your Patreon account, hover over the Pencil Icon on the left navigation menu and Click on the Manage button.
  • Find memberships with the address in question and click the Update button
  • You can choose another address on file, add an address, or choose I prefer not to receive benefits through the mail
  • Do this with each membership tied to that address
  • Once you’ve unlinked the address from active memberships, click the settings button from the left navigation menu list
  • Click on the Account link from the menu
  • In the Shipping address section of the page click the Edit button for the shipping address you are to deleting
  • Click on Delete Address, and confirm

FAQ

Q: Does Patreon support APO addresses?

A: Yes! You can select Armed Forces Americas, Armed Forces Europe, and Armed Forces Pacific from the State drop-down section.

Q: Does Patreon support international addresses?

A: Yes! You can select different countries using the dropdown at the top of the form. Scroll up or down until you find your country address. All international addresses require a valid phone number to be associated with them. If your phone number is from another country, click on the flag icon and scroll until you find your country.

How Patreon’s network works for members

Patreon’s network is built on connection, not attention. It’s a place to discover a new corner of the internet that rewards human creativity, helping you find creators and content you genuinely care about, while never losing sight of the creators you already support.

When a creator you support joins Patreon’s network, you’ll notice some changes to your Patreon app experience. This article explains what’s new, what you can control, and what stays the same.

What stays the same

  • Your existing memberships and access to paid content are not affected
  • Paid members continue to see paid posts they have access to
  • Your membership fees and billing don’t change unless you change your membership or the creator changes pricing
  • A creator’s past posts remain where they have always been

What’s new

  • In the Patreon mobile app, your Home screen has two tabs:
    • Home: A discovery feed showing posts and Quips from creators you already follow, ranked at the top, alongside recommendations for creators and communities you may not have discovered yet.
    • Memberships: A feed reserved entirely for posts and Quips from creators you’re already a member of (free or paid). No recommendations, just the creators you already support.
  • Posts from creators you already support are always ranked first in the Home feed, so you’ll never miss content from the creators you follow.
  • Your paid and exclusive posts are never shown to non-members in the discovery feed. Only public content appears in discovery surfaces.
Switch between feeds at any time
  • Use the Home tab to explore and discover new creators. Switch to the Memberships tab when you just want to catch up with the creators you already support.
Quick access to your memberships
  • You can quickly access a list of all the creators you’re a member of (free or paid) by tapping the icons in the top-left corner of the home tab. You can then tap any creator to jump straight to their page.
  • Quips are short, public posts that creators use to share quick updates directly in the Home feed, such as a behind-the-scenes moment, a quick thought, or a preview of upcoming work. You may see Quips in your Home feed from creators you don’t yet follow.
How to engage with Quips
  • You can interact with any Quip you see in your feed:
    • Like: Tap the like icon to show your appreciation
    • Comment: Tap the comment icon to leave a reply
    • Reshare: Share a Quip to spread it to others
Quips notifications
  • When a creator you support posts a Quip, you’ll receive an in-app notification. Quips are never sent by email.
  • To manage Quip notifications for a specific creator:
    • Tap Notifications in the top-right corner of the Home screen
    • Tap Your account
    • Find the creator in the list and adjust their notification settings individually
  • To turn off notifications for Quips from creators you don’t yet follow:
    • From the same screen, unmark the checkbox for Posts and Quips from creators you might like
  • Collaboration posts are public posts co-authored by two or more creators on Patreon.
  • When a creator you support collaborates with another creator, the post can show up in places you already browse on Patreon, even if you don’t follow the other creator yet.
  • Collaboration posts are public and free to view. You can like, comment on, and share them the same way you would with other public posts.
How to tell it’s a Collaboration post
  • Collaboration posts show the names of all contributing creators in the byline. If you see a post from a creator you follow that includes another creator’s name, it’s a Collaboration post.
  • If a creator you support is involved in a Collaboration post, either as the original author or as a collaborator, you’ll receive a notification when the post is published (depending on your notification settings).
  • If you see a Collaboration post from a creator you don’t follow, you can visit their page and choose to join for free or select a paid-membership option.

Shape your discovery experience

What appears in your Home feed is not fixed. Your activity helps shape what you see over time in the Patreon mobile app:

  • Like, comment, and join creators to see more of what you enjoy
  • Tap More on any post and select Not interested to see less content like this in the future
  • In any post, you can switch between viewing comments in chronological order or by the most engaging threads by tapping the sort option at the top of the comments section to switch between the two
  • To find posts you’ve already browsed or saved, tap Library , where you’ll find recently played, recently viewed, and saved posts all in one place
  • Tap on any creator in the Home feed to visit their page and explore their posts, collections, chats, and shop
  • Found a creator you want to revisit? Head to Explore and scroll down to the Recently Visited section to quickly return to any creator’s page you’ve recently explored
Select your interests (Coming soon)

When you first set up the app, you’ll be able to select topics and interests that shape your Home feed from day one. The more you select, the more relevant your feed becomes.

Report content that violates our guidelines

If you see something in your feed that you believe violates Patreon’s Community Guidelines, tap More on the post and select Report to flag it for review. For anything else, you can reach our Support team directly.

A note for fans of Adult/18+ creators

If you support Adult/18+ creators, you’ll still be able to access their posts through the feed and the creator’s page as you’d normally do.

At this time, Adult/18+ creators may not be shown in discovery surfaces the same way as all-audience creators, and some discovery features (such as Quips) may not be available for Adult/18+ creators.

We’ll update members as new experiences become available.

FAQ

  • No. You may get access automatically once a creator you support joins the network. There’s nothing you need to set up.
  • The Home feed includes recommendations for creators and communities you may enjoy, based on your existing memberships and activity. If you see something you’re not interested in, tap More on the post and select Not interested to adjust your feed.
  • Yes. Switch to the Memberships tab in the Patreon mobile app at any time to see only posts and Quips from creators you’re already a member of. This feed has no recommendations.
  • When a creator posts a Quip, you may receive an in-app notification. You can manage notification preferences for each creator individually from your Notification settings.
  • The Home feed is currently only available on the Patreon mobile app. You can view an individual Quip on desktop via a direct link or in the Quips tab on a creator’s page, but the feed itself isn’t available on desktop yet.
  • Yes. Swipe right or tap the icons in the top-left corner to the quick-access panel that lists all the creators you’re a member of. Tap any creator to jump straight to their page.
  • You can tap More on the post and select Not interested to see less content like this in the future.

How to make changes to your account (desktop)

Managing my profile basics

Managing my Account settings

Area

Shipping address

Joining a creator’s Patreon as a paid member

This article is about becoming a paid member to join a creator’s community on Patreon, what to expect, and what to do if a payment fails.

Who can become a paid member?

If a creator offers paid membership tiers, all fans can join the creator’s community. You’ll know that a creator has paid offerings if you see a “choose your membership” section on their Patreon with paid offerings.

Please note, that your billing schedule will depend on a creator’s billing schedule.

Choosing your membership

Many creators offer the option to become a monthly or annually paid member. If a creator offers annual membership, you can toggle between the monthly and annual prices of their tiers.

Once you’ve decided which membership tier you’ll join, click the Join button. Note that all members should abide by Patreon’s Community Guidelines, which act as the guardrails detailing the sorts of behaviors that are permitted and prohibited on Patreon.

What if a creator doesn’t have tiers?

Some creators may offer paid membership without the structure of tiers — members can join with a custom monthly price. To join a creator’s Patreon that does not offer tiers, click the Become a member button.

Failed payment help

If your payment is failing when you try to join a creator’s Patreon, check that your payment method has sufficient funds and is:

  • Not expired or canceled
  • Enabled for foreign, secure online, and recurring purchases — Look for these settings in your bank’s mobile app

You can also check that your bank or payment provider has your correct details (e.g., name, address, zip, etc.). If you add a new payment method, they may need to verify your identity for security, e.g., with a password, PIN, fingerprint, or code sent to your device.

Still not working?
  • Try a different payment method
  • Contact your bank or PayPal directly and ask that your provider allow future authorizations and charge attempts from “Patreon* Membership”

You can turn on backup payments from your payment settings to help ensure you don’t lose access to your membership benefits due to failed payments.

Managing my membership

You can make changes to your membership at any time — choose your device type below

  • Follow these steps while on your Member profile. You can check which profile you’re on by clicking your picture in the bottom left corner.
    • Click the Settings link from the left-side menu
    • On your Settings page, click the Memberships tab (this link will take you there)
    • Locate your membership, and click the View Details button
    • From here, you can switch tiers or cancel
  • Follow these steps while on your member profile. You can switch between member and creator profiles (if you have one) by tapping on your picture in the top right corner and tapping the Switch to button.
    • Tap on the memberships icon in the top right of the home screen
    • Locate and tap on your membership
    • Tap your current membership listed below the creator’s information
    • Tap on Edit membership
    • From here, you can switch tiers or cancel
  • Follow these steps while on your Member profile. You can check which profile you’re on by tapping the menu in the top left corner and then clicking on your picture at the bottom of the menu.
    • Tap on the menu in the top left corner
    • Tap on the Settings link from the menu
    • Swipe through the top menu and tap on the Memberships tab (this link will take you there)
    • Scroll down and tap on the creator
    • From here, you can switch tiers or cancel

FAQ

  • If you’ve joined a membership tier, the creator will have listed what you’ll have access to in the tier description. If the creator doesn’t offer tiers, you may find the creator’s benefits listed in their About section. If you’re unsure, you can also contact the creator directly on Patreon.
  • When you comment on a post, like a post or a message, react to a post or message, join a chat room, send a chat message, express interest in an event, join an event experience, and take other community actions, you are visible to those Patreon communities, and members of those communities can see your member profile.
  • Learn more about what is visible on your member profile.
  • There are a few reasons why you might not be able to comment on a post you have access to:
    • Your account email still needs to be verified: To add comments on a post you have access to, you’ll first need to verify your account email
    • Comments are disabled: Creators can disable post comments
    • Upgrade to add a comment: The creator has set comment access to Only paid members for Public posts
    • You may have sent too many comments recently: If you sent a lot of comments recently, come back later and try again
  • Learn more about why you might not be able to comment.

Manage my email notifications

Depending on whether you are a creator or a member, you can expect to receive different email notifications. Keep reading to learn how to switch off email notifications you don’t need.

Manage my creator page email notifications

  • While logged in to your creator account, click on the Settings button from the menu on the left-hand side
  • Click on the Email notifications tab
  • As a default, you’ll be opted in to receive all email notifications, however, you can switch off notifications you no longer want to receive
  • Click the Update email settings button

Manage my email notifications as a member

  • While logged in to your member account, click on the Settings button from the left navigation menu
  • Click the Email notifications tab
  • As a default, you’ll be opted in to receive all email notifications, however, you can switch off notifications you no longer want to receive
  • We’ll auto-save your changes

There is not an option to opt-out of receiving email notifications of private messages between you and your creators.

Want to unsubscribe from our marketing emails? Click the Unsubscribe links at the bottom of an email sent from our marketing team.

Manage your membership and activity visibility

As of May 27th, 2026, Patreon offers all creators more ways to manage how your memberships and activity show up across Patreon. As part of this, we’re updating some defaults around membership and activity visibility, and replacing the Full public profile and Community profile settings with new, more granular controls. Read more about these details below. These settings are currently only available for creators.

This article outlines what controls Patreon gives you over the visibility of some of your membership and activity information. You can choose whether your memberships are shown publicly and whether your activity may be highlighted to others.

You can also manage other privacy settings in this tab, including sharing your email with creators and Email import preferences.

How to access your membership and activity visibility settings

  • Click Personal settings (or Settings if you haven’t combined your profiles yet) from the left side menu
  • Select Privacy from the menu bar
  • Find Membership & activity visibility and click Edit
  • A pop-up will open with your visibility controls

Show my memberships

This toggle controls whether your memberships to creators will be shown publicly on Patreon, including on creator profiles and across Patreon’s activity and home feeds.

  • When this is on, your memberships to creators will be shown publicly
  • When this is off, your memberships to creators will not be shown publicly
  • If this global setting is enabled, you can also choose whether to show your membership to a specific creator publicly — see Hide visibility by creator below

Highlight my activity

This toggle controls whether your activity (e.g. likes and comments) may be highlighted in others’ feeds and whether people will see an activity tab on your creator page.

  • When this is on, your activity (e.g. likes and comments) may be highlighted in others’ feeds, and people will see an activity tab on your creator page
  • When this is off, your activity (e.g. likes and comments) will not be highlighted in others’ feeds, and people will not see an activity tab on your creator page

Activity on paywalled posts stays within that paid community, but, subject to your controls, can be shown to other paid members in that community, including on the home feed and your creator page. Only members of that creator’s applicable paid tier(s) can see it.

Hide visibility by creator

You can choose whether to show memberships publicly for specific creators and whether to highlight membership activity for specific creators. Under Hide visibility by creator, you’ll see a list of your active and past memberships.

For current memberships, you’ll see two checkboxes:

  • Hide membership — choose whether your memberships to this creator will be shown publicly
  • Hide activity — choose whether your activity in that creator’s community may be highlighted, including in others’ feeds and on your creator page

For past memberships, you’ll only see the Hide activity checkbox if you had previously chosen to hide that activity.

  • If you’ve chosen not to highlight your activity preferences for a specific creator, those settings will be saved even if your membership ends. However, you’ll only be able to adjust membership preferences for creators with whom you have an active membership.

When you’re done, click Save.

FAQ

  • Memberships you join before July 27, 2026 will not be shown publicly unless you choose otherwise.
  • No — if you want to ensure new memberships are not shown publicly, you’ll need to turn off Show my memberships globally. When this setting is off, none of your memberships will be shown publicly, including any you may have individually set to visible. There is no way to hide new memberships by default while still showing specific existing ones.
  • Head to your Privacy settings, click Edit next to Membership & activity visibility, and select Don’t highlight my activity. This will remove the activity tab from your creator page and your activity will not be highlighted in others’ feeds.
  • Yes — you can review and customize your visibility settings at any time, either before or after you combine your profile. Any changes you make before combining will carry over once your profile is combined. You can update your preferences at any time.
  • Because memberships are shown publicly (or not), subject to your settings, as we continue building features that help fans discover creators and communities this information may appear in additional places in the future. We’ll keep you updated if any additional changes take place.

Member currency settings on Patreon

As a member, you can choose to start a membership to creators in your choice of supported currencies. Please visit this article, Patreon’s supported currencies, to find a list of currently supported currencies. We are working on adding more currencies in the future.

Accepted payment methods

Depending on your device and location, we accept payments via PayPal, Apple Pay, Venmo, and the following cards:

  • Visa
  • Master Card
  • Discover
  • JCB
  • Diners Club

Selecting your local currency during checkout

To change your currency settings on a new membership:

  • Under the Order Summary section at checkout, your Currency will display under the total payment amount
  • At the bottom of the page, click on the Currency code displayed (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP, etc.)
  • Choose the preferred currency and click the Update button to save your settings. Your payment amount will automatically update in the Order Summary
  • Here, you’ll have the option to select your choice of supported currency. Click the Update button, and your payment amount will automatically update in the Order Summary
  • Continue following the steps to process your membership

Updating an existing membership

To change your currency settings on existing memberships:

  • Click on the Settings link from the left sidebar navigation (if you’re also a creator, click Your account in the bottom-left corner and select Settings)
  • Then click on the Memberships link from the submenu
  • Choose the creator you want to update your membership for and click the View details button
  • Click Edit next to the payment method
  • At the bottom of the page, click on the Currency code displayed (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP, etc.)
  • Choose the preferred currency and click the Update button to save your settings. Your payment amount will automatically update in the Order Summary
  • Continue following the steps to update your membership

Currency editing is currently not available for subscription billing, but we’re working to add this functionality in the future. If your creator uses subscription billing and you’d like to change the currency you pay in, you can cancel and sign up again in your desired currency. Keep in mind that this starts a new membership — if you’re on an annual plan, you’ll lose any remaining prepaid time and be charged again for a full year, rather than switching currencies mid-term.

Changing the currency preference

The currency preference determines what currency is displayed to you when browsing for new memberships. To change it, follow the steps below:

  • Click on the Settings link from the left sidebar navigation (if you’re also a creator, click Your account in the bottom-left corner and select Settings)
  • Then, click on the Account link from the submenu (if you’re also a creator, go to the Account settings section, and select Account)
