Russian*

Spanish

Spanish (Latin America)

Swedish*

Ukrainian*

  • We do not offer customer support for languages with an asterisk.

How it works

  • If you’re logged out and your browser language is a language we support, our site will appear in that language. Otherwise, the language will default to English
  • If you’re logged into Patreon, you’ll experience the site in the language indicated in your Basics settings
  • Our mobile apps will also be shown in our supported languages, based on the language settings of the user’s phone
  • Anything written by creators and patrons (posts, tier descriptions, messages, comments on posts, etc.) will not be translated and will remain in their original language
  • Creators and patrons will receive emails from Patreon in the supported language they’ve chosen in their settings. Otherwise, all emails will be in English

How to change your language preference

Anyone logged into Patreon on desktop or mobile web can change their language preference in their profile settings — here’s how!

  • While logged in to your patron profile click on the Settings button from the left sidebar navigation
  • Then, click on the Account link from the sub-navigation list
  • Scroll down to the Language preference dropdown, and choose your preferred language from the list of supported languages. We’ll auto-save your changes

Logged out visitors can change their preferred language using a selector in the footer of the site.

Suggested messaging for patrons

If you’d like to let your audience know about new languages supported on Patreon, you can use the suggested messaging below:

Sample post or message copy

Post Title/Subject Line: Patreon language support

Hey everyone,

Patreon is now available in [language]. For those of you who are [language] speakers, if your experience doesn’t automatically display in [language], you can change your language settings here: patreon.com

Updating my country of residence

If you’ve recently moved and pay VAT, be sure to update your country of residence to ensure that we charge you the correct VAT amount.

Learn more about VAT here: VAT (Value Added Tax) on Patreon

You can update your country of residence anytime you’re logged into your account. Just follow the steps below:

  • While logged in to your account, click on the Settings button from the left navigation menu, which will take you to your Basics page
  • Select your country of residence from the drop-down menu. You can begin typing your country or scroll through the list
  • If applicable, please also select the proper province or state that you live in. If you live in the US, enter your Postal Code of Residence as well
  • Click the Save button

What information am I sharing about myself with fellow community members?

Creators are now required to combine profiles

As of July 6th, all creators are required to have a single identity instead of separate creator and fan profiles. If you haven’t combined your profiles yet, your access to Patreon is temporarily restricted until you do. Combine your profiles now to restore access to Patreon. If you don’t take action in the next few weeks, we’ll automatically combine your profiles for you starting August 17th. Need help? Visit Combine your creator and fan profiles into a single identity or contact the support team for assistance.

When you subscribe to a creator, purchase a membership or product on Patreon, or otherwise engage with a creator — even if you are a creator yourself — you are joining a Patreon community associated with that creator. This article details what information may be visible to fellow community members.

This information may be displayed as part of your community profile, which is visible to fellow community members, and may include more information than your public profile, which is publicly accessible to anyone in the world. Please visit our resource about your public Patreon profile to learn more.

As of May 27th, 2026, Patreon offers all creators more ways to manage how your memberships and activity show up across Patreon. As part of this, we’re updating some defaults around membership and activity visibility, and replacing the Full public profile and Community profile settings with new, more granular controls.

  • When you take actions on Patreon — such as commenting on a post, liking a post or message, joining a chat room, or sending a chat message — members of those communities can see your community profile. The following information is always visible:
    • Your full profile name — this is the same name displayed on your public profile. You can use a pseudonym if you prefer not to use your real name. You can change this from your Basics settings
    • Your profile image — this is the same image displayed on your public profile. If you don’t upload one, the Patreon logo will be used. You can upload an image anytime from your Basics settings
    • When you joined Patreon — the date you created your account
    • Your bio — If you’ve added one, it will appear on both your public and community profile. If you haven’t added a bio, it won’t appear on either. You can add or customize your bio from your Basics settings
    • Your connected social media accounts — the same links displayed on your public profile. You can toggle these off at any time in your Social links settings. If you haven’t connected any, this information won’t appear on your profile
  • Yes — you have options depending on your account type:
  • If you’re a creator, you can control whether your memberships and activity are visible both publicly and to fellow community members at any time via the Membership & activity visibility setting in your Privacy settings. Visit our article on managing your membership and activity visibility to learn more.
  • If you’re a fan/member (no creator page), you can manage your visibility through your Full public profile and Community profile settings in your Privacy settings.
  • Note that only creators will see the new membership & activity visibility settings for now; fans will continue to see the options to enable or disable their Full public profile and Community profile settings.
  • Patreon is continuing to build out community features. In the future, the following information may also be visible to fellow community members:
    • A community-specific name, profile image, and bio
    • When you joined a specific community
    • Your membership tier and purchases within a community
    • Shared communities and shared chats with other members
    • Your community status, including any roles, awards, or badges
    • Your membership status with other creators
    • Your activity on other creators’ content
  • As a creator, you also have a community profile that your members can see as you interact with them in your community. Your community profile contains the same information as described above, but will also always show an indicator that you are the creator of that community — this cannot be turned off.

For a more complete explanation of what information may be shared with fellow community members, please review Patreon’s Privacy Policy.

Why does this creator’s page look different?

Creator pages on Patreon have a fresh new look. If you’re used to the classic design, you might notice that the page you’re visiting looks different.

We’ve heard from creators that they want a better way for fans to explore their work. To help with that, we’ve redesigned the creator home page. Fans have the same access to content as before. This guide walks you through what’s changed, what’s still available, and how to find your way around.

What’s new?

The updated creator page makes it easier for you to navigate through a creator’s work, see highlighted content, and easily explore all of their work without additional digging.

Exploring the new creator home page

When you visit a creator page, you’ll land on their Home tab by default. This tab is a curated overview of everything the creator offers — including recent posts, collections, and popular shop items — all organized into easy-to-scan shelves.

At the top of the page, you’ll see the creator’s header, which includes their bio, profile image, and the total number of posts they’ve shared.

You can also click the More button for quick actions, like:

  • Viewing the creator’s About page
  • Sharing the creator’s page
  • Gifting a membership to another fan
  • Checking your membership with this creator (if you’re a member)

Want to dive deeper? You can use the top-right menu to explore other sections, like Posts, Collections, or Shop.

How content is organized

The Home tab is made up of visual shelves that group the creator’s content by type or theme. Here’s what you might see as you scroll, depending on how the creator has set up their page:

  • Latest post – The most recent post from the creator
  • Recent posts – Scrollable view of the most recent posts
  • Popular posts – A mix of recent and highly engaged posts
  • All collections – Any additional collections beyond the first two
  • Quips – The most recent Quips from the creator.
  • Popular products – Top-selling items from the creator’s shop (if they have one)
  • Explore more – Additional popular posts you might enjoy

FAQ

  • If you’re not a member of a creator’s Patreon, you’ll still land on their Home tab — but you’ll see:
    • The creator’s bio at the top
    • Any public posts they’ve published
    • The tiers they offer, or the option to Join for free
  • Yes — you can see all posts in the order they were published in the Posts tab, from the top-right menu on the creator’s page.
  • This updated layout is currently only available on desktop and mobile web. We’re working on bringing it to the Patreon app — stay tuned!
  • Yes. All creators now have the updated creator page.
  • If you’d like to share feedback about the new page design, you can reach out to our Support team. Just click the Submit a request button at the bottom of the page to get started.

Your Public Patreon Profile

This article details what aspects of your public profile may be visible, what details you can add to your public profile for others to see, and your associated account settings.

Please note that your public profile is visible to anyone in the world, and so it differs from your community profile, which is visible to fellow Patreon community members. You can visit our resource about what information you are sharing with fellow community members to learn more about community profiles.

As of May 27th, 2026, Patreon offers all creators more ways to manage how their memberships and activity show up across Patreon. As part of this, we’re updating some defaults around membership and activity visibility, and replacing the Full public profile and Community profile settings with new, more granular controls.

What is visible on your public profile

When you create an account on Patreon, you automatically get a public profile. While other users can’t currently search for your public profile directly using Patreon unless you are a creator, your profile page may be linked when you comment on a post, like a post or message, react to a post or message, join a chat room, send a chat message, express interest in an event, join an event experience, and take other community actions. Also, anyone can navigate directly to the URL for your public profile page. If the visibility of a post, chat room, event experience, or other community space later changes, then the visibility of the associated comments, messages, likes, and reactions may also adjust along with it, and so may change who will be shown a link to your public profile.

What’s always visible on your public profile page
  • Your public profile name: You can use a pseudonym for your profile name if you prefer not to use your real name. You can change your profile name from Your account → Settings → Profile basics
  • Your public profile image: You can upload an image that you want to represent you, whether it’s an image of you or a photo of something else, like your beautiful dog. If you don’t upload an image, your profile image will default to an adorable fox avatar. You can upload a new profile image anytime from Your account → Settings → Profile basics
  • When you joined Patreon: The date that you created your Patreon account.
  • Social media profiles you may have connected: When you connect a social media account via Your account → Settings → Account → Social links, it will be publicly displayed on your public profile. You can choose not to display a social media account link in your public profile at any time by toggling it off in your Social links settings. If you haven’t connected any of your social media accounts to your Patreon account, then this information will not appear on your public profile
  • Your bio: A biographical description of yourself if you’ve added one to your Patreon account. If you haven’t added a bio, then this information will not appear on your public profile

Please note that all aspects of your public profile must comply with our Community Guidelines.

What else can you choose to display on your public profile

If you’re a fan (no creator page)

In addition to your profile name, image, account creation date, and connected socials, you can also choose to publicly display the following information on your public profile page by enabling your Full public profile setting in Your account → Settings → Privacy.

If your Full public profile setting is enabled, the following information will be publicly visible:

  • The creators you subscribe to and the date you started subscribing to them
  • The subscription, membership tier, or other recurring payment for each creator you subscribe to
  • The posts you’ve liked
  • The comments you’ve made
If you’re a creator

As a creator, you can manage the visibility of your memberships and activity at any time in Your account → Settings → Privacy. To learn more, visit our article on Managing your membership and activity visibility. We’re replacing your full public profile and community profile settings with new, more granular privacy controls, meaning this will take effect even if your full public profile setting was previously disabled.

For a more complete explanation of what information about you may be publicly visible, please review Patreon’s Privacy Policy.

Members: Billing

Annual membership details

In this guide, we’ll go over key membership details to help you decide if annual membership is right for you.

Not all creators have annual memberships available. If a creator has yearly plans, they’ll be listed in the tier descriptions and on the checkout page.

Starting an annual membership (not yet a member)

  • Log in to your Patreon account and find the creator’s page you want to join
  • Click the link for the annual discount directly below the Join button for the tier. You can compare the creator’s monthly and annual options on the checkout page before you confirm
  • Review your billing method and auto-renewal details in the Summary section of the checkout page – you may want to print or screenshot the page for your records
  • Click on the Confirm button to start your membership. You’ll pay for the year in full immediately.

Your payment instantly unlocks your access to the creator’s back catalog of content for your tier, and you’ll be set for the next year!

Switching from monthly to annual billing

  • Click Your Account in the bottom-left corner and select Settings
  • In the Account settings section, select Memberships
  • Filter creators by paid, find the one you want to switch to an annual membership, and click on it
  • In the Billing frequency section, select Switch to annual – if you don’t see this option, annual memberships aren’t available for this creator
  • Review the details on the checkout page and click the Subscribe now button

Please note that you’ll pay for the entire year upfront.

When is my next payment?

You have a whole year. The exact renewal date will depend on the creator’s billing model. If you’re not sure, you can consult your auto-renewal details for your membership on your Membership tab.

  • If the creator uses subscription billing, members will be charged upon signup and yearly on their join date in UTC
    • Example: You join a creator’s page with an annual membership on Nov 18, 2022, and pay $19.20 for the year. On Nov 18, 2023, your annual membership auto-renews, and you pay $19.20. Your annual membership will auto-renew on Nov 18 each year thereafter
  • If a creator uses charge-upfront billing, then members are charged when they join and yearly on the first of the month on PT, a year after the initial join date, and on that date every year until canceled
    • Example: You join a creator’s page with an annual membership on Nov 18, 2022, and pay $19.20 for the year. On Dec 1, 2023, your annual membership auto-renews, and you pay $19.20. Your annual membership will auto-renew on the 1st of December each year thereafter
What happens to my annual membership if the creator pauses their page?

When your creator pauses billing, your annual membership extends by one month.

For example, say you have an annual subscription set to end on November 1st, 2025. If your creator pauses their billing cycle in August 2025, your membership will extend by 1 month, and it will now end on December 1st, 2025.

Is my membership monthly or annual?

The Memberships page lists your payment schedules. Depending on how you signed up, your membership may be listed as:

  • Per year: you’re an annual member!
  • Per month: you pay monthly
  • Per creation: you pay on the first of each month on a per-post billing structure

Making changes to an annual membership

If you’re using the Patreon app, please see our guide on Updating your membership via the Patreon app.

Increasing your membership takes effect immediately because you pay upfront.

How to upgrade your annual membership
  • Click Your Account in the bottom-left corner and select Settings
  • In the Account settings section, select Memberships
  • Filter creators by paid, find the one you want to change tiers, and click on it
  • Click the Switch to another tier button
  • Find the tier you want to upgrade to and click the Join button
  • Review the details on the checkout page and click the Subscribe now button

You can also switch tiers by going to the creator’s page and clicking the Membership tab at the top of the page. When you increase your annual membership, we apply pro-rated credit for what you’ve already paid to the new amount, and you pay the remaining cost to upgrade. When you change an annual membership, it extends your term from that date.

Examples:

  • If you paid for a $120 tier and upgrade in the same month to a $140 tier, you pay $20 for the difference between the two.
  • If you paid $120 in April and upgrade in June to a $140 tier, only $100 from your initial payment is left, so you’ll pay $40 to upgrade.

In both of the above examples, your membership auto-renews in a year and you pay your new membership amount of $140 in full.

Decreasing your annual membership

At the moment, there’s no way to decrease your annual membership tier. You can, however, lower your tier level after your year membership has ended with a slight workaround.

You can cancel your membership near the end of your year term and then rejoin at a lower-tier option once the year term has passed.

Examples:

  • If the creator uses subscription billing: You start your annual membership on July 12, 2020. This means your yearly membership is set to expire on July 11, 2021, and renew on July 12, 2021. You can cancel your membership near the expiration date and rejoin after July 12, 2021, at any membership tier you’d like.
  • If the creator uses Charge upfront billing: You start your annual membership on July 12, 2020. This means your yearly membership is set to expire on July 31, 2021, and renews on August 1, 2021. You can cancel your membership near the expiration date and rejoin after August 1, 2021, at any membership tier you’d like
Can I switch from annual to monthly?

While you have an annual membership, you won’t be able to switch to a monthly membership. If you’d like to have a monthly membership, you can cancel the auto-renewal, and then rejoin the creator’s page with a monthly option after the year has passed.

I canceled and want to rejoin – will I have to pay again?

That depends! If you join, then cancel, and then rejoin all in the same month, you won’t be charged for those adjustments. If you join, then cancel in a later month and rejoin later on, you can expect to pay for extending your annual membership.

When you join or rejoin a creator’s annual membership, your yearly membership terms start from that date.

Example:

  • January 10, 2021 – Let’s say you join a creator’s annual membership for USD 20.16 for a year ($1.68/ month)
  • January 10, 2021 – You cancel because you only want a year of membership. Your year of membership will end on January 31, 2022 (If the creator uses charge-upfront billing) or on January 9, 2022 (If the creator uses subscription billing)
  • March 1, 2021 – You rejoin. You pay $5.04 ($20.16 - $15.12 from what you’ve already paid) immediately. This payment extends your membership term, and your membership will renew on April 1, 2022 (If the creator uses charge-upfront billing) or on March 1, 2022 (If the creator uses subscription billing)

Canceling an annual membership

Canceling will not affect your current membership term. After canceling, you’ll still be an active member and have access until your year of membership ends.

How to cancel annual membership auto-renewal:
  • Click Your Account in the bottom-left corner and select Settings
  • In the Account settings section, select Memberships
  • Filter creators by paid, find the creator whose membership you want to cancel, and click on it
  • Click the Cancel membership button
  • A pop-up will appear, then Confirm cancellation.
Will I be refunded after I cancel?

No. While canceling turns off auto-renewal, you’ll still have a membership for the year you paid for. For that reason, Patreon won’t refund any amount of what you’ve already paid the creator.

Will I still earn merch if I cancel my annual membership?

If you have an Annual membership, you’ll be charged for one year of membership up front and will start earning your merch after 3 monthly billing periods have passed. Feel free to check the help center article How to Claim my exclusive Patreon merch from a creator to learn more about merch cadences.

This will depend on the date of cancellation and your creator’s merch program.

If your creator is offering a one-time merch item:
  • If you cancel before 3 months have passed, this will interrupt your merch earning cycle
  • If you cancel after the 3 months, this won’t affect any merch earnings because you met the required timeframe to receive your merch item
    • Example: You join on Dec 12 and cancel on Feb 15th - you will still receive your merch item (3 months = 3 successful billings, in this case, Dec, Jan, Feb)
If your creator is on the loyalty program (You receive merch every 3 months):
  • You will need to be an active member for the whole year.
    • Example: You start a membership on Dec 12 and cancel in April; you wouldn’t earn the merch item that would be due on May 12. With an annual membership, you need to remain an active member for the duration of the year.

Annual membership refund policy

Patreon will not issue refunds for annual memberships, except under extraordinary circumstances, which are reviewed and granted at Patreon’s discretion. You are supporting a creator for their past and future work and getting access to content during your term. We cannot guarantee you will always like the quality or quantity of past or future work or that creators will have completed new work within the year, and these factors do not provide you with an automatic refund.

If for any reason you need to request a refund for your annual membership, you’ll need to contact your creator directly with that request. Here are our tips for requesting a refund from a creator: Recommendations for requesting a refund.

Creators can only refund charges within 90 days of the processing date. If a creator needs to issue a refund older than 90 days, they can do so off of Patreon (i.e., on PayPal or Venmo). This is true for both partial and full refunds.

Partial refunds

You may be able to get a prorated refund for the remaining months of your year term at our creator’s discretion. If the creator refunds a prorated amount of your term, you’ll lose access at the end of the month that the refund is issued. Reach out to your creator if you would like to request a prorated refund.

Full refunds

If a creator issues you a full refund for your annual membership, your access to the creator’s member-only content for your tier will be revoked.

You can request a partial or full refund from the creator you support. Please know that a refund of any type (partial or full) will result in a loss of access to the creator’s content.

Can I make a one-time payment?

You can purchase digital products and/or specific posts and collections as a one-time payment without needing a recurring membership. Creators can list their work for sale individually, making it easier for fans who prefer to make one-time payments to access the content they love.

When you purchase a product, the content is immediately unlocked, and you can view it anytime under your Purchases tab.

How to Purchase

Through the creator’s shop:
  • Visit the creator’s page and click on the Shop tab at the top (Note: This option is only available if the creator has a published shop)
  • Alternatively, you can access the shop directly via the link: patreon.com/[creator]/shop (Replace [creator] with the creator’s name)
Through posts and collections:
  • You can also purchase directly from individual posts or collections on the creator’s home if a creator has set their work for sale as a one-time purchase. Simply navigate to the post or collection you’re interested in and click on the Buy button to purchase as a one-time purchase. You can also access this work through a paid membership

Learn more about purchasing products here

Membership

If you’re interested in supporting a creator on an ongoing basis, Patreon continues to offer recurring memberships. You can learn more about how creators bill their members in How membership billing works.

Whether you choose to support creators through a recurring membership or prefer one-time purchases, Patreon offers flexible options to connect with and support the content you love.

Can I use PayPal on Patreon?

How does PayPal work with Patreon?

You can authorize your PayPal account as your payment method for your Patreon memberships. When we process your payment(s), we’ll use your linked PayPal wallet funding source.

PayPal requires an instant funding source for recurring subscriptions, such as Patreon memberships; however, they will always attempt to use your PayPal balance first. Only when there is not enough in your balance to cover a payment will PayPal use the funding source (e.g., a bank account or a credit card) you selected when going through the PayPal flow on Patreon.

  • How to add a new PayPal account to Patreon

Please note that beginning March 7, 2022, consumers in Thailand will no longer be able to use PayPal as a payment method as a result of new local regulations. Thailand-based consumers can update their payment method to Credit Card or Apple Pay.

Do I need a credit card to use PayPal with Patreon?

You can link a credit card during the Patreon checkout process. You can also use a bank account as your funding source; however, you’ll need to add it directly to your PayPal wallet.

Will pre-paid cards work?

A pre-paid or gift credit card is typically not accepted for recurring subscription payments. For this reason, we recommend using a credit card issued and linked to a bank account.

How do I use a bank account?

Our current PayPal flow does not allow for bank authorization. If you’d like to use a bank account for your PayPal funding source, you can add your account directly to your PayPal wallet.

Here’s how to add your bank account to your PayPal wallet: How do I add a bank to my PayPal account?

Once you’ve added your bank account to your PayPal wallet, you can add PayPal to Patreon and select your bank account during the authorization process.

Canceling a free membership

You can keep your free membership as long as you’d like; however, you can cancel if you no longer wish to receive updates about the creator’s work. This article has instructions for canceling a free membership on a Desktop and on the Patreon app for iOS and Android. If you need to stop recurring payments for a membership, please visit our canceling a paid membership page for detailed instructions.

- Click Settings from the left-side menu (if you're also a creator, click Your account in the bottom-left corner and select Settings )
- On your Settings page, click the [Memberships](https://www.patreon.com/settings/memberships) tab (if you're also a creator, go to the Account settings section and click on Memberships)
- Locate your free membership, and click More
- Click Cancel membership
- Your free membership is canceled — you can rejoin whenever you’d like
- Tap the shortcut at the top left corner of the Home screen to see a list of the creators you support
- In the Free section, tap on the desired creator from the list
- Tap More in the top right corner of the screen
- Tap on Your membership
- Tap on Leave membership
- Your free membership is canceled — you can rejoin whenever you’d like

Canceling a paid membership

If you’re unable to cancel your membership or see unexpected charges, we’re here to help. This guide walks you through how to cancel your membership on both desktop and mobile. You’ll also find answers to common billing and account questions in the FAQ section below.

🔐 Security tip: If you notice unfamiliar charges or can’t find your membership, try resetting your password. This can help identify if you have multiple accounts.

Canceling a paid membership

Choose your device below for step-by-step instructions:

- Log in to your account and switch to your member profile (if applicable)
- → Click your profile picture in the bottom-left corner to check or switch profiles
- Click the Settings link from the left-side menu
- Go to the [Memberships](https://www.patreon.com/settings/memberships) tab ([this link will take you there](https://www.patreon.com/settings/memberships))
- Locate your membership, and click the View Details button
- Click on Cancel membership, then confirm cancellation
- Decide whether to stay connected as a free member or toggle off this option and click Save and continue
- Optionally, complete the anonymous exit survey to share feedback with the creator
- Open the app and switch to your member profile (if applicable). You can switch between member and creator profiles (if you have one) by tapping on your profile image in the top right corner and tapping the Switch to button
- Scroll through the creators listed at the top of the Home screen and tap on the desired creator from the list
- Tap the three dots button in the upper right corner of the creator's Home screen and then select Your membership
- Choose Edit membership, then tap Cancel membership
- Scroll down and Confirm cancellation
- Manage your free membership option and tap Save and Continue
- Optionally, complete the anonymous exit survey to provide feedback

If you face any issues, send us a message for assistance.

FAQ

  • Your membership won’t renew for the next billing period.
  • If the creator uses per-creation billing, you might have a final charge for paid posts made before your cancellation.
  • You may have already canceled. Check your Billing History under Settings for past payments. If you see past payments and the creator is no longer listed in your Memberships, then you’ve unsubscribed.
  • Or
  • The creator may have removed your membership.
  • Or
  • You might have another account. Reset your password to check for accounts tied to other emails.
  • You may have another account. Try resetting your password with all possible email addresses. If you’re still being charged, contact support.
  • Patreon doesn’t typically offer refunds since payments go directly to creators. If you believe a charge was made in error, send us a message for review.
  • You’ll retain access to paid content until the end of your billing period. After that, access ends unless you re-subscribe.
  • Yes, you can re-subscribe to any creator at any time.
  • Patreon doesn’t currently offer a pause feature. To temporarily stop payments, you’ll need to cancel and re-subscribe later.
  • Creators aren’t directly notified when you cancel, but they may notice changes in their membership count.
  • Canceling before your billing date ensures you won’t be charged for the next period. Confirm the cancellation in your Memberships tab to avoid unexpected charges.

Account Security Tip: If you suspect your account is compromised, reset your password immediately. Consider updating passwords for other platforms if they are reused.

Charge upfront billing explained

This article details how charge upfront billing works, and what happens when you cancel or make changes to a charge upfront membership. Keep reading to learn more, or click the links below to jump ahead:

  • How charge upfront billing works
  • Upgrading your membership
  • Downgrading your membership
  • Canceling your membership
  • How Annual memberships work
  • FAQs

How charge upfront billing works

With upfront billing, you are charged when you join and then on the first of every month. The first charge unlocks access to membership benefits like the creator’s backlog of exclusive posts and you can start engaging with the creator’s Patreon community from day one. Charges on the first of the month give you access to membership benefits for that month (i.e., your June 1st charge gives you access for all of June).

Your Billing history lists all past payments with their corresponding date.

We process payments in Pacific Time (PT). If you are subscribing on the first of the month, check what time it is in PT first. For example, if you join on January 31st at 11:59 PT, your next billing date will be February 1st.

Upgrading your membership

When you upgrade or increase the value of your charge upfront membership, you’ll be charged the difference between your original tier value and your new tier value immediately. You’ll be charged your upgraded membership value in full on the first of the month.

For example:

  • On March 20th you start your membership at $10 and are charged upfront
  • On April 1 your membership renews and you pay $10
  • On April 15 you upgrade to the creator’s $15 tier – you pay a difference of $5 ($15 - $10 = $5)
  • On May 1 your membership renews at your new membership price and you are charged $15

Downgrading your membership

If you downgrade or decrease the value of your charge upfront membership, you won’t be charged to downgrade and you won’t receive a refund. When you downgrade, you keep your original tier access until the end of your membership period. You’ll be charged your downgraded membership value on the first of the month.

For example:

  • On January 7 you start your membership and are charged $15 upfront
  • On January 26 you downgrade your membership to the $5 tier. You keep your $15 membership access for the rest of January and are considered a $15 patron during that time
  • On February 1 your membership renews at your downgraded $5 amount, and you lose your higher membership access. The creator will see you listed as a $5 patron on their end

Canceling your upfront membership

Charge upfront memberships renew on the first of each month (midnight Pacific Time) until canceled. Canceling on the first of the month will not cancel pending first-of-the-month payments, and you won’t be refunded for any first-of-the-month payments already processed. We recommend canceling on the last day of a month to ensure your membership does not renew on the first.

When you cancel, you’ll keep your membership access for the remainder of your membership period (the end of the month).

For example:

  • On August 12 you start a membership and are charged $5
  • On September 1 your membership renews and you’re charged $5 for September access
  • On September 13 you cancel your membership. The creator is removed from your memberships list, but you’ll still have membership access for your tier for the rest of September
  • On October 1 your membership does not renew, and your membership access ends. You appear as a canceled patron on the creator’s account

How annual membership works with CUF

Some creators may offer annual membership access. With this option, patrons pay for the full year upfront to unlock membership access. Annual membership will automatically renew after one year on the first of the following month.

For example:

  • On August 7, 2024, you start an annual membership at $9.60
  • On September 1, 2025, your annual membership auto-renews and you are charged $9.60

If you upgrade your annual membership, pro-rated credit from what you’ve already paid is applied to the new amount, and you pay the remaining cost for upgrading. When you make changes to an annual membership, it extends your year term from that date.

Here are two examples:

  • If you paid for a $120 tier and upgrade in the same month to a $140 tier, you pay $20 for the difference between the two
  • If you paid $120 in April and upgrade in June to a $140 tier, only $100 from your initial payment is left, so you’ll pay $40 to upgrade

In both of the above examples, your membership auto-renews in a year and you pay your new membership amount of $140 in full.

How Annual Memberships work

Frequently asked questions about charge upfront billing

When will I receive all of my membership benefits?

Once you’ve successfully started your membership, you’ll have access to things like the creator’s Patreon-exclusive posts. If the creator offers access to their Discord server, you’ll be able to link your Discord and Patreon accounts immediately to be assigned your member role.

For benefits that aren’t managed by Patreon (i.e., physical benefits, or benefits delivered by the creator via messages), we recommend reaching out to the creator for time estimates.

I joined near the end of the month, will I still be charged on the 1st of the month?

Yes — you’ll be charged on the 1st of each month regardless of your join date. If you sign up on the 30th or 31st, you can expect a second charge on the 1st.

What does credit mean?

If you have a charge upfront membership, this credit is the amount you have already paid the creator for the current month

If you rejoin or upgrade, we credit you the amount you originally paid the creator at checkout.

Charged more than my membership amount

You can review your monthly billing details by visiting your Billing History while logged in to your Patreon account. The examples throughout this article are in US Dollar ($), however, it is possible that you could be billed in Euro (€) or British Pounds (£) depending on your billing currency. If you were charged more for your membership than you anticipated, it may be due to one of the reasons below.

No monthly max for a per-creation membership

Some creators on the legacy billing model (not available to new creators) are charging members per-creation, rather than a subscription billing. This means you are charged your membership fee for each paid post the creator publishes in a given month.

For example: You joined at $5 USD per post with no monthly max set. If your creator makes 4 paid posts, you’ll be billed for each one, and your monthly bill will total $20 USD.

To ensure you’re only ever charged the amount you’re comfortable paying, navigate to your Memberships page, click the View details button next to the creator, and enter a monthly max into the field shown.

For detailed steps, please visit How do I set a monthly max for my membership?

If you need a refund for a per-creation charge, contact Patreon Product Support, since they can’t be refunded through Billing History. For more details, visit our guide on How to request a refund.

Declined payments from previous months

If you have a declined payment in your billing history, note that we’ll attempt to charge you again. A retry can be triggered when you update your payment details, or if you attempt to re-pledge to a creator you had been declined with. We’ll retry your declined payment when you confirm your membership summary details. After ~30 days of payment declines, you’ll be converted to free member.

Please note that members whose payments were stuck in decline since before January 2024 had their memberships cancelled as of March 2026.

If you need assistance with retrying a declined payment, please refer to our dedicated guide: Failed payment help.

VAT (Value Added Tax)

We are required to charge VAT (Value Added Tax) to European members’ payments. Your fee breakdown will be listed when you make a pledge, however, added VAT won’t be reflected in your list of pledges on your homepage.

For more info on VAT, check out the article on How VAT works for creators on Patreon

Note: We charge your VAT based on the location you indicate in your Profile Settings page. If you’ve stated that you’re located in Germany, we will add German VAT to all of your memberships. If you’ve not indicated your country of residence, we will use your IP address to identify your location and VAT eligibility. Ensuring that your country of residence in your Profile Settings page is up to date is the best way to ensure you are charged the proper VAT amount.

Failed payment help

We understand how frustrating it can be when a payment doesn’t go through, especially when you’re eager to join a creator’s Patreon. The good news is that most payment issues can be resolved quickly by updating your payment details. To help you get back on track, we’ve outlined simple steps below to retry your payment and ensure uninterrupted access to your membership.

Retrying a failed payment

If your payment fails, we will automatically retry your payment method. However, you can manually retry your payment at any time by following the instructions below.

  • Follow these steps while on your member profile. You can check which profile you’re on by clicking your picture in the bottom left corner.
    • Click the Settings link from the left navigation
    • Click Memberships in the top menu bar
    • Click View details for the creator
    • From here, you can choose a different payment method or click the Edit link next to the failing payment method to trigger a retry
    • If your payment continues to fail, try adding a different payment method
  • Follow these steps while on your member profile. You can switch between member and creator profiles (if you have one) by tapping on your profile image in the top right corner and tapping the Switch to button for the profile you’d like to visit
    • Scroll through the creators listed at the top of the Home screen
    • Double-tap on the desired creator from the list
    • Tap the three dots button in the upper right corner of the creator’s Home screen
    • Tap on Your membership
    • Tap Edit membership
    • Tap on Edit payment method
    • You can choose to either Update your payment method by selecting an existing one from your account, or you can follow the on-screen steps to Add a new payment method

Other things to check

Should you still experience issues after retrying a payment, please check that your payment method has sufficient funds and is:

  • Not expired or canceled
  • Enabled for foreign, secure online, and recurring purchases — Look for these settings in your bank’s mobile app

You can also check that your bank or payment provider has your correct details (e.g., name, address, zip, etc.). If you add a new payment method, they may need to verify your identity for security, e.g. with a password, PIN, fingerprint, or code sent to your device

Turn on backup payments from your settings so that your membership isn’t interrupted if your payment fails.

Still not working?

If the payment continues to fail, there may be an authorization issue with the card network or issuing bank. If a payment continues to fail, you can:

  • Enabled for foreign, secure online, and recurring purchases from your bank’s mobile app or by calling your bank directly. There may be restrictions that exclude membership transactions
  • If you’re paying with PayPal, contact PayPal’s support team. They can check your account and assist with next steps

Please note that we’re unable to process transactions with gift credit cards. Since all memberships are auto-renewing, we require a bank-issued card for payments

Add backup payments

An easy way to avoid losing access to your membership benefits due to failed payments is adding backup payments to your account. Once turned on, your backup payment method will kick in automatically if your primary payment method fails.

To turn back up payments on a Computer or Mobile web

  • Visit Settings > More > Payment methods
  • Click the Turn on backup payments button
  • Click the Continue button to add your backup method or the Turn on button if you have another method already on file
  • You can turn off backup payments at any time

More about backup payments

  • Turning on backup payments applies to all your memberships, including future memberships. You’ll get an email before a backup payment method is used
  • Other membership settings, including price and when you’re charged, aren’t changing. Only how payments are made when a payment fails

FAQ

  • A failed payment can happen when a payment is not processed successfully. Here are some common reasons that payments may fail:
    • Insufficient funds
    • Expired credit card information
    • Incorrect payment details
    • The issuing bank has blocked the transaction
    • Patreon’s authorization has been revoked (most often with PayPal)
    • Card network or issuing bank authorization issues if it is the first time the payment method is used
  • You can contact your bank or PayPal for more information on why a payment has failed. Asking that they authorize future payments from Patreon may fix recurring issues.
  • If you’ve filed a PayPal dispute for Patreon in the past, you’ll need to add a new funding source to your wallet to continue using PayPal for Patreon payments. Filing a dispute with PayPal for a charge revokes our access to process payments on that PayPal funding source.
  • Patreon automatically retries failed membership payments. We’ll send members an email letting them know that the payment has failed. We don’t send the creator an email about the failed payment, however, they can see your billing status in their audience relationship manager.
  • Please note that after ~30 days of payment declines, you’ll be converted to free member. Members whose payments were stuck in decline since before January 2024, had their memberships cancelled as of March 2026.
  • If you’ve turned on backup payments, we’ll retry your payment with a different method if the original payment method fails. You’ll get an email before a backup payment is used.
  • We’ll send a confirmation email when a payment is processed successfully.
  • Membership access relies on a successful payment. If your payment fails, you won’t have membership access until the payment goes through. After ~30 days of failed payment retries, you will be converted to free member.

How do I update my payment information?

If your payment method is declined after a few attempts, we recommend trying a different one. Please note that after ~30 days of payment declines, you’ll be converted to free member. Members whose payments were stuck in decline since before January 2024, had their memberships cancelled as of March 2026.

For any support with retrying a declined payment, please refer to the guide Failed payment help.

How to add a new payment method

Click on your device type below for steps to update your payment information.

  • Follow these steps while on your Member profile. You can check which profile you’re on by clicking your profile picture in the bottom left corner.
    • Click the Settings link from the left sidebar navigation
    • From the menubar, click on More > Payment Methods
    • Click on Add payment method
    • Click the Card or PayPal button
    • Enter your card details and click Add, or select PayPal and click Add to log in to your account
    • If you want to transfer your existing memberships to your new payment method, you need to delete the payment method currently used for your membership
    • When you click Delete, a message will appear, asking you to Choose a new payment method for your memberships
    • Select the new payment method you’ve just added, click Next
    • A confirmation message will appear, letting you know your memberships have been updated. Click Done to confirm
  • Follow these steps while on your member profile. You can switch between member and creator profiles (if you have one) by tapping on your profile image in the top right corner and tapping the Switch to button for the profile you’d like to visit
    • Scroll through the creators listed at the top of the Home screen
    • Double-tap on the desired creator from the list
    • Tap the three dots button in the upper right corner of the creator’s Home screen
    • Tap on Your membership
    • Tap Edit membership
    • Tap on Edit payment method
    • Tap on Add a new payment method and follow the steps on the screen to add a new payment method of your choice. Once you finish, your membership will be automatically linked to the new payment method
    • You can change the payment method anytime by following these steps again and either selecting an existing payment method if you’ve added one before or adding a new one

If your card authorization declines, contact your bank and request that they accept all future charges from Patreon * Membership before reattempting.

If you get the message, Card already added to this account, exit the window and click Retry or Update next to your expired Card.

How to update your payment method

Need to make changes to your PayPal account? Log in to your PayPal account to update your wallet funding source.

Follow these steps while on your member profile. You can check which profile you’re on by clicking your picture in the bottom left corner

Here’s how to update a credit card on your Patreon account:

  • Click the Settings from the left sidebar navigation
  • From the menubar, click on More > Payment Methods
  • Click on the Edit button next to your credit card
  • Re-enter your credit card details with your updated expiration date, CVV, or billing zip code
  • Click on Add to confirm

How to remove a payment method

When deleting a payment method associated with any memberships, you’ll be asked if you want to transfer your membership(s) to a new or existing payment method. If you want to cancel your memberships instead, please follow this guide to cancel your membership(s).

How to delete a payment method

Follow these steps while on your member profile. You can check which profile you’re on by clicking your picture in the bottom left corner.

  • Click the Settings link from the left navigation
  • From the menubar, click on More > Payment Methods
  • Click Delete next to the payment method you want to delete
  • If the payment method you’re deleting is linked to any memberships, a message will appear asking you to Choose a new payment method — You can select an existing one or Add a new payment method
  • Follow the on-screen steps depending on what you choose
  • After unlinking any memberships from the payment method, click the Delete button to confirm payment method removal

Deleting a payment method with linked memberships will result in an immediate cancelation of those memberships. If this happens, you can re-activate your membership by rejoining the creator’s page from your Billing history.

Removing a payment method with linked memberships will not delete pending payments or declined bills made when you were an active member.

How iOS in-app purchases work for fans

All creators are now using subscription billing. If your account was still on a legacy billing model on November 1, 2026, we switched it automatically and emailed you when the switch was complete.

Key details depending on your previous billing model:

  • Per-creation: If you haven’t resumed billing yet, it stays paused until you review your new tier prices. Learn how to resume billing
  • First-of-the-month: Your existing members are still billed on the 1st of each month. New members are billed on the date they join

If you’re a creator looking to educate your fans on the impact of Apple’s App Store Fee, you can send or reference this article.

Apple is requiring Patreon to use its in-app purchasing system for purchases made in the iOS app in order for it to remain on the App Store for all fans and creators. This article details what’s changing and how it impacts memberships and sales initiated on the Patreon iOS app starting in November 2024.

What changed

As of November 2024, new purchases, including new memberships and digital goods made in the Patreon iOS app, are subject to Apple’s 30% App Store Fee.

The App Store fee does not apply to existing memberships and memberships made on other platforms.

For iOS users in the U.S.: Fans in the U.S. have the option to complete their purchase through Patreon’s mobile web checkout instead of using Apple’s in-app purchase flow. Purchases completed on the mobile web are not subject to Apple’s App Store fee.

How this impacts creators’ pricing

This change is required by Apple to keep the Patreon app on the App Store, meaning that this change will impact all creators. Creators control how Apple’s fee is applied to their membership tiers and digital goods prices in the iOS app by choosing one of the following options:

  • Increase the prices of the membership tiers and digital goods sold in the iOS app. This will help creators earn the same across platforms despite the Apple fee and is the default option
  • Keep prices the same across all platforms. This means that the creator absorbs the Apple App Store fee themselves and therefore earns less from sales in the iOS app

Unless creators choose to absorb the Apple App Store Fee themselves, new transactions in the Patreon iOS app will be more expensive than the same purchase on the web because of Apple’s App Store Fee. Please note that for any fan in the U.S., the default price will be the same as your web prices. These fans will only see the higher prices if they choose Apple’s in-app purchase system over web checkout, which is the default view and doesn’t include Apple’s fee.

If a member signed up before November 4, 2024, their ongoing membership won’t be impacted by the Apple fee. New members who signed up in the iOS app after November 4, 2024, may be charged a higher price on iOS because Apple charges a 30% processing fee. Creators control how the Apple App Store fee is applied to the price of their membership tiers, which means price differences may vary from creator to creator.

Example of how the Apple App Store fee affects the price of a membership sold on iOS:

How membership billing works

All creators are now using subscription billing. If your account was still on a legacy billing model on November 1, 2026, we switched it automatically and emailed you when the switch was complete.

Key details depending on your previous billing model:

  • Per-creation: If you haven’t resumed billing yet, it stays paused until you review your new tier prices. Learn how to resume billing
  • First-of-the-month: Your existing members are still billed on the 1st of each month. New members are billed on the date they join

Creators on Patreon use subscription billing: you’re charged when you join a paid membership and then on the same day each month. If you joined before your creator switched to subscription billing in November 2026, your billing date may be different. See below.

Sales tax will be applied to a membership payment where applicable. Patreon is required by law to add sales tax (including VAT or other similar taxes) to some payments made by members. Learn more about Patreon’s sales tax requirements.

Subscription billing

If a creator has subscription billing enabled, members are billed when they join a creator’s membership and then on the same day of each month thereafter. For example, if a member joins on the 5th of a month, they’ll be billed on the 5th of each month thereafter.

However, if a member is billed on the Nth day of each month but a subsequent month doesn’t have N days, the member is billed on the final day of that shorter month, and their billing day resets to that new day.

For example, if a member joins on March 31st, they’ll be billed again on April 30th and then on the 30th of each month thereafter. If they reach February and that February has 29 days (because it’s a leap year), they’ll be billed on February 29th and then on the 29th of each subsequent month. After a year of being billed on the 29th, that member would reach February with only 28 days, and their billing day would reset to the 28th day of each month thereafter.

Payments are processed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). Depending on your time zone, you might be charged up to 24 hours before the scheduled payment date

We regularly retry failed membership payments and notify members when a payment hasn’t gone through, so they can resolve the issue. Members whose payment retries repeatedly fail for ~30 days will be converted to free members.

If you joined before your creator switched models
  • If your creator charged a monthly price on the 1st of the month: you’re still charged on the 1st of each month
  • If your creator billed per creation: your membership now has a set monthly price, charged on the 1st of each month. If you set a monthly limit, you won’t pay more than that limit unless your creator changes your price. If your price increases, we’ll notify you, and the new price applies from the following billing cycle
  • Your creator may have paused billing while they review their new prices. You won’t be charged for the time billing was paused

Annual membership

Annual membership is a billing option where you pay upfront for a year of membership. You’re charged when you sign up and then yearly on your join date. Learn more details about Annual membership.

FAQ

  • The names of creators you support will not be included in your statement. Your payment will be processed as Patreon and listed as one of the following line items:
  • Credit card
  • PayPal
    • PATREON* Membership
    • CKO Patreon* Membership
    • PAYPAL *PATREON IN
  • Yes. If your payment declines, you can cancel your membership. We’ll stop retrying the payment, and you’ll lose access to paid benefits.
  • Creator’s billing model
  • What happens when you cancel
  • Subscription billing
  • If a member cancels before their next billing date, they retain their membership access until the next billing date (which depends on your join date).
  • Due to timezone differences, we recommend canceling at least 24 hours before your next billing date if you don’t want your bill to renew.
  • Annual membership
  • If you cancel your annual membership before your next charge date, you’ll retain your membership access for the remainder of the year you paid for. You’ll lose membership access after your next billing date.
  • Creator’s billing model
  • When you upgrade
  • Subscription billing
  • When members upgrade to a higher membership level, their billing date does not change. They’ll be charged the outstanding amount immediately and get access to the higher tier membership for the remainder of their billing period.
  • They’ll be charged their upgraded membership amount on their next billing date.
  • Annual membership
  • When a member upgrades an annual membership, the system credits a prorated amount for what they’ve already paid, and they pay the remaining upgrade cost.
  • When you update an annual membership, it extends your term for a year from that date.
  • Creator’s billing model
  • When you switch to a lower tier

  • If you believe you’ve been overcharged, first check your payment statement in your Billing history on Patreon. Reviewing a few months of billing may help you confirm where the additional amount is coming from—declining bills that process later can be alarming if you don’t know what they’re for.
  • If you have separate charges on your payment statement that don’t add up, you may have more than one account triggering charges. Please log out and then use password reset. You can enter other email addresses you own outside of your known account. If you get the message that we’ve sent you a password reset link to one of your other emails, you also have an account with that email address.

How to change your tier: a guide for members

This article provides instructions for changing your membership tier and what you can expect if you upgrade or downgrade your membership, depending on the creator’s billing model. If you wish to cancel your membership instead, please refer to Canceling a Membership.

How to change your tier

- Go to the creator's page
- Click More , then click Your subscription
- Scroll down and click Show more tiers
- If the creator offers lower tiers that you’d like to switch to, click on More tiers
- Select the tier you want to change to and click on the Subscribe button
- Review the payment details and order summary, and once you’re ready, click on Subscribe now
- Scroll through the creators listed at the top of the Home screen
- Double-tap on the desired creator from the list
- Tap More in the upper right corner of the creator's Home screen
- Tap on Your membership
- Tap on Edit membership
- Tap on Change membership
- Tap the Join button for your new tier, and follow the prompts to make the switch
  • Important: Memberships made with iOS in-app purchases must be edited via the iOS app. If you no longer have access to an iOS device, you can cancel your membership on web or mobile web and then resubscribe on your new device.

What happens if you upgrade your tier?

Creator’s billing model

When you upgrade

Subscription billing

When you upgrade to a higher membership tier, your billing date remains the same. You’ll be charged the outstanding amount immediately and gain access to the higher tier for the remainder of your billing period.

You’ll be charged the upgraded membership amount on your next billing date.

Per creation

You’ll get immediate access to the higher tier membership. Your higher membership applies to future paid posts up to your monthly max.

We won’t exceed your monthly limit, so you may not be billed for additional paid posts.

Monthly charge upfront

Payments already made for the month are credited toward the upgrade, and you pay the difference.

You will then pay your higher membership amount on the 1st of the month.

Monthly (non-charge upfront)

You’ll get immediate access to the higher tier membership.

There’s no charge to upgrade, and you pay your higher membership amount on the 1st of the month.

Annual membership

A pro-rated amount of what you’ve already paid is credited, and you pay the remaining upgrade cost.

When you upgrade an annual membership, it extends your term for a year from that date.

What happens if you switch to a lower tier?

Creator’s billing model

When you upgrade

Subscription billing

You’ll remain on your original tier until the next billing date.

You’ll have access to the lower-tier membership on your next billing date.

Per creation

Decreasing your membership will not change the amount of any pending bills already posted to your Billing history.

Your lower amount will be applied to future paid posts if your monthly limit has not already been met.

Monthly charge upfront

Decreasing your membership does not affect the current month’s membership access. Since you’ve already paid for the month upfront, decreasing affects your membership renewal on the upcoming first of the month.

We recommend switching to a lower tier closer to the end of the month for a smooth transition.

Monthly (non-charge upfront)

If you decrease your membership, your access is instantly limited to the new (downgraded) tier that you’ve joined.

Annual membership

At the moment, there’s no way to change your annual membership to a lower tier.

You can, however, join a lower tier after your year membership has ended with a slight workaround — You can cancel your membership near the end of your year term and then rejoin at a lower-tier option once the year has passed.

How to request a refund

Before proceeding, we recommend reviewing Patreon’s Terms of Use and Refund Policy. Patreon is a platform that facilitates payments from members to their creators. When we process a member’s payment, we send it to the supported creator’s balance. If you need to request a refund, please follow the instructions outlined below.

Requesting a refund directly from your Billing history

You don’t need to message creators directly to ask for a refund. You can request a refund right from your Billing history, within 60 days of the original payment. If you’re outside that window, you will be directed to contact Product Support:

  • In your settings, go to Billing History
  • Find the payment you’d like refunded
  • Click the three dots next to it
  • Select Request refund from the menu
  • Choose from a list of common reasons and provide additional written context, or select Something else and write your own
  • Once you have filled in all the information, Submit the request

After you submit, the creator will review it and decide whether to approve or decline it. You’ll be notified when they take action.

Creators are responsible for benefits and content distribution. While it is discouraged, it does not violate our terms if a creator doesn’t deliver expected benefits.

Per-creation charges: This refund request flow doesn’t support per-creation transactions. If you were charged per creation, please contact Patreon Product Support for help with your refund.

How to request a refund via Patreon Product Support

If you’re unable to request a refund directly from your Billing history, contact Patreon Product Support and provide documentation showing that products, services, or benefits were not delivered within the agreed-upon timelines.

Patreon will investigate the refund claim and determine whether to award or deny the request. If Patreon finds it in the fan’s favor, the refund amount will be deducted from the creator’s account balance.

How to request refunds for iOS in-app purchases

If you’ve purchased a digital product through the iOS Patreon app, you can also request a refund for your purchase through Apple. To do this, you would need to go through the Apple refund flow with your Apple ID. Apple will process refunds within 60 days of the purchase taking place. Whether you request a refund from a creator or from Apple, if the refund is granted, you will receive the full amount you paid back to your Apple account.

What if the creator declines the refund?

Since we have credited your payment to the creators’ balance, they can decide whether to approve the full refund or decline it. That said, Patreon may issue refunds at our sole discretion. Please be aware that requesting a refund does not guarantee that it will be approved. Patreon will review your refund request, and you will receive a notice of whether the refund is approved or denied. If a refund is issued, it can take 7-10 business days to process.

How to set a monthly max for a membership

Please note that per-creation memberships are only available to creators using the legacy billing model. All creators still using legacy billing must switch to subscription billing by November 1, 2026.

When you become a member to a creator who is charging per-post, you have the option of setting a monthly limit to your payments. This prevents you from being charged more than you’re comfortable with, if the creator makes several paid posts in a given month.

While the examples below are in US Dollars ($), you may be billed in one of our supported currencies, depending on the currency the creator chooses to bill in. To find a list of supported currencies, please visit our guide on Member currency settings on Patreon.

Setting a limit when you first confirm your membership

After clicking Become a Member for a per-post creator and choosing your tier, you will be brought to a membership confirmation page where you can set a monthly limit:

  • Select the I’d like to set a monthly limit button
  • Enter the maximum number of posts you’d like to support in a given month at your membership amount (e.g. 2 times per month at my $10 amount is a $20 max). This number indicates how many times you can be billed in a month, not the total monthly amount
  • Click the Update button to confirm

You’ll only ever be billed up to your monthly limit in a given month.

Setting a monthly limit while your membership is already active

You can set up a monthly limit to your membership at any time. You can also edit or remove your monthly max if you’d like.

Follow the steps below to set a monthly limit after you’ve already confirmed your membership:

  • Click the Settings link from the left sidebar navigation
  • Then click on the Active Memberships link from the menubar
  • Click the Edit link for the membership
  • On the following page, select the I’d like set a monthly limit button. In the field that appears, enter the maximum number of times you’d like to be billed in a given month. This number indicates how many times you can be billed in a month, not the total monthly amount
  • Click the Update button to save the change, and your monthly limit will be set up

Setting a monthly limit will not remove any already pending bills on your account. So if you’ve already been billed for a creator’s paid posts, setting a monthly max will not retroactively remove those pending bills. You can check your billing history for a breakdown of all bills created for your account.

Increasing your payment amount (not upgrading tier)

To join a membership tier, you must pay the minimum price the creator has set for that tier. This article explains how you can increase your payment to a creator to more than their minimum tier price. Increasing your payment is great if you prefer membership access to a lower-priced tier and want to give more. If you want to increase your payment amount to that creator without upgrading to a higher tier, keep reading below.

If you want to get the membership access granted by a higher tier, you’ll need to upgrade your membership tier. Increasing your payment amount is a way to give the creator more and stay in your current membership tier. Learn more about Changing your tier here.

If a higher-priced tier is sold out, we recommend contacting the creator to request that they increase the number of member spots in that tier.

How to increase your payment amount

  • Follow these instructions while viewing your member profile. You can switch between member and creator profiles (if you have one) by clicking your picture in the bottom left corner and selecting the profile you’d like to visit.
    • Go to the creator’s page
    • Click More and select Your membership
    • Click Edit for your current tier
    • Select Edit next to your payment amount
    • Select Custom amount, click on the price field, and then enter the amount you’d like to pay for your membership (it must be higher than the minimum price for the tier)
      • If your creator is on per-creation billing, you can type the amount directly under Choose what you pay
    • Click the Subscribe now or Continue with PayPal to confirm your changes
      • Tap on your creator list in the top upper right corner
      • Double-tap on the desired creator from the list
      • Tap More
      • Tap on Your membership
      • Tap on Edit membership
      • Tap on Change membership
      • Tap on the Custom amount field and enter an amount higher than your current membership tier
        • If your creator is on per-creation billing, you can type the amount directly under Choose what you pay
      • Tap Update
  • Members who join a creator’s page via iOS in-app purchase can upgrade to a higher tier. However, setting a custom payment amount is not currently supported.

What happens after I increase my membership payment amount?

Your membership access and perks will remain the same. If you choose to increase your payment amount without upgrading your membership tier, you’ll continue to enjoy the same tier benefits while paying more than the minimum required amount.

Depending on the creator’s payment schedule, if you join a higher tier, you may immediately be charged the difference between your previous tier and your new tier. If the creator uses our per-creation (legacy billing) or 1st-of-the-month billing, you won’t be charged immediately.

Learn more about creator billing options.

Paying with Sofort

Sofort is no longer an accepted payment method on Patreon. If your membership was funded via Sofort (shown as bank account in your settings), please update your payment method to a credit card or PayPal to keep your membership active

Using Apple Pay as your payment method

Checkout is quick and easy using Apple Pay. In this article, you’ll learn how to enable it, make payments with it, and how to remove it if you’d like to.

As of November 2024, new purchases, including new memberships and digital goods made in the Patreon iOS app, are subject to Apple’s 30% App Store Fee. The App Store fee does not apply to existing memberships and memberships made on other platforms.

For iOS users in the U.S.: Fans can complete their purchase through Patreon’s mobile web checkout instead of using Apple’s in-app purchase flow. Purchases completed on the mobile web are not subject to Apple’s App Store fee.

Enable Apple Pay as your payment method

If you would like to use Apple Pay for your Patreon memberships, you’ll first want to ensure the following:

  • A compatible device with the latest version of iOS or iPadOS, watchOS, macOS, or visionOS
  • A supported card from a participating card issuer
  • An Apple ID signed in to your Apple device
  • Face ID, Touch ID, Optic ID, or a passcode set on your device

To make sure your device has the payment service enabled and ready to use, check the steps to Set up Apple Pay.

Pay for your memberships with Apple Pay

Please note that we present Apple Pay as an option only when the device meets Apple’s criteria and guidelines.

When you’re ready to join a creator’s page, we’ll prompt you to select a payment method. Here’s how you select Apple Pay at checkout:

  • Tap the Join button on the tier you’d like to sign up for
  • If you’re in the iOS app, the Apple Pay payment prompt will open
    • If you’re in the browser, select Add new payment method, tap the Apple Pay button, and then select Subscribe now at the bottom
  • Select your preferred card and confirm payment through Apple Pay
  • Checkout is complete

After this step, a welcome message will greet you with more information about your membership.

Remove Apple Pay as your payment method

If you no longer wish to use Apple Pay for your memberships, you can switch payment methods by doing the following:

  • Log in to Patreon on a browser and select Settings from the left menu bar
  • In the top menu bar, choose More and then Payment methods
  • Select Payment Methods from the top menu bar
  • Find the payment method you want to remove and select the Delete button next to it
  • Once your memberships are transferred to a new payment method, you can select the Delete button in the pop-up

If you need help managing your payment methods, please check our dedicated article How do I update my payment information?

FAQ

  • The only way to use Apple Pay is to add it while pledging to a new membership or editing a current membership on an Apple device.
  • Yes, you can change your payment method by logging into your Patreon account and going to your Memberships in your settings. If you need further assistance managing a payment method, please check our guide on How do I update my payment information?
  • To use Apple Pay, you’ll need to ensure it is enabled. Please review our section on enabling Apple Pay for assistance.
  • Yes, Euros and Pounds are supported. For the full list of countries and currencies supported, please check our guide for the iOS in-app purchase system.
  • When payments decline through Apple Pay, it may be due to the Apple Pay card being added from a device that is no longer used. Apple Pay is device-specific, so if you received a new phone and Apple Pay was disabled on the old device, you will need to re-add Apple Pay in the pledge flow.
  • If Apple Pay is still declining, we recommend contacting your bank to ensure nothing is blocking payments or authorizations to Patreon. Once resolved, you can attempt to resolve the declined bill again. Please note that after ~30 days of payment declines, you’ll be converted to free member. Members whose payments were stuck in decline since before January 2024, had their memberships cancelled as of March 2026.

What does credit mean?

If you paid upfront or annually, you may notice a credit in the Summary section of the checkout page.

What does credit mean?

  • If you have a monthly charge upfront membership, this credit is the amount you have already paid the creator for the current month
    • If you rejoin or upgrade, we credit you the amount you originally paid the creator at checkout
  • If you have an annual membership, this credit is the amount leftover from your original yearly payment

In both cases, if you downgrade or delete your membership, you won’t receive a refund. Credit is non-transferable to another membership since the original creator has already received that payment.

What happens when I cancel?

BASICS

  • What you can expect after canceling depends on the billing model the creator has chosen
  • When you cancel the creator is removed from your Active memberships page
  • You can refer to your Billing history as your source of truth for payments we’ve processed
  • If you cancel a monthly (non-charge upfront) or per creation membership, you’ll lose access when you cancel
  • If you cancel a charge upfront or subscription billing membership, you’ll retain access until your next billing date

How do I know my creator’s billing model?

  • You’ll know that your creator used subscription billing if the processing date is listed as any day of the month and the Details section month matches the processing month (i.e., August 10th bills list the Details month as August). Please note that you may be charged up to 24 hours beforehand due to time zone differences.
  • You’ll know that you were charged upfront if the processing date is listed as the 1st of the month and the Details section month matches the processing month. (i.e., August 1st bills list the Details month as August)
