  • You’ll know that you were paying monthly (non-charge upfront) if the processing date is listed as the 1st of the month and the Details section lists the previous month (i.e., August 1st bills list the Details month as July)
  • You’ll know that your creator charges per creation if the processing date is listed as the 1st of the month or your cancel date and the Details section lists the previous month. With per creation, you’ll also be able to click into the billing details to review each post you supported for that month

Cancellation reference table

Use this table to understand what happens when you cancel for each billing model:

Creator’s billing model

What happens when you cancel?

Example

Subscription billing

If you cancel, you retain your original membership access up to the next billing date, which is determined by your join date. You are not billed on the next billing date and lose membership access.

If you rejoin before your original access has ended, you’ll keep your original bill date. If you cancel and rejoin after your original access has ended, you’ll be treated as a new patron and your new join date will be your monthly billing date.

Due to timezone differences, we recommend canceling at least 24 hours before your next billing date if you don’t want your bill to renew.

Let’s say you originally signed up on June 5th. If you cancel on December 1st, you’ll retain your membership access until approximately the 5th of January.

Monthly charge upfront

If you cancel before the 1st of the month, you’ll retain your original membership access until the next 1st of the month. When the 1st of the month comes, you won’t be charged and you’ll lose your membership access. Canceling on or after the 1st of the month will result in a charge for that month. Your membership will end on the following 1st.

You can rejoin at the same tier level and experience no billing changes. If you rejoin after your original access ended, you’ll be treated as a new patron, and you’ll pay in full when you join and monthly on the 1st after that.

Say you canceled on the 11th of December. You’ll retain your membership access through the 31st of December. On January 1st, you’ll lose membership access.

Annual membership

Similar to charge upfront billing and subscription billing, when you cancel an annual membership, you’ll retain access until your next bill date. On your next bill date you won’t be charged and will lose membership access.

If you joined on November 5th, and you cancel on June 1st, you’ll retain membership access until your year has completed.

Monthly (non-charge upfront)

If you cancel before the 1st of the month, you won’t be billed and will lose membership access as soon as you cancel.

You can rejoin at any point and will be treated as a new patron.

On October 20th you cancel your membership with a monthly charging creator. You’ve not yet been billed for your October access, and lose access as soon as you cancel the membership. Your last month of support will be listed in the Details section of your Billing history.

Per creation

When you cancel, we’ll process any pending bills on your account. Please check your Billing history for pending bills before canceling.

You have a $5 membership with a per creation creator with a monthly max of 2 posts. Your creator makes a paid post on May 16th, and then again on May 19th. Pending bills are placed on your account as soon as your creator publishes these posts. You cancel your membership on May 20th, and we immediately submit your pending bills to your payment method for a total charge of $10 ($5 x 2 paid posts).

Please note that if you cancel your membership after a creator has opted in to subscription billing and you rejoin later, your membership will be on our subscription billing model.

I canceled, will I still get my benefits?

For questions about the fulfillment of benefits or patron-only content after deleting your membership, reach out to the creator directly. Here’s our guide to help you message your creator with benefits questions: How do I send a direct message to a creator?

Where did my membership go?

If you can’t find your membership, payment, or posts from your creator, you may have more than one account.

Have I created a duplicate account?

Creating multiple accounts might happen for a few different reasons:

  • The original account with the membership might have been created with a typo version of your email
  • You might have created another account with an alternate similar email address you own
  • If you signed up with email and password, you might have created a second account with Continue with Facebook, Continue with Apple or Continue with Google options

What steps should I take to find my membership?

  • Check all of your email inboxes for Patreon and no-reply@patreon.com. This will help you track down which email you may have used
  • If you find an email from Patreon, like a post notification or welcome email, try logging in with that email address
  • If you suspect that you have a typo on your email or can’t find the account that has your membership, not to worry! Just reach out to our support team. We’ll be happy to help you get back in

Where do I find my billing history?

This article will cover where you can find a list of all payments you’ve made to creators. Your billing history will include the bill processing date, the charge amount, and which creator received your payment.

To access your billing history:

  • Log in to your Patreon account and click the Settings link from the left sidebar navigation
  • From the menubar, click on More > Billing History

All past payments you’ve made to creators will be listed by month. View a past year by clicking on the drop-down menu near the top of the page and selecting the year you’d like to review.

In your billing history, you can also manually download receipts of your payments, including VAT breakdown (If applicable).

The initial receipt of your first charge will be sent by email, and after this, you can access these self-serve via your billing history settings:

To access your receipts:

  • From the Billing History, find the charge you want a receipt for
  • You will find a clickable link (the date) above Billing Details, where you can access the receipt for that particular charge

If you pledge to creators that bill in different currencies, your receipts will be grouped by currency. Please note that if your local bank currency is not the same as the creator’s billing currency, this may show up as a converted amount on your bank statement.

Your bank should be able to provide you with the payment amount in both your local currency and the creator’s billing currency.

Why do I have a pending charge?

We place a temporary authorization hold for all $100+ charges.

This will be released within 72 hours and is either refunded or removed on your end, depending on your bank’s authorization holds.

Once we begin processing payments, you will be charged your actual membership amount, which will be sent directly to the creator.

If your card is declining, you may see an authorization and a charge if we had to reattempt your card. This is typically released by your bank within 72 hours as well.

To review your processed payments:

  • While logged in to your patron profile, click the Manage Memberships button (pencil icon) next to your membership in the left sidebar navigation
  • Click on Billing history from the top menu bar to review all payments we’ve processed

If an authorization is not falling off of your account, feel free to reach out to our team using the “Email Patreon Support” below to send us a note!

Note: If you were charged immediately for a membership, please visit the article Charge upfront billing explained.

Why haven’t I been charged yet?

Only members of creators charging upfront will have immediate charges. If you’re unsure if your creator charges upfront, you can review your Billing History page. If your charge date falls within the Supported Period, it indicates that your creator bills members upfront.

Members can expect to be charged when they join a creator’s membership and then on the same day of each month thereafter. It usually takes 24-48 hours for all payments to process, so it may take a few days after the renewal date. You’ll receive an email indicating whether your payment was successfully processed or declined. Alternatively, you can check your Billing History page for your payment status.

For more details, you can check our guide on How membership billing works.

Why is my updated membership pending?

Beginning October 1st, any changes made to your membership when you already have a bill that is pending processing will be scheduled or queued until the original payment has fully processed.

When you edit a membership that already has a payment processing, you will see a message letting you know that your update to the pledge is scheduled. This will be the same for upgrading or downgrading your membership.

While waiting for the original membership to process, you will see your updated membership in a “Pending” state in your Manage Memberships tab. Please note that while your update is pending, you will retain access to the benefits of the original membership.

Once the scheduled pledge is processed, you will be given access to the new tier’s benefits.

Why was I charged after canceling?

Does canceling stop charges?

Canceling a membership does stop future billing. That said, we will process any pending bills on your account upon cancellation.

Two situations would result in a pending bill on your account:

  • The creator you supported charged per creation, and they made a paid post(s) while your membership was active
  • Example:
  • You have a $1 per post membership. The creator publishes a paid post on July 9th, which generates a pending bill on your billing history. On July 20th, you cancel your membership — we process your payment for $1.
  • You can refer to your Billing history for information about the post date.
  • Your membership was active at the renewal date
  • Example:
  • You have a $5 monthly membership that is charged on the 12th day of each month. We will process your payment if you cancel on or after the 12th.
  • If our initial attempt to charge your membership payment is declined, we will reattempt.

Can I get a refund for this charge?

You don’t need to message creators directly to ask for a refund. You can request a refund right from your Billing history, within 60 days of the original payment. If you’re outside that window, you will be directed to contact Product Support. We recommend sending the following information with your request:

  • The amount of the transaction(s) you are requesting be refunded
  • The date(s) of the original transaction(s)
  • Your reason for requesting a refund

For more details, please visit our dedicated article on How to request a refund.

Why wasn’t I charged this month?

Creators can pause membership billing while their Patreon page remains accessible to members. If you aren’t sure whether you should have been charged, you can always check your Memberships tab to review your active membership and message the creator to follow up.

Reasons why you may not be charged

  • There are a few reasons why a creator might pause their page. They might be on vacation or may not have had enough time to make a post this month. We encourage creators to let their members know why they’re pausing their billing, so check your creators’ recent posts for any announcements
  • Another reason you might not have been charged is that your creator is on a legacy billing model that charges per creation and has not created any paid posts this month. You can check if your creator charges per creation by visiting your Billing history

If you’re concerned about a gap in benefits, feel free to message your creator directly. For more details about messaging a creator, visit our guide How do I message a creator?.

Creators can pause billing for multiple months. However, your payments will likely continue automatically next month.

Members: Taxes

European Union Strong Customer Authentication

For European Union patrons there may be an additional authentication flow when pledging. This is from their bank and will occur when adding a credit or debit card to the account, or pledging to a creator. This is to reduce fraud for card holders and may be required by patrons’ banks to comply with the EU’s Payments Services Directive 2.

This additional authentication flow will be a pop-up that presents the patron’s bank’s authentication page. The pop-up may request a username and password, a code sent to email or text, or any other authentication method supported by the bank. Patrons should contact their bank with any questions about fulfilling the authentication requirements, as Patreon does not control the form.

I am a patron. How does it affect me?

If you add a new credit or debit card, or pledge to a new creator, you may encounter a pop-up from your bank that requests extra verification. This could be a username and password, a code sent to email or text, or any other authentication method supported by your bank.

Here’s an example of what that pop-up might look like, using a card from the Netherlands:

Please note that if you have any questions or issues with one of these pop-ups, you would have to check with your bank as they are not controlled by Patreon.

I am a creator. Do I need to do anything?

Not at all! Patreon will be implementing this on the platform, so there will be no actions required from creators. Everything will be business as usual for you.

For detailed information on this directive, please review this summary from the European Commission.

How VAT works for members on Patreon

What is VAT?

Value Added Tax (VAT) is a tax assessed on the value added to goods and services — including digital products. It’s charged as a percentage of a price (e.g., $1.00 membership with 23% VAT will have a final cost of $1.23).

Many countries and regions require that VAT (or similar indirect taxes, such as GST, HST, QST, JCT, or sales tax - together herein “VAT”) be charged based on the location of the customer rather than the location of the provider. This applies to digital services provided through platforms like Patreon. In Patreon’s case, members are the customers of the sales through the platform.

In jurisdictions where Patreon is legally required to collect VAT or similar taxes, Patreon calculates, collects, and remits those taxes on applicable payments.

Here’s a list of VAT rates by country that you can refer to, VAT rates.

How does Patreon collect my VAT?

In situations where Patreon collects VAT, members will have VAT added to their relevant membership payments. Your creators’ earnings are not affected by the VAT applied on such sales. The VAT charges are generally processed and remitted via Patreon, although this may depend on location and local rules.

The VAT rate you’re charged depends on the location you set in your member settings. If this information is not provided, VAT will be applied based on your location at the time that you start your membership.

If you provide incorrect location information when joining, you may be charged the wrong amount of tax. You can update your member settings at any time so future payments are taxed correctly. However, we are generally unable to refund VAT already applied to processed payments.

I have a VAT number for my business, can I be exempt?

Patreon generally operates as a business-to-consumer (B2C) platform and treats member purchases as consumer transactions. At this time, Patreon does not generally support disabling VAT based on a member’s business status or VAT registration number. However, we would be happy to review specific circumstances on a case-by-case basis.

Where can I find a record of the VAT I’ve paid?

We list the amount of VAT added to your membership payments directly on your account.

Here’s how you can access your billing record with VAT:

  • While logged in to your member profile, click the Manage Memberships button (pencil icon) in the left sidebar navigation
  • Click on Billing history from the top menu bar to review all payments we’ve processed
  • Your payments will be listed with VAT by the process date. You can select the year you’d like to review from the drop-down menu. Beginning December 1, 2021, you can also download a VAT-compliant invoice from this page

Is my payment to a creator tax deductible?

If the creator is a legally recognized not-for-profit company and you receive nothing of value in return for your payment to them, then some jurisdictions allow the member to take a tax deduction.

Pledges to non-profits

What is a non-profit organization?

Non-profit organizations are entities who do not work for profits but rather for charitable, educational, social or other specific causes and are generally exempt from federal taxes and many state taxes. There are many different types of non-profits regarding eligibility and tax-deductible contributions.

If I pledge to this creator, is my pledge tax-deductible?

Your contribution, minus the value of any thank-you gifts you receive, is tax-deductible to the full extent provided by law.

For example, if the member pays $100, of which $20 is the deemed value of a tote bag, then only the $80 is considered to be tax-deductible.

Will I receive a document for tax purposes via email and/or mail?

Every month you will receive an email receipt for your payments on Patreon. Non-profit creators may also send you information directly concerning the tax deductibility of your payment. Unfortunately, Patreon cannot verify the legal status of Creators, and thus it is up to each individual Creator to provide the relevant required tax-exempt donation documentation.

What if I have more tax questions?

If you have additional questions about taxes on Patreon, please visit our Taxes help center articles under Creator Topics and Member Topics.

If you have more questions regarding taxes, please consult with your local tax professional.

Sales Tax on Patreon for Members

Tax laws in many countries and US states have evolved in recent years to require online marketplaces such as Patreon to apply sales tax/VAT to transactions that take place via their platform.

Patreon adds sales tax, VAT, GST, or other similar taxes (collectively herein also referred to as “sales tax” or “sales tax/VAT”) to member or customer payments in parts of the United States and several other countries as required by law. Review which countries sales taxes apply to here: List of locations where Patreon is collecting sales tax

The article and FAQs below include details about how sales tax applies to Patreon and what you need to know.

Who Does Patreon Charge Sales Tax To?

Whether or not you will pay sales tax/VAT as a member depends on where you are located, and what benefits the creators you support are providing. The laws and tax rates in effect in your country of residence will be applied whenever you pledge to a creator through Patreon, whether that’s monthly, annually, or per thing, or an ad-hoc commerce acquisition if the benefits offered are taxable in your location.

If Patreon is charging sales tax in your location, an additional line item will be listed on your receipt. Since tax laws and rates vary from country to country and state to state, the amount will be different for different members. The tax that Patreon collects as a result of these laws will be paid directly to your local government, and there are no Patreon fees on this portion of your payment.

About sales tax

  • Different jurisdictions will consider different things taxable. If you receive a benefit in return for your pledge, it is likely that it will be subject to tax. For example, many places have passed laws that make streaming content taxable so in those places, streaming video and audio would be subject to tax.
  • It is however useful to remember that different jurisdictions approach digital content differently and what one location deems a taxable benefit may not be consistent with the views of another jurisdiction.
  • If you are not receiving any benefits in exchange for your pledge or payment, the payment may not be taxable. For example, if you pledged an amount in excess of your set tier price, or you have given a pledge that falls outside of a set tier, your pledge could be deemed to not have any benefits associated with it.
  • The laws about what is taxable vary by location, but in many places, digital goods and content (downloadable and/or streamed) are also taxable.
  • Some members may decide to pledge outside of your set tiers. For example, you may have pledged an amount above the set tier price or the creator has given you the option to pledge without receiving pledge benefits. In many jurisdictions, this amount would be akin to a “tip” or gratuity and treated as non-taxable. However, in other jurisdictions given the conditions set or interpretation around this issue, it is not possible to treat such amounts as not taxable.
  • We are not offering this as an option at this time. Note however that in several jurisdictions, sales tax cannot be included in pricing.

Details on Sales Tax: How it works in different regions and how that applies to Patreon

Which benefits on Patreon will be considered taxable?

Outside of the United States, it is common for sales of most goods and services to be subject to VAT/GST. Also, in more and more jurisdictions, cross border sales of electronically supplied or intangible services, as well as imported physical goods are subject to tax chargeable by the seller.

Within the United States, what is taxable varies greatly by location. Generally, tangible goods are taxable in all states and taxability of digital goods and services is constantly increasing.

As a rough guide, we’ve broadly sorted benefits into 5 categories that are each taxed differently in US jurisdictions.

Typical Benefit Type

Examples

U.S. Status

Donations/Support

Support only. Languages such as “pledges whatever”

Currently exempt from Sales Tax in the majority of states

Professional Services

Live chats and phone calls

Exempt in the vast majority of states

Exclusive Community Access

Paid member-only posts, Discord, server access, polls

Taxable in roughly half the states

Streaming Content

Extra podcast episode per month, videos, bonus content

Taxable in roughly half the states

Downloadable Digital Goods

PDFs, computer game builds, downloaded color pages

Taxable in roughly half the states

Physical Goods

Candles, T-shirts, mugs, mailed coloring pages

Taxable in all states in which Patreon is collecting

FAQ

  • As referenced above, whether you are taxed, and at what rate, depends on both your location and the types of benefits the creator is providing in the tier you have pledged to.
  • Within the United States, rates currently range from 4% to 14%. To make things more complex, some locations tax certain things while others don’t (e.g. - “physical goods” vs. “digital downloads” vs. “digital streaming”). Outside of the United States, rates range from 5% to 27% in the countries where Patreon will charge and pay sales tax.
  • It is important to understand that tax rates and rules change frequently. Patreon monitors these changes, working with relevant resources as needed, to ensure that your members and customers are taxed at the current rate for their location and the benefits being provided.
  • Yes, it is very likely. We expect more states and jurisdictions will pass similar laws or regulatory changes in the future. We are constantly monitoring relevant tax obligations and will keep this page up to date and with as much warning as possible.
  • Sales tax applies to each transaction. For members or customers that pay per thing or one-off sales, if they are in a location that requires sales tax, and the thing the creator offers is taxable in their location, they will find sales tax applied to each monthly transaction where a paid ‘thing’ was posted during that month or otherwise, to the one-off transaction for which the payment is made.
  • Yes. While logged into Your Memberships, click on the Personal Settings button from the left navigation and then click on the More dropdown to select Billing history. Click the dropdown arrow next to a payment amount for an individual pledge to see how much sales tax, VAT, or similar tax was applied.
  • Also, for any new pledge, you should be able to see the tax being applied at checkout under the Sales or VAT line in Order Summary.
  • Patreon does not apply GST on payments from members and customers in Australia who pay creators also located in Australia. However, if those members and customers pay creators in other countries, Patreon may still charge them GST on those payments if the benefits they receive are taxable in Australia.

Members: Your benefits

Access my benefits

Every creator has a unique approach to benefit delivery – this is your guide to find and get the perks, or what we refer to as benefits, that a creator sets up through our platform.

How do I know what benefits I should get?

Creators typically list benefits in the About section of their page or the description of their tiers. You can find both under My membership when you visit a creator’s page and are a patron.

Have questions about what is or isn’t included in these descriptions? We recommend messaging the creator on Patreon to get answers.

Accessing posts

Many creators share benefits directly through our posting feature. Benefits like; patron-only videos, image sets, and private notes can all be shared through posts on Patreon.

There are a few different ways that you can view your creators’ posts:

  • Your Posts feed is your personalized feed with posts from all creators you support and follow. You can use the drop-down menu to filter the view by a certain creator.
  • Directly from the Posts section of your creator’s page
  • If your Email settings include notifications for new posts, you’ll receive an email every time a new post is available to you.

If there are locked posts that you believe you should have access to, review this how-to article for help with that: Unlock posts I should have access to

Access my Discord role

If your creator offers our Discord integration as a benefit, getting your Discord role couldn’t be easier. All you have to do is connect your Discord and Patreon accounts from your Profile settings under the Apps section –we do the rest behind the scenes! You can reference these articles for added help and information:

  • Get my Discord role
  • Issues with my Discord role

Access my private audio RSS

If you just joined a creator who offers Patreon hosted or integrated RSS feeds, we’ll send you an email with your link. If you lost that email, you have been a patron for a while, or your creator recently added this feature, you can access your link by visiting the creator’s page and checking the My membership section.

Want additional help subscribing? We’ve created this guide to help you subscribe using your RSS link.

My creator isn’t delivering

Creators are responsible for benefits and content distribution. It is not a violation of our terms if a creator doesn’t deliver benefits or they’re not as expected. Read more about our legal terms here.

If a creator stops creating content or fails to deliver a benefit as promised, here are a few steps we suggest you take:

  • Investigate the creator’s other content distribution channels
  • Some creators post their creations on Patreon, but sometimes they do it through other websites or services. If you don’t find anything on Patreon you may want to search around first.
  • Contact the creator
  • It’s possible that they simply forgot to send out a specific benefit, or maybe they’re delayed and are trying to catch up. Messaging the creator on Patreon is a good way to get information if they haven’t provided any.
  • Ask the creator for a refund
  • If you feel that you haven’t received your money’s worth, you can always ask the creator for a refund. They are not obligated to provide a refund, many creators are sympathetic to refund requests if benefits have not been received. We’ve made a best practices guide for requesting a refund from a creator.
  • Cancel your membership
  • If you can’t get in touch with the creator, or if you don’t think they have a good reason for not creating anything recently, then we suggest that you cancel your membership. Once you remove your membership, you’ll receive an exit survey that goes directly to the creator, so feel free to share your reason for leaving.
Here are a few steps we do not suggest taking:
  • Ask Patreon for a refund
  • We encourage patrons to contact the creator with their refund requests. We may issue a refund for a patron at our sole discretion. Most often, refunds are issued faster when the patron asks the creator to refund their payment. As mentioned above it is difficult to judge the creative output of a creator and we do not want to impose our judgment here. Learn more about our refund policy here.
  • Continue to support the creator if you are not happy with them
  • If you don’t believe the creator is worthy of support, then please do not continue to support them and expect a refund at some point in the future.

Add my private RSS feed to the Apple Podcast app

Creators are now required to combine profiles

As of July 6th, all creators are required to have a single identity instead of separate creator and fan profiles. If you haven’t combined your profiles yet, your access to Patreon is temporarily restricted until you do. Combine your profiles now to restore access to Patreon. If you don’t take action in the next few weeks, we’ll automatically combine your profiles for you starting August 17th. Need help? Visit Combine your creator and fan profiles into a single identity or contact the support team for assistance.

Here’s how to add your custom RSS link to the Apple Podcast app in order to get access to your creator’s patron-only content! This is a great option to listen to your creator’s member-only audio benefits on your mobile device.

How to find an RSS link on Patreon

- Make sure you’re logged in on your member profile
- Select the creator in the left-hand menu
- On the creator’s page, go to the Membership tab under the section Listen in other podcast apps
    - You can also find this option on the creator’s page by using the Podcast icon under their name and description. When you click the button, a pop-up will appear
- Select the Other podcasts apps option
- Then click the Copy button to get the link on your clipboard
- Make sure you’re logged in on your member profile
- On your home feed, tap the creator’s name in the upper menu
- After you select the creator, scroll down a bit, and the three dots will appear in the upper right corner. Tap it and choose the option Add to podcast app in the menu
- A new page will appear. Tap the Add button in the Apple Podcasts option
- You’ll be prompted to the Apple Podcasts app. The RSS link will already be filled, then tap Follow. The podcast will now be added to the shows you follow.
  • After joining the community of a creator who offers an RSS feed, you’ll receive a welcome email with more information about your new membership. Scroll down until you see a Listen your way section and copy the URL here.

How to add an RSS link to the Apple Podcast app

- Open the Apple Podcast app on your computer and click on File in the upper bar menu
- Then select the option Follow a show by URL
- Paste the RSS link you copied in the text field and click the Follow button
- You'll find the podcast populated under the Up Next section in the Home tab and also in the Library. You can listen to any unplayed episodes for your benefit tier immediately after joining
- Open the Apple Podcast app, tap on the Library tab along the bottom, and select the three dots option in the top right
- Select the Follow a Show by URL option
- Paste your unique RSS feed link and tap on the Follow button
- You'll find the podcast populated under the Up Next section in the Home tab and also in the Library. You can listen to any unplayed episodes for your benefit tier immediately after joining

Claim my exclusive Patreon merch from a creator

Some of your favorite creators on Patreon are offering exclusive patron-only merch. If a creator is offering merch on a tier you sign up for, you’re eligible to receive this merch if you meet a couple of requirements:

  • You have a shipping address in a country that we ship to, check which countries we ship to, here
  • You’ve been a patron for 3 consecutive months with successful payments after the merch offer launches

In this article we’ll go over:

  • How to receive merch as a new patron
  • How to claim merch as an existing patron
  • How to manage or update your shipping information
  • How to opt-out of receiving exclusive merch

Note: If you have an Annual membership, you’ll be charged for your year of membership up front, and will earn your merch after 3 monthly billing periods have passed.

How do I become a patron and receive Patreon-exclusive merch from a creator?

You’ll find a banner on creators’ pages who are participating in the merch for membership. If you have yet to become their patron, go ahead and select the Become a Patron button. Learn more about the steps to becoming a patron here:

How do I become a patron to a creator?

When starting your membership, make sure you select the tier corresponding with exclusive merch. You’ll know it’s the correct tier because of the icon included in the tier description.

When prompted, Be sure to enter your correct shipping address as this will be vital to receiving your merch.

Curious where we ship? We ship globally! Read our article on which countries we ship to.

You’ll also be required to enter your payment information on the right-hand side of the confirmation page. Review your payment and billing details before confirming.

You’ll receive a confirmation e-mail with details about your membership after you successfully become a patron.

Receiving Merch for membership as an existing patron

When a creator you’re a patron of adds merch as a benefit to a tier that you’re currently in, you’ll receive an e-mail letting you know about the merch. If you’re not currently joined in a tier that offers Merch for Membership, you’ll need to edit your membership to select the corresponding tier. Learn how to update your membership here:

How do I edit my membership?

After merch is added to a tier, you’ll become eligible to receive it after 3 consecutive successful membership charges. Past patronage doesn’t count towards the merch; you’ll need to be a patron for 3 consecutive months after the merch benefit launches to be eligible.

Once you become eligible to receive merch, you’ll receive a confirmation e-mail notifying you that you’ll be receiving your merch soon. You’ll also be asked to confirm your shipping address.

Important: If you need to change your shipping address, do so as soon as possible. We require you to update it within 3 days of the confirmation e-mail while we prep your package.

Once your item is shipped you’ll receive a confirmation e-mail including tracking details.

How to manage your shipping information

If you move or your address changes, you can always update it. The deadline to update your shipping details to ensure you receive your merch is 3 days from the confirmation e-mail mentioned in the section above.

Follow these steps to update your shipping address:

  • While logged in to your patron profile, click the Manage memberships button (the pencil icon) from the left sidebar navigation
  • Select Update next to the creator who includes exclusive merch
  • You’ll find a pop-up with the option to Add a new address
  • Be sure to select save once you’ve added your information

How do I opt-out of receiving exclusive merch?

If you’d like to continue supporting your creator but don’t wish to receive exclusive merch, you can opt-out at any time.

  • Visit your Active memberships page
  • Select Update next to the creator who includes exclusive merch.
  • You’ll find a pop-up with an option to opt-out. Select the I prefer not to receive benefits option.
  • Make sure to select save

If you have any additional questions, please don’t hesitate to reach out to merch@patreon.com.

Comment on a post

One of the perks of being a member is commenting on the work your creators share with you. Comments are a great way to show your love and communicate with a creator’s community. This article will detail how to add your comment on the desktop and mobile app. All comments should abide by Patreon’s Community Guidelines, which act as the guardrails detailing the sorts of behaviors that are permitted and prohibited on Patreon.

If you see that commenting has been disabled on a post, it means that the creator has set comment access to paid members only or they’ve disabled commenting for their post(s). Learn more about disabled comments.

How to add comments

  • Let your voice be heard! You can add a comment to posts you have comment access to.
    • To add your comment, click on the comment field box and type your comment
      • You may need to first click Comment to expand the comment section
    • Click the Reply button or type the Return/Enter key on your keyboard to add your comment
  • Replying to a comment
    • Click on the post you’d like to view
    • Click Comment
    • Find the comment you’d like to respond to and select Comment below it
    • Type your comment, and once you’re happy with it, click the Reply button or hit the Return/Enter key on your keyboard — Your comment will be threaded under the comment you are replying to
  • Editing or deleting a comment
    • Revisit the post that you left the comment on and click More
    • Click on the Edit or Delete button, depending on the action you’d like to take
  • Make sure you’re using the latest version of the Patreon app for Android or the Patreon app for iOS. While logged in to the Patreon app, you can comment on any post you have comment access to. To leave a comment via the app:
    • Tap on the post you’d like to view
    • Tap Comment to add your comment or scroll down to the comments section
    • Once you’re happy with your comment, tap Send to load your comment
  • Adding an image to your comment (Early access)
    • While writing your comment, tap Add image to attach a photo from your device’s gallery
    • Once you’re happy with your comment, tap Send to load your comment
  • Adding an image to a comment is an early access feature, rolling out automatically to a limited number of creator communities — there’s nothing you need to do on your end. If your creator’s community has this enabled, you’ll see the option to Add image next to the comment field box.
  • Replying to a comment
    • Tap on the post you’d like to view
    • Tap Comments
    • Once in the comments section of a post, find the comment you’d like to respond to and select Comment below it
    • Type your comment, and once you’re happy with it, tap Send to load your reply — Your comment will be threaded under the comment you are replying to
  • Editing or deleting your comment
    • Tap on the post you want to edit your comment for
    • Tap Comments
    • Locate your comment and tap More
    • From here, you can edit or delete your comment

Creator likes

If a creator likes your comment, you’ll see a badge on your comment with their profile image. You can hover over the badge to see the creator’s name.

FAQ

  • You can only view the comments section of posts you have comment access to. This means that if the post is for paid members and you’re no longer a paid member, you won’t be able to edit or reply to comments for that post any longer.
  • No. Your comment can be viewed by the creator and other fellow members who have access to the same post.
  • Unfortunately, there’s no way to guarantee that a creator will interact with their comments. Some creators have very active members, and comments can be missed. If you want to send your creator a personal note thanking them, you can send them a direct message
  • In order to leave comments on a creator’s public post, you’ll need to have an active membership with the creator. If the creator has set their comment access to all members, you can have either a free or paid membership. If the creator has set comment access for only paid members, you’ll need to select a paid offering to add your comment(s).
  • Learn more about why you may not have comment access
  • Yes! If you are a creator, you’ll be able to comment on creators’ posts that you have comment access to.
  • Not yet everywhere. This is currently an early access feature available to a limited number of creator communities, so you may see this option on some posts and not others. It’s only available in the Patreon mobile app for now — desktop doesn’t have it yet.

Experience your creator’s Drops

Drops are unique events where creators share new audio or video content live. These releases are accompanied by a countdown timer and a live chat, allowing you to engage and experience the content alongside other members and maybe even the creator themselves. This article will guide you through the different phases of the member experience when checking out your creator’s Drops.

Before the live drop

Watch out for upcoming drops from your favorite creators. Starting 7 days before the drop, you’ll see a preview with a countdown timer on your homepage and the creator’s page. This helps you know when to expect the release.

You can click the I’m interested button to get reminders and notifications about the drop. You can also comment and react to others’ comments during this phase.

  • 24 hours before the drop: The content will feature prominently at the top of the creator’s page.
  • 2 minutes before the drop: You’ll get a push notification to join the drop and see the live countdown. At this point, you can click on Join the drop, see the number of people who have also joined, and participate in the live conversation
  • 10 seconds before the drop: You’ll see a countdown until the content is released

During the live Drop

During the live Drop, you can click the Join the Drop button to watch or listen, comment, and react in real-time directly underneath the content. If you tapped I’m interested you will receive a push notification letting you know the Drop is live.

The creator might also join the live chat, making the experience exciting and engaging for everyone.

Post Drop

After a drop finishes, you will continue to have access to watch or listen, read existing comments, and react and comment indefinitely, just like any other post. The drop will stay highlighted on the creator’s page for 24 hours after release, making it easy for you to find it.

Fan tools for keeping Live safe (Members: Your benefits)

Report a message

Members can report messages that they feel are violating Patreon’s Community Guidelines directly to creators. We encourage everyone to review, uphold, and enforce these guidelines to keep your community safe.

How to report a message:
- Visit the specific chat you’d like to delete
- Hover over the message, and click More
- Click Report Message
- Visit the specific chat you’d like to delete
- Tap and hold the message to expand menu options
- Tap Report Message

Block a member

Members can also block other members in order to continue interacting with a chat while hiding messages from particular members.

How to block a member:
- Visit the specific chat you’d like to delete
- Hover over the message, and click More
- Click Block Member
- Visit the specific chat you’d like to delete
- Tap and hold the message to expand menu options
- Tap Block Member

Report a live

Members can report an ongoing Live if they feel the content or environment violates Patreon’s Community Guidelines. We encourage you to review, uphold, and enforce both sets of guidelines to keep your community safe. Once you report a live, the creator’s stream is suspended for all viewers, and the creator is notified.

How to report a live:
- In an active Live, click More
- Click Report this creator
- Indicate why you’re reporting the live, and click Continue
- In an active Live, tap More
- Tap Report
- Indicate why you’re reporting the live, and tap Continue

Closed Chats

If you’re watching a Live and suddenly can’t send messages in the chat, don’t worry—it just means the creator or their moderators temporarily turned chat off.

This is a normal part of how some Lives are managed, especially when things get busy or the creator wants to focus attention elsewhere.

What you can still do
  • You can still watch the Live and enjoy the stream.
  • You’ll still see all previous chat messages, including new ones from the creator or moderators.
  • Once chat is turned back on, you’ll be able to post again.

Muting

If you’re watching a Live or participating in a Community Chat and suddenly can’t send messages, it may be because you’ve been temporarily muted by the creator or a trusted moderator. This feature helps creators keep things respectful and on track for everyone watching.

This isn’t a ban—you can still enjoy the Live and follow the chat, but you won’t be able to post messages for a little while.

What being muted means
  • You’ve been muted for a limited time: 15 minutes, 1 hour, or 24 hours. You will see a message letting you know how long the mute lasts.
  • You can still watch the Live and read messages in the chat.
  • You just won’t be able to send messages until the mute expires.

Removal from Live

If you suddenly can’t access a Live you were just in, it’s possible the creator or a trusted moderator removed you from that Live session. This action—called Remove from Live—is used to help keep the experience safe and respectful for everyone.

What it means
  • You were removed from the Live video and chat.
  • You won’t be able to rejoin that specific Live session.
  • You’re not blocked—you can still watch future Lives from that creator, unless you’re blocked separately.
Why it happens

Creators and their moderators use this option to keep the Live environment comfortable for everyone. It might be used if something you said or did was disruptive or against community guidelines.

Getting Discord access

If you’re not yet familiar with Discord, it’s an all-in-one voice and text chat app where you can get access to your creator’s Patreon-exclusive community. Check out our What is Discord? article to learn more.

How do I link my Discord account to Patreon?

If you need to create a Discord account, we will guide you through that during this process:

  • Log in to your Patreon account
  • Click Your account , then Settings
  • Click Connected Apps
  • Click on Discord and then click the Connect button
  • Enter the email address or phone number you use to log in with Discord and your password and click the Login button
  • Click the Authorize button
  • You’ve successfully linked Discord to Patreon! You may need to refresh the page
I’m not getting the pop-up window to log in to Discord

This typically happens if you have an ad blocker or browser extension that is blocking pop-up windows. Please disable these extensions while connecting Discord to Patreon.

Joining and Leaving a creator’s Discord server

Once you’ve connected your Discord and Patreon accounts, any servers you’re eligible to join will appear on the Discord Apps settings page. Click the Join server button to get your role.

If at any point you’d like to leave the creator’s server, you can click the Leave server button to be removed. You can always re-join the server from your Discord app settings latter on.

FAQ

  • If you’ve connected Patreon and Discord, we recommend disconnecting and reconnecting Discord to Patreon. Before doing so, log out of Discord and clear your cache and cookies to start fresh. Reconnecting will reestablish communication between the two apps. Here’s an article to guide you through this: Discord isn’t working for me
  • If you’re still not finding your creator’s server, check that you’re in the correct tier to unlock Discord access. This section of our help center guide will help you confirm your tier: How to check your tier level
  • Check the creator’s Patreon for the Discord logo on your tier description.
  • If you think you were assigned the wrong role, there are a couple of things you can do to double-check:
    • Click the active membership associated with this benefit located on the left side menu on your Recent feed. On the Creator’s Patreon, click the Membership tab to check if your creator added the Discord role name to the tier description
    • Message your creator directly on Patreon — they’ll know which roles they’ve assigned to which tiers. Learn how to message your creator with this guide: How do I message a creator?

How can I join a Live on Patreon?

When your favorite creator goes Live on Patreon, it’s your chance to connect in real time — with them and with others who have access to the Live.

Joining is easy, and this guide will walk you through how to find a Live, join in, and know what to expect.

Get notified about Live events

If you have access to a Live event, we’ll let you know when it starts so you don’t miss out. You’ll receive:

  • An email notification as soon as the Live begins
  • A push notification if you use the Patreon app and have notifications turned on
  • For scheduled Lives, you’ll get an email/push when the Live is scheduled (this could be days or hours in advance), plus a push notification 5 minutes before it starts

These alerts help you join right on time — whether it’s a surprise Live or something you’ve been counting down to.

Where to find a Live

Before joining, make sure you’re logged into your Patreon account. You can join from your browser (desktop or mobile) or via the Patreon app on iOS or Android.

You can join a Live from several places:

  • Your Home Feed — Live events appear in your feed on both desktop and mobile
  • The creator’s page — If a creator is Live, it will be featured on their page
  • If the creator selects the option, a banner will appear at the top of Community Chats so you can jump in directly
  • Shared links — Creators may post or share direct links you can use to join
  • Notifications — Tap the link in your email or push notification to go straight into the Live

Some creators are testing Ticketed Lives during a limited beta. Access to a Live depends on how the creator has set it up — in some cases, you may see Lives that require you to buy a ticket before you can join.

If the Live is scheduled but hasn’t started yet, you’ll see a countdown timer showing when it begins. Before entering the post, you’ll also have the option to add the event to your calendar so you don’t miss it.

Joining a Live

When you join a Live — whether it’s just starting or already in progress — you’ll enter the stream directly from your browser or the Patreon app.

If the Live hasn’t started yet, you’ll land in a waiting room with a gradient background and your creator’s avatar.

First time joining? You’ll be asked to agree to the terms of participation before entering. This step is only required once.

Once the Live begins, the stream will start automatically — no need to refresh or rejoin.

Interacting during the Live

Once you’re in the Live, you’ll see the video (or audio) stream and a chat where you can connect with your creator and other members.

  • On the computer, the chat appears next to the stream
  • On mobile, it overlays the video

Ways to participate:

  • Say hello, react to what’s happening, or ask a question in the chat
  • Use emoji reactions to engage without typing
  • View images shared by the creator — only creators can post images, but everyone in the chat can see them

Setting up Notifications

Want to make sure you get notifications about your favorite creator’s Lives? Here’s how to get set up:

- Head to Personal Settings in the left navigation bar
- Select Email notifications, and click on the creator for whom you want to enable email notifications
- Use the toggle for Lives to determine whether you are notified about scheduled and current Lives via email
- Tap your profile icon in the upper right corner
- Select Settings, then Notification Settings, and scroll down to tap on the creator for whom you want to enable notifications
- Select the boxes for Lives to get notified via email and/or push notifications when the creator schedules or starts a Live

Watching a Live after it ends

If your creator shares the Live afterward, you can watch the replay in a post on their page. Not all creators post replays, so it’s a good idea to check their posts or reach out to them directly.

When a replay is available and the creator has enabled chat display, you’ll be able to see the message interactions alongside the livestream recording. This feature enhances your experience by providing context from the original livestream. If you decide you no longer want to see the chat, you can easily close the panel by clicking the X in the top right corner. To reopen it, simply click the speech bubbles icon in the bottom menu.

How do I message a creator?

This article will guide you through sending direct messages to creators whose communities you’ve joined on Patreon.

When can I message a creator?

You can privately message creators on Patreon if one of the two conditions is true:

  • You have one processed payment with the creator through Patreon
  • You currently have an active membership with the creator on Patreon

If you are not yet a paid member and want to reach out to a creator, you’ll need to contact them outside of Patreon.

Due to some recent changes, the ability to filter messages by Unread is not currently available.

How to message a creator from your Inbox

If you’ve processed one payment with a creator, you can send them a direct message from your Inbox even if you’ve canceled your membership. You can search by keywords or creator name to find a message thread.

Follow the steps below to message a creator from your Inbox:

- Click Chats
- Click [Direct messages](https://www.patreon.com/messages?mode=campaign&tab=direct-messages)
- Your conversations will be listed on the left panel of your inbox page. Click into the search box and type your creator’s name to find a message thread or start a new conversation from the dropdown
- Click on the creator to begin a conversation
- Type up your message and hit Enter or click the Send button
    - While typing your message, if you want to enter a new line, hit Shift + Enter
  • If you have a message thread with a creator, you can find a previous message with them on the left-hand panel.
    • Tap on Chats
    • Tap on Direct messages
    • You can tap on an existing message to see a past conversation or tap on at the top right corner to start a new direct message thread with a creator
    • Type your message in the text field and tap on the Send button when you’re happy with your message

How to message a creator from their Patreon

If you have an active membership with a creator, you can send them a private message directly from their page on Patreon. If you are a former member and would like to send a creator a direct message, you can do so from your inbox.

To message a creator from their page, do the following:

  • On Desktop, select the creator you want to message
  • Once you’re on their page, click More
  • Type up your message and hit Enter or click the Send button
    • While typing your message, if you want to enter a new line, hit Shift + Enter

FAQ

  • Your membership may have been removed. If you’ve been blocked from having a membership with a creator, you won’t be able to message them.
  • Not at the moment. If you need to fully delete all data from Patreon.com, you can submit this request from our Privacy Center.
  • Direct messages can only be sent from creators to their members and from members to their creators. There currently isn’t a way for members to send direct messages to one another.
  • There are two ways you can engage with other members who are in the same communities as you:
    • Comments: If a creator you’re a community of has comments enabled for their posts, you can add your comments to the conversation
    • Community chats: If a creator whose community you’ve joined has community chats for their members, you can engage with other members through chats you have access to
    • Learn more about community chats.
  • Fans who have been suspended by Trust & Safety go into a read-only mode in which the fan is unable to message the creator.

How to find a creator’s posts and Quips

As a member, posts and Quips can be found in a few different places across Patreon on Desktop and the Patreon mobile app. This article details where you can find and enjoy the work creators share with you.

On Desktop

Home feed

When you log in, you’ll land on the Home screen. This is where you’ll find the latest updates from creators you’re subscribed to.

Finding Quips on Desktop

Quips may appear in your Home feed on desktop. You can also visit a creator’s page to browse their Quips in the Quips tab, or in the Quips shelf on their Home tab if they have chosen to add one. Creators can also share direct links to individual Quips.

How to search through a creator’s posts

When you visit the Posts tab on a creator’s Patreon page, you can filter by a specific time, media type, and tier, or search by keyword to find exactly what you’re looking for:

  • Media type, tier, and month: Use these filters to browse audio, image, video posts, and more. You can filter content by membership tier and by month and year
  • Search bar: Search using keywords to quickly find a specific post
  • Sort order: Switch between newest to oldest or oldest to newest
View a creator’s collections

Some creators use collections to organize their posts by topic or theme. If you’re a member of a creator who uses collections, you’ll find a Collections tab on their page.

Clicking on the Collections tab takes you to a page listing all of the creator’s collections. At the bottom of the page, you’ll also see posts tagged by the creator if they use tags to organize their work.

Your access to posts depends on your membership. If you can’t see some posts, it may be because they’re exclusive to a different membership tier. Learn more about why you can’t access posts.

On the Patreon mobile app

Home tab

When you log in or tap on the Home tab in the bottom menu, you’ll arrive at the app home screen. The Home screen is split into two tabs:

  • Home feed: A discovery feed showing posts and Quips from creators you don’t yet follow, alongside creators you already support. Posts from creators you’re already a member of are always prioritized
  • Memberships feed: A feed reserved entirely for posts and Quips from creators you’re already a member of. Use this tab to keep up with your existing memberships without the discovery mix

There’s also a shortcut in the Home tab that lets you quickly see a list of the creators you support, so you can jump straight to a creator’s page and catch up on their latest posts without scrolling the feed.

Finding Quips on the app

Quips appear in both the Home feed and the Memberships feed on the app, alongside posts from creators you support. You can also view all of a creator’s Quips by visiting the Quips tab on their page.

Finding creator’s work in your Library

The Library in the bottom menu is where you can find all your saved and in-progress content in one place. This includes:

  • Recently played: Audio and video posts you’ve been listening to or watching
  • Recently viewed: Posts you’ve browsed recently
  • Saved posts: Posts you’ve saved for later
  • Purchases: Digital products you’ve bought from creators
  • Automatic downloads: New episodes from podcasts, music, or audio from creators you support, downloaded automatically when this setting is enabled

To learn more, visit our guide on navigating the Patreon app as a member.

View a creator’s collections

Some creators use collections to organize their posts by topic or theme. If a creator has collections, you can visit the Collections tab on their page to browse them.

Your access to posts depends on your membership. If you can’t see some posts, it may be because they’re exclusive to a different membership tier. Learn more about why you can’t access posts.

Search through a creator’s posts on the app

To search for a specific post, visit a creator’s Patreon page and tap Explore in the top right corner of the screen:

  • Type the name of the post in the search bar
  • Use the media quick links to filter by media type (Audio, Video, Image, Text, Polls, Links)
  • Tap Filter to sort by oldest posts first or to show only posts within your membership

How to fix issues with your audio RSS feed (Member)

This step-by-step guide will help you troubleshoot potential issues with your private RSS feed so you can get back to enjoying your creator’s work. Remember, you’ll only receive a private RSS feed if a creator you support offers this feature through Patreon. To learn more about the Podcast settings, see the How to use your audio RSS guide.

Resolving Audio Issues on the Patreon App

If you’re experiencing issues listening to audio within the Patreon app from creators you joined, try the following steps:

  • Power off and then restart your device
  • Log out of your account on the Patreon app
  • Uninstall and then reinstall the Patreon app. Use the latest versions linked below:
    • Patreon app for iOS
    • Patreon app for Android
  • Log back into the Patreon app

To ensure your device runs at its best, it’s essential to regularly check for software updates and install the latest version available. If you find yourself in an area with poor reception, connecting to WiFi can greatly enhance your connectivity and overall performance.

Resolving Issues with Your RSS Link

Since the RSS link relies on third-party apps, you may encounter issues while trying to listen to your podcast. Try the following steps:

  • Uninstall and reinstall your podcast app
  • Unsubscribe and then resubscribe using the custom RSS link found in the Membership tab of the creator’s Patreon
  • Refresh the feed on your podcast app. Many apps use the pull-down feature or provide a refresh button
  • If you receive an error message like “URL/server cannot be found,” the RSS link may have been mistyped or miscopied. Try copying and pasting the RSS link again

When using a computer, you can find the RSS link in the Membership tab on the creator’s Patreon page. In the App, it’s available by tapping a Creator on your home feed, then tapping the three dots in the upper right corner, choosing the option Add to podcast app in the menu. If there is no RSS link, try refreshing the page, clearing your cache, or using an incognito browser.

Additional Troubleshooting Scenarios

  • Some podcast apps may not support private RSS feeds. Try using a different podcast app or RSS feed reader.
  • If your podcast app reports an invalid feed format, ensure the RSS link is correctly formatted. Additional characters or spaces can sometimes cause issues.
  • If you’re facing playback issues, check if the error is specific to one episode or all episodes. If it’s just one episode, there may be a problem with the file itself. Contact the creator for assistance.
  • The RSS link may occasionally need to be refreshed. If you suspect this is the issue, unsubscribe and resubscribe to the RSS feed using the most recent link provided.
  • Ensure your Patreon account is active and in good standing. Issues with your membership status can sometimes affect your access to the RSS feed.
  • Ensure that the third-party podcast app has the required permissions to access data on your device. Check the app settings and permissions.

If troubleshooting steps don’t work

If you’re still experiencing issues with your RSS feed, we recommend trying a different podcast app or RSS feed reader to see if the problem persists. Not all RSS apps support every RSS link, so using an alternative could help determine if your feed is functioning properly. Check out our article on how to use your custom audio RSS link for guidance on this process. If the issue continues across multiple apps, it may indicate a problem with the feed itself.

When to Contact Support

If these troubleshooting steps don’t resolve the issue, we recommend trying a different podcast app or RSS feed reader to subscribe. If problems persist, submit a request with Patreon Support, as there may be an underlying issue that our team can identify and troubleshoot.

How to gift memberships to other fans

When you gift a creator’s paid membership to someone else, you’re sharing great creative work while helping to grow a creator’s community.

This article covers how to gift a creator’s membership to another fan and redeem a gift from another fan on Patreon. To see how to redeem a gift from a creator, see this article.

Key things to know

Gifting a membership
  • You’ll need a Patreon account to gift a membership. If you don’t have an account yet, you can create one to start gifting
  • You can gift between 1-12 months of membership to any of a creator’s tiers as long as the tier is not limited. If a creator offers annual memberships, gifts of 1 year of membership will be at the discounted annual membership price
  • Only creators who use subscription billing can have their memberships gifted
  • Fans need to be 18+ to purchase gifts from 18+ creators

Please note: Gifted members are not eligible to earn merchandise rewards. Only memberships with payments made directly from the member’s own account are eligible for merch — progress toward merch rewards doesn’t begin until the member’s account successfully makes a payment.

Gifted Membership Scenarios

Use the toggles below to explore common scenarios and see how gifted memberships affect access and billing:

  • Let’s say someone who is already a member of a creator in their entry-level tier is gifted a membership to the same creator, at the same tier. In this case, the gift will apply as soon as it’s redeemed, and the paid period pauses.
  • For example:
    • Original Billing Date: 15th of every month.
    • Gift Redemption Date: 25th.
    • Gift Coverage Period: 25th to the 25th of the following month.
    • Remaining Paid Access: 20 days left on the original subscription when the Gift was redeemed, which runs immediately after the Gift period ends.
    • Next Billing Cycle: Starts after the remaining 20 days are finished (on the 15th).
    • Specific Access Period (Gift + Remaining Days): Paid access runs from the 25th (end of gift) to the 14th (the day before the original billing date).
  • Someone who is already a member of a creator in their entry-level tier is gifted a membership to the same creator at the higher tier. In this case, the gift will apply as soon as it’s redeemed, granting access to the high-tier benefits immediately and pausing the paid period.
  • For example:
    • Original Billing Date: 15th of every month
    • Gift Redemption Date: 25th
    • Gift Coverage Period: 25th to the 25th of the following month
    • Remaining Paid Access: If the member doesn’t upgrade, they will drop back to their prior tier when the gift period ends and will still have 20 days of paid access left on the original subscription when the Gift was redeemed, which runs immediately after the Gift period ends.
    • Next Billing Cycle: Starts after the remaining 20 days are finished (on the 15th).
    • Specific Access Period (Gift + Remaining Days): Paid access runs from the 25th (end of gift) to the 14th (the day before the original billing date).
  • Someone who is already a member of a creator at the middle-tier is gifted a membership to the same creator at a lower tier. In this case, the gift will apply as soon as it’s redeemed, granting access to the tier benefits immediately and pausing the paid period.
  • For example:
    • Original Billing Date: 15th of every month
    • Gift Redemption Date: 25th
    • Gift Coverage Period: 25th to the 25th of the following month
    • Remaining Paid Access: If the member doesn’t upgrade, they will revert to their prior tier when the gift period ends and will still have 20 days of paid access left on the original subscription when the Gift was redeemed, which runs immediately after the Gift period ends.
    • Next Billing Cycle: Starts after the remaining 20 days are finished (on the 15th).
    • Specific Access Period (Gift + Remaining Days): Paid access runs from the 25th (end of gift) to the 14th (the day before the original billing date).
  • When a member cancels a Gift before the gifting period ends, they lose access right away. If a paid membership exists, billing resumes immediately, using the remaining days of paid access from the original subscription when the Gift was redeemed.
  • You can only have one gifted membership per tier at a time. If you try to redeem a second gift for the same creator, regardless of tier, you’ll receive an error message. You can either wait for the current gift to expire or cancel it in Membership Settings.
Redeeming a gift membership
  • People with an active paid membership can now redeem gifted memberships without disrupting their current subscription
  • People must have or create a Patreon account to redeem a gift
  • Gifts must be redeemed within 90 days. Unclaimed gifts will expire and are not eligible for refunds or exchanges, even for anything else of equal value
  • Gifts can be redeemed on desktop and mobile web
  • Once the recipient redeems the gift, they will have access to the selected membership tier until the gift period ends. They will receive notifications to remind them 3 days before the gift expires
  • Recipients need to be 18+ to redeem gifts from 18+ creators

Purchasing a gift membership

Where to begin

You can start gifting from a few different places:

  • Through banners on creator pages
  • Through the overflow menu on posts
  • A Gift membership button on select posts
  • By typing patreon.com/creatorURL/gift directly into your browser

Each option leads you to the same gift creation flow, but the entry point determines where you first see it. Please note that when gifting a post, you will have the option to choose any tier that unlocks access to it, and your recipient will receive access to the selected membership tier for the number of months you choose.

What you need to get started

In the gift creation form, all you need to do is:

  • Select the tier
  • Define the membership duration as either 1 year, 1 month, or custom months (up to 11 months)
  • Choose the quantity of gifts you want to purchase
  • Add a custom message, if you’d like to
  • Proceed with the payment with an existing valid method saved, or add a new one
Step-by-step to complete your gift

To gift a paid membership to a creator of your choice, follow the instructions below while logged in on a desktop:

  • Add ‘/gift’ to the end of the creator’s Patreon URL (patreon.com/[creatorURL]/gift) or select the Gift banner visible in various locations on the creator’s page
  • A new page will open for you to Create a Gift
  • Select the tier, duration, and quantity you wish to purchase
    • You can also add a custom message, which is available right below the gift preview on the middle-left side (optional)
  • Once you’ve made your selection, go ahead and select Go to payment
  • Check out with a valid payment method saved to your account, or add a new payment method, and choose Buy now
    • If you purchased a gift for friends and family, copy the gift link and send it to your recipient
    • The gift will be available to redeem for 90 days before it expires
  • You’ll receive an email confirmation of your purchase, with the gift link for reference if you’ve purchased a friends and family gift

Please note: If you purchased a gift for the creator’s community — currently in Beta testing with a small group of creators — the creator will receive an email confirmation and can share your gift with their community.

Redeeming a friends and family gift

To redeem a gift, please create or log in to your Patreon account on desktop or mobile web and follow the instructions below. Mobile app redemption is not currently supported.

  • Click the link shared by your gift-giver
  • Click Claim now
  • When you’re ready, click Continue to start your gifted membership. Once activated, the membership will be valid until the date shown
  • Choose whether to stay on as a free member for updates at the end of your gift period
  • Start accessing all paid benefits to your gifted tier!
Converting a gift to a paid membership

At the end of the gift period, the recipient will lose access to the membership unless they choose to stay on as a paid member of the creator.

To facilitate this, we send a reminder notification 3 days before the gift expires, including an option to add payment details to turn their gift into a paid membership. They won’t be charged until after the gift period concludes.

FAQs

  • Anyone logged into a Patreon account can purchase a gift for another fan. Guest checkout is not available at this time. Note that only fans who have indicated they are 18 years or older can purchase a gift from 18+ creators.
  • Yes. You must be logged in to purchase a gift. If you don’t have an account, you can create one during checkout.
  • You can gift 1–12 months of membership for any non-limited tier that the creator offers. If the creator offers annual memberships, 12-month gifts automatically receive the annual discount.
  • To see whether a creator can be gifted, look for a Gift icon on their home page, or when you open a post. If you do not see a Gift icon, that creator cannot currently be gifted.
  • Yes. You can select how many gifts you want to buy in the checkout. To do so, simply select the tier you want to gift, and edit the ‘Quantity’ number up to 100 gifts. Once you’ve completed checkout, the link can be shared and redeemed up to the number of gifts you’ve purchased (max 100 gifts). If you’ve purchased multiple community gifts, the creator will be able to share that many gifts (up to 100) with their community.
  • No, any existing sales and discount codes will not apply to the gift price. However, if a creator offers annual memberships and you gift a 12-month membership, the annual discount will be reflected automatically at purchase.
  • New, free, existing, or cancelled members can redeem gifted memberships without canceling their current subscription. Please note that if a member redeems a gift to a lower tier, they might lose access to some posts. When the gift is for the same or a different tier than the current one, the billing cycle will continue uninterrupted, and gifted access will apply automatically once redeemed. This makes gifting more seamless for both fans and creators. Note that only fans who have indicated they are 18 years or older can redeem gifts for 18+ creators.
  • Yes. You must log in or create an account to redeem a gift membership.
  • You will be unable to claim a gift if:
    • The gift was purchased over 90 days ago and has expired
    • You’re attempting to claim a gift on the Patreon mobile app, which is not currently supported yet. You’ll need to switch to desktop or mobile web
    • You’re attempting to claim a gift for an Adult/18+ Creator, having indicated that you are not 18 years or older
  • Yes. Gifts must be redeemed within 90 days. Unclaimed gifts expire and cannot be refunded or exchanged.
  • Patreon provides a platform for members and customers to pay creators directly. For this reason, in most cases, Patreon will not provide refunds or exchanges on behalf of creators. Creators can issue refunds at their discretion within 90 days of purchase. Any refund requests should be made directly with the creator. Learn more about requesting a refund. Unclaimed gifts that have expired after 90 days of purchase will not be automatically refunded.
  • Your billing is paused, not canceled. When you redeem a gift:
    • Your current paid membership pauses immediately.
    • Your gifted membership begins right away at the gifted tier.
    • When the gift ends, your previous paid membership resumes, including any remaining access time you had already paid for.
  • Example: If you were 10 days into your billing cycle when you redeem a 1-month gift, you pause that cycle with 20 days remaining. After the gift ends, those 20 days resume.
  • Yes. You can redeem a gift for a higher tier, a lower tier, or the same tier. Regardless of the tier difference, your paid plan pauses and resumes after the gift ends.
  • You cannot redeem a gift that you bought yourself.
  • No. Even when purchasing multiple gifts:
    • Each gift is tied to its own redemption token, even if delivered through a single link
    • A single Patreon account can redeem each unique token only once
    • A link cannot be reused to activate multiple gifts for the same account
  • No. The subscription is paused, not canceled. After the gift, the member resumes their original tier and their billing schedule picks up where it left off.
  • Creators can share community gifts in whatever works for them, social media, posts, or through direct messaging.
  • If you’ve purchased the community gift anonymously, recipients will not see who gifted the membership. The creator will always see who has shared the gift. If you opted to purchase the community gift with your name visible, recipients will see that you gifted the membership on the redemption page.

Terms & Conditions

You may purchase a non-renewing, fixed-term membership subscription to a creator’s available tier as a gift for a specific recipient of your choosing, or for distribution to members of a creator’s community (“Gift Membership”).

Upon completion of payment, we will either: (a) generate a redemption link for you to share with your selected recipient through which they can redeem the Gift Membership, that sets out the tier, creator, fixed term of the gift, and, if you elect, your name and message to the recipient; or (b) provide one or more redemption links to the creator for distribution to their community or otherwise cause the redemption links to be distributed to that creator’s community on Patreon. Creators that are providing redemption links may choose to distribute Gift Memberships at their discretion and are under no obligation to do so. We reserve the right to modify the distribution method in the future without notice.

To redeem a Gift Membership, the recipient must have or create a Patreon account. Redemption must occur within 90 days of purchase (the “Redemption Period”). If not redeemed within the Redemption Period, the Gift Membership will expire and access will not be granted.

If redeemed, the recipient will enjoy access to the gifted tier for the fixed term, provided they maintain a Patreon account. Access will automatically end when the term expires.

All Gift Membership purchases are final. No refunds or exchanges (including for unredeemed gifts) are permitted. Nothing in these terms entitles any gift recipient to enforce rights against Patreon.

How to use your audio RSS

If you’ve joined a creator’s Patreon who has a podcast, you may have access to a private audio RSS feed to listen to the creator’s work on the go.
