RSS, or Really Simple Syndication, allows you to subscribe to a web feed that updates with audio files—or audio extracted from videos—from the posts a creator publishes on Patreon

If a creator has enabled our private RSS feature, this article will help you locate your RSS link, subscribe to it on a podcast app, and learn key details about using your private RSS feed. For troubleshooting, visit our article about How to fix issues with your audio RSS feed.

How to locate and use your audio RSS

If private audio RSS has been enabled for your membership, you can locate your private RSS link in three places on your account:

- Go to the creator's page
- Click on More
- Click Your membership
- Go to the option Listen in other podcast apps
- Select either Spotify or Other podcast apps. A pop-up will appear
    - If you selected Spotify, click the Connect to Spotify button to listen to your exclusive RSS feed on your Spotify account
    - If you choose to listen on Other podcast apps, click on the Copy button to get the link to your clipboard
    - If the creator has more than one podcast, you’ll see a list of all available podcasts
- Paste the link into your podcast app or RSS app of choice - most apps will have the option to subscribe to a private RSS
  • You can also access your audio RSS link by clicking on the Collection tab on the creator page and selecting the podcast from the list. Once you’re on the Collection page, click the Add to podcast app button. A pop-up will show up, and then click Copy to get the RSS link in your clipboard. After that, you can paste it into your preferred podcast app.
  • After joining a creator’s membership with a podcast show, you’ll receive an email notification with an option to copy your RSS subscription link. To locate the email, try searching your inbox for:
  • Congrats, you’re now a member of [Creator’s name]
    • Go to the creator’s page
    • Tap More
    • Tap Add to podcast app. If you are on an Android device, this will copy the link to your clipboard. If you are on iOS, you’ll be prompted to open one of the compatible apps or copy the RSS link
    • Paste the link into your podcast app or RSS app of choice. Most apps will have the option to subscribe to a private RSS
  • You may also access your audio RSS link on mobile web by visiting the creator’s Patreon and clicking on the Membership tab to locate your link for other podcast apps or to listen on Spotify.

Finding episodes once you subscribe

Each podcast app is different, but generally, you can find the episodes by searching for a section that says Episodes, Shows, or Library within the podcast app.

Key things to know about your private audio RSS

  • Do not share your private RSS link
  • It is unique to your membership and contains an authorization token that links directly to your account. Sharing your private link with others is a violation of Patreon’s Terms of Service. If we detect a link being shared outside of your account, the link may be automatically reset, and repeated violations could temporarily suspend your ability to comment or send DMs to creators. Continued sharing could result in further action to protect creators’ content
  • Apps that share RSS feeds with other users are generally restricted from hosting our feeds, and many are blocked
  • Your account may be blocked if the feed is found on another site
  • Some apps do not support podcast authentication
  • Learn more about which apps your private RSS will work with
  • Some apps require creators to submit feeds themselves and may charge a fee
  • These apps will not allow you to add your RSS feed because the Patreon creator cannot create a feed without authentication
  • Not all posts will show up in your feed
  • Only podcast episodes will appear in your RSS feed. These can include audio posts or audio extracted from video posts, but they must be designated as podcast episodes by the creator. This means that not all audio or audio from videos will show up—only those the creator has specifically added to their podcast
  • Other types of posts, such as text, videos, or external audio links (like SoundCloud), will not appear in your RSS feed. You can access these media types by visiting the creator’s Patreon page directly.
  • Data fees from your phone company may apply when you download podcasts
  • Many podcast apps have settings to limit the number of downloads per show, such as downloading only the three newest episodes. You may also set your app to download only over WiFi rather than using your phone’s data connection. Please check the settings on your phone and the app you use for more information

I don’t have my Discord role

If you’ve connected your Discord account to Patreon, but aren’t finding that a creator’s server has been added on Discord, we’re here to help.

In this guide, we’ll help you through:

  • Checking that your creator has our Discord integration enabled
  • What to do if you don’t have access to the server
  • Next steps

Does the creator offer Discord roles?

You can find out whether or not a creator offers Discord roles by visiting their creator page. Even if they say that they offer Discord as a benefit, they might not have the integration properly set up.

You can check out their Tier by going directly to their page. If you can’t find the Discord logo followed by the text: Includes Discord Rewards at the bottom of the reward tier description, then the integration is not set up properly.

If you should have a role on their server, but don’t find Includes Discord Rewards, get in touch with your creator – they’ll likely need to troubleshoot their Discord set up on their account.

I don’t have access to my creator’s Discord serverIf it’s been a few hours and you still don’t have access to a creator’s Discord server, then there are a few troubleshooting steps you can try that should get everything up and running. Before going through the steps below, make sure that the Discord account you’ve connected to Patreon is also the account you’re logged into on Discord.

  • First, disconnect your Discord and Patreon account. To do this, click on Settings from your patron profile. Then click on Connected Apps from the menubar, and click on the Disconnect button for Discord.
  • Log out of Discord — here is how to log out of Discord
  • Head back to your Connected Apps and click on the Connect button next to Discord.
  • Log back into your Discord account — you should now have your correct role.

If you still don’t have access to the Discord role tied to your Tier:

If you have followed these steps and still don’t have access, there may be an issue with how the creator has set up their Discord Bot.

We recommend reaching out to the creator, to ensure their Patreon Bot is above the roles in their Discord server. Here is an article that will help them out check that their Discord integration is set up properly.

I still don’t have my role in Discord – what next? If you have followed these steps and still don’t have access, it’s likely that something isn’t quite right with the integration on the creator’s end.

In order for our Discord Bot to work, the creator must not assign the Bot to any of their Tiers and the Patreon Bot must be above their other roles.

We recommend reaching out to the creator and asking them to check their Bot position – is it above their roles in their Discord server?

Here is an article that may help them out.

Once the creator moves their Bot above other roles in their server and makes sure the Bot is not assigned to your Tier, you should be all set.

If things still aren’t working as they should, scroll down and send us a note about the issue. Please include as many details as possible: browser type, device type, are you on the mobile app? These details will expedite the process.

Join community chats

Make sure you follow this guide while in your member profile. You can use the profile switcher to change between your creator and member profile by tapping on your profile picture in the top right corner of the Home tab

What is a community chat?

A community chat is where you can chat with creators and other members outside of the comment section. Connect with your favorite creators and get to know people from all over the world who share your interests and passions!

How community chats work

Join a community chat

Follow the steps below to join a community chat:

  • If you are also a creator, follow this guide while in your member profile. To check, click on your profile photo in the bottom left corner and click on your member profile if your creator profile is selected.
    • Click on Community on the right-hand side
    • Click on the chat you want to join and agree to the guidelines — By agreeing, you allow your name and photo to be shown in the chat. You also agree to follow Patreon’s Community guidelines and Privacy policy
  • Make sure you follow this guide while in your member profile. You can use the profile switcher to change between your creator and member profile by tapping on your profile picture in the top right corner of the Home tab .
    • Go to the Patreon mobile app (Android or IOS) and tap the Community tab from the bottom app menu. You can also find the Chats tab on any creator’s Patreon page that offers chat.
    • Tap on the chat you want to join and agree to the guidelines — By selecting I agree, you allow your name and photo to be shown in the chat. You also agree to follow Patreon’s Community guidelines and Privacy policy

Once you join and open a chat, you can go to that chat’s settings page by clicking on View details below the chat’s name (web) or by tapping the chat name at the top (app). This is where you’ll find:

  • The chat guidelines
  • More chats from the same creator
  • Other members with access to the chat

Access to chats is based on the membership option your creator selected for each individual chat; this means that depending on the membership option you are in, you may have access to different chats than a person with a different membership option.

All chats you have access to as part of your membership will show up on your Community tab on both the app and web, so you can join them by agreeing to the guidelines. You can also do this through the Chats tab when visiting the creator’s Patreon page on the mobile app.

Chatting with the creator and other members

There are several ways members can interact with each other and with the creator through chats:

  • Type a message:
    • App: You’ll find the option to type your message at the bottom of the screen. Once you’re done, tap the arrow on the right side to send
    • Web: At the bottom of the screen, you’ll find a text box where you can type your message. Click enter or click the arrow on the right side to send
  • Start or reply to a thread:
    • App: Press and hold the message you want and tap Reply in thread
    • Web: Click the message you want and type your reply on the right-hand side of the page
  • React to messages:
    • App: Press and hold a message until you see the option to add a reaction with an emoji
    • Web: Click on a message and select the emoji from the list that pops up
  • Share photos directly from your device: You and other members can share photos directly from your device by tapping on the photo icon when writing a message

Chat guidelines and reporting

Chat guidelines are rules for the community space, and they exist to keep you and the community safe. You will not be able to join a chat without first agreeing to the chat guidelines.

You can check the chat’s guidelines anytime by opening a chat and clicking View details below the chat’s name (web) or tapping the chat name at the top (app). This will take you to that chat’s settings screen, where you’ll find the Chat guidelines.

How to report a message:

You should feel comfortable reporting messages that don’t adhere to or abide by chat guidelines directly to the creator.

Here’s how you can do it:

  • If you are also a creator, follow this guide while in your member profile. To check, click on your profile photo in the bottom left corner and click on your member profile if your creator profile is selected.
    • Click on Community on the right-hand side
    • Click on the chat you want to open
    • Select the message you want to report and click the three dots button … next to the emojis
    • Click Report message — You’ll be asked why you are reporting the message. Select the reason that applies
  • Make sure you follow this guide while in your member profile. You can use the profile switcher to change between your creator and member profile by tapping on your profile picture in the top right corner of the Home tab .
    • Go to the Patreon mobile app (Android or IOS) and tap the Community tab from the bottom app menu
    • Tap on the chat and press and hold the message you want to report
    • Select Report Message — You’ll be asked why you are reporting the message. Select the reason that applies
    • Tap Confirm

Please note that reporting a message is not anonymous. Your creator will be notified that you reported the message, and they will decide whether to keep or delete it. On the other hand, the person who sent the message will not know you reported it.

Block a person
  • If you are also a creator, follow this guide while in your member profile. To check, click on your profile photo in the bottom left corner and click on your member profile if your creator profile is selected.
    • Click on Community on the right-hand side
    • Select the chat you want to open
    • Click on any message the person you want to block sent and click the three dots button (…) next to the emojis
    • Click Block a person
  • Make sure you follow this guide while in your member profile. You can use the profile switcher to change between your creator and member profile by tapping on your profile picture in the top right corner of the Home tab .
    • Go to the Patreon mobile app (Android or IOS) and tap the Community tab from the bottom app menu
    • Select a chat
    • Tap on any message sent by the person you want to block and long press the message until you see the option to block
    • Select Block person then tap the Block button to confirm

Blocking someone means you will stop seeing their messages on chats. When someone you block sends a message to a chat you’re a part of, they will show up with the following message “You Blocked [Name], Unblock”.

What being muted means

Members can be muted for 24 hours in a chat. If you’ve been muted in a chat, you’ll see a message letting you know that you’ve been muted, along with the amount of time left before you can message in that chat again.

FAQ

  • There is no limit to how many chats you can join. If the creator is using chats and they are available for your membership, you will always have the option to join that chat.

Listen to audio on the Patreon app

The Patreon mobile app offers a range of features that can take your listening and viewing experience to the next level. Download the app and tap on the Play tab to start enjoying the latest content from your memberships or pick up where you left off.

Listening on Android TV App? This article covers the Patreon mobile app. On Android TV, you can watch video and listen to audio, but queueing and autoplay aren’t available yet. See Navigate the Patreon app as a member for what’s currently supported.

Library

The Library tab is where you can find all content saved or in progress. You can tap the arrows to go through the full list.

The Library is organized into three sections:

  • Recently played: Audio and video posts you’ve been listening to or watching, listed in order of recent activity
  • Recently viewed: Posts you’ve browsed recently
  • Saved posts: Posts you’ve saved for later

Tap Your account in the top right corner of the Library tab to manage:

  • Automatic downloads: When enabled, audio and video posts from creators you’re a member of are automatically downloaded to your device for offline listening and viewing
  • Delete finished downloads: Removes audio and video posts from your device once you’ve finished listening to or watching them, helping you manage your storage
  • Video download quality: Adjust the quality level for downloaded videos. A lower quality uses less storage space, while a higher quality provides a better viewing experience

Audio Player controls

There are several ways you can interact with our audio player to enhance your listening experience:

  • Resume listening: When you pause the player in the app and come back, your position is saved so you can resume playback right where you left off
  • Skip forward and back: By tapping on the forward or backward skip button, you can easily skip ahead or go back in 15-second intervals
  • Adjust the audio scrubber: You can move the playback position forward or backward by dragging the slider left or right, or by tapping on a specific point on the timeline of the audio
  • Adjust playback speed : The Patreon podcast player offers different playback speeds (0.25x to 2x), allowing you to adjust the speed to your liking
  • Casting Audio from a mobile device : You can cast audio using iOS Airplay if you’re on an Apple device, or Chromecast if you’re using Android. If there are no compatible devices nearby, the cast option is grayed out
  • Sleep timer : You can set a timer for the audio file to stop playing after a set amount of time
  • Add to queue : Control what’s playing next by adding audio posts to your queue

Managing Your Queue

Looking to line up multiple episodes or posts? The queue lets you build a seamless listening experience.

  • Tap the ••• menu on any audio/video post and choose Add to queue
  • Open the Queue from the mini player or full player to view your lineup
  • From your queue, drag items to reorder or swipe left to remove them

With the queue, you can curate your listening session and enjoy content without stopping between posts.

Want to turn off autoplay? Tap your profile icon in the top right corner, go to Settings , select Advanced settings, and toggle off Autoplay media. This gives you full control over what plays next.

Listen to Patreon exclusive audio on Spotify

If you have a membership with a creator who uses our Spotify integration, you can now start listening to your favorite podcasts directly on Spotify! Keep reading below to learn more.

How to link your Spotify account to Patreon

You’ll need to link your Patreon to your Spotify account in order to listen to your Patreon-exclusive episodes on Spotify. You can do this from your Patreon account or directly from Spotify.

When using Patreon on your computer, you can see if a creator has synced their Spotify account to their Patreon by going to your Membership tab on the creator’s Patreon page. You’ll notice a Spotify button under the section Listen in other podcast apps if the creator you’re a member of offers that option for your membership.

If you already have a Patreon account and a membership with a creator that offers the option to listen on Spotify, log in and follow the steps below

From Patreon
- Click Settings from the left-side navigation menu (if you're also a creator, click Your account in the bottom-left corner and select Settings)
- Select More and then [Connected apps](https://www.patreon.com/settings/apps) (if you're also a creator, you'll see Connected apps directly)
- Click on Spotify under App Integrations and select the Connect button
- You’ll be prompted to log in with your Spotify account. If you don’t have a Spotify account, you can also sign up instead by clicking on Sign up for Spotify
- Follow the instructions on the screen and click Agree
- You've successfully linked your Spotify account to Patreon! From the [Connected Apps](https://www.patreon.com/settings/apps) page, you can see a list of Available exclusive Podcasts with links to Listen on Spotify that are available as part of your membership
- Go to the creator's profile
- Tap More
- Tap Add to podcast app
- A new page will appear. If the creator has enabled distribution on Spotify, you’ll see the option on this page. Tap the Add button in the Spotify
- You’ll be prompted to log in with your Spotify account. If you don’t have a Spotify account, you can also sign up instead by clicking on Sign up for Spotify
- Follow the instructions on the screen and click Agree
- You've successfully linked your Spotify account to Patreon! You will see a page with a list of exclusive Podcasts you can listen to on Spotify as part of your membership
From Spotify

You can also link your Patreon account from Spotify directly. If you don’t have a Patreon account or a membership to that creator, you can sign up for both from your Spotify account and unlock access to the content:

  • Go to Spotify and make sure you are logged in to your account
  • You can use the search if there’s a particular creator you are looking for
  • You’ll find that the Patreon exclusive content will be marked by a padlock with a Paid tag
  • Click on the padlock icon next to the locked episode
  • A prompt will show up, letting you know you need to support the creator to access the exclusive Patreon audio. Click on the Let’s go button
  • You’ll be asked to link your Patreon account to Spotify. You can either log in with your existing account or sign up and create a new one
  • After logging in/creating an account, click Agree
  • If you don’t have a membership with the creator, you’ll be asked to choose a membership to join the creator’s community on Patreon
  • Add your payment information or use a saved payment method if you have an existing account
    • You can check what payment methods and currencies are currently accepted in our Patreon currency settings article
    • The Order Summary will give you a full breakdown of your payment
  • You’ll be taken to a Spotify page listing all the podcasts you have access to
  • You can also access your podcasts from your Connected Apps page on Patreon using a computer, where you can see a list of Available exclusive Podcasts with links to Listen on Spotify that are available as part of your membership

How to listen to your content on Spotify

Once you’ve connected your Patreon to Spotify, you can easily access the content in different ways directly from Patreon.

From your Settings
  • Click Settings from the left-side navigation menu (if you’re also a creator, click Your account in the bottom-left corner and select Settings)
  • Select More and then Connected Apps (if you’re also a creator, you’ll see Connected apps directly)
  • You’ll find a list of Available exclusive Podcasts with links to Listen on Spotify. Playable content on Spotify will be based on your membership access

Note: This option is not available on the Patreon app.

From your Membership page
- Go to the creator’s Patreon page, then click More
- Click on Your subscription
- Scroll down and select Spotify in the Listen in other podcast apps menu
    - As an alternative, you can also use the Podcast icon under the creator name and description on their page. When you click the button, a pop-up will appear.
- You’ll be prompted to the creator’s Spotify page, where you can listen to your podcasts. The episodes will show up on your Spotify like any other podcast
- Go to the creator's page
- Tap More , then select Add to podcast app
- A new page will appear. Tap Add button in Spotify
    - You’ll only see this option if the creator has enabled distribution on Spotify
- You’ll be prompted to the Spotify page of the exclusive podcast that you can listen to as part of your membership. Each podcast will have a link to listen to on Spotify directly.

FAQ

  • In order to listen to your Patreon-exclusive episodes on Spotify, Spotify needs to know which Patreon-exclusive episodes you have access to.
  • To that end, when you link your Spotify account to Patreon, you are sharing with Spotify a unique ID for yourself along with the list of creators you support on Patreon and the membership tiers to which you belong for each of those creators
  • You can do so from your Connected apps page. Click on Disconnect next to Spotify.
  • You won’t be able to listen to the episodes on Spotify once you disconnect your Patreon from the integration, but you can always connect again later to regain access.
  • You can see this information by going to your Membership tab on the creator’s Patreon page. If your creator is using the integration and if it’s available as part of your membership, you’ll find a Spotify button under the Listen in other podcast apps section.
  • The integration only supports audio posts. Any other posts, such as video posts, will not appear on Spotify.
  • After your membership term ends, you will no longer have access to the paid episodes on Spotify. When you lose access depends on the billing model chosen by the creator:
    • If you cancel a monthly (non-charge upfront) or per creation membership, you’ll immediately lose access to the paid episodes
    • If you cancel a charge upfront or subscription billing membership, access to paid episodes will be revoked at the end of your final billing cycle
    • When you cancel an annual membership, access to paid episodes will be revoked when your yearly membership ends
  • If the episodes are locked on Patreon, that will also be the case on Spotify.
  • Spotify access will mirror Patreon, so if an audio post is locked to you on Patreon, it will also be locked on Spotify.
  • Verify your payment status
  • By default, we lock a creator’s posts when a member payment declines and the same happens with Patreon content on Spotify. You can check your payment history to ensure everything is up to date. If you need any support with retrying a declined payment, please refer to this help guide: Retry my payment (decline)
  • Check your membership access
  • Some episodes might not be available to you if they’re not part of your membership. If an audio post is labeled as Locked on Patreon, you can click the Locked button to check which membership options have access. If your membership option isn’t listed, the creator didn’t include your membership when publishing the audio post, so you won’t be able to listen to it on Spotify.
  • Still can’t access the content?
  • If you’ve confirmed the above information and you are still having issues, here are a few troubleshooting steps you can take:
    • Confirm that you are logged into the correct Patreon, and Spotify accounts
    • Log out of your Spotify and Patreon accounts. Clear your cache and cookies and log back in
    • Disconnect and reconnect your Patreon account with Spotify. You can do this from the Connected Apps tab

Live notifications

When a creator schedules or starts a Live, you may get notified by email, push notification, or in your Patreon feed.

How Live notifications work

If a creator has email and push notifications turned on for their Live, you can get notified at a few key points:

  • When the Live is scheduled: You’ll get a notification letting you know the creator has scheduled a Live
  • Shortly before a scheduled Live starts: You’ll get a reminder, like a Live starts soon notification
  • When the creator goes live: You may get a creator is live now notification

If a creator turns off notifications when creating or scheduling their Live, you won’t receive the scheduled or Live now notifications for that Live.

Why am I not receiving notifications when a creator goes live?

A few things can affect whether you get a Live notification:

  • The creator turned off notifications for that Live. If this setting is off, you won’t receive Live notifications for it
  • You’re not included in the Live’s audience. Lives can be limited to certain tiers, so you’ll only get notified if you have access to watch it
  • Your notification settings are turned off. Check your notification settings and make sure Live notifications are turned on for email and/or push
  • Delivery may be delayed. Live notifications can take about a minute to send, so for very short or spontaneous Lives, the Live may end before you get the email
  • The email may have gone to spam or another folder. If you’re expecting an email, check your Spam, Promotions, or Social folders

Why am I receiving so many notifications when a creator goes live?

It’s normal to get more than one notification for the same Live — Patreon can send up to three: one when it’s scheduled, one as a reminder shortly before it starts, and one when the creator goes live. See “How Live notifications work” above.

You might also get extra notifications if:

  • You have both email and push notifications turned on — you’ll get one for each
  • You follow the creator from more than one Patreon account — if you have access through multiple accounts, each one gets its own notification
  • The creator scheduled multiple Lives or made multiple Live posts — each Live sends its own notifications

If you don’t take action in the next few weeks, we’ll automatically combine your profiles for you starting August 17th. Need help? Visit Combine your creator and fan profiles into a single identity or contact the support team for assistance.

This article serves as a guide to both members and non-members who have purchased or are considering purchasing from a creator who sells their work on Patreon.

Purchasing

Browsing the shop

To visit a creator’s shop on Patreon, you can either:

  • Go to their creator page and click on the Shop tab located at the top
  • Directly access through the link: patreon.com/[creator]/shop — (Make sure to insert the creator’s name in the [creator] section of the URL)

You can use the Sort button at the top left corner to filter the products to make it easier to find what you’re looking for. If you’re logged in and a paid member of that creator, you can see which items you get for free as part of your existing membership with that creator - Alternatively, you can also find all products included in your membership on your Purchases page.

Digital products

You can purchase digital products like videos, podcast episodes, images, and other files directly, whether you’re a member or not, through a creator’s Shop tab.

If you want to know more about a specific product, clicking on it will open a Product details page. Each product has its own dedicated product page where you can check information such as

  • Price
  • File type and size
  • Video and Audio files: You can check the file stream length, and, if available, you can also preview a clip of the content before purchasing it
  • Description of the product
  • Other products in the creator’s shop
Posts and collections

In addition to digital products, creators may also offer individual posts and collections for sale. Posts and collections available for sale will be visible in the creator’s Shop tab alongside other digital products. You can also purchase these directly from the specific post or collection on the creator’s page.

How to purchase

Mobile app purchasing on the iOS app is rolling out to fans in select countries and currencies. Visit our iOS in-app purchases: country & currency page for more information about where iOS in-app purchases are currently supported. Fans in other countries will be able to browse and view products on the mobile app but will only be able to purchase on the desktop or mobile web.

You can purchase through either the Computer or the Patreon app and access them in the Purchases tab, regardless of where the purchase was initially made.

- Click on the Buy now button next to the product you want to purchase
- You’ll be directed to a checkout page. Since you need a Patreon account to complete a purchase, you’ll be asked to either create an account or log in during the checkout process
- The Order Summary will give you a full breakdown of your purchase, including any sales tax that might be applicable – Read more about [Sales Tax on Patreon](https://support.patreon.com/hc/articles/360043055071-Sales-Tax-on-Patreon-for-members#h_01GS97JX5K7T4K20NMN48BCB3Z)
- If you have a saved payment method, you can use it to checkout. If you don't have a saved payment method, you'll be prompted to add one to complete the purchase
    - You can check what payment methods and currencies are currently accepted in our [Patreon currency settings](https://support.patreon.com/hc/articles/204606275) article
- After completing the checkout, you can immediately view the item. You will also receive an email receipt with the link to your product
- Tap on the creator’s profile image to access the creator's home screen
- Tap the Shop tab
- Choose the product you want to purchase and tap the Buy Now button at the bottom of the screen
    - You can only purchase products through the iOS app if you’re located in the US or Canada. If you’re located in another country, you can still browse creator shops on the iOS app, but when trying to purchase, you’ll see a “This product isn’t available in your country” message on the screen
- After tapping Buy Now, you’ll be directed to the checkout process:
    - If you’re on Android: You'll find a payment details screen where you can check your payment method and your Order Summary
    - If you’re on iOS: You’ll go through the native Apple store purchasing flow, and you’ll use the payment method associated with your Apple account
- After completing the checkout, you can immediately view the item. You will also receive an email receipt with the link to your product
    - If you purchased on iOS, you will get a receipt from Apple with a Manage link that leads to your Apple App Store purchase page

Accessing my purchases

Products you’ve purchased and have access to as part of a membership will automatically be available to you in your Purchases tab. Here’s how to access the Purchases tab:

  • If you are also a creator, follow this guide while in your member profile. To check, click on your profile photo in the bottom left corner and click on your member profile if your creator profile is selected.
    • Log in to your Patreon account
    • Once logged in, navigate to the Purchases tab. You can find this tab on the left-side navigation menu
    • Alternatively, you can also access your purchase by clicking on the provided link in your receipt email
  • Make sure you follow this guide while in your member profile. You can use the profile switcher to change between your creator and member profile by tapping on your profile picture in the top right corner of the Home tab.
    • Log in to your Patreon account
    • Once logged in, navigate to the Purchases tab
    • Alternatively, you can also access your purchase by clicking on the provided link in your receipt email
Viewing my Purchase History

If you want to keep track of your purchases and access your receipts, you can easily access your purchase history by following these steps:

  • If you are also a creator, follow this guide while in your member profile. To check, click on your profile photo in the bottom left corner and click on your member profile if your creator profile is selected.
    • Go to your Settings on the left navigation
    • Click on More and select Billing history
    • You can filter by Purchases to view your product-related billing history and receipts
    • If you want to download a receipt for your purchases, click on the Receipt link below Payment
  • Make sure you follow this guide while in your member profile. You can use the profile switcher to change between your creator and member profile by tapping on your profile picture in the top right corner of the Home tab.
    • Click on the menu in the top-left corner and go to your Settings
    • Select Billing history
    • You can filter by Purchases to view your product-related billing history and receipts
    • If you want to download a receipt for your purchases, click on the Receipt link below Payment
Purchased products becoming unavailable

If a product is unavailable in your Purchases tab or when you visit the product page, it was either deleted by the creator or did not meet our Community or Benefit Guidelines and cannot be accessed on Patreon. Products labeled as unavailable in a creator’s shop cannot be purchased.

We work with creators when products do not meet our Community Guidelines; however, there is no guarantee that the product will become available again. Please refer to the section below for more information about contacting a creator if a product becomes unavailable or is deleted.

Requesting a refund on a purchase

If you have any questions or need to request a refund for a digital product, you can easily get in touch with the creator by following these steps:

  • If you are also a creator, follow this guide while in your member profile. To check, click on your profile photo in the bottom left corner and click on your member profile if your creator profile is selected.
    • Go to your Purchases tab. You can find this tab on the left side navigation menu
    • Locate the specific item you would like to inquire about or request a refund for
    • Click on the product
    • Click on the three dots button in the top right corner
    • Select Message creator — Write your message to the creator — we recommend including your Order ID from your receipt in your message
    • Once you have finished writing your message, click the send button to forward it to the creator
  • Make sure you follow this guide while in your member profile. You can use the profile switcher to change between your creator and member profile by tapping on your profile picture in the top right corner of the Home tab.
    • Go to your Purchases tab
    • Locate the specific item you would like to inquire about or request a refund for
    • Click on the product
    • On the product page, click on the …(three dots) button located in the top right corner.
    • Click on Message Creator
    • Write your message to the creator. Once you have finished writing your message, click the send button to forward it to the creator

Reporting content

Keeping Patreon’s community safe is important to us, so we ask that you report any product that you believe does not meet our Community Guidelines. Here’s how you can do it:

  • If you are also a creator, follow this guide while in your member profile. To check, click on your profile photo in the bottom left corner and click on your member profile if your creator profile is selected.
    • Click on a product from the creator’s shop or, if you purchased it already, from your Purchases tab from the left navigation
    • You’ll find a three dots button button in the upper right-hand corner
    • Click on Report. You’ll be taken to a page where you’ll be asked to provide a reason for the report
  • Make sure you follow this guide while in your member profile. You can use the profile switcher to change between your creator and member profile by tapping on your profile picture in the top right corner of the Home tab.
    • Tap on a product from the creator’s shop or, if you purchased it already, from the Purchases tab
    • You’ll find a three dots button button in the upper right-hand corner
    • Click on Report. You’ll be taken to a page where you’ll be asked to provide a reason for the report

Trust and Safety might not directly share the result of their investigation or any follow-up actions that they might consider taking as a result of your report. If a reported product does not meet Patreon’s Community Guidelines, the creator will be notified, and the product will be hidden from their shop so it is no longer available for purchase. If you purchased a product that has since been hidden, it will be unavailable in your Purchases tab and may ultimately be deleted.

FAQ

  • No, anyone can purchase from a creator’s shop. The only requirement is that you create a Patreon account.
  • Accepted payment methods and currencies are the same as those currently supported for paid memberships. You can read more in member currency settings.
  • We are required by law to apply sales tax/VAT to purchases made in certain jurisdictions. You can see a breakdown of where we’re collecting sales tax from and what those tax rates are on Sales Tax on Patreon.
  • You can see more details about your payment and any tax paid at any time on your Billing history.
  • A product may be unavailable for a couple of reasons:
    • The creator has unpublished the product: if you already purchased the product, you can find it in your Purchases tab
    • The product did not meet our Community Guidelines, or it was deleted by the creator: the product is no longer accessible on Patreon
  • Please note that products that are marked as unavailable in a creator’s shop cannot be purchased.
  • Prices on the iOS app are higher by default to account for Apple’s App Store fees, charged by Apple. This ensures that creators earn at least the same amount on a product sale as they do if you purchase on the web.

Redeeming a gift from a creator

This article covers how fans can redeem complimentary memberships gifted by creators. For resources on how fans can redeem memberships gifted by other fans, see this article.

How gifting works

Here are some key things to remember about how gifts from creators work as a fan:

  • If a creator gifted you a membership, you can redeem it by visiting their unique gift link. You must have or create a Patreon account in order to redeem the gift
  • People with an active paid membership can now redeem gifted memberships without disrupting their current subscription
  • At the end of the gift period, you will lose access to the paid benefits unless you choose to stay on as a paid member of the creator. You will only be charged after your gifted membership ends
  • Gift redemption is available on desktop or mobile web. Mobile app redemption is not yet available
  • You must be 18 years or older to receive a gift from an Adult/18+ creator
Gifted Membership Scenarios

Use the toggles below to explore common scenarios and see how gifted memberships affect access and billing:

  • Let’s say someone who is already a member of a creator in their entry-level tier is gifted a membership to the same creator, at the same tier. In this case, the gift will apply as soon as it’s redeemed, and the paid period pauses.
  • For example:
    • Original Billing Date: 15th of every month.
    • Gift Redemption Date: 25th.
    • Gift Coverage Period: 25th to the 25th of the following month.
    • Remaining Paid Access: 20 days left on the original subscription when the Gift was redeemed, which runs immediately after the Gift period ends.
    • Next Billing Cycle: Starts after the remaining 20 days are finished (on the 15th).
    • Specific Access Period (Gift + Remaining Days): Paid access runs from the 25th (end of gift) to the 14th (the day before the original billing date).
  • Someone who is already a member of a creator in their entry-level tier is gifted a membership to the same creator at the higher tier. In this case, the gift will apply as soon as it’s redeemed, granting access to the high-tier benefits immediately and pausing the paid period.
  • For example:
    • Original Billing Date: 15th of every month
    • Gift Redemption Date: 25th
    • Gift Coverage Period: 25th to the 25th of the following month
    • Remaining Paid Access: If the member doesn’t upgrade, they will drop back to their prior tier when the gift period ends and will still have 20 days of paid access left on the original subscription when the Gift was redeemed, which runs immediately after the Gift period ends.
    • Next Billing Cycle: Starts after the remaining 20 days are finished (on the 15th).
    • Specific Access Period (Gift + Remaining Days): Paid access runs from the 25th (end of gift) to the 14th (the day before the original billing date).
  • Someone who is already a member of a creator at the middle-tier is gifted a membership to the same creator at a lower tier. In this case, the gift will apply as soon as it’s redeemed, granting access to the tier benefits immediately and pausing the paid period.
  • For example:
    • Original Billing Date: 15th of every month
    • Gift Redemption Date: 25th
    • Gift Coverage Period: 25th to the 25th of the following month
    • Remaining Paid Access: If the member doesn’t upgrade, they will revert to their prior tier when the gift period ends and will still have 20 days of paid access left on the original subscription when the Gift was redeemed, which runs immediately after the Gift period ends.
    • Next Billing Cycle: Starts after the remaining 20 days are finished (on the 15th).
    • Specific Access Period (Gift + Remaining Days): Paid access runs from the 25th (end of gift) to the 14th (the day before the original billing date).
  • When a member cancels a Gift before the gifting period ends, they lose access right away. If a paid membership exists, billing resumes immediately, using the remaining days of paid access from the original subscription when the Gift was redeemed.
  • You can only have one gifted membership per tier at a time. If you try to redeem a second gift for the same creator, regardless of tier, you’ll receive an error message. You can either wait for the current gift to expire or cancel it in Membership Settings.

Redeeming a gift from a creator

Gifting has been simplified, making it easier to claim a gift. When you click a gift link, you’ll see a clear “Claim now” button and can start accessing the membership immediately.

To redeem a gift, please create or log in to your Patreon account on desktop or mobile web. Mobile app redemption is not currently supported.

  • Click on the creator’s gift link, and click Claim now
  • You’ll be prompted to log in to your Patreon account or create one if you don’t already have one
  • You’ll see a confirmation message that your gift period has started
  • You can opt to stay on as a free member after your gift period ends or choose to uncheck the box if you don’t want to stay on as a free member
  • Now you’re ready to access your paid membership benefits!

Viewing your membership expiration date

You can see how much time you have left on your gifted membership by clicking on the Settings link from the left-side menu and accessing your Memberships tab. You can also see this on the Membership tab of each creator’s page.

At the end of the gift period, you will lose access to the membership unless you choose to stay on as a paid member.

You will receive a reminder notification 3 days before the gift expires, including an option to add payment details to turn your gift into a paid membership. You won’t be charged until after the gift period concludes.

Converting to a paid membership

If a creator has gifted you a membership and you want to continue receiving paid benefits after the gifted period ends, you’ll need to complete the membership process by adding a payment method and opting into a paid membership. You will be charged once the gift period expires.

  • Click on your Settings from the left menu
  • Click on the Membership tab and view Gifted memberships
  • Select Extend for the membership you want to extend
  • You will see your monthly or annual payment amount, which you can choose to increase. Learn more about increasing your membership here
  • Fill in your payment information, if you don’t already have a payment method saved
  • Click the Subscribe now button to complete the checkout process

Your gifted membership will convert to a paid membership, and your payment method will be charged when the gift period ends.

FAQ

  • You will be unable to claim a gift if:
    • The gift was purchased over 90 days ago and has expired
    • You’re attempting to claim a gift on the Patreon mobile app, which is not currently supported yet. You’ll need to switch to desktop or mobile web
    • You’re attempting to claim a gift for an Adult/18+ Creator, having indicated that you are not 18 years or older
  • Creator-to-fan gifts are given by the creator. Please do not forward a gift link unless asked by the creator who gifted it.
  • Your gifted access starts as soon as you claim the gift and expires at the end of the gift period, which is between 1 and 12 months. The creator sets the gift availability redemption period, gift length, and number of gifts that can be claimed. You will receive a notification and email 3 days before your gifting period ends.

Share my support for a creator on social media

Social media is a great way to tell people who you’re supporting on Patreon! The Share buttons found on the creator’s page allow you to share their page on your Facebook or X feed.

Here’s how to share your support on social media:

  • Go to the creator’s Patreon page.
  • On the right side of the page, below the creator’s name, you’ll find a Share button.
  • You will see the option to share the creator page on Facebook, X, Tumblr, and Pinterest.
  • Click on the button for the feed you’d like to share this information with.

If you aren’t logged in yet, it will ask you to enter your login credentials. You can choose to add additional text about what you are sharing as well.

Troubleshooting Discord issues

This article serves as a guide to troubleshooting any issues you might have with Discord as a member. If you don’t know the steps to connect Discord to your Patreon account, please follow How do I connect Discord to Patreon (member) instead.

I’m not getting the pop-up window to log in to Discord

This typically happens if you have an ad blocker or browser extension blocking pop-up windows. Please disable these extensions while connecting Discord to Patreon

I’m not getting my role or access to my creator’s server

If it’s been a few hours and you still don’t have access to a creator’s Discord server, here are a few things you can check:

Check your tier level

It’s a good idea to check your tier level and if the creator offers Discord roles for that tier. To do this, please follow the steps below:

  • While logged in to your Patreon account, go to your creator’s Patreon (You need to have an active membership with this creator)
  • Click on the Membership tab at the top of their Patreon
  • Scroll down, and you’ll find a Your membership section in which you’ll find a description of your tier. If the tier offers Discord as a benefit, you’ll find a Discord logo followed by the text: Includes Discord Rewards at the bottom of the tier description

If you should have a role on their server, but you don’t find Includes Discord Rewards at the bottom of the tier description, get in touch with your creator – they’ll likely need to troubleshoot their Discord setup on their account.

Is your payment in good standing?

As with most rewards a creator offers, Discord roles depend on your billing status. If your payment declines, you will no longer have access to the role included in the tier you joined.

You can check your payment history to ensure everything is up to date.

Here’s how to verify your payment status:

  • While on your member profile, click the Settings link from the left sidebar navigation
  • From the menubar, click on More > Billing History link from the menubar
  • Scroll through your past payment history — if you notice any declined bills, you can click the Retry button and go through the necessary steps to reattempt the charge

If you need any support with retrying a declined payment, please refer to this help guide: Retry my payment (decline)

Are you in over 100 Discord servers?

Discord’s free offering lets users join up to 100 servers. If you’ve joined over 100 servers, you can upgrade to Discord’s Nitro offering (limit of 200 servers) or leave a different server before the Patreon bot can assign you to your creator’s server.

Are you still experiencing issues getting your role/ access to your creator’s server?

If you’ve checked everything on this list but you’re still not able to get your role/ access your creator’s server, please follow the steps below:

  • Disconnect your Discord and Patreon account. You can do this by clicking the Disconnect button next to Discord in your Patreon Apps settings
  • Log out of Discord. Here is Discord’s guide to help you log out: How do I log out?
  • Clear your cache and cookies
  • Head back to your Apps settings and click on the Discord Connect button
  • Authorize Discord again, and you should have your correct role!

Lastly, the issue may lie with the creator’s integration setup. You can message the creator directly on Patreon to ensure their Bot is above the roles in their Discord server.

Feel free to share these instructions to guide them through any potential issues: Discord isn’t working for my members.

What is Discord? (Member)

Discord is an all-in-one voice and text chat platform where creators can create invite-only worlds for members. Our Discord integration syncs creators’ Discord server roles with their Patreon tiers to grant exclusive access and permissions to members.

Discord does a great job of explaining what exactly a server is and how to use them here: Beginner’s Guide to Discord

Glossary of Discord terms

Discord has a specific vocabulary. Below are some terms they use and we use when describing Discord and Patreon’s integration. Please note the definitions below are taken directly from Discord’s resources and will be updated if changed by Discord.

Server: Servers are the spaces on Discord. They are made by specific communities and friend groups. The vast majority of servers are small and invitation-only. Some larger servers are public. Any user can start a new server for free and invite their friends to it. Creators often offer access to their exclusive invite-only servers as a Patreon benefit.

Channel: Discord servers are organized into text and voice channels, which are usually dedicated to specific topics and can have different rules.

  • In text channels, users can post messages, upload files, and share images for others to see at any time.
  • In voice channels, users can connect through a voice or video call in real-time, and can share their screen with their friends - we call this Go Live.

Roles: Roles are a way of designating who is who in a server. Creators will link their Patreon tiers to specific roles. If a creator offers Discord access, you’ll be assigned a role in their server that corresponds to your tier level. Roles can have their own set of server and channel-specific permissions.

DMs and GDMs: Users can send private messages to other users as a direct message (DM), as well as start a voice or video call. Most DMs are one-on-one conversations, but users have the option to invite up to nine others to the conversation to create a private group DM (GDM), with a maximum size of ten people. Group DMs are not public and require an invite from someone in the group to join.

Go Live: users can share their screen with other people who are on a server or a DM with them. This may be disabled by the server admin, so may not be possible when you join a creator’s member-exclusive server.

How can I get access to a creator’s Discord server?

Since our integration is synced with creators’ Patreon tiers, you can access their server by joining one of their tiers with Discord as an offered benefit. If a creator offers member-exclusive access to their server, you can link your Discord account to Patreon on your Apps settings page once you’ve joined the creator’s tier.

We’ve made this resource to guide you through how to connect Discord and Patreon.

Is Discord free?

Yes, it’s free to use! All you have to do is create an account: Create your Discord account.

Which podcast apps will my custom audio RSS link work with?

This article will go over which mobile apps can be used to listen to the audio posts your creator publishes on Patreon by using the RSS link for both iOS and Android. It will go over what an RSS feed is and how it may be a part of your membership. Along with that, we will cover the apps that do not work and some best practices on how to go about using the link in the most effective way.

What is an RSS feed?

RSS is short for Really Simple Syndication. It’s a great way to subscribe to a source of information or entertainment, such as a podcast, and get brief updates delivered to you. These sources are called feeds.

Many podcasters on Patreon offer private audio RSS feeds as part of their memberships. If you’re a member of a creator offering a private RSS link, you’ll be able to listen to their feeds in a podcast app.

Apps that will work with your custom RSS link

Below are the iOS and Android apps that work with Patreon. Please note, those with an asterisk (*) means also offer a paid service, and they may also offer ad-free streaming.

IOS Apps that work:
  • Apple Podcast (Visit our article on how to add your private RSS feed to your Apple Podcast app)
  • Castro (Visit this article on how to add your private RSS feed to your Castro app)
  • Downcast (Visit this article on how to add your private RSS feed to your Downcast app)
  • OverCast (Visit this article on how to add your private RSS feed to your OverCast app)
  • Pocket Casts* (Visit this article on how to add your private RSS feed to your Pocket Casts app)
  • Swoot
Android Apps that work:
  • Beyond Pod
  • Dog Catcher*
  • Player FM * (Important: you must register an account with them to import our private RSS.)
  • Pocket Casts * (Important: Visit this article by Pocket Casts support center to know more)
  • Podcast Addict*
  • PodcastGuru*
  • Podcast Republic*
  • Podcasts Tracker*
  • Podcasty
  • PodKicker
  • Swoot

Apps that will not work with your RSS link

Android apps that we’ve tested and do not work:
  • DoublePod
  • PodBean
  • Podcast App
  • PodcastHD
  • PodcastOne
  • Podomatic
  • Spotify (While Spotify does not support private podcast feeds, you can still listen to Patreon audios on Spotify. Read more below or go directly to the Help Center article: Listen to your Patreon exclusive audios on Spotify)
Apps that do not support authentication:
  • TuneIn Radio
  • Stitcher
  • Castbox
  • Amazon Music

Listen to your podcasts on Spotify

If you have a membership with a creator who uses our Patreon Spotify integration, you can listen directly to Spotify without needing an RSS link.

Visit the Membership tab on the creator’s Patreon to see if they have synced their Spotify and Patreon accounts. You’ll notice a button that says Listen on Spotify if the creator with whom you have a subscription offers that option for your membership.

Learn more about how to Listen to your Patreon exclusive audios on Spotify

What else should I know about my RSS link and feed?

Here are some important things to keep in mind when using your private RSS feed as a member:

  • Don’t share your private RSS Link! It is unique to your membership and contains an authorization token that links directly to your account. Sharing your private link with others is a violation of Patreon’s Terms of Service. If we detect a link being shared outside of your account, the link may be automatically reset, and repeated violations could temporarily suspend your ability to comment or send DMs to creators. Continued sharing could result in further action to protect creators’ content
  • Some apps will not allow you to add your RSS feed because they don’t support authentication on podcasts. As we discover these apps that are not compatible with RSS feeds, we will list them here in the not working section below
  • There are some apps that require the creators to submit the feeds themselves (and usually pay a fee to do so). These apps will not allow you to add your RSS feed because the Patreon creator, who owns the podcast, has no way to create a feed without authentication
  • Only audio posts that your creator has uploaded will populate your private RSS feed. Video and text posts will not appear in your feed. Additionally, audio link posts (like Soundcloud), will not appear in your RSS feed. Fear not — you can still access these posts by logging in to Patreon on your desktop, or the Patreon app
  • Data fees from your phone company may apply when you download podcasts. Many podcast apps have settings to limit the number of downloads per show; for example, downloading only the three newest episodes rather than all new episodes. Also, you may be able to set your app to download only over WiFi rather than using your phone’s data connection. Please check the settings on your phone and the app you use for more information

Why can’t I access posts?

Are you also a Patreon creator? From July 6, if you haven’t combined your creator and fan profiles yet, you won’t be able to use Patreon as usual, including posting and receiving payouts. To learn more, visit our guide on how to combine your creator and fan profiles into a single identity. Or if you’re ready, combine your profiles now.

One of the benefits of becoming a member is getting access to exclusive content via posts. If you’re not getting access to posts, there are a few things you can check to troubleshoot any issues.

Accessing posts from your emails?

Links to posts in email notifications give you access once without being logged in. If you follow the link from your email again, you may need to log in to view the post.

How to check membership access

If a post is labeled as Locked, you can click the Locked button to check which tiers have access. If your tier isn’t listed, the creator didn’t include your membership option when publishing the post.

If your tier is listed but you still don’t have access, please keep reading for other possible fixes.

Verify your payment status

By default, we lock a creator’s posts when a member’s payment declines. You can check your payment history to ensure everything is up to date.

Here’s how to verify your payment status:

  • On Desktop, click Settings from the left-side navigation menu (if you’re also a creator, click Your account in the bottom-left corner and select Settings)
  • Click More and select Billing history (if you’re also a creator, you’ll see Billing history directly)
  • Scroll through your past payment history — if you notice any declined bills, you can click the Retry button and go through the necessary steps to reattempt the charge

If you need any support with retrying a declined payment, please refer to the guide Failed payment help.

Please note that a member with a payment decline for over 1 month will be switched to a Free membership. The members whose payments had been stuck in decline since before January 2024 had their memberships terminated as of March 2026.

Confirm your membership details

Creators can segment post access based on the membership tiers they offer. That means you could be in a creator’s highest tier and come across a post you won’t have access to. You can check your membership details to confirm your access level.

How to check your membership details:

  • On Desktop, click Settings from the left-side navigation menu (if you’re also a creator, click Your account in the bottom-left corner and select Settings)
  • Click on Memberships in the top menu (if you’re also a creator, find the Account settings section, and click Memberships)
  • Find the creator in the list and click the View Details button to check your tier and membership details
  • From here, you can click Switch to another tier if you accidentally joined the wrong one, or if your membership shows as Custom pledge (which means you’re not in a tier and won’t have access to tier-specific content)

If the tier you switch to is priced the same as your current payment, you won’t be charged anything extra. Switching to a higher-priced tier may result in an immediate charge for the difference. Learn more about how billing works when you change tiers in our guide on How to change your tier.

Have you recently canceled?

If your membership was charged upfront and you recently canceled, you’ll have post access for the remainder of the current month (e.g., if you cancel on Jan 15th, you’ll have access through Jan 31st).

If your membership was monthly (non-charge upfront), or per creation, you’d lose access to posts when you cancel. You can learn more about what to expect when canceling: What happens when I cancel?

If you were charged with Subscription billing and you recently canceled, you’ll have post access until your membership ends (i.e., if your membership began on Jan 1, you’ll have access through Feb 1).

Accessing content outside of Patreon

We offer a variety of posting options for creators to share their podcasts, videos, and images with members. Even so, we understand that many creators prefer keeping their exclusive content on a site they manage outside of Patreon.

If you find yourself locked out of content that your membership should give you access to, and you’ve gone through the checklist in this article, reach out to the creator for the next steps in regaining access.

FAQ

  • If a post is locked for your membership but you believe you should have access, please let your creator know. They’ll know more about what posts you should be able to access and can fix post access issues if there’s a mistake.
  • Each creator has a unique approach to how they run their membership. Creators can set post access in the following ways:
    • Everyone: A gift to the world from your creator! These posts are available to everyone.
    • Paid members: All of a creator’s paid members will be able to view the post’s content — even folks with a custom pledge
    • Select tiers: Creators can select specific tiers with access to the post. This means that even if you’re in a higher tier, you may not have access to the post’s content. Read through your membership description for more information on expected access to posts. If you’re unsure, messaging the creator asking for clarification could clear things up.
  • Check in with your creator if your membership mentions access to benefits from all lower tiers. The post locked to you may not be benefit-related (like a call to upgrade). It could be an easily fixed mix-up or a change to the membership structure.
  • We give members the option to Choose what you pay at every tier. You can always give more than your tier costs, even if you don’t want to join a higher one.
  • We recommend upgrading your membership tier and not just the payment amount. Increasing your payment amount will not unlock new post content if you don’t select the higher tier.

Why can’t I comment on posts?

There may be a few reasons why you’re unable to comment on a post that you have access to, including that the creator may have disabled comments for all posts or a particular post, comment access isn’t included in your membership, or comments are being filtered. This article will detail the reasons why you may not be able to comment on a post that you can access.

Your email address is not verified

In order to add comments to posts you can access, you’ll first need to verify your email address. If you haven’t taken this security measure, you can click on the Verify your email link to complete this step. Once your Patreon account email has been verified, you can add your comment.

If you created your Patreon account with your Google account or Apple Sign-on, your email address is considered verified.

Comments are disabled

There are two reasons why you may see the message “comments are disabled for this post”:

  • If you are seeing this message on all of a creator’s posts, it means that the creators has decided not to allow comments on their posts.
  • If you are only seeing the message on some of a creator’s posts, it means that the creator has decided to disable comments for those posts in particular.

Creators can retroactively disable comments, so you may notice that comments are disabled on posts you had previously been able to comment on.

Upgrade to add a comment

If you are seeing a note that you can “upgrade to add a comment,” it means that the creator has given comment access to only paid members. Creators have the option to give comment access to all members, only paid members, or to not allow comments on posts. The option to upgrade to add a comment indicates that only paid members can add comments. Click the comment field to upgrade to a paid offering to add your comment.

Comment filtering

If a creator has enabled comment filtering for comments, we’ll automatically hide comments that may be spammy or potentially harmful to their community. If you believe that your comments are being mistakenly filtered, please submit a request to our support team for help.

The comment was removed by the creator

It is possible that the creator is moderating the comment section of their posts and determined that your comment should be removed. If you suspect this, you may be able to direct message the creator to learn more about the rules of engagement for their Patreon.

Learn more about direct messaging a creator.

Patreon says I can’t comment

To keep Patreon safe for everyone, we may limit your commenting ability if you have violated our Community Guidelines or we notice a higher-than-normal number of comments in a given time. If you see a message that you’re not able to comment at the moment due to spamming, you’ll need to wait a bit to add your comment later.
